records.title: Digital Platform on Precision Farming
records.description: The Digital Platform of Precision Farming is a national pilot project (2025-2026) that aims to develop and test a comprehensive digital platform for precision agriculture in Belarus. The platform will integrate various technologies including GIS, GPS, remote sensing, and data analytics to support farm management and optimize agricultural production. A national pilot that equips selected farms across Belarus with precision-farming capabilities and measures results in real field operations. One enterprise per region was selected (two in Minsk region), with planned investment of about USD 2.1 million and delivery of machinery plus upgrades in 2025.
records.abstract: National pilot under the state “Digital Development of Belarus” programme
records.owner_name: Ministry of Agriculture and Food of the Republic of Belarus

_annotations.Impact: The platform can boost productivity and sustainability by enabling precision farming that optimizes inputs and reduces environmental impact across Belarus. Key risks are adoption friction (new routines like calibration, soil sampling discipline, and data interpretation), data quality traps (wrong boundaries or weak sampling leading to “precisely wrong” recommendations), operational dependency (GNSS issues, hardware upkeep, mixed-fleet integration causing downtime), and uneven benefits if pilots favor large enterprises while smaller farms lag behind.

records.title: Digital technologies in agriculture and rural areas
records.description: Digital technologies in agriculture and rural areas is a comprehensive status report that examines how digital applications, platforms and data-driven tools are reshaping agricultural production, value chains and rural livelihoods. The report aims to identify the different scenarios where the process of digital transformation is taking place in agriculture. In addition, enablers are identified, which are the factors that allow adopting and integrating changes in the production and decision-making processes. These enablers include human, social, and ecosystem-level capacities that allow digital technologies to be adopted, used, and scaled effectively in agriculture, once basic conditions such as infrastructure, affordability, and policies are in place. Finally identified through cases, existing literature and reports demonstrate how substantive changes are taking place in the adoption of digital technologies in agriculture.

records.title: Digital technologies and solutions for beekeeping
records.description: The resource entitled “Digital technologies and solutions for beekeeping” provides an overview of how digital technologies are used in beekeeping and introduces beekeepers to their benefits. The innovations introduced span from precision beekeeping, record-keeping, traceability and market access, and efficient information exchange and capacity development. The technologies discussed range from simple bee scales to high-end blockchain solutions, providing a factsheet that benefits small-scale beekeepers in rural areas as well as tech-savvy bee farm owners, particularly in accessing finance.
records.abstract: An overview of innovative tools to support beekeepers
records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher
_annotations.Impact: The solutions outlined in the resource serve as a factsheet, providing an overview of how different digital technologies are integrated into beekeeping. The resource enables farmers to understand the benefits, constructive and practical input, and ways to improve decisions to increase value and livelihoods within the beekeeping practices. As of August 2025, the policy received a total of 752 downloads.

records.title: Digital technology and agricultural markets
records.description: Digital technology and agricultural markets is a resource designed to provide a non-technical overview of emerging digital technologies and their influence on agricultural markets and food value chains. The focus is on e-commerce platforms and distributed ledger technologies such as blockchain that enable more efficient and inclusive agricultural markets by reducing information asymmetries and transaction costs and improving financial inclusion along food value chains. The publication examines how digital platforms, artificial intelligence, distributed ledger technologies and 3D printing reshape information flows, improve efficiency, and strengthen the inclusion of small farmers in formal market systems.

records.title: Digital Valley Albania (DiVA)
records.description: Digital Valley Albania (DiVA) is a European Digital Innovation Hub project established to accelerate digital transformation among Albanian small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), with special emphasis on agriculture and tourism sectors. DiVA provides support for SMEs to adopt advanced digital technologies, improve operational capacities, access markets and innovation ecosystems, and contribute to Albania’s broader digital economy and rural development.
records.abstract: National digital-innovation hub accelerating digital transformation of SMEs

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Digital Valley Albania aims to bridge the digital gap among Albanian SMEs, notably in agriculture and tourism, thereby strengthening their competitiveness, productivity, and ability to integrate into modern value chains. According to the website, participating SMEs typically achieve 20 percent improvement in digital maturity and operational efficiency, and the same amount of percentage increase in enhanced cybersecuirty practices, and better environmental and social responsibility scores. Similarly, a reported 15 percent reduction in energy cost through digitalization was reported.

records.title: Digitalized Farm Advisory Services (IADK/AGRIVI)
records.description: This good practice is an example of how a farm management software platform was used to professionalize and scale advisory services for smallholder farmers when the Initiative for Agricultural Development in Kosovo (IADK) partnered with AGRIVI to digitize agricultural advisory services in Kosovo. Previously, advisory support was largely paper-based, making it difficult to track farm activities, standardize recommendations, and provide timely guidance to farmers. IADK adopted AGRIVI’s farm management software to: 1) Digitize farm records and advisory workflows; 2) Improve communication between advisors and farmers; 3) Provide data-driven crop management recommendations; 4) Increase transparency and efficiency in advisory delivery.
records.abstract: Digital advisory practice connecting IADK advisors with farmers
records.owner_name: Initiative for Agricultural Development of Kosovo (IADK)

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Digitalized Farm Advisory Services aims to improve advisory reach and quality by strengthening day-to-day communication and record-keeping between advisors and farmers through a single digital channel. The case study reports that IADK supports around 500 farmers per year, and that about 70 percent are smallholders, with the digital workflow helping address gaps in production, investment planning and information flow.

records.title: DIVINE (Demonstrating Value of agrI data sharINg for boostiNg data Economy in agriculture)
records.description: DIVINE is a Horizon Europe research and innovation project that aims to demonstrate the cost–benefit and added value of agricultural data sharing. The project develops an agricultural data space ecosystem to support interoperability, data governance, and data sharing across the agri-food sector. It validates data-sharing approaches through four pilot cases covering different agricultural production systems across multiple EU countries, providing evidence to support policy makers, technology providers and other stakeholders involved in the agricultural data economy.
records.abstract: Research and innovation project
records.owner_name: National Technical University of Athens (NTUA) – Institute of Communication and Computer Systems (ICCS) (project coordinator)

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher
_annotations.Impact: DIVINE pilots cover four agricultural production systems across multiple EU countries and demonstrate data-sharing approaches to support data-driven analysis and decision-making. The project aims to develop and validate analytical and benchmarking methods and support improved transparency and assessment of environmental performance through interoperable agricultural data. With a total project budget of EUR 3 954 797.50, DIVINE delivers reusable assets including the Agricultural Data Space Ecosystem (ADSE), the AIM+ semantic model, and IDS-compliant connectors.

records.title: Ebazaar.ge
records.description: Ebazaar.ge is a digital marketplace platform designed to connect Georgian farmers, cooperatives, and agribusinesses with buyers across the country. The solution enables the online listing, promotion, and sale of agricultural products, supporting market access, rural development, and food system efficiency. Ebazaar.ge is relevant for improving agricultural value chains and supporting food security through digital trade.

records.title: DRON.BEL
records.description: DRON.BEL is the brand of LLC “DronService”, providing turnkey agrodron operations for applying herbicides, insecticides, fungicides, desiccation and foliar feeding, with an end-to-end workflow: field digitization, mission planning, drone application, and reporting. The company also trains operators, offers in-season repair/service (incl. on-site response), and builds mobile mixing/charging stations to scale drone teams’ throughput.

records.title: eKontingente
records.description: eKontingente is a web-based platform operated by the Swiss Federal Office for Agriculture (FOAG) for managing general import permits and tariff quota shares for agricultural products. The platform is used in Switzerland by authorized importers and competent authorities to apply for permits, participate in quota-share auctions, request or transfer quota shares, and submit required declarations under different allocation procedures.
records.abstract: Web platform managing agricultural import tariff quotas

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: eKontingente aims to improve transparency and efficiency in administering agricultural tariff quotas by providing a single digital platform. The solution helps distribute limited import volumes among many actors through rule-based procedures and reduces administrative burden for FOAG, customs authorities and companies by digitizing processes and integrating with customs and financial IT systems.

records.title: E-Government Promotion for Improved Public Service Delivery

Implemented by UNDP in partnership with national institutions, the project aims to modernize public service delivery through online platforms, strengthen data governance and improve access to services for citizens and businesses, including rural communities.

records.title: Enhancing Multi‑Hazard Early Warning System to Increase Resilience of Uzbekistan Communities to Climate‑Induced Hazards
records.description: The project supports the Government of Uzbekistan in strengthening national capacities for climate risk monitoring, forecasting and early warning. It focuses on transitioning from hazard-based to impact-based multi-hazard early warning systems, enhancing institutional coordination, and improving the availability and use of climate and disaster risk information to support preparedness and response to climate change-induced hazards.
records.owner_name: Government of Uzbekistan; Green Climate Fund; United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher
_annotations.Impact: By mid-2024, the project reported the installation of 25 automated weather stations, 10 photoelectric meteorological stations and 47 hydrological measurement devices across seven regions of Uzbekistan. Project activities also included the training of 450 technical staff, the equipping of six emergency management centres, disaster preparedness training for more than 850 rural residents, and evacuation drills involving over 3 000 participants. According to project reporting, the upgraded multi-hazard early warning system provides national coverage and serves an estimated 32 million people, including approximately 11 million people living in high-risk areas. The transition from hazard-based to automated, impact-based forecasting is intended to enable earlier warning dissemination and support more risk-informed planning and preparedness compared to previous systems.

records.title: e-Podsticaji
records.description: e-Podsticaji is a national online portal within the eAgrar system that enables farmers in Serbia to submit applications for agricultural subsidies and rural development incentives electronically. _annotations.Impact: e-Podsticaji aims to make agricultural support more transparent and efficient by reducing paperwork and centralizing subsidy applications in a single portal. records.title: Climate Resilience and Agriculture Development Project (CRAD)
records.description: The Albania Climate Resilience and Agriculture Development Project (CRAD) is an integrated project focuses on improving innovation in agriculture, enhancing smart irrigation, and access to local and European Union markets. Specifically, to implement the objectives, a) the project targets to support the development of five Micro Food Hubs in the peri-urban areas in Tirana, Shkodra/Lezha, Vlora and Gjrokastra, b) develop two food product clusters in the regions of Berat and Dibra including olive oil, processed fruits and vegetables, and traditional food aiming to improve the rural tourism sector, c) create a Climate Smart Agriculture IT Platform to collect information such as soil type, hydrometeorological data and agriculture practices while guiding the farmers toward resilient agriculture practices, and lastly, d) modernize selected irrigation and drainage schemes to improve high-value agricultural production.

It serves small and medium-scale growers, artisan food makers and buyers (including households, restaurants and institutions) by enabling producers to list products, manage orders and reach multiple demand points without intermediaries. The platform provides farmers with online shopfront space and tools to display and sell farm products.

records.title: Copenhagen Food Cooperative (Københavns Fødevarefællesskab)
records.description: Copenhagen Food Cooperative (KBHFF) is a member-based and volunteer-driven food cooperative in Copenhagen, Denmark that facilitates direct access to locally produced organic and biodynamic fruit, vegetables and other food products through its website while strengthening community ties. Members can join and order their produce online. It serves both small producers and consumers seeking affordable organic food by organising weekly pre-ordered produce bags, communal pick-up points and cooperative decision-making. Members actively contribute labour and governance, helping reduce cost, build local food solidarity and address market access challenges faced by small growers and ethical consumers alike.
records.abstract: Cooperative member management and trading platform

_annotations.Impact: KBHFF aims to enhance local food access, community engagement and producer–consumer relationships in and around Copenhagen. As a cooperative model, it lowers costs for members by combining purchasing power with volunteer labour and prioritising organic and biodynamic products, sourced directly from small Danish farms. According to the KBHFF website, it supports hundreds of weekly vegetable and fruit distributions, encourages shared responsibility and promotes sustainable consumption patterns.

records.title: Cortilia
records.description: Cortilia is an intermediary that connects consumers with farmers and food producers through a centrally managed e-commerce and home-delivery service. It serves urban consumers seeking high-quality, traceable food and producers looking for stable market access. Cortilia is handling online ordering, payments, quality control and last-mile delivery. Cortilia relies on a digital e-commerce platform combined with data-driven logistics, inventory management and routing systems to coordinate sourcing, fulfilment and distribution at scale.
records.abstract: Farmer-to-consumer e-commerce supported by an intermediary

_annotations.Impact: Cortilia aims to support market access for small and medium-scale producers, improve product traceability and transparency, and enable consumers to make more informed and sustainability-oriented food choices. As of January 2026, the platform serves over 100 000 customers in Italy. Through data-driven logistics and demand forecasting, Cortilia.it aims to reduce food waste and optimise distribution, while its benefit-corporation model and B-Corp certification embeds social and environmental objectives alongside commercial performance.

records.title: Cula
records.description: Cula is a digital platform for monitoring, reporting, and verifying (MRV) focused on scaling carbon removal. The platform validates real-time data across the carbon removal supply chain, enabling traceability, standardized reporting, and the generation of verified carbon credits. Its functionalities include an open data interface (Carbon Hub) for scientific validation, as well as integrated tools for tracking operations, supporting certification processes, and optimizing project performance. The solution also ensures open data access through Carbon Hub where Carbon Dioxide Removal (CDR) science community can verify and account for. Specifically, Cula aids in integrating daily operation, tracking services, certification and efficiency optimization to build trust with buyers and partners.
records.abstract: Digital infrastructure including MRV platform for carbon removal projects

_annotations.Impact: Cula aims to bridge the gap between real-life processes and carbon credit to showcase effective carbon removal projects across the globe. As demonstrated in the Cular Carbon Hub, the platform tracked approximately 52.7 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent through its monitored carbon removal processes. Some of the documented sinks include projects in Germany, Sweden, and Taiwan. As of October 2025, Cula also plans to explore other carbon removal technologies such as enhanced rock weathering and direct air capture.

records.title: Curriculum for training of Multi-actors Agricultural Innovation Platform facilitators
records.description: Curriculum for training of Multi-actors Agricultural Innovation Platform facilitators is a comprehensive training resource developed by FAO to build capacities of facilitators for establishing and operating MAIPs. The curriculum introduces nine modules covering facilitation of innovation agenda identification, co-innovation, co-learning, market linkages, entrepreneurship, enabling environment creation, monitoring and evaluation, and workplan development. It emphasizes participatory action research, multi-actor interactions, and digital literacy to empower smallholder farmers and value chain actors through inclusive and collaborative innovation processes. MAIP is established in rural communities where farmers and key value chain actors become empowered through participatory action research, knowledge co-creation and application, market linkages and so on.

The platform leverages AI, IoT, and sensor technology for autonomous monitoring and early disease detection, supporting food security and resource efficiency.

records.title: Wiejska
records.description: Wiejska is a web-based aggregator platform that connects local farmers and food producers in Poland directly with consumers through online ordering and coordinated weekly deliveries. The initiative serves small-scale producers seeking alternative routes to market and consumers interested in purchasing fresh, locally sourced food. Farmers cooperate to pool and organize deliveries.
records.abstract: Aggregator marketplace for farmer products
records.owner_name: Kujawsko-Pomorskie Agricultural Advisory Centre, Minikowo, Poland is an administrator and coordinator of the initiative.

_annotations.Impact: Wiejska aims to strengthen short food supply chains in Poland by enabling consumers to purchase fresh, locally produced food directly from nearby farmers through an online ordering system with coordinated weekly deliveries. The marketplace platform aims to improve supply chain transparency by providing information on product origin and producers, support local food consumption, and reduce the number of intermediaries between farmers and consumers. For farmers, it aims to offer an alternative route to market that can increase market visibility, retain a larger share of the final price and reduce dependence on conventional wholesale channels.

records.title: xSeedScore
records.description: Computomics xSeedScore is a machine learning-based decision-support solution designed to accelerate plant breeding and trait optimization for agriculture. xSeedScore enables breeders to predict crop performance, select optimal crosses, and develop climate-resilient varieties, supporting food security and sustainable production. The solution integrates genotypic, phenotypic, and environmental data to deliver actionable insights for breeders and researchers.
records.abstract: Machine learning-based decision-support solution for predictive plant breeding and trait optimization

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher
_annotations.Impact: xSeedScore aims to enable breeders to identify up to 10 times more outstanding candidates for commercial pipelines, to reduce time to market by up to 6 years, and double prediction accuracy compared to standard methods. The solution can support climate-smart breeding, reduce resource-intensive field trials, and promote biodiversity by enabling the development of diverse crop varieties adapted to specific climates. .

records.title: Weather data helps farmers to improve their productivity
records.description: Caritas is a weather data and advisory service project designed to improve agricultural productivity and climate resilience in Tajikistan by deploying low-cost, open-source weather stations, providing real-time data for local forecasts, and delivering tailored weather-water-climate services to smallholder farmers and rural communities. The project supports food security and rural livelihoods by enabling better decision-making for planting, irrigation, and risk reduction.
records.abstract: Weather data and advisory service project

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher
_annotations.Impact: The initiative contributes to improved access to localized weather and climate information for agricultural decision-making in Tajikistan. Project documentation and field observations report that the use of weather-based advisory services supports farmers in adjusting agricultural practices, including timing of sowing and harvesting, in response to changing weather conditions. In some project areas, participating farmers report improvements in soil and water management practices and reduced exposure to climate-related risks such as erosion and flooding. The deployment of a nationwide network of low-cost weather stations supports more accurate local forecasts and the provision of weather-water-climate services for agricultural users, contributing to strengthened climate resilience of rural livelihoods.

records.title: VITIROVER
records.description: Vitirover is an autonomous robotic mowing solution designed to manage vegetation mechanically in vineyards and other perennial cropping systems. The robot operates continuously at ground level without the use of chemical herbicides and is intended to support sustainable vegetation management in complex terrains such as vineyards, orchards and other managed landscapes.
records.abstract: Autonomous robotic weeding solution

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher
_annotations.Impact: Demonstration projects and early commercial deployments indicate that Vitirover enables continuous mechanical vegetation control without herbicides in perennial cropping systems. The solution aims to reduce reliance on chemical weed control and fossil-fuel-intensive machinery, while maintaining vegetation at controlled height. Outcomes and benefits vary depending on site conditions and management practices, and large-scale quantitative impact assessments are still limited.

records.title: Türkiye’s Strategic Plan of the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry 2024-2028
records.description: Türkiye’s Strategic Plan of the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry 2024-2028 outlines a comprehensive five-year strategic plan, which includes seven goals, 32 targets, and 153 performance indicators. The policy identifies the medium and long-term priorities of the ministry, enabling the allocation of resources according to strategic priorities. Among the seven goals, sustainable production, rural development, and digital transformation play key roles. Under sustainable production, the policy intends to enhance efficiency and quality in plant and animal production, develop aquaculture, and ensure food safety. Meanwhile, rural development focuses on improving the quality of life and economic opportunities in rural areas, focusing on family businesses, women and youth. Lastly, digital transformation-related strategies involve upgrading information technology infrastructure to support modern agricultural practices and decision-making processes. Other priorities under the policy include resilience and adaptation, resource management, capacity building, and international engagement.
records.abstract: Medium and long-term priorities in rural development, agriculture and forestry, and digital transformation
records.owner_name: Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry, the Republic of Türkiye

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The policy aims to create a meaningful impact to meet the needs of citizens by using public resources effectively, economically, and efficiently. Specifically, the strategies envision to take into account factors such as climate change, global food supply and security, population growth, migration movements, geopolitical risks, natural disasters, and epidemics, among others. The policy is expected to improve coordination and efficiency in agricultural governance through enhanced data availability and digital decision-support tools. Potential impacts include increased productivity, improved resource-use efficiency, strengthened climate resilience, and improved access to digital public services for farmers.

records.title: TTZ
records.description: TTZ offers technologies for precision agriculture, combining GPS navigation hardware, farm management software, and field monitoring tools. The solutions include automatic tractor guidance (autopilot) systems and parallel driving GPS navigation, which help agricultural machinery operate more accurately and reduce overlaps during field operations such as seeding, fertilization, and spraying. TTZ also provides an information-analytical platform for farm management, enabling farmers to collect and analyze production data and manage field activities, as well as agro-meteorological stations that monitor weather conditions directly in the field to support agronomic decision-making.

records.title: Transforming agriculture with digital automation
records.description: “Transforming agriculture with digital automation” is a policy brief designed to outline the state of digital automation technologies in agriculture and their potential to transform agrifood systems. The brief notes that digital automation technologies have great potential to enhance the precision of agricultural operations, improve working conditions, and address environmental challenges. It explains that the world is in the early stages of a wave of automation that forms the backbone of precision agriculture. Such early development supports more efficient, site-specific farm management and improved productivity. The resource highlights that these technologies can mitigate risk and improve farmers’ wellbeing while enabling producers to apply inputs where and when needed, thus maximising resource-use efficiency, saving costs and reducing negative environmental impacts.

records.title: The Food Assembly (La Ruche qui dit Oui)
records.description: The Food Assembly is an online marketplace for local food hubs, distributing products from farmers. The Food Assembly’s operational model revolves around local collection points, i.e. Assembly locations. Producers remain autonomous: they choose the collection point they want to supply to, they decide what to offer each week, set their own prices, and can define minimum order thresholds. Consumers place orders during a fixed online ordering window for a particular collection point. If a producer’s minimum order amount is not reached and delivery does not happen, buyers are reimbursed according to the platform’s rules. Distribution occurs during a short, predefined pick-up slot at the Assembly location. The design of the model emphasises face-to-face exchange (a “pop-up market” feel), but who physically hands over products can vary in practice by Assembly and producer arrangements. Some of Assembly hosts even offer door-step delivery to the consumers, charged at extra fee.
records.abstract: Aggregator marketplace for farmer products

_annotations.Impact: As of January 2026, The Food Assembly has been implemented across seven European countries, with over 1500 collection points across those markets. The network involves around 10 000 producers supplying local food through the platform, with approximately 160 000 members buying regularly in Food Assemblies. The average distance travelled by food to reach the collection point - across the markets - is 49 kilometres, in comparison to thousands of kilometres of food miles for supermarket bought produce.

records.title: The Digital Blue Revolution
records.description: “The Digital Blue Revolution” is a publication designed to explain how cloud computing, the internet of things (IoT), artificial intelligence and machine learning are facilitating the sustainable growth of aquaculture production. The publication explains how the intelligent application of digital technologies and meaningful processing of data guide feeding, farming decisions and resource-efficient production in fish and shrimp farming. The publication presents concrete examples of how digital tools are being adopted in aquaculture. Similarly, the publication highlights improvements in production efficiency, reduced feed waste, enhanced fish welfare, and reduced environmental impact.

records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The resource reports that feed conversion ratio (FCR) reductions ranged between 5 percent and 28 percent in 2020 among IT-engaged aquaculture companies. Feed control centres, with investment costs reaching up to USD 14.6 million, can distribute feed to as many as 15 million salmon per operator.

records.title: The Biodrone Portal
records.description: The Biodrone Portal is an end-to-end platform that transforms aerial data from drones, satellites, and aerial surveys, into insight-driven decisions. The solution can be used for counting and categorizing objects, calculating values, detecting damages and identifying risks. The main applications are forest inventory including detecting dead trees, calculating biomass, identifying fire risks, tracking tree species, detecting diseases and assessing carbon capture, supporting harvesting and conservation decisions, and invasive species detection for identifying and monitoring invasive plants or animals.
records.abstract: AI-powered aerial image processing platform

_annotations.Impact: In 2021-2022 The Biodrone Portal enabled mapping of 15 000 hectares of storm-damaged forest in Norway, supporting recovery of 2.8 million m³ of timber and preventing further losses from pests and fire. The solution can reduce costs compared to helicopter surveys and improve worker safety. The platform has users in fifteen countries.

records.title: Tedaruk
records.description: Tedaruk is an electronic portal that centralizes the procurement of food products by state-funded institutions in Azerbaijan through a single online point of contact for public buyers and suppliers. The portal allows public organizations to publish their annual food needs and run procurement procedures, while food producers and sellers can submit offers.
records.abstract: National e-procurement portal for public food purchases

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Tedaruk facilitated the procurement of food products worth USD 75 million through state orders in 2024, with 7.1 percent savings of allocated state funds recorded during the procurement process. The portal was used in 2024 by 90 purchasing organizations that acquired 209 types of food products via the portal from 73 contracted manufacturers and sellers. The solution aims to strengthen centralized procurement of food products under state orders, ensure more transparent and efficient use of public funds, promote participation of local farmers and food producers in public markets, and support social welfare.

records.title: Supporting New Farmers in Belarus
records.description: Supporting New Farmers in Belarus is a project that provides training and financing support for new farmers and agri-food small and medium enterprises (SMEs). The project aims to support entrepreneurship in agriculture and rural development by providing access to knowledge, skills, and financial resources. UNDP (with Joint SDG Fund support) and the Ministry of Agriculture and Food conducted an in-depth review of agri-food sector financing and proposed mechanisms to support innovative projects and improve interaction between producers and retail chains. A key output was a beginner-farmer training program designed from a survey of 176 respondents, addressing common gaps in taxation, law, accounting, government support and access to finance.

records.title: Strengthening digital agricultural extension and advisory services in smallholder farming
records.description: Strengthening digital agricultural extension and advisory services in smallholder farming is a policy-oriented resource designed to provide guidance on enhancing digital extension and advisory services for small-scale farmers. The document examines barriers to digital adoption such as the lack of infrastructure and reception coverage, high cost of digital devices and management and maintenance of information and communications technology (ICT) facilities and products, weak regulatory framework, as well as poor institutional capacity and governance. The document also outlines key enabling conditions and highlights good practices that improve access to timely information, market links, and technical support in rural areas.

records.title: Soil Heroes Foundation
records.description: Soil Heroes Foundation is a non-profit organisation committed to accelerating the transition to regenerative agriculture by trialing and demonstrating regenerative farming practices on working farms, documenting ecological and agronomic outcomes, and sharing their findings publicly. The initiative operates practical on-farm trials (on the Klompe Farm), combining ecological practices such as composting, cover cropping, biodiversity strips, no-till, organic fertilisers with scientific monitoring of soil, water, biodiversity and crop performance. The verification and modern farm approach of the initiative builds evidence that regenerative agriculture is ecologically viable, economically feasible, and beneficial for climate, biodiversity, and food systems.
records.abstract: Non‑profit initiative verifying regenerative agriculture successes

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher
_annotations.Impact: According to reports available online, Soil Heroes Foundation maintains 360 hectares of farms that have been converted to regenerative management. It also supported business cases such as initiatives in making compost in large quantities, and a collaborative output called Guidebook for Farmers was created together with Klompe Farm.

records.description: Solvi is an agricultural analytics software that offers a full solution for drone-based mapping and assessment of field trials. The platform automatically combines drone images into accurate maps and offers tools to mark and edit field trials. Users can generate statistics for each plot and plant counts with plant-level data. records.title: SmartScript™
records.description: SmartScript™ is a digital agronomic solution that transforms in-season crop and weed maps into variable-rate (VRA) herbicide prescriptions. The platform divides fields into management zones based on weed pressure and canopy conditions and assigns appropriate herbicide rates or treatments to each zone. The solution helps focus on weed control inputs where they are needed most and reduces the need for blanket applications across entire fields.

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: SmartScript™ aims to support more precise herbicide use which can lower overall chemical use and application costs while maintaining or improving weed control. The solution also contributes to better production outcomes by enabling more consistent crop stands and reduced competition from weeds.

records.title: Smart Village Knezica
records.description: Smart Village Knezica is a Digital Innovation Hub (DIH) and agricultural cooperative in rural Bosnia and Herzegovina that connects farmers, technology experts and local stakeholders to co-create smart village solutions. The smart village is a digital farm, experimental fields and a pilot vineyard where digital tools are tested in real production conditions and supports farmers with advice and capacity-building for e-business development and market access.

_annotations.Impact: Smart Village Knezica aims to help agricultural producers in the Prijedor region improve competitiveness, reducing resource waste and supporting better production planning. The smart village has established an experimental vineyard of around 1 hectare with six grape varieties, equipped three pilot farms with sensors and smart irrigation systems, and plans or has delivered around 24 workshops and training events for farmers and rural youth, supporting wider uptake of digital tools in the region.

records.title: Smart Coop
records.description: Smart Coop is an innovative solar-powered poultry farming solution implemented in Mirogoshch, Belarus under the GEF/UNDP Small Grants Programme aimed at making small-scale poultry farming cheaper, simpler to run, and attractive for agro-ecotourism. The system automates key functions such as ventilation, lighting, temperature, and humidity control through IoT sensors and mobile applications. Each coop is designed for 10 birds and integrates sustainable energy solutions with modern farming technology.

records.title: Smart farmers – Learning with digital technologies
records.description: Smart farmers – Learning with digital technologies is a resource designed to explore how digital technologies strengthen agriculture human capital. The brief states that digital agricultural technologies, innovations and data are transforming business models and practices across entire value chains, helping address bottlenecks in productivity, postharvest handling, market access, finance and supply chain management. It examines how digital technologies can be used to build skills and knowledge among agricultural producers, drawing on global cases to inform investments in human capital.

records.title: Smart AgriTech Connect (SATECON)
records.description: Smart AgriTech Connect (SATECON) is a capacity building project that strengthens digital agriculture knowledge across Western Balkan universities. Through the SATECON project, partners develop strategies and tools that improve the adoption of smart agricultural technologies, including drones, sensors, automation, data analytics, and robotic systems. The team focuses project activities on six key agricultural sectors: viticulture, fruit growing, olive cultivation, livestock farming, greenhouse production, and mariculture.

records.title: Smart agriculture in Uka Farm
records.description: Uka farm, situated in rural Albania, integrates Vodafone’s smart agriculture technology to monitor farm operations such as planting, irrigation, and pesticide application. With this technology integration and partnership, the farm helps control and monitor the quality of their produce through the real-time data gathering of soil humidity and light intensity.
records.abstract: Technology integration for planting, irrigation, pesticide application, and harvesting

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher
_annotations.Impact: According to an interview from the owner of Uka Farm in 2022, the use of Vodafone technology improved the accuracy of digital interventions in production and harvesting, while reducing the need for several technologies in farm operations due to interoperability of the technology. The interview also mentioned that with the technology integration the Uka farm implemented, they are eligible to apply in the Albania’s Agency for Agriculture and Rural Development for grants, serving as the pilot study that can potentially connect many farms in the country. The integration envisions to provide full solution connecting hardware, software, and internet connectivity for farms in Albania.

records.title: Sistem tržišnih informacija poljoprivrede Srbije (STIPS)
records.description: STIPS is a web-based market information service system providing weekly and monthly local prices for fruits, vegetables, livestock, grains, inputs and selected dairy categories across Serbian markets to support transparent trading, farm planning and food security decisions.
records.abstract: Web-based local market prices information system
records.owner_name: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management of the Republic of Serbia

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher
_annotations.Impact: STIPS aims to improve agricultural market transparency in Serbia through the regular collection and publication of price and market data. The system has operated continuously since the early 2000s and produces weekly and monthly market bulletins, detailed reports, and searchable online databases by product and location. Information is disseminated through the STIPS web portal and other communication channels. Data collection relies on a national network of market reporting centers staffed by trained reporters, supporting the regular publication of price bulletins and analytical reports.

records.title: Siberian and Belarusian Scientists to Boost Urban Farm Yields with Digital Solutions
records.description: Researchers from Siberian Federal University (Russia) and Belarusian partners are collaborating to improve multi-tier (vertical) plant cultivation systems used in urban farms and indoor agriculture. The goal is to increase the yield and quality of lettuce grown in controlled environments. The team studies LED phytolighting impacts on red-leaf lettuce yields and develops a digital model (Digital Twin) to optimize energy consumption in vertical city farms.

records.title: ShefDoza
records.description: The vertical farming microgreens pilot in Bielaaziorsk transforms a former metal workshop into an urban farm specializing in organic microgreens. The system utilizes a hydroponic setup with automated lighting, irrigation, and air conditioning to maximize space efficiency and produce high-quality crops in an urban environment. It produces around 12 varieties (from sunflower to kohlrabi) on a fast cycle (7–10 days to harvest) and is positioned to scale through partnerships with local restaurants and food chains, supported through an EU-backed local economic development program implemented with UNDP and the Ministry of Economy.
records.abstract: Vertical farming pilot for microgreens production in Bielaaziorsk

_annotations.Impact: The vertical farming pilot demonstrates sustainable urban agriculture practices, producing fresh, organic microgreens locally. The system maximizes space efficiency and reduces transportation needs, contributing to local food security and sustainable development.

It produces around 12 varieties (from sunflower to kohlrabi) on a fast cycle (7–10 days to harvest) and is positioned to scale through partnerships with local restaurants and food chains, supported through an EU-backed local economic development program implemented with UNDP and the Ministry of Economy.
_raw.Impact: The vertical farming pilot demonstrates sustainable urban agriculture practices, producing fresh, organic microgreens locally. The system maximizes space efficiency and reduces transportation needs, contributing to local food security and sustainable development.

records.title: Self-evaluation and Holistic Assessment of Climate Resilience of Farmers and Pastoralists (SHARP)
records.description: Self-evaluation and Holistic Assessment of Climate Resilience of Farmers and Pastoralists (SHARP) is a participatory tool developed by FAO Land and Water Division that enables smallholder farmers and pastoralists to assess their own climate resilience across 13 agro-ecosystem indicators. The tool has three phases: 1) a participatory self-assessment survey of smallholder farmers and pastoralists regarding their climate resilience; 2) a double gap analysis and assessment of the responses at local level with the farmers and pastoralists in a rapid assessment and through a cross-sectional review of multiple assessments, including with local government officials and policy makers, to assess agricultural and pastoral policies regarding effectiveness and gaps; 3) the use of all data collected, in conjunction with climate and scientific data, to inform and guide farmers’ practices, curricula, and local and national policies.
records.abstract: Participatory tool for resilience assessment tool for smallholders
records.owner_name: Land & Water Division, Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher
_annotations.Impact: SHARP aims to integrate the tool within participatory and community-driven programmes, such as farmer field schools. The tool has been implemented in over 45 programs across Africa, Asia, and Latin America, fostering inclusive resilience of dialogue, community learning, and integration of results into policy. Pilots in Uganda, Senegal, and Mali generated community-level scoring and informed Farmer Field Schools curricula.

records.title: Sentera FieldAgent
records.description: Sentera FieldAgent is an agronomic analytics platform that turns drone-based crop imagery into actionable field insights for scouting, crop monitoring, and agronomic decision-making. The solution helps users identify variability and problem zones early and supports more targeted decisions for replanting, fertilization, irrigation, weed pressure mapping, and field trials.
records.abstract: Precise agronomic analytics platform for crop insights

_annotations.Impact: Sentera indicates that FieldAgent helps agronomic teams scout faster and more consistently. As reported by the company, FieldAgent can deliver near real-time analytics in the mobile app while the drone is still in flight, and can cover around 700 acres per hour at roughly 97 percent accuracy, providing substantially more measurements than manual field checks and reducing the risk of undetected crop issues.

records.title: Second Rural Enterprise Development Project
records.description: The development objective of the Second Rural Enterprise Development Project for Uzbekistan is to support the expansion of rural enterprise activity, investments, and job creation in regions supported by the project. The project comprises of three components. The first component, enterprise development will facilitate the establishment and growth of farms, agribusinesses, and rural enterprises in the targeted rural areas through the provision of technical support and business facilitation activities. It consists of following sub-components: (i) business incubation and mentorship; (ii) partnership and value chain development; (iii) climate smart and green technology demonstration; and (iv) women’s entrepreneurship development. The second component, access to finance will address key constraints to accessing finance faced by farmers, agribusinesses, and other beneficiaries engaged in agriculture and rural economic activities. It consists of following sub-components: (i) credit line for farmers, agribusinesses, and rural enterprises for climate-resilient investments; (ii) partial credit guarantees under the state fund for support of entrepreneurship; and (iii) technical assistance to participating financial institution (PFIs) and the state fund for entrepreneurship support. The third component, project management will support the implementation, management, monitoring and evaluation of the project.

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The project aims to strengthen rural enterprise development, improve access to finance and support job creation in Uzbekistan’s regions. Expected outcomes include increased enterprise activity, employment generation, and improved resilience of rural economic activities, subject to project implementation and evaluation. As an intermediate implementation result, 21 Business Incubation Hubs have been established to provide enterprise support services to rural entrepreneurs. Final development outcomes will be assessed through ongoing monitoring and evaluation during project implementation.

records.title: Roadmap for Digital Transformation in the Agricultural Sector
records.description: Roadmap for Digital Transformation in the Agricultural Sector is a national policy and planning document that proposes AGRI-SYS, a unified agriculture platform for North Macedonia. The document outlines how AGRI-SYS can bring together existing digital tools, advisory services and market information into a single gateway where farmers and other stakeholders access timely, localized information and online public services for agriculture.
records.abstract: Guiding the AGRI-SYS national agriculture platform

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The roadmap highlights expected impacts on productivity, service quality and inclusiveness in North Macedonia’s agricultural sector. The document anticipates that AGRI-SYS aims to reduce duplication among existing portals, lower transaction costs, and improve the timeliness and targeting of agrometeorological, advisory and financial services, while also strengthening evidence-based policymaking.

records.title: Road to the Future - Developing Competencies in Precision Agriculture
records.description: Road to the Future - Developing Competencies in Precision Agriculture is a 2025 SDG pilot initiative in Belarus (Mogilev region highlighted) that raises the prestige of agricultural professions\nand builds early competencies in precision agriculture for preschool and school-age children and youth through interactive workshops, lectures, and practical sessions in dedicated Precision Farming Centers.
records.abstract: Pilot to build youth competencies in precision agriculture
records.owner_name: UNDP; Government of Belarus; TTZ LLC

_annotations.Impact: 55 educational events delivered across five Precision Farming Centers; more than 1 000 children participated along with 38 families. Participants learned via interactive formats (including simulators and GIS practice). Children produced 40 videos that gained 5 000+ views on a dedicated YouTube channel. An interactive teaching aid “Modern Agriculture” was produced and adopted by educational institutions, with reported use in Belarus, Russia, Kazakhstan, and Uzbekistan; participating colleges planned ongoing integration from 2026.

The solution serves consumers seeking seasonal, organic and ethically produced food, and farmers looking for stable alternative market access outside conventional retail.

_annotations.Country of origin: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
_annotations.Impact: Riverford aims to strengthen short food supply chains in the United Kingdom by enabling direct online sales of organic food from farms to households, improving transparency on product origin and production practices and reducing reliance on conventional retail intermediaries. Riverford aims to provide farmers with stable demand and fairer, more predictable prices through long-term sourcing relationships, while offering consumers convenient access to seasonal, organic food delivered nationwide. As of January 2026, intermediary supplies hundreds of thousands of customers in the United Kingdom annually and sourced from over 325 family farms.

records.title: Revalcon
records.description: Revalcon is a smart-irrigation solution provider offering end-to-end hardware and software for efficient water management in agriculture. Revalcon’s system enables farmers to automate irrigation based on real-time soil, weather and sensor data, reducing water and energy use, optimizing crop water supply, and facilitating resource-efficient farm management. The solution addresses challenges in water scarcity, labor costs, and inefficient irrigation practices, thereby promoting sustainable agriculture and rural development.

records.title: Proba.By (Проба Бел)
records.description: Proba.by (ООО «Проба Бел») is a precision agriculture service provider focused on soil agrochemical analysis and nutrient management planning to improve crop yields and optimize fertilizer use. In practice, they offer a technology-enabled soil diagnostics service that includes: 1) Automated soil sampling using specialized equipment with GPS-referenced sampling points and consistent sampling depth. 2) Laboratory analysis of soil samples covering 130+ agrochemical parameters, including pH, macro- and micronutrients, humus content, electrical conductivity, soil type, and base saturation. 3) Digital mapping of fields, including variable-rate fertilizer application maps based on sampling grids of about 1–3 hectares. 4) Agronomic recommendations and nutrient management plans developed by experts based on the analysis results. 5) Agronomic support for implementing the recommended fertilization system.
records.abstract: Soil agrochemical analysis and nutrition recommendations

_annotations.Impact: Claimed outcomes include profitability uplift (15–30%), fertilizer cost reduction (up to 30%), and “profitability yield increase” of 10–40%. Operational metrics listed on the site include sampling throughput (~1000–1500 ha/day) and report turnaround (10–20 working days).

records.title: Preparedness and Resilience to Disasters Project
records.description: Tajikistan Preparedness and Resilience to Disasters Project is a disaster risk management and resilient infrastructure project designed to support disaster recovery, strengthen the resilience of critical roads, and enhance disaster risk management capacity in Tajikistan. The project focuses on climate-resilient reconstruction of roads, modernization of disaster communication and information systems, and capacity building for emergency response, directly benefiting rural communities, farmers, and public sector institutions. The project is relevant for food security, rural development, and climate adaptation.
records.abstract: Disaster risk management and resilient infrastructure project

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher
_annotations.Impact: The project aims to benefit 566 000 people in flood-affected areas with rehabilitated roads, 861 000 people with more resilient roads, and 6 284 800 people with improved access to disaster information and response systems. The project targets the rehabilitation of 24 km of roads, reinforcement of 8 bridges, protection of 50 high-risk sites, and establishment of 3 regional crisis management centers. The project contributes to reduced disaster risk, improved rural connectivity, and strengthened climate adaptation capacity.

records.title: Plantage
records.description: Plantage is a cooperative member management and trading platform, whereby food consumers can join online and pay for a minimum of one share of the cooperative to become a member. Cooperative members then can sign-up for an additional monthly payment to receive weekly vegetable boxes from a local farm. Boxes are delivered to a nearby pick-up location or to the member’s doorstep. Platage operates on community-supported agriculture (CSA) basis, which means that the cooperative plans the seasonal activities in the field, volumes of production and weekly harvesting volumes based on the number of active subscriptions. Planning based on actual demand allows to reduce risk when allocating resources and reduce waste, when making decisions on how much to harvest each week.
records.abstract: Cooperative member management and trading platform

_annotations.Impact: Plantage aims to strengthen local short food supply chains by providing a stable, subscription-based outlet for small-scale vegetable production and by directly linking consumers to the costs and realities of farming. The solidarity-based CSA model improves income predictability for the farm and reduces market risk by sharing production risks with members. For consumers, the solution aims to increase access to seasonal, locally produced food and increase awareness of sustainable agricultural practices.

records.title: NEA.gov
records.description: The National Environmental Agency of Georgia provides climate, hydrometeorological and early-warning services supporting national climate-change mitigation and adaptation efforts. The service delivers long-term and real-time weather forecasts, hydrological and meteorological measurements, flood-risk zoning, climate statistics, and warnings for natural hazards including avalanches and heatwaves. The system supports agriculture, water management, infrastructure planning and public safety in alignment with Georgia’s obligations under UNFCCC, Kyoto Protocol and the Paris Agreement.

records.title: Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) Tracking Tool
records.description: The Nationally Determined Contributions Tracking tool is an offline tool designed to assist countries in collecting the information required to track progress made in implementing and achieving their NDCs. The tool assesses the progress of NDC implementation by comparing planned versus implemented mitigation and adaptation actions. Similarly, the solution also estimates the GHG reduction achieved from the implementation of mitigation actions compared against the sector or national baseline and NDC target scenario. This tool is particularly useful in preventing double accounting and overlapping of mitigation actions of countries as well as in distinguishing results of mitigation actions that are linked to the carbon market from national GHG emission reduction targets.

records.title: National Strategy on Agriculture and Rural Development for the Period 2021–2027
records.description: The National Strategy on Agriculture and Rural Development 2021–2027 (NSARD) is the Government of North Macedonia’s principal policy instrument for the agri-food sector and rural areas. NSARD sets out a multi-dimensional approach to sector modernization, competitiveness, and sustainability, with a focus on: (i) direct payments and market regulation; (ii) rural development and structural transformation; (iii) sustainable management of natural resources and climate adaptation; (iv) food safety and quality; and (v) knowledge, innovation, and digitalization. The strategy is aligned with EU CAP and SDGs and operationalizes a comprehensive monitoring and evaluation framework with defined targets for productivity, rural employment, digitalization, and environmental performance.

records.owner_name: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management, Republic of North Macedonia

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher
_annotations.Impact: NSARD aims to increase net value added in agriculture by 43 percent, double the share of rural development funding, raise agri-food exports to EUR 835 million, and improve productivity, digitalization, and environmental sustainability. Key targets include 95 000 ha irrigated land, 15 percent women farm holders, and 10 000 young farm holders by 2027.

records.title: Nationally Determined Contribution Expert Tool (NEXT)
records.description: Nationally Determined Contribution Expert Tool (NEXT) is a greenhouse gas accounting tool used to support annual environmental impact assessment for the Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Use sector (AFOLU). NEXT provides a 30-year series of annual and accumulated estimates of carbon removal and greenhouse gas emission reductions from actions determined by Parties in their climate policies. The tool can help countries to interpret, track, and scale up ambition of their nationally determined contributions (NDC) which could ultimately inform the global stocktake of the Paris Agreement in a harmonised way.

records.title: National Farm Survey
records.description: The National Farm Survey (NFS) has been conducted by Teagasc on an annual basis since 1972. The survey is operated as part of the Farm Accountancy Data Network of the EU and fulfils Ireland’s statutory obligation to provide data on farm output, costs and income to the European Commission. A random, nationally representative sample, of between 1,000 and 1,200 farms depending on the year, is selected annually in conjunction with the Central Statistics Office (CSO). Each farm is assigned a weighting factor so that the results of the survey are representative of the national population of farms.

records.description: The National Agricultural Grants Portal is a digital project developed to provide transparent access to agricultural financial support programs across Georgia. The platform consolidates multiple grant schemes, including support for livestock and beekeeping, small and medium-sized producers, collection and distribution companies, agrifood enterprises, farm-recovery assistance programmes, and market-intervention schemes such as substandard apple crop support. records.title: Nashe Vse
records.description: Nashe-Vse is an intermediary with e-commerce platform that connects Ukrainian consumers with local farmers and artisanal producers through direct online ordering and home delivery of food products. The initiative serves small-scale producers seeking collective market access and consumers interested in purchasing fresh, locally produced food with known origin.
records.abstract: Farmer-to-consumer e-commerce supported by an intermediary

_annotations.Impact: Nashe Vse aims to strengthen short food supply chains in Ukraine by enabling consumers to purchase food directly from local farmers. The e-commerce platform aims to improve transparency by providing information on product origin and producers, support consumption of locally produced food and reduce the number of intermediaries between farmers and consumers. Nashe Vse emphasises working with small and medium farming households. As of December 2025, the platform features approximately 72 individual farmers, based on a manual count of publicly visible producer profiles.

records.title: Modernization of Real Property Registration and Cadastre Project
records.description: The Modernization of Real Property Registration and Cadastre Project aimed to establish an efficient, transparent and accessible real property registration and cadastre system. The project supported the digitalization of land and property records, improved business processes, and strengthened institutional capacity to enhance land administration and support e-government services.
records.abstract: Digital land administration modernization

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher
_annotations.Impact: According to World Bank implementation and results reports, the project contributed to measurable improvements in land administration performance. By project completion, procedures to register property rights were reduced from 9 to 5. The integrated registration and cadastre system was deployed nationwide and connected to national GIS infrastructure. Approximately 3.46 million direct beneficiaries were reported, of which about 33 percent were women. More than 7.3 million cadastral and registration records were digitized, exceeding original targets, and digital cadastre coverage reached about 90 percent of inhabited territory.

records.title: Meteobot
records.description: Meteobot is an automatic weather-station solution designed to deliver real-time and historical data on weather and soil conditions directly from the field, enabling farmers and agronomists to monitor rainfall, temperature, humidity, wind, soil moisture and other environmental parameters. The platform supports agronomic decision-making — including irrigation scheduling, crop protection timing, fertilization, and harvest planning — thereby contributing to optimized crop production, resource use efficiency, and risk reduction from weather and climatic variability.
records.abstract: Weather- and soil-monitoring station system for precision agriculture

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher
_annotations.Impact: Meteobot aims to offer precise, data-driven farm management solutions through timely weather and soil information, which can help optimize irrigation, pesticide and fertilizer use, crop protection timing, and reduce yield losses due to adverse weather — thereby improving productivity and resource efficiency.

records.title: Mapping affordable and transferrable climate-smart technologies for smallholder farmers
records.description: The publication consists of a multi-country mapping and assessment of affordable and transferrable climate-smart technologies aimed at addressing food security and climate resilience challenges faced by smallholder farmers. Implemented through a tripartite collaboration between FAO, IFAD and IsDB, the initiative identifies technology options that can be adapted across different agro-ecological and socio-economic contexts to support sustainable agrifood systems.
records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO); International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD); Islamic Development Bank (IsDB)

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher
_annotations.Impact: The initiative produced a comprehensive inventory and assessment framework for affordable and transferrable climate-smart technologies relevant to smallholder farmers in 10 countries. The results aim to provide an evidence base to support informed decision-making, prioritization and future investment in technologies that can enhance resilience, reduce losses, improve productivity, and strengthen agrifood value chains.

records.title: Leveraging space technology for agricultural development and food security
records.description: “Leveraging space technology for agricultural development and food security” is a joint FAO and UNOOSA technical resource designed to present the current applications of space technology, particularly satellite imagery and global navigation satellite systems (GNSS), in agriculture. The publication explains that satellite imagery and GNSS data provide high-resolution information essential for precision agriculture, effective water management, crop monitoring and accurate weather forecasting, thereby supporting informed decision-making and promoting sustainable agricultural practices. The document highlights that space technology enables the monitoring, analysing and managing of agricultural activities, land use and environmental conditions for various applications, including precision agriculture, pest and disease control, soil fertility management and sustainable land-use planning.
records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher
_annotations.Impact: The publication reports that over 17 000 satellites have been launched since the beginning of the space age and that more than 2 900 new satellites were placed into orbit in 2023 alone, significantly increasing access to Earth observation data. The publication also reports that the FAO Hand-in-Hand Geospatial Platform integrates over 2 million layers of open-access geospatial and agricultural statistics data and supports more than 70 member countries, strengthening data-driven agricultural decision-making and food security planning.

records.title: LandVisor™
records.description: LandVisor™ is a geospatial decision-support solution for rangeland management that combines field data collected by certified consultants with remote sensing imagery and GIS-based analysis. The solution generates vegetation maps focused on specific problem species and land conditions, which are used by consultants to provide tailored brush and weed management recommendations, including guidance on herbicide treatment strategies. LandVisor™ supports ranchers in prioritizing management interventions to improve forage availability and grazing capacity on rangelands.

records.title: Kosovo’s Digital Agriculture Programme Action Plan for 2025-2028
records.description: In partnership with FAO, the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Rural Development of Kosovo officially launched the Digital Agriculture Programme and Action Plan 2025-2028. The policy serves as a structured strategic framework and roadmap to transform Kosovo’s agriculture sector and rural areas. Three strategic objectives were developed. The first target aims to establish and improve e-government and data infrastructure. This step enables the enhancement of efficiency and data-driven decision-making in the sector. Secondly, the creation of an inclusive functional network of digital services is proposed to improve access to agriculture advisory services, and knowledge exchange as well as to foster collaboration. Lastly, the policy prioritizes the development of human capital to assist in the digital transformation of the agriculture sector. Under this objective, the digital skills improvement across stakeholders combined with a supportive digital agriculture ecosystem are expected to thrive and scale up during the implementation.
records.abstract: Strategic framework to drive overarching priorities in digital transformation for agriculture and rural areas
records.owner_name: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Rural Development

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The strategic roadmap will be beneficial in guiding the government of Kosovo in several ways. Firstly, the policy provides a multi-annual programme to productively drive the transformation of the agriculture digitalization sphere in the country. Similarly, the adjustment of information management systems can be properly aligned with the EU Common Agricultural Policy, which can assist as a solid foundation in establishing a Digital Public Infrastructure for Agriculture as well as extending digitalization services across key actors. Lastly, the policy roadmap can reduce administrative burdens while supporting the implementation of the e-government strategy in the country and improving digital skills and literacy among the rural population. Overall, the policy can provide insights in data-driven policy making, monitoring of policy impact, and distributing knowledge and resources all over the country.

records.title: Knowledge4Policy (K4P)
records.description: Knowledge4Policy is a web-based evidence platform designed to organise, synthesise and deliver scientifically robust knowledge from JRC-led ‘knowledge services’. These services are comprised of 26 themes that organise, tailor, and present scientific knowledge to directly inform policymaking and related research. Some of the thematic areas include biodiversity, global food and nutrition security, earth observation, and health promotion and disease prevention among others. Other knowledge services outside agriculture and digital infrastructure organize data on migration and demography, participatory democracy, cancer research, and disaster risk management. The solution also provides policymakers across Europe with a shared database, policy‑layer interfaces and evolving online communities, bridging the science–policy gap and supporting evidence‑informed decision‑making. Additionally, an online community where scientists and policymakers are also established to collaborate in transferring scientific knowledge into public policy.

records.title: IRRIOT
records.description: IRRIOT is a wireless precision irrigation automation system for agriculture and horticulture that controls field irrigation without in-field cabling or grid electricity. The solution allows users to set and manage irrigation schedules remotely, automate watering based on sensor data and weather information, and control multiple zones.
records.abstract: Wireless IoT precision irrigation system for agriculture

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: IRRIOT reports that wireless precision irrigation can reduce water use by up to 50 percent and increase crop yields by around 30 percent compared with manual irrigation, while also saving hundreds of work hours and lowering electricity consumption. IRRIOT case studies describe deployments on farms in at least eight countries and company projections of more than 1 000 installations globally by 2024, indicating growing adoption and environmental benefits such as reduced runoff, eutrophication and soil erosion.

records.title: Investing in trade digitalization: the case of ePhyto
records.description: The resource “Investing in trade digitalization: The case of ePhyto” is a resource designed to guide countries in planning and financing the transition from paper-based to digital trade systems for issuing phytosanitary certificates. The publication focuses on Electronic phytosanitary certificates or ePhytos and outlines institutional, financial, and technical requirements for modernising agricultural trade procedures. Other highlights include how digitalisation improves efficiency, transparency, and resilience. Four country case studies are highlighted in the document, namely Serbia, Egypt, Ukraine and Uzbekistan.
records.abstract: Electronic means for issuing the phytosanitary certificates
records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The resource encourages countries to make full use of electronic phytosanitary certificates due to its cheap, safe, and responsive transport system. documents that global trade in plant products is expected to grow 11 percent by 2032 and highlights how digital systems reduce delays, errors and greenhouse gas emissions associated with paper-based certification.

records.title: IPARD III Programme 2021-2027 of Albania
records.description: The project Instrument for Pre-Accession Assistance for Rural Development (IPARD) III 2021-2027 Programme in Albania is the European Union’s financial support to improve competitiveness, sustainability, and alignment with agricultural standards. The project is a multi-annual funding programme established by the European Commission to support rural development and the agri-food sector in candidate and potential candidate countries of the European Union. It is designed to help those countries align with the EU’s rural development and food systems policies, thereby contributing to improved agricultural productivity, food security and rural livelihoods.

Additionally, some of the expected achievements and targets of the project include the modernization of 930 farms and agri-food processing enterprises, 160 young farmers receiving support from IPARD, and 250 recipients of IPARD investments that support rural diversification and business development.

records.description: ICAERUS is a project that advances safe, effective drone use in agriculture, forestry, and rural communities. The project explores the use of drones in five application areas, validating them in real contexts and equipping stakeholders with training and practical guidance. The project explores multi-purpose drone services and identifies risks, added value; support informed decision-making with inclusive business and governance models; build capacity for competitiveness and sustainability; and enable trusted scale-up across Europe.
