records.title: Hortee
records.description: Hortee is a marketplace that connects local fresh food producers directly with consumers, enabling the purchase of vegetables, fruit, and other fresh products through a unified online platform. Consumers place separate order with each farmer and agree on pick-up or delivery on a case-by-case basis. Farmers are responsible for delivery of the products. Hortee provides a payment functionality for each transaction.
records.abstract: Aggregator marketplace for farmer products

_annotations.Impact: Hortee aims to strengthen local short food supply chains by improving direct market access for small and medium-scale food producers and reducing reliance on intermediaries. By enabling producers to sell through a digital marketplace, the solution could support higher producer margins, faster sales cycles and improved visibility of local products, while offering consumers easier access to fresh, locally sourced food.

records.title: Herbs for Growth (HEBO)
records.description: HEGO is a cross-border project implemented in Greece, Moldova, Georgia and Armenia to modernize the herb sector and promote the sustainable cultivation of endemic and endangered herb plant species. The project aimed to reduce unsustainable wild harvesting by training farmers to adopt diversified herb cultivation practices and develop higher-value processed herb products. HEGO supported farming entrepreneurship, improved product quality, facilitated research-to-business partnerships and strengthened international trade connections.

records.title: H2020-AURORAL
records.description: AURORAL is a European Union–funded project that develops an open and interoperable digital ecosystem for rural communities. The project developed eight pilot deployments across seven European countries, covering five application domains including smart farming, energy, mobility, health and tourism. The pilots aim to reducing rural–urban digital divides by enabling interoperable digital services and shared data infrastructures in rural areas.

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher
_annotations.Impact: AURORAL focuses on increasing connectivity and delivering a digital environment of smart objects interoperable services platforms able to trigger dynamic rural ecosystems of innovation chains, applications and services. Thus, AURORAL contributes to increase economic growth and create jobs in rural areas and to tackle significant societal challenges, contributes to overcoming digital divide between rural and urban areas and to develop the potential offered by increased connectivity and digitisation of rural areas.

records.description: GÖRSENTAM offers a suite of precision agriculture technologies combining hardware, IoT infrastructure, and AI-driven analytics to support data-based farm management through an app, where it delivers field-specific early warnings, alerts and recommendations for pest and disease control and fertilization.
records.abstract: Suite of agricultural technology

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher
_annotations.Impact: GÖRSENTAM aims to reduce routine field inspections by allowing producers and advisors to monitor microclimate, disease risk and pest populations remotely and receive field-specific warnings and recommendations, improving the timing of plant protection and fertilization while lowering input costs. records.title: FoodCloud
records.description: FoodCloud is a digital platform that facilitates the redistribution of surplus food from food businesses to charities and community organizations. The solution aims to reduce food waste while supporting communities by improving access to surplus food that is safe for consumption.
records.abstract: Digital platform that facilitates the redistribution of surplus food

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher
_annotations.Impact: According to the company website, FoodCloud facilitated the redistribution of surplus food in Ireland and internationally between 2014 and 1 December 2024. Over this period, approximately 338.9 million meal equivalents were redistributed through the platform, supported by 5,700 food-donating branches. FoodCloud also reports estimated avoidance of 425,528 tonnes of CO₂-equivalent emissions associated with the diversion of surplus food from waste streams. These figures represent aggregated outputs reported by the organisation.

records.title: Funding digital transformation of land administration
records.description: The publication “Funding digital transformation of land administration” is a policy brief designed to guide financing for e‑government land administration upgrades that transition paper-based registries to fully digital systems. The publication provides a practical guide for land administration system digital transformation, which includes bottom-up empowerment to enable transformation pivoting, alignment to broader government policy goals and the Strategic Development Goals, and data-driven monitoring and evaluation among others. The document concludes with key message on embracing digital disruption as an opportunity for both operational improvements and strategic advancement and ensuring that digital inclusivity of women and vulnerable groups are considered for inclusive, interactive, and intelligent land administration system.

records.title: FAO eLearning Academy
records.description: FAO eLearning Academy is a global platform offering over 500 multilingual courses on food security, sustainable agriculture, climate resilience, and digital innovation. The solution offers free access to topics covering global interest and is made available in a range of formats. These include elearning courses for self-paced learning, blended learning programmes, massive open online courses (MOOCs), technical webinars, online tutored courses, mobile learning, face-to-face training workshops and university master’s and postgraduate degree programmes. Meanwhile, relevant courses on digital agriculture include GeoTech4Tenure, which explains the importance of tenure security for the good outcome of development investments by incorporating technology on the recoding processes; the Global Information System on plant genetic resources, teaching basic features and advantages of using digital object identifiers in the context of global information system; and others.

records.title: Facing the challenges of broadband deployment in rural and remote areas
records.description: The Broadband Handbook is a policy guide that outlines the challenges faced by rural and remote areas in terms of broadband connectivity. The resource significantly devotes a presentation of case studies and good practices drawn from several European Union member states, highlighting what worked and the lessons learned. The 12 rural broadband project case studies were from Finland, France, Hungary, Italy, the Netherlands, Portugal, Slovenia, Spain, and the United Kingdom. Lastly, the document synthesizes case studies and discusses essential requirements to successfully connect rural and remote areas. Some conclusions include the need to involve IT specialists in private operator’s plans in the concerned areas, carry out strong preliminary checks on the economic and financial situation of the provider, and to close the involvement of small local operators can help in lowering the digital divide.

records.title: eUprava
records.description: The eGovernment Portal of the Republic of Serbia is a centralized digital platform that provides various services in health, education, family planning, and business and finance among others. While the platform offers several services, Open Balkans and Electronic People’s Initiative assist in rural development, trade, and social protection of the citizens. Open Balkans enables the activation of an identification number for the citizens of Serbia, which they can use for electronic services in North Macedonia and Albania. An active Open Balkans ID number also allows access to the labor market. Meanwhile, the Electronic People’s Initiative follows a grassroots approach wherein citizens propose the adoption, amendment, supplement, and even termination of the validity of the constitution, laws, and other regulations. The portal also allows users to register plant protection products, as well as the enlisting of distributors and importers of agricultural products.

records.title: Evja
records.description: Evja is a decision support system (DSS) designed to support growers through real-time monitoring, data analytics, and predictive agronomic models. The system is widely used across horticultural and high‑value crops—including greenhouse vegetables, berries, flowers, and orchard crops—where microclimate variability strongly influences irrigation and disease‑risk decisions. The solution combines wireless field sensors with cloud-based AI/ML analytics to deliver actionable insights on irrigation, nutrition, crop protection, disease risk, growth, and yield prediction.

_annotations.Impact: Since commercial launch in 2018, Evja claims to have monitored hundreds of hectares across multiple countries; its systems have helped growers optimize irrigation, reduce chemical and water use, improve crop protection timing, and increase yield consistency and quality under a precision-farming regime

records.title: Digital Development of Belarus (2021–2025)
records.description: The State Programme "Digital Development of the Republic of Belarus" 2021-2025 was a national policy framework that promoted digitalization across sectors including agriculture. records.title: Digital Agriculture and AI Innovation Roadmap for the Global Agrifood Systems Transformation
records.description: The publication “Digital Agriculture and AI Innovation Roadmap for the Global Agrifood Systems Transformation” translates the high-level ambition of more efficient, inclusive, resilient, and sustainable agrifood systems into a three-year action plan. The roadmap establishes a multistakeholder ecosystem that pools knowledge of infrastructure and funding across shared missions and priority use cases. As part of this ecosystem, it introduces an AI governance toolkit that provides criteria and principles to guide the design selection of monitoring and scaling of digital agriculture and AI initiatives.
records.abstract: Three-year action plan
records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher
_annotations.Impact: The roadmap’s main goal is to turn promising digital agriculture ideas into local, needs-driven, safe, interoperable, and scalable solutions. Specifically, its aim is to shift AI initiatives from scattered pilots and centralised monoliths towards a coordinated and goal-oriented framework. Some of the key achievements mentioned in the report is the first iteration of the roadmap concept based on the April 2025 Digital Agriculture and AI Innovation Dialogue. This resulted into the identification of core ingredients of the framework to become relevant to the community, which includes shared services, governance toolkit, and a demand-to-product pipeline.

records.title: Climate Action Review Tool
records.description: The Climate Action Review (CAR) Tool was developed jointly by FAO and UNDP as part of the SCALA Programme. The resource offers a practical step-by-step approach to identifying actionable entry points for transformative change, drawing from adaptation actions outlined in NDCs and NAPs. The tool is adaptable to various country contexts and strategic priorities, facilitating evidence-based adaptation planning through participatory methods. The key aspect of the tool revolves around assessing the potential impact of planned adaptation measures on enhancing the resilience of agrifood systems in the context of climate variability. This assessment uses six elements and 20 indicators of transformative climate action, employing both quantitative and qualitative analyses to compare current and planned adaptation actions. The tool addresses obstacles such as limited resources and technical capacity that present significant challenges to the implementation of institutional frameworks such as the Nationally Determined Contributions and National Adaptation Plans.
records.abstract: Practical tool for actionable roadmap in climate mitigation and adaptation
records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

_annotations.Impact: The CAR Tool aims to provide national adaptation planners and practitioners with practical guidance for transitioning from high-level NDC and NAP planning to actual implementation of locally relevant adaptation actions in agriculture and land-use sectors, fostering transformative systems-change potential.

records.title: Casa Miam
records.description: CASAMIAM is a software that enables independent farmers, artisans and food producers in France to create their own online shops for direct sales and Click & Collect ordering. It serves small producers seeking a simple and cost-effective way to reach local customers while retaining full control over pricing and client relationships. Casamiam addresses barriers faced by producers in setting up e-commerce shop, such as technological complexity, commissions and administration, by offering a low-cost template for e-commerce website.
records.abstract: E-commerce shop builder for farmers

_annotations.Impact: Casamiam encourages digital participation by smallholder producers by lowering barriers to e-commerce channels adoption. The platform enables producers to anticipate demand, reduce phone coordination and build customer relationships. It also contributes to improved local supply chain visibility by allowing consumers to discover nearby producers and reserve products online. As of January 2026, Casamiam tools have supported over 10 000 online orders.

records.title: Carbonfuture
records.description: Carbonfuture offers a digital trust infrastructure for durable carbon removal, connecting carbon removal suppliers, certifiers, and buyers through transparent monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) platform. The digital trust infrastructure includes tools and services that help suppliers bring projects to market and enable buyers to invest in carbon removal. The infrastructure ensures the integrity of carbon removal and enables it to scale. The platform operates as an integrated workflow connecting suppliers, certification bodies, and buyers. Carbon removal suppliers are onboarded through dedicated supplier services and undergo due diligence to assess project quality and readiness. Once approved, project data is continuously collected and processed through Carbonfuture’s digital MRV system, enabling real-time tracking and traceability of carbon removal activities. The platform then facilitates third-party verification and certification by accredited bodies, ensuring compliance with recognized standards. Verified carbon removal credits are issued and made available on Carbonfuture’s marketplace, where corporate buyers can access high-quality, traceable credits to meet their climate commitments.
records.abstract: Digital infrastructure including MRV platform and marketplace enabling verifiable carbon removal projects

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Carbonfuture aims to make carbon removal scalable, transparent, and trustworthy for buyers, suppliers, and regulators. According to Carbonfuture’s webpage, success stories include ensured transparency for clients tracking every truckload of biochar from point of departure to destination, and successful integration of dMRV to enable rapid improvements of technology while driving costs and showing progress to credit buyers. Several success stories can be found on the online solution page.

records.title: CACILM-2: Innovative Micro Earth Reservoirs and Digital Water Management in Kyrgyzstan
records.description: CACILM-2 is a project designed to improve water management and agricultural resilience in Kyrgyzstan through the deployment of micro earth reservoirs with geotextile and geomembrane liners, drip irrigation systems, and digital water monitoring. CACILM-2 aims to increase water use efficiency, support climate adaptation, and enhance food security by enabling precise irrigation, transparent water accounting, and sustainable land management for smallholder farmers and rural communities.
records.abstract: Integrated water management and digital monitoring for climate-resilient agriculture
records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher
_annotations.Impact: The initiative has supported improved irrigation of water management in the Kochkor District through the installation of remote water sensors and micro earth reservoirs, with planned expansion to achieve full system coverage. Automated monitoring and improved infrastructure have contributed to increased water use efficiency, reduced crop losses caused by water shortages, and more reliable irrigation supply, supporting agricultural productivity and food security. Climate-resilient water management practices have enhanced farmers’ capacity to adapt to droughts, reduced glacier melt, and variable precipitation. Centralized monitoring has improved transparency and equity in water distribution, strengthened institutional capacity for data-driven decision-making, and contributed to more sustainable water governance and rural livelihoods in Kyrgyzstan.

records.title: BeeOmonitoring
records.description: BeeOmonitoring is a digital solution developed by BeeOdiversity that uses bees as bioindicators to monitor plant biodiversity and detect agricultural and industrial pollutants. By analysing pollen collected by bees, the solution provides scientific indicators that support environmental monitoring, land management and biodiversity-related decision-making in agrifood and natural resource contexts.
records.abstract: Biodiversity and pollution biomonitoring

_annotations.Source: The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and reviewed by an FAO researcher
_annotations.Impact: BeeOdiversity reports that the biomonitoring solution supports more than 100 project sites per year across approximately 20 countries. Monitoring activities cover around 100 000 hectares annually and involve the identification of more than 200 plant species each year. The initiative reports pollination coverage of approximately 250 000 hectares per year and the detection of around 50 different pesticide substances annually. BeeOdiversity also reports that its activities contribute to raising awareness among more than 50 000 people per year and support biodiversity-related actions, including planting initiatives involving approximately 200 000 plantings annually. These outputs support improved understanding of biodiversity status and environmental pressures in agrifood and land-use systems.

records.title: Airba Fresh
records.description: Airba Fresh is a web-based online grocery and fresh food delivery platform that provides urban consumers in Kazakhstan with convenient access to fresh produce and everyday food items through online ordering and home delivery. The initiative serves households seeking time-saving and reliable food purchasing options while supporting structured distribution of fresh products. Airba Fresh addresses challenges related to convenience, limited access to fresh food through traditional retail, and fragmented last-mile delivery. The solution is built on a website and desktop-based e-commerce system, supported by digital payments and online customer communication tools, enabling product browsing, order management and coordinated logistics through a single digital interface.

_annotations.Impact: Airba Fresh aims to enable urban consumers to shop locally by providing direct online access to fresh food sourced from nearby producers and suppliers. By offering information on product origin and delivering fresh food directly to households, the platform promotes transparency, trust and more informed purchasing decisions. For farmers and local suppliers, Airba Fresh aims to offer an alternative route to market with only one intermediary between producer and consumer, reducing reliance on traditional wholesale channels and potentially improving farmer’s margins and market visibility.

The initiative serves households seeking time-saving and reliable food purchasing options while supporting structured distribution of fresh products. Airba Fresh addresses challenges related to convenience, limited access to fresh food through traditional retail, and fragmented last-mile delivery. The solution is built on a website and desktop-based e-commerce system, supported by digital payments and online customer communication tools, enabling product browsing, order management and coordinated logistics through a single digital interface.
_raw.Impact: Airba Fresh aims to enable urban consumers to shop locally by providing direct online access to fresh food sourced from nearby producers and suppliers. By offering information on product origin and delivering fresh food directly to households, the platform promotes transparency, trust and more informed purchasing decisions. For farmers and local suppliers, Airba Fresh aims to offer an alternative route to market with only one intermediary between producer and consumer, reducing reliance on traditional wholesale channels and potentially improving farmer’s margins and market visibility.

records.title: Agrio
records.description: Agrio is an AI-powered plant health and crop protection app designed for farmers, agronomists, and growers. It allows users to take photos of plants to automatically detect diseases, pests, and nutrient deficiencies using computer vision technology, and then provides tailored treatment and integrated pest management recommendations. In addition to plant diagnosis, Agrio offers tools such as hyper-local weather forecasts, growing degree day tracking, satellite-based crop monitoring, scouting reports, and team collaboration features. Overall, it functions as a digital plant health assistant that helps users identify problems early and make more informed crop management decisions.

records.title: AckerBox
records.description: AckerBox is an intermediary with e-commerce platform that allows urban customers to purchase farmer produce and pick up their order in one of the self-service collection points. Alternatively, customers can shop and self-check-out at the collection point. Self-service collection points are unique to the model and are managed from refurbished shipping containers. Products include regional vegetables, preserves, baked goods and milk products.
records.abstract: Intermediary selling farmer produce via collection points

_annotations.Impact: AckerBox provides alternative direct to consumer distribution channel to smallholders, bypassing large retail players. AckerBox is available in 14 locations across Austria. AckerBox has sold over 14 million regional items since its launch, with over 3 900 000 purchases made. The solution allows consumers to support and buy from local farms, and provides alternative direct to consumer channel for farmers. The solution might also have positive environmental impact, as it reduces the food miles.

records.title: Agricultural Stress Index System (ASIS)
records.description: The Agricultural Stress Index System (ASIS) Web Platform is a satellite‑based digital solution designed to identify agricultural areas affected by drought or abnormal vegetation stress worldwide. ASIS calculates the agricultural areas affected by drought, and classified as slight, moderate, and severe. The platform uses seasonal and non‑seasonal vegetation indicators, crop phenology layers, and anomaly maps, which are updated three times per month as soon as new satellite data become available. ASIS offers multi-annual data archive (back to 1984), contributing to various climate and socio-economic studies.

_raw.Description: The Agricultural Stress Index System (ASIS) Web Platform is a satellite‑based digital solution designed to identify agricultural areas affected by drought or abnormal vegetation stress worldwide. ASIS calculates the agricultural areas affected by drought, and classified as slight, moderate, and severe. The platform uses seasonal and non‑seasonal vegetation indicators, crop phenology layers, and anomaly maps, which are updated three times per month as soon as new satellite data become available. ASIS offers multi-annual data archive (back to 1984), contributing to various climate and socio-economic studies.

As of February 2026, some of the use cases featured on the platform's website include Global Information and Early Warning System (GIEWS) Early Warning Reports.

records.title: Agro Window
records.description: The Agro Window is a dedicated agricultural credit guarantee scheme implemented by the Kosovo Credit Guarantee Fund to improve access to finance for farmers and agribusinesses. By sharing lending risk with participating financial institutions, the Agro Window reduces collateral requirements and encourages banks to extend medium- and long-term loans to the agricultural sector. The scheme supports investments in primary production and agribusiness development, contributing to rural economic growth and financial inclusion. Agro Window offer guarantees to financial institutions covering the credit risk to micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) that are active in agriculture sector, being registered in KBRA or farmers possessing the Farm Identification Number (FIN)
records.abstract: Agricultural credit guarantee window

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Reported results include expanded agricultural lending supported by guarantees with KCGF citing EUR 14.5 million in Agro Window-financed loans to 370 enterprises and farmers by October 2020. According to resources online, the solution improved lender decision-making through reduced information asymmetry and more standardised agro-finance analysis. KCGF also specifies the Agro Window guarantee parameters up to 60 percent of principal up to EUR 50 000, and up to 50 percent above that threshold, with maturities up to 120 months, which are intended to improve access to finance for eligible farmers and agribusinesses.

records.title: Animal register and food production capacity register
records.description: The Animal register and food production capacity register is managed by Food and Veterinary Agency (FVA) and helps identify and re-register livestock and maintain registries of approved and registered food business capacities. The system supports traceability, transparent ear-tag management and official controls, and strengthens food safety and animal health governance through structured data capture and reporting. The FVA plans to contract veterinary clinics and supply them with identification and registration numbers, thus covering all costs for equipping animals on farms with registration numbers, at no cost to farmers.

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth
SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

_annotations.Impact: The system solution aims at improving traceability of animals and food production capacities, enabling faster response to animal-health events and stronger official controls. By supporting re-registration and standardized ear tags, it seeks to reduce misuse of ear-tag numbers and increase transparency. With future interoperability such as with Simplified Integrated Administration and Control System (IACS), the animal register and food production capacity register has the ambition of further strengthening policy making intelligence and risk-based inspections.

records.title: Digital Agenda of Kosovo 2030
records.description: The Digital Agenda of Kosovo 2030 (AD 2030) is a horizontal, cross-sector government policy framework that sets Kosovo’s direction for digital transformation through 2030, positioning digitalisation as a driver of competitiveness, inclusion, and more efficient service delivery. The agenda is designed as a long-term programme that can be reviewed and updated as technology and societal needs evolve, and it is anchored around five strategic objectives—secure advanced digital infrastructure; digital transformation of businesses; digitalization of public services; a digitally skilled population and an innovation/R&D ecosystem; and a sustainable cybersecurity ecosystem—which, in practical terms, aim to expand high-capacity connectivity, accelerate digital uptake in the economy, improve the availability and quality of e-services, raise digital skills and innovation capacity, and strengthen trust and resilience in the digital space. The agenda was initiated by the Ministry of Economy through the Kosovo Digital Economy (KODE) project, and it was approved by the Government of Kosovo.

records.owner_name: Ministry of Economy of the Republic of Kosovo

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth
SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

_annotations.Impact: The policy expects to deliver measurable targets in 2030. These are defined through measurable 2030 targets, including: 100 percent household coverage with 1 Gbps networks and 100 percent 5G coverage of populated areas; increased digital adoption in the private sector (e.g. 75 percent of enterprises using cloud / big data / AI); expanded digital public services including 100 percent of online availability of key public services, the entire population with access to medical records via e-register, and 80 percent of citizens using digital identification); and strengthened digital skills such as 80 percent of adults with at least basic digital skills).

records.title: Digital innovation supports data gathering for better fisheries management
records.description: The resource “Digital innovation supports data gathering for better fisheries management” is designed to strengthen the collection, standardisation and use of fisheries data for effective management decisions. Effective fisheries management involves decisions about the utilization of fish stocks, species selection, fishing locations, seasons, and catch limits while balancing social and economic gains with the preservation of marine ecosystems. The resource explains that access to reliable and up-to-date data is critical and presents FAO-developed tools and platforms that supply the data needed to facilitate the effective management of fisheries at national, regional and global levels.
records.abstract: Factsheet
records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

_annotations.Source: ["The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI), reviewed by an FAO researcher and validated by a member of the initiative&apos","s organization"]

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The AdriaMed Trawl Survey Information System is used by over 17 research institutions in the Mediterranean region and has become the de facto reference data management tool for several Mediterranean countries. The Fisheries Performance Assessment Toolkit was successfully piloted in 10 fisheries over a five-year period with researchers, fishers, fish workers, the private sector and decision-makers in Cabo Verde, Côte d’Ivoire, Ecuador, Indonesia and Senegal. As of June 2024, FAO mobile data collection platforms are fully operational in Saint Lucia, Suriname and Trinidad and Tobago, are being piloted in Bangladesh, Grenada and Lebanon, and are in initial implementation stages in Guyana, with plans for deployment in Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, Dominica and Egypt.

records.title: Digitalization and child labour in agriculture
records.description: Digitalization and child labour in agriculture is a research-based resource designed to examine how blockchain and GIS can strengthen child labour risk monitoring in the cocoa sector. In particular, the resource assesses the potential role of blockchain technology and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) in collecting and sharing data on cocoa-growing areas in Ghana, and how this could contribute to monitoring and ultimately preventing child labour in those areas. During an inception mission undertaken by FAO in Ghana, open consultations with various stakeholders in the cocoa sector led to the identification of a number of Key Data Elements (KDEs) to inform the design of a blockchain system, with the objective to facilitate real-time, cost-efficient and collaborative monitoring of the risk of child labour in cocoa-growing areas in Ghana.
records.abstract: Exploration of blockchain and GIS for child labour risk monitoring in cocoa production

records.title: e-Government Strategy Kosovo 2023–2027
records.description: The e-Government Strategy Kosovo 2023–2027 is the Government’s core framework for accelerating public-sector digitalization in support of the Digital Agenda of Kosovo 2030. It is built around three enabling areas: vision and leadership, technology, and digital skills. The strategy promotes user-centric public e-services, whole-of-government architecture and strengthened public-sector capacities and is implemented through six strategic objectives and an Action Plan (2023–2025). It was developed through a multi-stakeholder process led by the Office of the Prime Minister and the Ministry of Internal Affairs, with technical support from the Estonian e-Governance Academy.

SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

In addition to the strategy, an action plan has been formulated with specific actions, timeline and budgetary implications to fulfil the strategic objectives of the strategy.

records.title: Regulation EU 2021 2115 Common Agricultural Policy Strategic Plans
records.description: Regulation EU 2021 2115 establishes the framework for the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) strategic plans implemented by Member States and financed through Union agricultural funds. The regulation defines common objectives of instruments and governance requirements while granting flexibility to Member States to design national interventions aligned with local needs. It integrates income support sectoral measures and rural development actions within a single strategic planning and performance framework.

records.title: Evolution of food e-commerce during the COVID-19 pandemic
records.description: The resource entitled “Evolution of food e-commerce during the COVID-19 pandemic” is an FAO investment brief that analyzes the rapid surge of online food purchasing and its implications for fresh fruits and vegetables (FFV) retail. The resource highlights the emergence of new actors, services and business models such as quick-commerce and omnichannel strategies and provides policy recommendations and investment priorities for sustainable integration of e-commerce into urban food systems while minimizing socioeconomic and environmental risks.

records.title: Grants Management Information System (Grants Register)
records.description: The Grants Register is an electronic Grants Management Information System developed and used by the Development Agency to handle rural development grants under Instrument for Pre-Accession Assistance for Rural Development (IPARD)-like programs. The system allows farmers to apply for agricultural grants online and enables the Agricultural Development Agency (ADA) to oversee the full grant process – from application intake and approvals to payment disbursement and field inspections.
records.abstract: Electronic platform for managing agricultural grants in Kosovo
records.owner_name: Agricultural Development Agency (ADA), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Rural Development (Kosovo)

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The introduction of the Grants Management Information System aims at improving transparency and accountability in the grant disbursement process – all applications and decisions are recorded in the system, making it easier to audit and reducing opportunities for corruption or favoritism. Since its inception, the Grants Register aimed at helping to standardize grant management procedures and reduce opportunities for misuse of funds. The platform features modules for farmers to upload application documents via a web portal, for officials to process payments and authorizations, and for tracking on-farm inspections. This digital solution was introduced to improve transparency and efficiency in disbursing farm grants, replacing some of the paper-based workflows with a more traceable and streamlined online process.

records.title: Green Agenda for The Western Balkans
records.description: The Green Agenda for the Western Balkans is a regional policy framework aligned with the European Green Deal, structured around five pillars: climate action including decarbonisation, energy and mobility, circular economy, biodiversity, pollution reduction in air, water and soil, and sustainable food systems and rural areas. The working document guides reforms and investments across the Western Balkans, including measures relevant to climate-smart and resource-efficient agriculture. Digitalisation will be a key enabler for the above five pillars in line with the concept of the dual green and digital transition.

records.title: Simplified Integrated Administration and Control System (IACS)
records.description: Simplified Integrated Administration and Control System (IACS) is a streamlined set of interoperable digital registries and workflows used to manage agricultural support schemes in Kosovo, enabling farmer registration, land parcel referencing and direct payment processing in a single operational chain. Built around the Electronic Farmers Register (eFR), a simplified Land Parcel Identification System (sLPIS) and a Direct Payment Support Register, the platform aims at strengthening eligibility checks, inspection planning and payment traceability, supporting more transparent and efficient delivery of subsidies and pre-accession (IPARD) assistance and measures. The eFR is a digital database managed by Kosovo’s Payment Agency, designed to determine farmers’ eligibility for financial support from public authorities and other sources. sLPIS is a GIS-based system for mapping and checking agricultural parcels while the Direct Payment module manages applications, controls and payments for support schemes. Together, they form the backbone of Kosovo’s digital subsidy administration
records.abstract: Farm registry, land identification, and direct payments
records.owner_name: Ministry of Agriculture Forestry and Rural Development - MAFRD, Kosovo; Paying Agency under the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Rural Development (MAFRD); Agency for Agricultural Development (AAD / Agjencia për Zhvillimin e Bujqësisë – AZhB)

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth
SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

_annotations.Impact: The combined eFR–sLPIS–Direct Payment system has transformed subsidy administration in Kosovo from fragmented, fully paper-based processes into a structured digital workflow even if some components remain paper based. The integrated system has created a single registry of more than 60 000 farms, each with a unique ID, reducing duplicate claims and improving targeting. Mapping of parcels in sLPIS increases the accuracy of area-based payments and allows better control of land-related measures. The Direct Payment module speeds up processing and supports auditable decision-trails, contributing to greater transparency and institutional trust. While many applications are still facilitated through municipal offices, the digital backbone reduces paperwork and travel and creates a unique identity and mapped holding for each participating farm. Future upgrades aim at a further integration with other national e-government systems in particular through the e-Kosova platform.

records.title: Kosovo Vineyard Cadastre and Wine Quality Control System (SVV v.1.3)
records.description: SVV v.1.3 is Kosovo’s vineyard cadastre and wine-quality control information system. The platform maintains a georeferenced register of vineyard parcels for varieties and owners and supports regulatory workflows, including vintage declarations and requests to place wines on the market, including internal market, export and import. The system also supports administrative controls and quality assurance through laboratory sample analysis and organoleptic evaluation.

records.title: Strategy for Agriculture and Rural Development (SARD) 2022–2028
records.description: The Strategy for Agriculture and Rural Development (SARD) 2022–2028 is Kosovo’s policy framework for reform and investment in the agri-food and rural sector, aligned with EU approximation and the Common Agricultural Policy. It promotes an inclusive, productive and competitive agro-rural economy through four objectives covering farm competitiveness, natural resource management, rural businesses and employment, and institutional reform, including digitalization and knowledge transfer. The Strategy addresses constraints such as land fragmentation, outdated machinery, infrastructure gaps, high input costs and limited access to finance, and guides Government programming and donor alignment, including IPARD preparation.
records.abstract: Multiannual reference guide and strategy for agriculture and rural development
records.owner_name: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Rural Development (MAFRD), Government of Kosovo

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The policy sets measurable intended targets and defines impact through a results framework with mid-term and final targets. Under Strategic Objective 1, for example, it targets: a 20 percent increase of gross value added in the agriculture sector by 2028 (baseline shown as 477 million euro), an addition of 5 percent in annual work units), and 14.28 percent labour productivity increase by 2028. Beyond competitiveness, SARD’s indicators and action plan cover environmental and rural development outcomes such as targets linked to soil erosion reduction and climate/renewable-energy related indicators, as well as rural development measures (employment/local development instruments such as LAGs). The Strategy also connects impact to strengthened institutional performance and alignment with CAP-type indicator approaches including AKIS establishment as part of the broader performance logic.

records.title: Agrarian Information System (AGIS)
records.description: AGIS is a comprehensive agrarian information system supporting the management of EU agricultural funds, including the Rural Development Program (RDP), Common Market Organization (CMO) and national agricultural subsidies. The platform serves as a paying agency, where the European Commission sends their payment to deliver financial support to beneficiaries. Additionally, the system enables paying agencies to administer applications, evaluate projects, conduct on-the-spot checks, manage irregularities, process payments, conduct risk analysis and produce monitoring and financial reports in line with EU regulations.

_annotations.Impact: AGIS aims to strengthen the efficiency, transparency and accuracy of EU agricultural payment administration by centralizing financial processes, monitoring, reporting and compliance management. AGIS has been deployed by the State Intervention Fund in the Czechia and the Agricultural Paying Agency in Slovakia.

records.title: AGMRI
records.description: AGMRI is a high-resolution aerial imagery and analytics platform that delivers actionable intelligence to growers and ag retailers. The solution enables monitoring of crop health, emergence, weed pressure, nutrient deficiencies, disease risk, and yield forecasts using high-resolution imagery, weather, soil, and machine-data layers. The platform supports data-driven decision making to optimize farm management, reduce risk, and improve agronomic and economic outcomes.

records.description: ABACOFarmer is a digital farm management platform that helps farmers plan agricultural activities, maintain digital farm records, and comply with national and European regulatory requirements. records.title: AgriCloud
records.description: AgriCloud is a digital agriculture platform that provides real-time meteorological data and decision support insights for farmers. The solution performs crop monitoring organized in one platform to generate early weather, disease, and pest alerts. The system integrates field weather stations soil monitoring devices and cloud-based analytics to support irrigation planning pest and disease alerts crop growth monitoring and risk reduction. The platform also includes a Financial Forecast module that provides farmers with monthly production potential estimates, ideal planting periods, and projected income calculations based on expected yields and crop prices

records.title: Agricultural Sector Policy Note for Bosnia and Herzegovina
records.description: The Agricultural Sector Policy Note for Bosnia and Herzegovina Trade and Integration policy note highlights key steps to improve the subsistence of rural population through agri-food sector improvement and evolve into a more competitive import and export country. Based on the identified constraints in the agri-food sector such as viability of fragmented arable lands poorly defined property rights and farmers receiving low prices for their outputs, the policy note proposes proper allocation of public resources in areas such as food safety services, research and education, and a shift in direct price and output subsidies. Lastly, the policy note details key digitalization-focused objectives: complete the ongoing digitalization of existing maps and land-books; (ii) record land registration data in electronic databases; (iii) harmonize cadastre and land registration information; and (iv) expand work with the Cadastre Agencies, based on the forthcoming results of the eight ongoing pilots under the World Bank-financed Land Registration Project.

records.owner_name: Poverty Reduction and Economic Management Unit Europe and Central Asia Region, World Bank

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The policy note aims to provide concrete steps for the country to develop the sector and programmes. These include institutions, agricultural education, research, extension services, and information systems; all components that are emphasized in the policy document. Specifically, targeted future benefits include digitalization of land administration systems, strengthened food safety institutions, and improved agricultural information services, through which are expected to enhance sector competitiveness and support more efficient, transparent service delivery.

records.title: AgriSound’s Polly™
records.description: Agrisound’s Polly is an insect monitoring solution designed to detect pollinator activity in real time using bioacoustic technology. The sensors attract a wide range of insects through their size, shape and colour and capture sound signatures to identify levels of pollinator presence.
records.abstract: Bioacoustic monitoring solution to detect real-time insect activity

_annotations.Country of origin: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
_annotations.Impact: The technology aims to strengthen biodiversity monitoring by providing accurate and continuous data on pollinator activity as well as supporting evidence-based actions to restore ecosystems improve crop pollination and reduce dependence on managed pollinator species. Agrisound’s Polly™ devices have already been rolled out across 18 additional sites in the UK as of January 2026, following successful trials. These devices now cover 120 habitats across more than 1 000 hectares, representing 8 percent of all British growers.

records.title: Agriculture 4.0 Information and Communication Technology for future Agriculture
records.description: Agriculture 4.0 – Information and Communication Technology (ICT) for future Agriculture is an Erasmus+ project that strengthens digital skills and competences in agriculture through Vocational Education and Training (VET). Agriculture 4.0 develops and pilots a Farming 4.0 curriculum, an e-collaboration platform and practical handbooks that introduce key ICT tools for farm management and advisory services.

_annotations.Impact: Agriculture 4.0 aims to improve the digital skills of young farmers, advisors and teachers and to increase the capacity of VET systems to address agriculture-related ICT needs. Within the project, 50 students, 30 advisors and 15 teachers are directly involved in testing the Farming 4.0 curriculum and materials, while multiplier events in each partner country are designed to reach a wider group of VET institutions, extension services and policy makers and to support broader uptake of digital agriculture training.

records.title: AgriThon
records.description: AgriThon is a competition platform, and a capacity-building and startup-incubation project designed to support innovative agriculture and agribusiness solutions in Armenia. The competition is implemented by the ICARE-Armenia Foundation within the framework of the USAID-funded AGRI CAMP programme. The project provides mentorship, training and competitive seed support for young agripreneurs, researchers, cooperatives and early-stage teams working on digital agriculture concepts, sustainable production practices and value-chain improvements. Meanwhile, AgriThon 2 explored innovations such as producing eco-friendly can straw hanging mushroom bags, a digital system that automatically informs actors about adverse conditions, among others.

records.title: Agro-informatics Platform
records.description: Agro-informatics Platform - How to create and share a story is a resource introducing the story feature of the FAO Agro‑informatics Platform, which enables users to create interactive narratives from geospatial data. Stories consist of captured scenes—such as maps, datasets and visualizations—that guide viewers through themes or analyses. They help transform data into clear visual journeys, highlighting key insights across time periods, geographic patterns, or the effects of specific changes. The resource outlines how each scene preserves the exact map view and configuration, enabling users to structure analyses as step-by-step narratives.
records.abstract: User guide on How to create and share a story
records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)

_annotations.Impact: The publication illustrates how story-creation capabilities enhance communication, learning, and collaboration. It shows that stories allow users to move beyond static maps and visually explain why data matter and what they reveal about agriculture, land or socioeconomic dynamics. The guide notes that these tools support evidence-based dialogue, collaboration and communication of geospatial analysis, illustrating the impact of certain land changes with clarity and context.

records.title: CHAMELEON
records.description: CHAMELEON is a Horizon Europe project using integrated drone-based technology to support data-driven decision-making in agriculture, livestock, forestry and pest management. In agriculture, the project focuses on CO₂ sequestration and biomass estimation, as well as irrigation, water-stress monitoring and management. In livestock, it supports behavioural analysis and protection of animals, including early and non-intrusive lameness detection. In forestry, the solution develops a plant health assessment toolkit. For pest management, it tests selective spraying applications for low-risk fertilization and forest health protection.

records.title: CODECS
records.description: CODECS is a Horizon Europe research project that analyses the costs and co-benefits of farm digitalization in real farming systems across Europe. CODECS works with farmers and Agricultural Knowledge and Innovation System (AKIS) actors to assess how tools such as precision technologies, farm management systems and data platforms affect productivity, profitability, environmental performance and social outcomes
records.abstract: Project on sustainable farm digitalization ecosystems in Europe

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: CODECS aims to demonstrate how digital tools can support more productive and sustainable farming by coordinating 21 Living Labs across diverse farming systems and documenting their costs and co-benefits. records.title: Cows and Hectars
records.description: Cows and Hectars is a digital module in the State Agrarian Registry of Ukraine that allows farmers who keep cattle and cultivate land to apply online for state support. The initiative links information on cows and hectares of land in one place so that support rules can be checked and managed more easily.

records.owner_name: Ministry of Agrarian Policy and Food of Ukraine

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Cows and Hectars aims to contribute to the broader impact of the State Agrarian Registry, which has enabled the disbursement of financial and technical aid to more than 40 000 farmers, amounting to over UAH 2 billion. The initiative aims to improve the quality and consistency of data used to administer schemes, thereby reducing errors and strengthening targeting public support. The module also demonstrates good practice in modular, GIS-enabled design that can be replicated for other themes such as crops, horticulture or climate-resilience measures, supporting more agile digitalization of agricultural support systems.

records.title: Connecting VET Teachers to Agriculture 4.0
records.description: Connecting VET Teachers to Agriculture 4.0 is an Erasmus+ project that strengthens digital skills and competences in agriculture by focusing on vocational education and training for Vocational Education and Training (VET) teachers. The project develops and pilots the Teachers for Farming 4.0 online course, together with a Farming 4.0 curriculum, guidelines and handbooks that show how Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) tools can be integrated into agricultural teaching and advisory work.
records.abstract: Online course for teachers on digital agriculture

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Connecting VET Teachers to Agriculture 4.0 aims to improve the capacity of agricultural VET systems to respond to labour market needs for digitally skilled workers. According to available report on the project, in North Macedonia, 20 teachers from seven VET schools enrolled in the pilot course and 16 teachers from six schools successfully completed it. In Hungary, 61 teachers from 22 VET schools enrolled in the pilot training and 51 successfully completed it.

records.title: Digital Agriculture Market (DITAP)
records.description: Digital Agriculture Market (DİTAP) is a national digital marketplace connecting agricultural producers with buyers through contract farming and direct online sales. The platform covers plant, animal and fisheries products and follows the chain from seed to fork. Producers can sell their products at fair prices, and consumers and agri-food industries can access quality products more reliably.
records.abstract: Online marketplace for connecting Turkish farmers with buyers along the agri-food chain
records.owner_name: Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry of the Republic of Türkiye

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: DİTAP intends to help farmers obtain better prices and more predictable demand, reduce dependence on intermediaries, and strengthen bargaining power. The digital space can reduce food loss and waste through better planning of production and logistics. Public statements from the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry in 2020 reported that the marketplace had already facilitated around TRY 150 million in transaction volume and attracted over 100 000 registered buyers and sellers.

records.title: Mokrin
records.description: Digital Village in Mokrin is a village-level digitalization project that turns Mokrin, in the North Banat district of Serbia, into a pilot digital village where farmers and residents use Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) to modernize agriculture and everyday life and local business opportunities. The village combines on-farm infrastructure, digital platforms and tailored training.
records.abstract: First digital village in Serbia for smart agriculture and rural revitalization

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Digital Village in Mokrin has so far enrolled around 30 agricultural holdings, including at least 24 farms and more than 100 farmers, and has installed about ten agro-meteorological stations and organized at least ten training and information events. The initiative aims to increase farm profitability and input efficiency, foster joint market initiatives, and strengthen the long-term viability of Mokrin as a rural community by reducing outmigration and attracting younger residents back to agriculture.

records.title: EU4AGRI project
records.description: EU4AGRI is a five-year EU-funded project in Bosnia and Herzegovina that modernizes the agri-food sector, creates and preserves rural jobs and supports recovery from the COVID-19 crisis. The project raises investment in primary production, processing and rural businesses, expands advisory services and economic opportunities in rural areas, and improves the policy and institutional framework for agriculture and rural development in line with the EU’s Common Agricultural Policy.
records.abstract: Supporting agriculture competitiveness and rural development in Bosnia and Herzegovina

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: EU4AGRI aims to strengthen the competitiveness and resilience of agri-food sector. By 2025, it had launched 24 public calls, channelled nearly EUR 15 million in EU grants and leveraged an additional EUR 8 million in private co-financing. EU4AGRI has supported 211 investment projects and reached 2040 agri-food operators, creating over 300 new jobs, many for women and young people in rural areas. Among the 2082 stakeholders supported, 1623 were small farm holdings. Additionally, the project worked with 28 local governments, 6 science and research institutions, and 8 advisory service providers, enhancing both grassroots and institutional capacities.

records.title: Nation in Action
records.description: Nation in Action is a non-formal education and entrepreneurship platform that supports youth in Armenia to develop AgriTech startup ideas. One EU-GAIA-supported startup call attracted 10 green agriculture companies and selected three winners: a digital irrigation control app, a digital platform for agricultural extension and a circular solution turning coffee grounds into biodegradable organic fertilizer.

records.title: Proofminder
records.description: Proofminder is a leaf-level farming software that uses high-resolution imagery and artificial intelligence to generate plant- and leaf-level insights for crop production. Proofminder supports field crops, vegetables, orchards and vineyards to detect weeds, assess plant population, monitor crop health, and estimate yield potential across entire fields. The solution provides instant leaf-level insights, supports production goals sustainably, saves time, and maximizes return on investment.
records.abstract: AI leaf-level crop monitoring platform

_annotations.Impact: Proofminder aims to support higher productivity, lower environmental impacts, and stronger resilience of crop production systems. The company indicates that leaf-level insights can increase yield and profitability by around ten percent, while reducing chemical input use by up to eighty percent, and cut labour and save time. The Proofminder website also highlights collaborations with agri-food value chain actors such as Corteva Agriscience, Bonduelle, Bonafarm Csoport, as well as participation in initiatives such as EUREKA Innowwide and EIT Food.

records.title: RIMpro
records.description: RIMpro is a digital decision support system designed to support pest and disease management in fruit orchards and vineyards. The solution integrates real-time weather data with scientifically validated biological models to calculate infection and development risks for key pests and diseases. It supports growers and advisors in timing crop protection measures and applying integrated pest management practices.
records.abstract: Decision support system for pest and disease management for fruit and grape production

_annotations.Source: ["The initiative was developed with the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI), reviewed by an FAO researcher and validated by a member of the initiative&apos","s organization"]
_annotations.Impact: RIMpro has been used for more than 25 years in fruit and grape production contexts and is implemented in over 40 countries worldwide. By providing weather-based risk assessments for pests and diseases, the platform aims to supportevidence-based decision making that can contribute to more targeted crop protection, potentially reducing unnecessary pesticide applications.

records.title: TUMO Labs AgriTech Incubation Program
records.description: TUMO Labs AgriTech Incubation Program is a technology incubation project that supports young adults in Armenia to develop AgriTech startup ideas through an intensive ideation and mentoring process. The programme provides structured training, coaching and business model development to help teams design digital agriculture solutions. Ideation Kickoff is a 48-hour event where up to 60 participants are selected and evaluated on leadership and teamwork, followed by an Incubation Adventure phase lasting 12 weeks in which six leaders form teams and use market research and user feedback to shape AgriTech ideas. Market Entry Support provides three to six months of mentoring for up to three finalists, while comprehensive support spans all stages through business model refinement, pitch preparation, and guidance on digital tools and acceleration options.
records.abstract: AgriTech technology incubation programme

_annotations.Impact: TUMO Labs aims to create a pipeline of digital agriculture ventures that strengthen farm productivity, improve resource use, and connect early-stage solutions. The programme supports teams through hybrid online and in-person workshops supporting development and preparation of investor-ready pitches.

records.title: LIFE VitiCaSe
records.description: LIFE VitiCaSe (Viticulture for Soil Organic Carbon Sequestration) is a four-year EU LIFE project that is piloting a practical approach to carbon farming in European vineyards. The central idea of the project is to help winegrowers increase soil organic carbon (SOC) through sustainable soil management, transforming these climate benefits into measurable, verifiable and tradable carbon credits. VitiCaSe brings together Image Line (project's coordinator), CREA, SMEs, associations and leading wineries in Tuscany and Veneto, combining research, digital innovation and field demonstrations.In short, VitiCaSe translates “carbon farming” from concept to practice for viticulture, aligning climate mitigation with resilient and profitable vineyard management.
records.abstract: Carbon Farming LIFE Project applied to Viticulture (Project 101113620 - LIFE22-CCA-IT-LIFE VitiCaSe)

_annotations.Source: Information provided by a member of the organization
_annotations.Impact: The climate impact of LIFE VitiCaSe is supported by solid agronomy and careful monitoring. While the Grant Agreement projected 3,363–7,396 tCO₂e removals over four years, CREA’s preliminary analysis suggests around 13,834 tCO₂e between 2024 and 2027, pending final data. Beyond carbon storage, vineyards show higher fertility, stronger water retention and reduced erosion, boosting resilience to climate extremes. Economically, the project provides a clear pathway to certification and carbon credit sales, reinforced by environmental and cost-benefit analyses. With four pilot sites already applying improved practices as of January 2026, results can be scaled and transferred via Image Line’s network, promoting climate-smart viticulture across Europe.

records.title: Qoldau
records.description: The Qoldau.kz platform is a digital ecosystem used in Kazakhstan that supports farmers and other agribusiness actors by offering a range of services — including agricultural-related services — as well as non-agricultural government and business services. The platform features 1) Virtual grain warehouse (Astyq Qoima) — a digital system for monitoring grain stocks and storage, functioning as a “virtual warehouse” to help farmers and grain handlers manage inventories.; 2) Grain receipts registry (AgriBonds) — a register of holders of agricultural and grain receipts that supports transparency of grain collateral and transactions; and other services.

records.description: FarmReal was a web-based app and mobile app facilitating the creation of virtual social links and promoting the support of traditional goat rearing and goat cheese production by tourists and customers in Ferraria de São João (Portugal). Through FarmReal, users could adopt goats in the village's community herd and become “virtual shepherds", monitoring the behaviour and daily lives of the goats in terms of physical activity, socialization and milk production, while tracking their grazing locations.

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Besides the recreational and educational aspects of the project, the users were contributing to the sustainability of the community herd, and thus to the revitalization of dairy goat production based on the region’s traditional agro-forest grazing system. FarmReal attracted investments into rural communities and preserves the traditional ways agricultural products are produced.

records.title: Cloudfarms
records.description: Cloudfarms is a fully cloud‑based swine production management platform that centralizes farm data and analytics to support pork producers of all sizes. The platform offers a variety of services such as sow management, breeding and multiplication, boar and semen analysis, and other farm management related functionalities like collecting real-time data of swine health. The technology addresses the challenge of inefficient, labor-intensive, and fragmented data recording in pig production by enabling real‑time, mobile‑enabled data capture and comprehensive traceability across the supply chain.

records.title: SoilOptix
records.description: SoilOptix® is a precision soil mapping system that couples non‐contact passive gamma spectroscopy with strategic soil sampling and software analytics to deliver high‐definition maps of 25+ soil properties. Typical surveys provide ~335+ data points per acre (≈827/ha), turning spatial variability into actionable layers for pH, texture, CEC, macro/micronutrients, bulk density, and plant‐available water. Outputs are GIS/VRA‐ready (CSV/SHP) and integrate with farm platforms to support site‐specific management.

_annotations.Impact: Spacenus aims to reduce nitrogen overuse, support regenerative agriculture, and provide carbon transparency across farming operations. Further, it can contribute to enhanced yield stability, lower input costs, facilitate evidence-based climate action, nutrient stewardship and GHG reduction at scale. According to the company’s website, achievement includes enabling up to 30% nitrogen reduction while maintaining yield and supporting GHG mitigation.

records.title: Nedap dairy ecosystem: CowControl, FarmControl, and MilkingControl
records.description: The Nedap Dairy Ecosystem is a digital herd management platform that integrates CowControl, FarmControl and MilkingControl to improve animal health, welfare and dairy productivity. records.title: Oxbury Bank
records.description: Oxbury is a UK-based digital bank dedicated to agriculture that offers financing tailored to farm production cycles. Its products include seasonal input credit, flexible working capital, and long-term loans for farm investment and modernization. The Farm Credit facility allows farmers to purchase inputs from approved suppliers, with invoices automatically uploaded into the online banking platform for payment and account monitoring. Oxbury also provides a Transition Facility linking finance to the adoption of more sustainable and low-carbon practices.

_annotations.Country of origin: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Oxbury aims to support financial resilience in UK agriculture by providing credit aligned with production cycles and farm input needs. According to their annual report, in 2024, the bank reported £1.6 billion in customer lending balances and £1.2 billion in deposits, with £400 million net lending growth. Its Farm Credit facility has processed over 100,000 supplier invoices, improving liquidity and cash flow for farm businesses.

records.title: Agro.Club
records.description: Agro.Club is a digital marketplace that connects farmers, grain buyers, and input suppliers through mobile and web platforms. records.title: E‑Planner
records.description: E‑Planner is a free tool that uses AI-driven spatial modelling to produce high‑resolution and interactive suitability maps for ecological interventions. Some of the management options users can explore are habitats for seed-rich birds, flower-rich pollinators and wet grasslands restoration as well as woodland creation, water resource protection, and agri-environment schemes. E-planner is also developed alongside e-surveyor, a complementary mobile app to assist in environmental monitoring. The initiative addresses the increasing pressure among farmers to deliver a wide range of environmental goals from their land and producing food.

records.title: DeLaval Herd Management
records.description: DeLaval herd management is a digital farm management solution acting as a unified system that integrates milking, feeding, reproduction, and health data for sheep and goat herds. Ultimately, it aims to overcome inefficiencies in livestock farming by improving productivity, herd health, and operational control.

records.title: Nofence Virtual Fencing
records.description: Nofence Virtual Fencing is a solar‑powered collar with cloud‑connected app system that creates and manages virtual fences for cattle, sheep and goats. There are two collar types being offered: the cattle collar is built tough to withstand the strength and wear from cattle while sheep and goal collars are relatively smaller and lighter. Key features include drawing digital boundaries on a smartphone, collars guiding animals with audio cues before a mild pulse, real‑time herd visibility, remote boundary edits, and Bluetooth beacons that suspend virtual fences inside barns or shelters. Nofence addresses agricultural and technology challenges such as time‑ and material‑intensive fence construction, inflexible grazing layouts, difficult terrain where physical fencing is impractical, and limited animal visibility—while coping with power/connectivity constraints via solar charging and LTE‑M/2G backhaul.

records.title: Dairy Union of Kazakhstan Knowledge Base (База знаний)
records.description: The Dairy Union of Kazakhstan Knowledge Base is a comprehensive online repository of news, reports, laws and regulations, invitation to events and participation and other resources for the dairy sector of Kazakhstan. The knowledge base has user-focused categories. These include webpages for farmers, producers, consumers, and sellers. The section dedicated to farmers can access information on sanitary norms and requirements, step-by-step instructions in milking, and good practices. Meanwhile, the food producers section provides supply and demand information, regulatory documents, and reports such as trends and technologies in cheese production and other dairy products. Additionally, the section for sellers and consumers supplies safety and food productions regulation, and food consumer dictionary, respectively.

_annotations.Impact: The knowledge base aims to disseminate knowledge through a centralized repository of resources and information materials across the dairy sector. records.title: Copernicus case studies on agriculture
records.description: Copernicus is Earth observation component of the European Union’s Space programme. The platfrorm stores sustainability tools and case studies that use Earth Observation and in-situ data for agricultural purposes. These Earth Observation data are sourced from Copernicus, a platform spearheaded by the European Union’s Space Progamme, providing satellite, ground-based, airborne, and seaborne measurement systems. As of July 2025, there are nine available use cases and reports focusing on topics such as 1) precision farming, 2) sustainable farming, 3) coffee, biodiversity, and health, 4) biomass indicators, 5) drought monitoring, 6) crop monitoring, 7) crop and yield forecasting, 8) drought surveillance, and 9) soil water index.
records.abstract: Earth observation component of the European Union’s Space programme

_annotations.Impact: The outputs from the case studies highlight several impacts such as the access to products that are complementary to in-situ observations, fusion of data that improves the temporal resolution of other satellite products, provide a platform that can serve as world-leading platform for the use and re-use of sustainable and competitive agriculture-centred Earth observation data, among others.

records.title: Belarusian Universal Commodity Exchange (BUCE)
records.description: The Belarusian Universal Commodity Exchange is a trading and auction platform that ensures the implementation of market pricing principles and equal access to commodities for all market stakeholders. Agricultural products are one of the four major categories that BUCE focuses on, providing an organized wholesale market and facilitating the movement of goods. These agricultural products include milk and whey powder, industrial casein, dairy butter, cottage cheese, rennet cheeses, meat, flour, rawhides, oilcakes, vegetable oils and seeds. BUCE also offers information and analysis services where subscribers can gain access to the most up-to-date and accurate information on the commodity exchange market of the Republic of Belarus.

records.title: AquaCrop
records.description: AquaCrop is a crop-water productivity model developed by FAO Land and Water Division that simulates how crops respond to varying water availability under different climates, soils, and management practices. The initiative is widely used for irrigation planning, yield forecasting, and sustainable resource management, supporting farmers, researchers, and policymakers in tackling water scarcity challenges. The software tool provides a user-friendly platform to apply these functions in practice.
records.abstract: FAO Crop Water Productivity Model

_annotations.Impact: In field trials across Europe and Central Asia, AquaCrop has shown high predictive accuracy, with simulated wheat and maize yields typically within ±10 percent observed values under varying irrigation regimes. These results support the initiative for optimizing water management and improving yield forecasts in regions facing increasing water scarcity. AquaCrop is deployed globally, with documented applications in more than 25 countries. The impact is further supported by a wide body of peer-reviewed publications and FAO technical reports, as well as embedded training videos and tutorials available on the website.

records.description: The Türkiye Climate Smart and Competitive Agricultural Growth Project is supported by the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry with support from the World Bank. The project promotes climate-smart practices, efficient irrigation, and digital tools while enhancing veterinary and extension services. records.title: AgroHub
records.description: AgroHub is a project initiated by Tirana’s Department for Rural Economic Development and managed by the Tirana Agrikulture S.R.L company. The initiative’s objective is to develop new logistic points for the collection and food sale,and prioritize agricultural production in rural areas. The conceptualization of the project is intended to go beyond the private market. To do so, farmers and small producers receive access to public markets designed to bring agricultural players together, increase their production, and participate in export opportunities. The hub functions as an agency for rural and agricultural development, providing advisory services such as assistance in putting together dossiers, and submitting applications to potential government funding. Overall, AgroHub aims to address the major issues of rural development, small-scale agricultural production, territorial cohesion, product quality and the link between consumers and producers.

records.title: AfiAct II
records.description: AfiMilk's smart sensor monitors and records the essential aspects of milk yield, identifying cows that have lower or increased milk production conductivity. The sensors provide data on short-term detection of health problems, long-term genetic potential, protein and fat milk components to detect ketosis, nutritional issues and digestion-related problems, and scans of lactose content to accurately identify mastitis. Other key features of the sensor include detecting Sub-Acute Ruminal Acidosis (SARA) which allows farmers to treat the related grow by adapting the feed regime, identifying feed problems that assist in decision-making for the next milking session.

records.title: AfiFarm
records.description: Afifarm Herd Management Software is an application to effectively manage animal inventory, health problem detection, and intervention for milking, health, and fertility. The app utilizes real-time information and trend analysis to improve cow and farm management. The initiative’s main features are summarized into 1) comprehensive fertility detection from heat signs, timing insemination, and cow performance, 2) smart monitoring of early indications of heat stress, food and comfort issues among herds, 3) intelligent health detection and notification for signs of ketosis, mastitis, fresh cow’s diseases, digestion problems, among others, 4) and guided milking times and flow, and monitoring of milking progress.

records.title: AfiCollar
records.description: AfiCollar is a smart neck collar designed for monitoring individual cows and groups. The smart collar provides information for accurate heat detection, rumination and eating time, health of individual cows, and group digestion. The collar’s main benefits are the heat detection feature which monitors herd’s pregnancy rate, and the accurate monitoring of rumination and eating patterns. Through the collar, farmers receive health alerts about the overall animal behaviour and wellbeing.
