records.title: WHEATWATCHER
records.description: WHEATWATCHER is a project that offers an integrated digital solution for soil, plant, and food system monitoring in response to global challenges like climate change and food insecurity. The project integrates the needs of various stakeholders to tailor solutions for monitoring chemical, biological, and nutritional factors affecting wheat from field to flour. WHEATWATCHER's scalable system supports farmers, millers, and policymakers across Europe with real-time insights via a cloud platform and decision support tool. The initiative addresses global challenges like climate change and food insecurity.

_annotations.Impact: WHEATWATCHER aims to deliver positive impacts by improving soil health, enhancing food safety, and promoting sustainable farming practices. The initiative targets to develop innovative solutions such as stationary platform designed for continuous soil quality assessment, mobile unit for real-time soil scanning, and remote sensing tool for large-scale soil health monitoring and stress detection, among others. Moreover, WHEATWATCHER's scalable design seeks to support EU Green Deal goals, boosts traceability, and contributes to healthier ecosystems and rural communities.

records.title: Digital Transformation in Agriculture and Rural Areas
records.description: The resource Digital Transformation in Agriculture and Rural Areas presents Horizon 2020 and Horizon Europe projects, highlighting the immense work of the projects to transform agriculture and rural areas. The document first presents the reasons why innovation on digitalization in the sector matter. These justifications include improved decision-making capabilities and practices through data-driven insights, the potential to offer consumers greater transparency on food production, and facilitation of digital transformation for the benefits of European citizens and businesses. Secondly, the success stories in-lined with digital solutions cover stories on the use of smart solutions citing projects such as SmartAgriHubs, ROMI and Pantheon. Sustainable digitalization in rural areas, on the one hand, highlights projects such as ICAERUS, SPADE, Chameleon, DESIRA; all doing various works to assess the impacts of digitalization and explore solutions such as drones and robotics, among others. Lastly, the resource outlines relevant information databases to support the digital transformation process.

In the future, the resource stresses the strategic interventions that can support the uptake of digital technologies, increased research and innovative investments to develop new digital solutions, and assess the socio-economic impacts of digitalization.

records.title: Agri-food Data Portal
records.description: Agri-food Data Portal is a platform that houses data on several aspects of agriculture and common agricultural policy (CAP) at the national and European level. records.title: Agri Sustainability Compass
records.description: Agri Sustainability Compass is an interactive tool showing 20 key indicators for the three sustainability pillars in agriculture: 1) Economic performance, 2) Social performance, 3) Environmental and climate performance. The tool provides a detailed definition of each indicator with accompanying statistics and insights. The initiative enables users to have a better understanding of the economic, social, environmental and climate status and performance of each Member State. A unique feature the tool offers is the quick assessment of the trend in each indicator using three categories, namely evolution in the desired, neutral or mixed, and undesired direction.  The site is managed by the Directorate-General for Agriculture and Rural Development.
records.abstract: Interactive tool for monitoring agricultural sustainability

_annotations.Impact: Overall, the Agri Sustainability Compass aims to help users understand how the farmers and the agricultural sector are performing over time in simple terms and dynamic presentation of data. According to the resources online, the tool aids in quickly debunking some common misconceptions about agriculture, proving that the sector is not starting from zero to achieve sustainability. The tool also facilitates the transparent and monitoring requirement of CAP since many of the parameters of the compass are part of the CAP indicators.

records.title: Strategy for Development of Agriculture and Fisheries through 2030
records.description: The Strategy for Development of the Agribusiness and Fishery Sectors of the Russian Federation through 2030 is a comprehensive policy document outlining key objectives and economic policy measures for the Russian agriculture, fisheries and rural development over the next decade. One of the eight policy objectives focuses on the digital transformation of the agribusiness sector. This involves the creation of a national platform to have a unified digital industry data model, ensuring traceability of regulated agribusiness products, and providing e-government services. Under the same objective, the policy also calls for more strengthened digital services for effective agricultural land rehabilitation and land reclamation.

records.title: Smart Farming Club (SFC)
records.description: The Smart Faming Club is a Russian-based expert community with members of over 225 agricultural enterprise and farms as of May 2025. SFC aims to promote and transform the agribusiness industry through technological progress and developments. The members receive benefits such as unique educational models, radio broadcasts, and coverage of the club’s activities on social networks, among others. The club follows thematic formal and informal events, both offline and online. Club meetings feature intellectual agendas with distinguished speakers addressing the current topics and issues on the technological and innovative development of farm enterprises. Additionally, thematic workshops on the development of modern soft skills that are important for managing technological transformation are also part of the development the members can benefit from.
records.abstract: Expert community for agricultural and technological development

_annotations.Impact: SFC’s mission is to promote the agribusiness industry by leveraging technological progress and developments. In the future, SFC is envisioned to engage in the development of standards and regulations in the field of digitization and automization, and the preparation of proposals for the design and regulation of legal frameworks in the agriculture sector. Another promising trajectory of the club is the analytical and research activities concerning digitization issues. Such involvements position SFC as a consulting body in specific technical solutions as well as projects involving large-scale implementation of information technology in agricultural production.

records.title: Growz
records.description: Growz is a mobile application that utilizes artificial intelligence and big data to assist smallholder farmers in the form of personalized farming advice, marketplace forbest deals on fertilizers and agrochemicals, and access to micro-finance and agro-loans. Through the mobile app, Growz offers crop-centric solution for efficient crop and field management. These solutions include a step-by-step guidance on crop management based on their field data, third parties, AI analysis, and pests and diseases identification and treatment using AI-based advisory. Users can also access supply markets based on their needs and the recommendations the app provides, as well as access to finances in the form of micro-finance, agro-loans.
records.abstract: AI and big data-powered platform for crop diagnostics and agricultural advice

_annotations.Impact: Growz aims to address global problems such as soil degradation and water shortage through innovative data-driven digital solutions like artificial intelligence and big data, enabling farmers to increase their yields, income, and their sustainability practices. Additionally, Growz acts as a bridge between researchers and farmers to optimize their fields while ensuring that the results of research reach the farmers. The initiative draws inspiration from the idea that farmers do not have to leave their homes to manage their farms, and that they can solve  problems through agricultural maps powered by algorithms, and large database of pests and diseases.

records.title: Central Asia-as-a-Platform Strategy and Digital Solutions Centre for Sustainable Development
records.description: The Central Asia-as-a-Platform Strategy and Digital Solutions Centre for Sustainable Development is a working paper that analyses the digital readiness of Central Asian countries, detailing the impact of global trends, and the digital policies, strategies, and initiatives to respond to such trends. Key proposal that is highlighted in the resource is the establishment of Digital Solutions Centre for Sustainable Development in Almaty, Kazakhstan. The centre will serve as a digital platform and implementor of subregional digital strategy. The initiative addresses challenges such as fragmented access to digital resources, lack of coordinated regional solutions, and limited data sharing between institutions; inspiring Central Asian governments to make digital integration an explicit national policy priority.

records.title: Digital Skills Toolkit
records.description: Digital Skills Toolkit provides a comprehensive framework for governments, policymakers, educators, and industry to develop strategies for strengthening digital skills across all segments of society. The roadmap proposed by the toolkit starts from building on digital transformation strategy which consolidates existing strategies, policies and programmes involving digital skills. The establishment of responsible body who will identify stakeholders from government, private and social sectors is necessary to activate multiple-stakeholder engagements. The second part of the roadmap details plan creation which proposes Digital Skills for Life and Digital Skills for Work. The first framework provides the general population with the digital skills to succeed in life while the latter emphasizes the skills needed to succeed both in the IT sector and the broader workforce. Lastly, the third and last stage explores the implementation of developed mechanisms. This part proposes to establish a mechanism for approving, coordinating, and monitoring of programmes alongside data collection of changes in skills levels, and systematic reviewing of progress to identify necessary corrections if needed.
records.abstract: Guide for creating effective national digital skills and strategies

records.title: AgriDataSpace: Building a European framework for a secure and trusted agricultural data space
records.description: AgriDataSpace is a policy brief that provides a roadmap to create a Common European Agricultural Data Space (CEADS) enabling secure and trusted agricultural data sharing. CEADS was launched in January 2025 aiming to deploy and operationalise the data space to ensure secured and trusted data sharing for the agrifood sector. To operationalize the aims of the initiative, common visions include treating CEADS as a decentralised system working as a network rather than a central European solution, the data space is built on four pillars which include Legal and Ethics framework, multi-stakeholder governance, Sustainable business model, and Technology agnostic. Similarly, CEADS aims to open its solution to all agrifood actors wherein the policy provides tailored incentives for each actor categories. The proposed CEADS organization will ensure the compliance and handling of complaints, conduct regulatory investigations, and impose sanctions for violators.
records.abstract: Building blocks and roadmap scenarios for secured data sharing

_annotations.Impact: AgriDataSpace is expected to increase economic, environmental, and societal value of the agrifood sector while maintaining high standards of privacy, security, and ethics.

records.title: Hail Protection System Locator SWG 1.01
records.description: The Hail Protection System Locator SWG 1.01 is a stationary shock wave generator designed to protect agricultural land from hail damage. It covers approximately 120 hectares per unit and is remotely managed via a centralized cloud-based interface. The system integrates IoT sensors and GIS mapping, allowing real-time monitoring and control of multiple stations simultaneously.

records.title: iAgro
records.description: iAgro is a mobile app developed by Agrobit that transforms smartphone into a 3D scanner for precision farming. The solution leverages AI, augemented reality, computer vision, 3D modeling and cloud computing. The app takes biometric and biophysical data of tree crops, and exports reports, maps and history of vegetation health and status. Additionally, iAgro can facilitate a complete 3D scan on the target plant to get its 3D model acting as a digital twin. Through this process, the app captures biometric parameters such as thickness, height, and canopy volume, and vigor parameters like leaf area index, and tree row volume. iAgro also provides users with recommendations on optimal doses of agrochemical application and water.
records.abstract: 3D scanner mobile app for precision agriculture

_annotations.Impact: The app aims to reduce the use of chemical inputs and water up to 50 percent to lower the environmental impacts on air, aquifers, soil, and on rural communities, promote sustainable agricultural practices, and improve resource management, among others.

records.title: Crop Calendar
records.description: Crop Calendar is a free web-based application that provides information on planting, sowing, and harvesting periods for over 100 crops in different countries and agroecological zones. The initiative serves as a living platform where validated data from national authorities is continuously updated to support agricultural planning. Users can view crop-specific details such as planting and harvesting periods, crop cycles, and optimal sowing windows based on agroecological zones. The tool addresses timing and knowledge gaps using a structured GIS-based system.

_annotations.Impact: Crop Calendar helps smallholder farmers and advisors reduce crop losses by improving the timing of planting and harvesting for over 100 crop in more than 80 countries. In Europe and Central Asia, localized crop calendars help optimize productivity and strengthen resilience to climate variability.

records.title: The Robot who wants to be a pollinator
records.description: The project employs participatory action through a rural performance entitled, "The robot who wants to be a pollinator." The narrative of the rural performance centres on a robot who is on a mission to monitor biodiversity in farms. To fulfill the robot's mission, the project leverages robotics through built-in computer vision and machine learning capable of capturing videos and images of pollinating insects. The initiative addresses the issue on pollinator's decline as one of the most threatening problems concerning biodiversity loss. Apart from the development and testing of the robot on field, the project also explored theater presentation where the robot sits at the centre of the performance, reflecting how its adoration for flowers brought it closer to pollinators. The project was developed within the European Commission project STING (Science and Technology for PollinatING insects), a collaboration between the Directorate-General for Environment and the Joint Research Centre.
records.abstract: Rural performance using robots to monitor pollinators

_annotations.Impact: Rural performance acted as a material deliberation method to address the issue of pollinators decline. Based on the project, the initiative actively engaged social actors, beyond scientists and experts, into (re)framing the challenges in pollinator population collapse. Moreover, the initiative elicited the expression of local and embodied knowledge on pollinators and biodiversity, brought into the discussion subjective values of nature of farmers and citizens, and fostered the initial ideation of local collaborative initiatives to address pollination decline in their territory.

records.title: Tractor.uz
records.description: The Tractor.uz website facilitated the purchase of agricultural machinery and equipment in Uzbekistan. The website featured a catalogue with information on each product, and served as a one-stop-shop where farmers could browse, select and purchase a wide range of farming equipment, such as tractors, disc harrows, potato diggers, etc. The website offered information about the products, and while it did not facilitate purchase transactions, it featured a contact form and telephone helpline for those seeking help in how to make a purchase.

records.title: Soplidan.ge
records.description: Soplidan.ge was a food-commerce website and mobile application that facilitated the sale of rural products directly by producers in Georgia. Products could be paid for electronically and delivered within the country and abroad. The company behind the e-commerce also offered a consultancy service to farmers on various topics, and contained digital farmers’ stories and a producers’ call request feature, while offering also messenger e-commerce integration.

records.title: Marneuli
records.description: Maradisi and Dioknisi, villages of Georgia (collectively called Marneuli villages), are home to a vibrant community of farmers whose primary activities are greenhouse vegetable production and open-field crop production. These villages are home to a close-knit, forward-thinking community, with women playing a pivotal role in agricultural cooperatives, farms, small businesses, and local self-help groups. Digital connectivity is a cornerstone of life in Maradisi and Dioknisi. With stable 4G internet coverage and widespread ownership of smartphones and computers, residents actively use platforms like WhatsApp and Facebook to exchange information and market their produce. However, the villages face increasing challenges from climate-related issues, including droughts, harsh winters, and floods. To address these, Maradisi and Dioknisi were chosen as the first pilot sites for FAO’s Digital Villages Initiative (DVI) in Georgia. Under this initiative, several digital interventions have been introduced to improve farming practices, tackle agricultural challenges, and enhance productivity.
records.abstract: Pilot village under the FAO Digital Villages Initiative (DVI)
records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

_annotations.Source: Information provided by a member of the organization

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The digital technologies such as the agrometeorological weather station and IoT enabled greenhouse monitoring system, TelAgri advisory services, Farm Management System introduced by DVI in Marneuli villages are anticipated to enhance farming practices by providing data-driven recommendations, improving farming efficiency, and helping farmers adapt to agricultural challenges. Through introduction of digital pest traps to the digidal demo farm of the Agricultural University of Georgia, the project aimed to support the overall digital agriculture ecosystem in Georgia.

records.title: Mokro
records.description: Situated in the hilly region of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Mokro, with its altitudes ranging from 700 to 1,000 meters above sea level, is a community whose main economic activities are agriculture, forestry, and wood processing, with a focus on livestock farming and, more recently, greenhouse vegetable production. Since the COVID-19 pandemic, there has been an increased interest and demand for land and rural living in Mokro, indicating opportunities for the development of agriculture and rural tourism. Under the “Digital Villages in Action” (TCP/RER/3905) project”, digital scales, greenhouse monitoring and control systems, and a marketing website are implemented to support local farmers.

records.title: Development of an e-commerce platform (D2C) for small and medium-sized farmers and returned migrants agri-entrepreneurs
records.description: "Development of an e-commerce platform (D2C) for small and medium-sized farmers and returned migrants agri-entrepreneurs” is a feasibility study examining the potential of an e-commerce platform tailored to small and medium-sized farmers and returned migrant agri-entrepreneurs in the Republic of Moldova. The study provides an overview of online commerce among agricultural producers in the country and specifies the steps to be taken for the future development of the platform.  It was prepared based on data garnered from national and international reports and online resources, as well as primary information obtained from 29 in-depth interviews, complemented by four group discussions involving over 30 producers, financial institutions, online platform administrators, information technology specialists, state institution representatives and other stakeholders. The study explores two possible future scenarios for the e-commerce platform: Scenario 1) Recreating the platform from scratch; and Scenario 2) Developing the existing platform (online store/marketplace). The report draws upon the findings of a multicriteria study to describe a series of interventions leading to the creation of a functional, long lasting and sustainable tool. Possible technical functionalities are proposed and prioritized in three categories as 1) absolutely necessary; 2) recommended; and 3) prospective.
records.abstract: Feasibility study and roadmap recommendations
records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: This feasibility study paves the way for the development of an effective and long-lasting e-commerce platform for Moldova, identifying opportunities, optimal scenarios and the necessary interventions required for the launch of an e-commerce platform that connects producers and consumers. The resource envisages the creation of an ecosystem that allows the free entry and exit of any operator who can bring benefit to their areas of competence. In short, the resource aims to increase the economy of a region that is at risk of falling behind in the agricultural sector if it fails to address systemic problems and to encourage innovations targeting the formation of a competitive and efficient environment in which the risks of bottlenecks are minimized.

records.title: National e-Agriculture Strategy
records.description: Under the "Support to the development of national e-agriculture strategy" project provided through FAO’s Technical Cooperation Programme (TCP/TUR/3703/C2), FAO supported the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry (MAF) of Türkiye in developing a National E-Agriculture Strategy. The Strategy provides several strategic recommendations: 1) Enhance communication and coordination among critical stakeholders to facilitate cross-sector collaboration; 2) Strengthen policy, legislative, and regulatory frameworks requirements to build sustainable and scalable ICT applications; 3) Identify and develop key databases, their linkages, access, and interoperability to enable building of actionable information services; 4) Improve market access, risk mitigation, disaster management, and logistics to enhance income generation and profitability; 5) Identify and improve processes and mechanisms using ICT solutions and services to enhance the effectiveness of agricultural stakeholders; 6) Develop capacity at all levels to sustain and benefit from e-agriculture solutions and services; 7) Strengthen the capacity of human resources in line with the e-agriculture concept; 8) Give priority to digital systems in agricultural supports.

records.title: National programme of action for the digitalization of agriculture and rural areas
records.description: Under the "Preparing the grounds for digital transformation of agriculture" project provided through FAO’s Technical Cooperation Programme (TCP/UZB/3808), FAO supported the Ministry of Agriculture of Uzbekistanin developing National programme of action for the digitalization of agriculture and rural areas. The national digital agriculture programme of action outlines four strategic pillars to align with Uzbekistan's agricultural priorities: (1) developing an enabling environment by improving ICT infrastructure, rural connectivity, and regulatory frameworks; (2) transforming government operations through eGovernment systems and enhanced agricultural data management; (3) promoting knowledge, skills, and innovation via digitalized advisory services, education, and research; and (4) fostering market growth by expanding access to tailored digital services and driving rural innovation.

records.title: Brežani and Tršće
records.description: The Brežani-Tršće rural community is situated in the picturesque basins of two rivers, Zgošća and Trstionica. The key agricultural assets include greenhouse vegetable cultivation, on-farm dairy operations with milk processing, and cattle husbandry, in which a cow-calf system is employed. Brežani-Tršće’s robust cultural-historical legacy, well-developed infrastructure, and promising entrepreneurial and tourism opportunities offer significant potential. Rich in such natural resources as fertile land and pristine water sources, as well as cultural and historical landmarks, Brežani-Tršće is uniquely positioned for the championing of sustainable agricultural practices and for capitalizing on the developing agritourism market. Under the “Digital Villages Initiative in Action” (TCP/RER/3905) FAO project, digital scales, greenhouse monitoring and control systems, and a marketing website are implemented to support local farmers.

records.title: Roadmap for the digitalization of agriculture
records.description: Under the "Provision of Technical Assistance on E-agriculture to the Ministry of Agriculture" project provided through FAO’s Technical Cooperation Programme TCP/TAJ/3810/C8, FAO supported the Ministry of Agriculture of the Republic of Tajikistan in developing a roadmap for the digitalization of the agriculture sector. The national roadmap for the development of digital agriculture in Tajikistan proposes to focus on four overarching strategic outcomes – or pillars – to achieve the vision and the agricultural priorities for the country: Pillar 1: To develop the foundations for digital agriculture (“Foundations”). Pillar 2: To harness data and building e-government systems for agriculture (“E-government and data”). Pillar 3: To advance agricultural knowledge, skills and innovation (“Knowledge, skills and innovation”). Pillar 4: To grow a market ecosystem for digital agriculture (“Market Ecosystem”).

records.title: E-agriculture strategy (2022-2027)
records.description: Under the "Building the grounds of e-agriculture" project provided through FAO’s Technical Cooperation Programme (TCP/BIH/3704/C4), FAO supported the Ministry of Agriculture, Water Management and Forestry in Bosnia and Herzegovina in developing an E-agriculture strategy. The strategy lays out five strategic priorities: 1) P1 - Accelerating digital transformation of agriculture in the public sector; 2) P2 - Practical use of ICT solutions at farm level; 3) P3 - Development of institutional and individual capacities on digital agriculture; 4) P4 - Improving digital infrastructure in rural areas; 5) P5 - Raising awareness on the benefits of implementing ICT solutions in agriculture.

records.title: Aghali
records.description: Under its State Program of Socio-Economic Development, Azerbaijan is actively promoting the concept of smart villages with a first pilot in Aghali village. This village relies on small-scale household farming, with residents growing crops like watermelon, tomatoes, and various fruits, while facing challenges such as a lack of diversification, underdeveloped farming infrastructure, and the ongoing presence of landmines that hinder larger agricultural projects. In addition to the State Program, Aghali is supported by FAO through the “Digital Villages in Action” (TCP/RER/3905) project and World Bank under the “Azerbaijan Smart Villages Program: Inclusive and Innovative Approaches to Rural and Local Development ASA”.

records.title: Boyalı
records.description: Boyali village, located in the Güdül district of Ankara province is renowned for its Angora goat breeding, known also as Mohair goats, which are considered a cultural heritage due to their historical, geographical, agricultural and commercial significance. Livestock breeding constitutes a major economic activity in Boyali, where the approximately 25 000 animals, and the favourable altitude and climate all contribute to the production of high-quality mohair. Under the “Digital Villages Initiative in Action” (TCP/RER/3905) FAO project, the integrated digital goat farming system is integrated to enhance this heritage by combining precision technology, real-time data, and digital tools to optimize livestock management, improve productivity, and ensure sustainable farming practices.
records.abstract: Pilot village under the FAO Digital Villages Initiative (DVI)

_annotations.Source: Information provided by a member of the organization
_annotations.Impact: The integrated system is expected to improve livestock health, reduce losses, and improve overall farm productivity, directly supporting farmers in Boyali. By providing real-time data and expert advisory services, its goal is to empower farmers to make informed decisions, ensuring sustainable and efficient farming practices. Inclusion in the Hep Yerinden platform has the aim to expand market access for the local women’s cooperative, boosting their income and promoting the economic empowerment of women in the community.

records.title: GrainSense
records.description: GrainSense is a handheld and flow-based grain analyzer that uses near-infrared spectroscopy to provide instant measurements of protein, moisture, oil, and carbohydrate content from small samples or flowing grain. Data is timestamped with GPS, stored in the cloud, and visualized via mobile and web dashboards, supporting real-time decision-making for farmers, grain handlers, and processors.
records.abstract: Handheld grain analyzer

_annotations.Impact: GrainSense aims to improve decision-making during harvest and storage, optimizes grain quality management, reduces waste, and increases profitability. According to the solution’s website, over 276 000 measurements have been taken globally across 48 countries.

records.title: Wisecrop
records.description: Wisecrop is an agricultural operating system for farmers, cooperatives, advisors and institutions. It integrates modules for crop monitoring, irrigation and fertilization scheduling, pest and disease alerts, operational planning, and activity tracking from planting to harvest. The platform centralizes farm records, supports compliance and reporting, and enables better coordination of labor and resources, addressing challenges of input efficiency, documentation burden and decision-making under uncertainty.
records.abstract: Farm management decision-support system

_annotations.Impact: The solution aims to improve farm efficiency, reduce input costs, and enhance sustainability by providing data-driven recommendations and operational visibility. The platform can support traceability and compliance digitization across multiple farms. According to Wisecrop website as of July 2025, users have achieved savings of over 240 EUR per hectare in irrigation costs, a 20 percent reduction in phytosanitary treatments, and significant time savings in logbook management, reducing the process from months to hours.

It performs precision tasks such as seeding, weeding, spraying and soil preparation with minimal supervision, helping address labour shortages and improve operational efficiency. The robot is compatible with standard farm implements and can power attached equipment, allowing it to support a wide range of crop management applications.

records.title: TMS Treescout
records.description: TMS TreeScout is an AI-supported tractor‑mounted sensor-based system that scans individual trees in an orchard to generate tailored prescription maps, empowering fruit growers to reduce inputs, increase yields, and optimize precision orchard management. With each pass the solution assesses bloom density, vigor, and tree variability, then prescription maps guide users to make precision fertilization, pruning, thinning or spraying actions tailored to each tree. It addresses labor shortages, input inefficiencies, and yield variability, enhancing precision tree-level management.
records.abstract: Tractor-mounted sensor for precision orchard management

_annotations.Impact: The solution aims to improve orchard productivity, sustainability, and profitability by enabling per-tree management based on real-time sensor data. By providing precise prescription maps for fertilization, pruning, thinning, and spraying, it can support more efficient input use, reduce agrochemical application, and enhance canopy uniformity. As per July 2025, the company reported that trials in European orchards have shown up to 90% reduction in agrochemical use and EUR 3,100–3,500 per hectare increase in crop value.

records.title: BluLeaf
records.description: BluLeaf is a modular, cloud-based precision agriculture platform that integrates data from sensors, weather stations and satellite imagery to optimize farm operations as irrigation scheduling, fertilization planning and crop monitoring, helping farmers and advisors improve resource efficiency, reduce input use and enhance sustainability in agricultural production. It integrates multiple components: 1) BluLeaf DSS, a decision support for irrigation, nutrition, and crop protection, 2) BluLeaf QMS, a quality management tools for ensuring compliance of products and industrial processes, 3) BluLeaf LAB , a software for laboratory analysis instruments, 4) BluLeaf IoT, a rental and maintenance of professional agricultural sensors and 5)BluLeaf FMIS, a farm management information system for large-scale data integration.
records.abstract: Decision Support System (DSS)

_annotations.Impact: BluLeaf aims to improve water and nutrient use efficiency, reduce nitrate leaching, and support climate-resilient farming through data-driven decision-making. As per a publication published in 2019, the benefits from field trials include water savings of around 25 percent. The modular design could allow farms and organizations to adopt only the components relevant to their needs. A potential barrier could be digital adoption in low-tech user groups, addressed via advisory and cooperative-led support.

records.title: Digitalizing Russia’s Agricultural Sector: Challenges and Solutions
records.description: The  publication titled “Digitalizing Russia’s Agricultural Sector: Challenges and Solutions” by Yakov & Partners offers an analysis on the status of the digital transformation of Russia’s agricultural sector, and provides proposals to enhance the sector’s productivity and resilience through policy and technological solutions. Firstly, the report presents the increasing trend of production and exports in the country where digitalization serves as the tool to maintain such growth. Secondly, the document then enumerates objectives that the Ministry of Agriculture should deliver such as an end-to-end information management system, transition to Agriculture 4.0, improved productivity, and lower production costs. Key highlights within the publication are the tailored Digitalization Index that aims to conduct benchmarking for Russia in comparison to other countries such as the USA, Brazil, Germany, and France, among others. Then, the publication proposes measures to ramp up agricultural digitalization through the creation of a platform for processing and storing data that would guide decision-making, establishment of a single anonymous agricultural databank, and the need to shift the focus of the digitalization programs to provide better support to small and medium-sized enterprises. Lastly, from the results of the digitalization assessment, the report outlines two possible development scenarios where potentials results position the level of digitalization having no impact on Russia’s digitalization level or surpassing countries such as France in terms of digital maturity.

_annotations.Impact: Digital agriculture solutions highlighted in the report can facilitate access to state support programs for small and medium-sized farmers, and in return, the government can receive transparent data on the industry and sector.

records.title: AgriLAND
records.description: AgriLAND was a database designed to facilitate lease mediation and foster greater communication among participants of land market, connect the owners of unutilized land with active local farmers and facilitate the transfer of land rights in Armenia. The system contained three main business processes or workflows: incorporating parcel(s), requesting parcel(s), and placing an open request for parcel(s)/area(s). AgriLAND was developed as part of the FAO technical assistance project “Establishment of land management instruments and institutional framework to address land abandonment” (TCP/ARM/3705), which supported the development and operationalization of new regulatory framework and introduction of a set of land management instruments to address the abandonment of agricultural land and improvement of farm structures in Armenia.

records.title: E-Agro
records.description: E-Agro, or the Electronic Agricultural Information System (EAIS), was a state-run government portal in Azerbaijan. The information system was developed as a single database of farmers and the resources they use.  A unified geographic information system was incorporated into the app, supporting the collection of data on administrative-territorial boundaries, as well as on areas of crop-specific production, greenhouse areas, enterprises and facilities under the Ministry, and details of lands, land-use changes, salinized areas and new areas assigned for cultivation, among other relevant information. The system could also set up real-time monitoring mechanisms to ensure the proper implementation and development of agricultural processes, including those based on satellite data. Additionally, farmers could apply for subsidies and insurance through the system, and request relevant documents. Limited advisory services could also be provided through the app, addressing topics such as seed varieties and the COVID-19 pandemic.

records.title: GreenAral
records.description: GreenAral was a web-based app and mobile application that provided vital information for those doing business in the agriculture and environmental sectors in the Aral Sea region. It supported day-to-day operations through the provision of learning resources, advisory materials, networking and insightful ideas. The content was tailored for the Republic of Karakalpakstan. The advisory materials were provided in the form of articles, videos and other media, and supplied information about sustainable agricultural technologies and practices created by consultants listed on the website. Additionally, a map-enabled database listed agribusiness-related enterprises along with their contact details. The Agri-market page displayed prices for at least 50 major agricultural products, and was updated weekly based on a review of all major wholesale markets in all 14 districts and in Nukus city.

records.title: Automated Information System of State Land Cadastre in Kazakhstan
records.description: The Automated Information System of the State Land Cadastre was a web-based portal based on GIS technologies that was developed to automate the collection and provision of cadastre data for individuals and enterprises, and to automate the provision of cadastre-related government services. The system was developed with the goal of optimizing the training and certification of cadastral service specialists, and offerred information on government services related to land ownership, rights documentation and the respective service fees. The portal could be used to access various interactive maps, such as those charting geobotanical and soil characteristics, sowing conditions and security zones, as well as a general cadastral map.

records.description: SroPasture was an early warning system designed for pasture users, providing crucial meteorological information and pasture-related data to help mitigate the impacts of hazardous weather conditions and adapt to changing climate patterns. records.title: RegioCart
records.description: RegioCart (short for “regional shopping cart”) was an online marketplace designed to support regional agri-food markets in Germany by facilitating direct digital sales between producers and consumers. The platform enabled transactions related to sales, delivery scheduling, invoicing, accounting, and payments. It was tailored for local agri-food producers—including farmers, butchers, beekeepers, winemakers, and bakers—and featured intuitive tools for sellers to manage product listings, delivery windows, and order deadlines. The platform complied with Regulation (EU) 1169/2011 on food information and included automatic invoice generation and integrated accounting.

records.title: Blue Marble
records.description: Blue Marble’s Parametric Climate Protection Solution is a financial risk management tool designed to mitigate the adverse effects of climate-related disasters on agricultural production. The solution provides predefined payouts triggered by specific weather events such as droughts or floods, eliminating the need for on-site damage assessments. This model reduces transaction costs, ensures timely payments, and increases financial resilience among smallholder farmers.
records.abstract: Climate-triggered insurance for farmers

_annotations.Country of origin: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
_annotations.Impact: The initiative has provided insurance coverage to thousands of farming households. records.description: Agrility is a decision-support tool that identifies field zones with potential yield potential, monitors crop development, and provides daily update of the yield estimate through latest weather data. The tool provides assistance from sowing to harvest through spatial information. Agrility has a dedicated team of experts that work on big data, geostatistics, agronomics, modelling, and IT-related systems to enhance precision farming. Agrility supports the growing of maize, oil seed rape, wheat, barley, fodder grass, and sunflower.

The FieldBee Navigation App provides tools for creating and managing field boundaries, planning navigation lines and recording field operations — accessible on smartphones, tablets, or dedicated FieldBee tablets.
records.abstract: GPS-based tractor guidance and autosteering system

_annotations.Impact: The overall aim of FieldBee is to make precision farming technologies affordable and accessible to farmers worldwide. According to company information, FieldBee operates in more than 60 countries and serves over 6 000 customers. As per the company’s website, its users have reported reducing input and labour costs by 10–15 percent and achieving return on investment within one farming season, even on medium farm areas of 10–15 hectares.

records.title: Irrigated Agricultural Development Project in Ararat and Armavir (IADAAM)
records.description: The IADAAM project provides support to the Government of Armenia in shaping policies aimed at the modernization of irrigated agriculture. It offers substantial assistance at the local level, particularly to farmers and stakeholders involved in designing, promoting, and financing pilot initiatives in the Ararat and Armavir marzes. The project also focuses on climate change adaptation, aiming to enhance the resilience of agricultural production against extreme weather events such as droughts, heavy rainfall, and hail. Aligned with the UN Sustainable Development Goals, IADAAM emphasizes the inclusion of women, young farmers, and youth through active engagement in project activities and access to grants. Key components of the initiative include technical assistance to the Ministry of Economy of the Republic of Armenia, development of operational frameworks for investment grants, and support in communication and project management. Looking ahead, the project intends to promote the adoption of smart agriculture technologies and strengthen capacity within the farming community.
records.abstract: Enhancing productivity and sustainability of irrigated agriculture in the Ararat and Armavir regions

_annotations.Impact: The project is expected to improve water use efficiency, increase crop yields and quality, and enhance farmers’ access to expert advice and market opportunities. By fostering the adoption of digital and smart agriculture practices, IADAAM aims to build resilience, support sustainable resource management, and strengthen the overall competitiveness of Armenia’s agricultural sector.

records.title: Orwaco
records.description: Orwaco’s online e-commerce platform provides access to biohumus (vermicompost) produced through the recycling of organic waste using red Californian worms. This material serves as the foundation for a range of organic fertilizers intended to support soil improvement, enhance productivity, and contribute to plant growth and development. In addition to product offerings, the website features agricultural advisory services delivered by a certified agronomist. These services include terrain assessment, consulting on specific agricultural challenges, and comprehensive agronomic support throughout crop vegetation cycles. The platform also covers the establishment and maintenance of vegetable gardens, greenhouses, fields, and orchards; greenhouse crop management; participation in farm planning; and the development of crop growth strategies, including plant nutrition systems and fertilization plans. Further services involve regular monitoring for diseases and pests, implementation of control measures, guidance on chemical and biological pest control methods, crop management consulting, and support for seedling care and fertilization. Detailed reporting is also part of the advisory offering.

_annotations.Impact: Orwaco provides farmers with access to organic fertilizers and agricultural advisory services. Through its platform, users can obtain certified biofertilizers suitable for organic farming, along with expert guidance on crop management, soil improvement, and pest control.

records.description: Beesync is a smart solution for beekeepers, which provides smart hives with carefully designed sensors that listen to the heartbeat of the colony: weight, temperature, humidity, sound, and bee activity. records.title: InFARM
records.description: InFARM is an online system developed by FAO to assist countries in aggregating and analysing antimicrobial resistance (AMR) data from animals and food. The app facilitates the structured reporting of AMR surveillance at a national level and supports the sharing of this information for global monitoring. The collected data are securely stored, and can be updated and managed by authorized national entities, ensuring the integrity and confidentiality of the information. InFARM also allows for the controlled public dissemination of AMR data, aligning with international efforts to address AMR challenges. A key feature of InFARM is its commitment to data privacy, offering separate access points for private and public data sharing to accommodate varying levels of data sensitivity. Data is collected through a framework that can be viewed by all countries in the form of a manual containing the following headings: Reporting Cycle, Scale of Activities and Level of Representativeness of AMR Data; Step in the Food Chain; Sample Sources/Surveillance Sites; Surveillance Purpose; Surveillance Programmes; Samples; and Microorganisms.
records.abstract: International FAO antimicrobial resistance monitoring system
records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

_annotations.Impact: This IT app will potentially contribute to a global antimicrobial resistance monitoring app through collaboration with other international organizations. InFARM could potentially lead to improved national and global responses to antimicrobial resistance. Its capacity to streamline data could enhance the effectiveness of AMR management strategies in the food and agriculture sectors, potentially slowing the spread of resistance and contributing to better public health outcomes. The future plans for InFARM (as outlined in the roadmap presented during “The InFARM System and Current Perspectives on AMR Surveillance in Food and Agriculture” webinar, hosted as part of the World AMR Awareness Week [WAAW]) include a global rollout with increasing data integration capabilities, the publication of comprehensive global reports on AMR and the facilitation of annual data calls. The expansion phase aims to integrate InFARM with other data apps, thereby broadening its utility and reach. By 2026, the consolidation phase is expected to be completed, establishing InFARM as a central AMR and AMU surveillance data hub, supporting ongoing capacity building and ensuring that the system remains at the forefront of global health initiatives.

records.title: Online Gardening Platform in Kyrgyzstan (Cадоводство в Кыргызстане)
records.description: Gardening in Kyrgyzstan is an online platform that consolidates international and local knowledge related to gardening in Kyrgyzstan. It offers information in the form of educational and reading material or interactive databases for Kyrgyz farmers. The platform includes technological guides for cultivating fruits and berries, which detail the costs associated with purchasing seedlings, plant protection products guidance, equipment for drip irrigation systems guidance. It also provides educational video materials on agrotechnology for fruit and berry cultivation and plant protection. The platform has information on normative legal acts, the State Register of Plant Varieties and Hybrids, a list of recommended varieties by region, and the concept of cluster policy for agrarian development in Kyrgyzstan. Additionally, it offers databases for agricultural enterprises, such as licensed nurseries, gardeners, processing and logistic enterprises, and suppliers. Furthermore, the platform allows farmers to monitor two agrometeorological stations, one in the Kadamzhai district of the Batken region, and the second in the Nookat district of the Osh region. records.title: AgriAcademy
records.description: AgriAcademy is a freely accessible digital education app designed for agribusinesses in Ukraine. Launched by the EBRD in December 2022, its primary goal is to enhance access to knowledge and technology for small- and medium-sized agricultural enterprises, addressing the shortage of professional skills in agribusiness. The app is offering 18 specialized courses as of November 2023, covering a wide range of topics, from crop production and water management to livestock management and the use of drones. These online courses are designed based on Master’s degree programmes at leading agricultural universities, and have been adapted to suit the specific needs of Ukrainian agribusinesses. Upon the successful completion of their training, the participants receive a certificate. The app also features webinars, blog posts and consultations, further supporting the learning experience.

records.title: Drought Early Warning System
records.description: The Advanced Drought Early Warning System – a joint initiative of Uzhydromet and the UNDP in Uzbekistan – is designed to bolster the climate resilience of Karakalpakstan's drought-affected farming communities by providing early warnings of the possibility of low water and drought in the region. The system allows for the forecasting of available water resources in the current year in the upper reaches of the mountain rivers of Uzbekistan, located in the zone of natural flow formation, as well as in the lower reaches of the Amu Darya River – a zone known for its intensive water use for various purposes, primarily for the irrigation of agricultural lands. Predictions of future water levels in the lower reaches of the Amu Darya River are carried out for different periods – in January, February and March.
records.abstract: Advanced system for drought prediction and water resource management

_annotations.Impact: The system aims to significantly improve the drought preparedness and climate resilience of the farming communities in Karakalpakstan. It supports better water use planning in agriculture, contributing to sustainable water management and a reduced vulnerability to climate-induced water scarcity.

records.title: VR-tour
records.description: The Fruit Producers and Exporters Association of Moldova provides prospective buyers with the opportunity to pay virtual visits to selected fruit producers and exporters in Moldova through the use of 3D panorama imaging technologies and videos. The tours allow the viewing of the entire horticultural infrastructures of more than 20 member producers and exporters, from production to post-harvest handling. Buyers interested in Moldovan fruit and grapes can take a virtual tour of orchards, vineyards and post-harvest facilities, and see the modern cold storage facilities and other available sorting, grading and packaging equipment in use.
records.abstract: Virtual tours for fruit producers and exporters
records.owner_name: Fruit Producers and Exporters Association Moldova Fruct

_annotations.Source: FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices
_annotations.Impact: The virtual tours, by providing buyers with a means of visiting local producers and exporters, allow fruit producers to overcome geographical barriers, thus facilitating trade and sales. Under the COVID-19-related restrictions in particular, the tours helped producers overcome the lack of international exhibitions and trade fairs and the limited opportunities to travel. Such virtual tours allow producers to reach a much wider audience, and to optimise their promotional costs alongside traditional marketing activities, with a potentially much more significant impact.

records.title: Smart Sut
records.description: SMART SUT is an online knowledge portal operated by the Diary Union of Kazakhstan that provides farmers, processing industry, consumers and sales entities with information related to product quality, markets, regulatory changes, recent research, relevant news, etc. The Diary Union’s expert group includes international-level professionals with many years of experience. records.title: Too Good To Go
records.description: The aim of Too Good To Go is to save food that’s “Too Good To Go”, being a smartphone application that connects customers to restaurants and stores with unsold food surplus. The app serves as a marketplace connecting businesses with surplus foods with consumers looking to rescue their meals. Rather than discarding surplus foods at the end of the day, the producers foods can sell them off a reduced retail price (typically one-third of the original price) and collected by consumers from the store at a pre-set time (often 30 minutes before closing). The consumer can download the app freely and browse the available offers in their area via an integrated map, make their selection and pay for the goods through the app. To collect the meal, the customer simply presents the in-app order confirmation voucher to the store or restaurant.
records.abstract: Mobile app that saves unsold food from going to waste

_annotations.Impact: The value to the consumer comes from their access to high-quality restaurant food sold at up to a 70 percent discount. The company claims that more than 139 million meals have been sold through the app to date, contributing to the reduction of CO2 production. The app also provides an opportunity to users to discover restaurants, bakeries, hotels and grocery stores that they would not otherwise make purchases from. The value of the app to suppliers comes from the sale for surplus food that would otherwise go to waste, although at a reduced price, contributing to revenues. Furthermore, partnering with TGTG boosts the corporate social responsibility image of companies.

records.title: Rapid Alert System for Food and Feed
records.description: The Rapid Alert System for Food and Feed (RASFF) is an e-notification and communication system for food quality control used by EU member states to prevent harm to European consumers and consumers of products originating in the EU. The system ensures the communication of risks to public health associated with food or feed with the EU members and non-member states directly through the online open RASFF notification portal “RASFF Window”. Members of the RASFF network use the system to notify other members of any serious risk to public health linked to food or feed, whether direct or indirect, allowing potentially harmful products to be traced and taken off the market. The system thus facilitates the flow of information among member states and food importers, provides a round-the-clock monitoring service, and ensures the efficient and urgent notification of food safety risks.
records.abstract: E-notification and communication system for food quality control of the European Union

SDGs.value: SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

_annotations.Impact: The EU maintains some of the highest food safety standards in the world, thanks largely to the solid EU legislation in place. RASFF is pivotal in ensuring the flow of information, allowing swift action when public health risks are detected in the food chain. According to information of the Commission’s portal, many food safety risks have been averted before they could harm European consumers, thanks to RASFF.

records.title: Precision agriculture in seedling production
records.description: Dritan Sula is a vegetable seedlings producer in Gorican in the Berat district of central rural Albania who launched a small-scale agribusiness in 1994, and who, for the first 9 years, used primarily traditional technologies to produce seedlings, carrying out most processes by hand. In 2003, he decided to invest in his business, increasing the growing area of his greenhouse to 3000 m2 and installing a system for the automatic control of temperature and humidity. After noticing a lack of uniformity in the quality of his seedlings associated with the imprecise manual operations, especially during irrigation, spraying and plant feeding, he made further investments in 2016 to introduce precision agriculture to his business, setting up automated and remote control for spraying and irrigation operations.
records.abstract: Dritan Sula’s vegetable seedlings farm

_annotations.Impact: Prior to his investments in precision agriculture, the internal temperature of the greenhouses was checked by thermometer and regulated manually using a diesel -powered central heating system, and staff would simply open the windows to increase ventilation. Watering and pesticide applications were also done by hand. With the introduction of innovative technologies, the owner significantly reduced his manpower needs, and improved the production and quality of seedlings, achieving significant efficiencies. Most of the remaining staff are women, whose working conditions have been improved with the introduction the new technologies. Their duties are now less onerous and their contact with chemicals, fertilizers and pesticides has been vastly reduced. The investments have been validated by the market in terms of increased sales resulting from the improvements in quality, and by other farmers who have introduced precision agriculture technologies to their own operations after witnessing the successful results achieved by Sula.

records.title: Plant-O-Meter
records.description: Plant-O-Meter is a multispectral precision agriculture device that enables the assessment of the physiological condition of plants. Plant-O-Meter analyzes and evaluates the health of the plant in terms of photosynthesis process, as well as fertilization and irrigation needs. The system features also the Plant-O-Meter™, a mobile app downloadable via Google Play. The app is a free companion software to the Plant-O-Meter™ sensor devices, with the main functionality to gather data from the sensor device(s), synchronize data acquisition sessions and forward CSV data files for further processing.
records.abstract: Multispectral device for on-the-spot assessment of plant physiological conditions

_annotations.Source: ["Desktop research","Information provided by a member of the organization"]
_annotations.Impact: Plant-O-Meter generates maps of available optical vegetation indices, which is valuable data when creating fertilization prescription maps, predicting yield and determining chlorophyll levels in plants, while also highlighting changes in vegetation, among other uses. Bitgear applies the principles of the circular economy by focusing on a modular design, repairability and the intensification of the use of the sensor, making the production of the device more sustainable.

records.title: OneSoil Scouting
records.description: OneSoil Scouting is a mobile application developed by OneSoil to help farmers remotely monitor crops, increase yields, and reduce seed and fertilizer costs. The app functionality facilitates the automatic identification of field boundaries using AI and satellite imagery, the tracking of field vegetation using the NDVI index and identifying problem areas, the detection of productivity zones over several years, provides weather forecast to identify the optimum time for spraying, and facilitates the creation and download of prescription maps for phosphorus, potassium and nitrogen applications. For advanced and more experienced users, the app offers data visualization from agricultural equipment and variable-rate application of seeds and fertilizers in their web app. The OneSoil web app is interoperable with various brands of agricultural equipment.
records.abstract: Free farming app for precision agriculture

_annotations.Source: FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices
_annotations.Impact: A representative of the organization states that OneSoil users receive an average of 136 000 push notifications containing new NDVI images per month. By 2020, OneSoil had defined field boundaries in 57 countries. The app can support farmers in time management and planning, and helps them see how their crops are growing and how the fields are performing, thus identifying which areas require interventions. The app can aid in crop disease outbreaks by highlighting changes in the vegetation index, allowing farmers address the issue in a timely manner. The weekly scouting facilitated by the app can bring savings to farmers in both time and money, allowing them to monitor their fields remotely and thus avoid unnecessary field visits. The app also contributes to sustainability by supporting the more efficient use of land, water, fuel, fertilizer and pesticides.

records.title: OLIO
records.description: OLIO is a peer-2-peer mobile app that connects users addressing the problems of food and material waste in their home & local community by facilitating exchanges and trade at a community level. Users take a photo of any spare food, clothes or furniture in their possession and upload it to the app; their neighbours then receive customized alerts letting them know something new has been added. They can then request what they want and arrange a pick up time via private messaging within the app. The handover of the food takes place on the doorstep or in a public location, generally on the same day. There are options to give, sell or lend items in different sections of the app. If they want to sell the item, there is a secure payment portal within the app.
records.abstract: Mobile app for peer-2-peer sharing of food and second-hand items

_annotations.Source: ["Desktop research","FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices"]
_annotations.Country of origin: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
_annotations.Impact: Launched in 2016 in the United Kingdom, OLIO now has over 3 million members. According to the website, users have together saved 11 million food portions –equivalent to taking 33 million car miles off the road. Half of all the food added to the app is requested within 30 minutes. Although OLIO was first launched in the United Kingdom, most of its activity is outside the country, where food has been shared successfully in 54 countries to date. OLIO’s growth both within the UK and beyond has been powered by the over 60 000 people who have reached out to offer to help spread the word about OLIO (Ambassadors), and by the 10 000 trained volunteers (Food Waste Heroes) who collect and redistribute unsold food from local businesses such as Tesco, Pret a Manger and Compass Catering. OLIO started out as a food waste elimination app, but has now moved on to include recyclables and items with second-hand value, such as furniture, clothes and household items.

records.title: INSYLO
records.description: INSYLO is a decision-making tool for farmers and feed suppliers based on a smart volumetric IoT sensor and software application, and is used to measure the content of silos, facilitating the remote management of stocks and optimizing the production and distribution cycles of animal feed. INSYLO allows users to monitor the content of their silos via their smartphones and to be alerted when stocks are low. The app provides accurate and updated information about the current state of the silos in real time, including the level and weight of content, and the available volume, temperature and humidity inside the silo. The silos are monitored continuously, and all data are stored on the Cloud for future reference. This decision-making tool can give farmers and feed suppliers high-value insights into their daily operations, aiding in the selection of the optimum time to replenish the stocks in each silo, thus minimizing logistics costs.
records.abstract: Smart solution to measure silo content

_annotations.Source: FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices
_annotations.Impact: INSYLO facilitates the management of stock levels in silos via a smartphone, and provides notifications when stocks are low, eliminating the need for manual inspections. INSYLO thus facilitates the remote management of stocks in the silos of livestock farms, and the optimisation of the animal feed production and distribution cycles. INSYLO also assists food suppliers by automatically sharing stock information with their customers and in the processing of restocking orders. According to the company's website, INSYLO can provide savings of up to EUR 500 per silo per year in labour and transport costs, while eliminating the risks associated with silo inspections and contributing to the environment by reducing CO2 transport emissions by up to 25 percent. The key benefit of INSYLO is its ability to optimize logistics and production by providing previously unknown demand variables in the form of accurate live data and predictive forecasting. Furthermore, the zero-maintenance sensors reduce the risk of associated workplace accidents, improving the quality of life of farmers, and allowing them to focus on their core activities.

_raw.Description: INSYLO is a decision-making tool for farmers and feed suppliers based on a smart volumetric IoT sensor and software application, and is used to measure the content of silos, facilitating the remote management of stocks and optimizing the production and distribution cycles of animal feed. INSYLO allows users to monitor the content of their silos via their smartphones and to be alerted when stocks are low. The app provides accurate and updated information about the current state of the silos in real time, including the level and weight of content, and the available volume, temperature and humidity inside the silo. The silos are monitored continuously, and all data are stored on the Cloud for future reference. This decision-making tool can give farmers and feed suppliers high-value insights into their daily operations, aiding in the selection of the optimum time to replenish the stocks in each silo, thus minimizing logistics costs.
_raw.Impact: INSYLO facilitates the management of stock levels in silos via a smartphone, and provides notifications when stocks are low, eliminating the need for manual inspections. INSYLO thus facilitates the remote management of stocks in the silos of livestock farms, and the optimisation of the animal feed production and distribution cycles. INSYLO also assists food suppliers by automatically sharing stock information with their customers and in the processing of restocking orders. According to the company's website, INSYLO can provide savings of up to EUR 500 per silo per year in labour and transport costs, while eliminating the risks associated with silo inspections and contributing to the environment by reducing CO2 transport emissions by up to 25 percent. The key benefit of INSYLO is its ability to optimize logistics and production by providing previously unknown demand variables in the form of accurate live data and predictive forecasting. Furthermore, the zero-maintenance sensors reduce the risk of associated workplace accidents, improving the quality of life of farmers, and allowing them to focus on their core activities.

records.title: Ferraria de São João
records.description: Ferraria de São João is a Smart Village located in the District of Coimbra under the Municipality of Penela in the Central region of Portugal. Ferraria de São João adopted a “smart village” approach under the European Commission's Smart Rural project to address the specific challenges faced by the village, such as depopulation and ageing, the weak local economy, and the consequences and impacts of the forest fire of June 2017 that devastated the surroundings of the village. The village has adopted three smart solutions: the creation of a Village Protection Zone, the promotion of the FarmReal digital app, and the development of agritourism.

records.title: HofladenBOX
records.description: The HofladenBOX marketplace allows customers to buy directly from various regional suppliers, reducing the involvement of intermediaries, and bringing customers who want to buy regional products together with small-scale suppliers. HofladenBOX handles the digital platform  and all the stages in the food supply chain, from handling to logistics and marketing. Around 60 farmers carpool do deliver their orders twice a week to the HofladenBOX team, which packs the ordered products in boxes and delivers them to the customer. For many farmers, HofladenBOX has become an important distribution channel, allowing jobs to be maintained in regional agriculture. The system contributes to reductions in CO2 by reducing transport, and packaging materials are also reduced.
records.abstract: E-marketplace that connects food customers with farmers in Fürth Smart Village

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The project has multiple impacts. The end-users (customers) benefit from the access provided to regional, fresh food produced by small producers, thus improving their nutrition, decreasing the costs of transport and reducing their carbon footprint. At the other end of the chain, farmers and regional producers benefit from a fairer market and the ability to set their own prices, while gaining access to a broader market, as well as intermediary-free marketing and logistics operations. This is foreseen to have a positive impact on the sustainability of producers. Environmentally speaking, the project contributes to the reduction of CO2 through the short transportation routes associated with regionally produced products.

records.title: Hands Free Farm
records.description: The world’s first fully automated farm project, being carried out in the United Kingdom, makes use of precision farming to address the challenges associated with stagnant yields and soil compaction. Most farms make use of large and heavy conventional machines in their operations, which compress the soil and make it less productive. This pilot project investigated the automation of farming processes and the implementation of precision agricultural practices, such as drilling wheat into cover crops, and improving the accuracy and field coverage of machinery. Ultimately, the project aims to increase yields and reduce input costs through the better application of products and more efficient vehicle use.

records.title: FAO Food Price Monitoring and Analysis (FPMA) Tool
records.description: The FAO Food Price Monitoring and Analysis (FPMA) Tool is a web-based app linked to existing national data collection systems that allows national and international stakeholders to easily monitor, analyse and disseminate price information on a wide range of agricultural commodities on the markets around the globe with daily or monthly frequency. FPMA facilitates the easy visualization of time series data and aids basic price analyses and reporting. FPMA also provides early warnings of high food prices at a country level that may negatively affect food security. As of January 2023, FPMA features over 1300 domestic and international food price series (i.e. commodity prices in markets across countries) and analytics. The tool was developed in 2010 under an FAO initiative to monitor the soaring food prices.  FPMA also has country-level versions that contain a broader selection of commodities and markets than available in the global tool. National FPMA tools have been implemented in Tajikistan and Guatemala, and works are continuing in Zimbabwe and Uzbekistan.

SDGs.value: SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

_annotations.Impact: FPMA allows easy access to the large amounts of data stored in its database and sourced from national stakeholders. Price intelligence can empower agricultural stakeholders in making educated pricing decisions for their activities and businesses.

records.title: Farm management software and autonomous machinery to increase efficiency in organic farming
records.description: Suzana Dimitrievska is an organic farmer in North Macedonia who has increased the efficiency of her family farm through the adoption of farm management software and autonomous machinery. In 2017, growth in demand led the farmer to carry out a cost-benefit analysis comparing the benefits of manual work versus using an automatic sorter. She found an optical colour sorter machine on the market that was able to identify and sort over 123 different types of crops, herbs and agricultural products by size, colour and form. In the same year, extraordinarily high temperatures heavily affected the farms’ production (apricot, watermelon, beans, chickpeas and sunflower). The farmer decided to invest in precision agriculture (making use of such ICTs as soil mapping and aerial imagery), which provided her with vital information about how and when to irrigate her crops for maximum efficiency.

_annotations.Impact: The software supports the farmer in the planning and monitoring of her crops, while also minimizing labour costs and reducing the outlay on gas and organic fertilizer, thereby increasing profits. The farm management software allows Dimitrievska to make more informed greater decisions, and she has seen her investment pay off. She can run her farm more efficiently using the software to keep records, track costs, manage seasonal workers and analyse the profitability of each of her crops. After using the software for 1 year, Dimitrievska realised that some of the crops she had been cultivating for years were not economical, leading her to look into more profitable options. The autonomous machinery has improved efficiency at a farm level, especially in packaging tasks, while the use of precision agriculture solutions has reduced losses of crops and mitigates the effects of climate change.

records.title: Farmer Web Portal
records.description: The Farmer Web Portal in Bosnia and Herzegovina is a web-based application that is operated by the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management that allows individual and commercial farmers to identify any incentives to which they are entitled, to download the related application forms, to apply online and to monitor the status of their submitted applications. Similarly, municipal, cantonal and federal institutions and inspection agencies can supervise the spending of funds through the app. The Farmer Web Portal seeks to support farmers in taking advantage of the financial incentives available to them, to improve their agricultural production and, overall, to contribute to rural development. The app also serves as a source of such information as rules and regulations.
records.abstract: Portal for farmers to track and apply for government subsidies
records.owner_name: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management of Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina

SDGs.value: SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

_annotations.Impact: The Farmer Web Portal supports the dissemination of agricultural subsidies, making the process more efficient for the Ministry of Agriculture by reducing human errors and automating the entire process. The portal also increases awareness of farmers of their rights to subsidies, and provides them with the ability to apply for subsidies remotely. The portal also provides easier access for farmers to forms and data, thereby easing bureaucratic procedures and decreasing the “idling” time of farmers. The Farmer Web Portal unifies the subsidy payment procedures, and ensures transparency and accountability among agricultural stakeholders.

records.title: DoctorP
records.description: DoctorP is a mobile application that helps farmers and other users identify diseases in plants from photographs and provides treatment recommendations. The app currently supports the identification of multiple diseases in decorative houseplants and the following 12 crops: apples, barberry, cherry, cotton, wheat, corn, hemp, cucumber, grapes, tomato, strawberry and pepper. The app can also identify common diseases that are not limited to a specific crop.
records.abstract: Mobile application for the detection of disease in plants and treatment recommendations

_annotations.Impact: DoctorP is an agricultural application with the ability to identify crop diseases in the early stages of production, allowing farmers to take necessary measures to prevent the spread of disease and protect their yield. User activity from 1 May 2022 to 30 September 2022 led to successful predictions in the following crops: apples (550), barberry (185), cherry (390), cotton (105), wheat (85), corn (250), hemp (80), cucumber (290), currants (195), grape (145), tomato (680), strawberry (350), pepper (50) and blueberry (110). The application and its machine learning algorithms are undergoing continuous improvement, and plans are in place to introduce a customized model for potato, barley, cabbage, raspberry, blackberry and salad in 2023.
