records.title: Beekeeper’s Companion App
records.description: The Beekeeper's Companion is a mobile application developed by HiveTracks to provide both experienced and new beekeepers with an innovative means of managing their beekeeping operations. The app facilitates the tracking of hive histories, including the health and productivity of the bees, provides immediate and long-term weather forecasts, guides the user through the hive inspection process, etc. Combining these multiple functions in one app supports the user in making informed decisions throughout the season and year in beekeeping practice.

records.title: AgroRadar
records.description: AgroRadar by AgroInsider is an app that integrates, aggregates and analyses Copernicus Earth Observation radar (SAR) data and sampling data from the field that it then uses to develop value-added information that can help farmers and other users improve their yields, and monitor the condition of their land plots, forests and water bodies, etc. AgroRadar can detect anomalies in the soil, water and plants on agriculture plots, and then produce and develop smart sampling strategies and yield forecasts, calculate the spatial structure of any observed region, calculate different spectral bio-diversity indices, detect changes in land occupations and record events in the field, among other tasks. Subscribers can access the results of AgroRadar’s monitoring and inspections of the spatial and temporal dynamics of farmers' lands, as well as the constantly produced analytics. The app makes predictions and alerts farmers of any anomalies in soil, water or plants.
records.abstract: Tool for the detection of soil, water, and plant anomalies by means of remote sensors

_annotations.Source: FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices
_annotations.Impact: AgroRadar can support decision-making and provide tailor-made reports for farmers and stakeholders. It supports the application of smart soil nutrition practices for all types of crops, thus helping to reduce operational risks, to optimize the use of inputs and soil-plant-water processes, to reduce waste and pollution, and to maximize outputs. Additionally, AgroRadar can provide farmers and other users with real-time alerts on associated land, water and forest risks.

records.title: Bee King app
records.description: BeeKing is a web and mobile phone application that has been developed to aid beekeepers in the management of their hives and the challenges they encounter through manual reporting. Sticky fingers and gloves make the manual recording of apiaries and hives or the handling of digital tools hard for beekeepers. The app allows inspection data or notes to be entered vocally or using NFC sensors and beekeepers, and to control the app in hands-free mode. The app also features a community app for the sharing of experiences, connecting beekeepers with their peers, and thus addressing the lack of access to assistance and a collective information database, allowing beekeepers to benefit from the knowledge and experience of others.
records.abstract: Mobile app for beekeepers in Teili Smart Village

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The BeeKing app aims to ease the administration and management of beekeeping activities. Beekeepers can use the mobile app to keep comprehensive records of their apiaries and hives, to monitor bee health and the amount of collected honey and pollen, and to trace the reasons for closing colonies. The collected data aids in the making of more evidence-based decisions, while also allowing exchanges of information, knowledge and good practices with other beekeepers.

records.title: Agroistok
records.description: Agroistok is a system of agrometeorological stations in the East and South-East Planning Regions (i.e. administrative units) of North Macedonia that provides agrometeorological advisory services to farmers, including weather information and forecasts, and notifications of possible plant pest and disease outbreaks via a mobile application (Meteobot) and website. The forecasts cover air temperature, relative humidity, rainfall, atmospheric pressure, wind speed and direction, cloud cover, fog (i.e. visibility), dew point and likelihood of storms.
records.abstract: System of agrometeorological stations in the East and South-East Planning Regions of Macedonia
records.owner_name: Centers for Regional Development under the Ministry of Local Self-government

_annotations.Source: Information provided by a member of the organization
_annotations.Impact: The freely available weather information helps farmers better organize such agricultural activities as irrigation or harvesting in the field. The humidity and temperature indicators support farmers in deciding on the right time to harvest, and ensuring that the seeds contain the right percentage of water. records.title: Agro Space
records.description: Agro Space website was developed jointly by AgroInformAsia, Kyrgyzstan and AgroInform.TJ in Tajikistan as a hub for the hosting of various digital products developed for farmers. Among the accessible products are several applications providing information on crop production, cattle breeding, beekeeping, pest and disease management; solutions providing access to virtual marketplaces and retail market prices in Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan; and other tools that are accessible both online and offline. The website also hosts a library containing more than 600 online materials, an agricultural map, a news portal, agro-calculators and other products. There is also a link to a YouTube channel where users can access educational and informational videos. The AgroSpace website is supported by a Telegram Bot that provides guides to the operation of the digital tools and that allows access to some of the services provided by the bot itself (e.g. weather forecasts, market prices, etc.) or redirects users to other websites. The website Agro Space won second prize in the International “Eurasian Digital websites 2019” competition organized by the Eurasian Economic Commission.

records.title: SMS agroline
records.description: The SMS-based “Agro-consulting and Ads” by AgroInformAsia is a communication and advertisement tool implemented in Tajikistan that targets farmers in rural areas. The tool provides such information as weather forecasts and market prices, advice on the use of fertilizers, information about diseases and pests, as well as advice on crop input use, post-harvest handling, etc. The tool also serves as an early warning system, sending out SMS alerts in cases of frost, heavy rain, high temperatures, floods, storm warnings, unforeseen weather events, disease and pest outbreaks, etc. SMS-based agro-consulting and ads AgroInformAsia is part of the Agro Space website developed jointly by the AgroInformAsia company in Kyrgyzstan and AgroInform.TJ in Tajikistan as a hub for the hosting of various digital products developed for farmers. The initial version of the system was launched in 2010 by the Neksigol Group under the technical guidance of the UNDP as part of the “Aid for Trade” project, and HELVETAS under the "Local Market Development" project, and Neksigol took full control of the tool in 2016.

records.title: Plant Protection mobile app and online platform by AgroInformAsia
records.description: The Plant Protection mobile app is a digital tool that provide farmers in Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan with expert-verified information about protecting their plants from pests, diseases and weeds. The tool provides information about the different plant protection products available in their countries, including biologics, and the correct and safe use of products against pests, diseases and weeds on cultivated crops. The app forms part of the Agro Space app – a web-based app developed jointly by Neksigol Group and AgroInformAsia that hosts various digital products developed for farmers.
records.abstract: App providing farmers with information of pests, diseases and weeds

_annotations.Source: Information provided by a member of the organization

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: By improving farmers' access to expert-verified instructions, this tool can prevent the excessive and unnecessary use of chemicals, thus reducing the impact of agricultural activities on the environment, while also helping farmers to reduce their plant protection costs. records.title: zypl.score
records.description: zypl.score is an AI-based credit scoring software developed by zypl.ai that enables financial institutions to automate their decision-making processes related to micro-loans. It reduces the average time taken for a micro-loan decision to 10 minutes.
records.abstract: AI-based credit scoring software

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: zypl.score allows financial institutions to automatically review loan applications with high accuracy and speed using machine learning algorithms. Banks and microfinance organizations are thus able to provide more loans with a lower percentage of delinquencies. zypl.score increases the speed at which microloans can be underwritten, accurately predicts the creditworthiness of potential lenders and reduces the rates of non-performing microloans. zypl.ai has built on the experience gained in the Tajik market to successfully deploy their scoring algorithms in the markets of Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.

records.title: Maps AgroInformAsia
records.description: Maps AgroInformAsia is an online geographic information system containing electronic agricultural maps of Kyrgyzstan, Russia and Tajikistan that aims to support effective decision-making related to investments, as well production, harvest and processing planning. The electronic maps provide information about the production of over 50 types of agricultural products at a district level, including sown areas, crop yields, soil fertility indicators, field boundaries, processing company locations, storage facilities, greenhouses and agrostores, as well as border transit points and communication routes for exports and imports. Maps AgroInformAsia is part of the Agro Space suite developed jointly by the AgroInformAsia company in Kyrgyzstan and AgroInform.TJ in Tajikistan as a hub for the hosting of various digital products developed for farmers. The tool was developed in 2014 by a Neksigol and AgroInformAsia consortium, with technical guidance provided by the UNDP under the “Aid for Trade in Central Asia” project.
records.abstract: Electronic agricultural maps

_annotations.Source: Information provided by a member of the organization

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Maps AgroInformAsia can help fill gaps in the necessary data for analyses of agricultural economics, land degradation, food security, research farming systems, nutrient residues and the impact of climate change. The maps convert large quantities of primary data into an accessible, convenient and interactive format, thus providing users with digestible information that they can use to make informed decisions related to the production, supply, sale and export of a particular product. The system also facilitates regional trade by providing information on the location of border transit points and communication routes for exports and imports, as well as other resources. Maps AgroInformAsia won the parent app (Agro Space) second place in the international “Eurasian digital apps 2019” competition, organized by the Eurasian Economic Commission.

records.title: Cattle and Forage crops mobile apps by AgroInformAsia
records.description: The Cattle and Forage Crops Mobile Apps are a suite of complementary applications for farmers and veterinarians that guide them through cattle care, breeding processes and the cultivation of fodder crops. The Cattle app provides farmers with information about feed and feeding, stables suitable for keeping and breeding livestock, diseases, and veterinary services and pharmacies in Kyrgyzstan. Users can also reach veterinarians and other professionals via the app, while veterinarians can use the app to store captioned photos of cattle. The Forage Crops app provides information about seeds, soil quality and fertility, nutrient management, existing diseases and pests in the region, different approaches to pest and disease control, weed management, including biological control, and environmentally friendly farming, as well as a wealth of other information related to forage crops. Both apps feature lists of local agri-input suppliers, veterinary services and pharmacies. The Cattle and Forage Crops Mobile Apps are part of the Agro Space  platform, a web-based platform developed jointly by Neksigol Group and AgroInformAsia for the hosting of various digital products developed for farmers.

records.title: Echki Sutu farm goat management
records.description: This good practice is based on the integration of such basic digital technologies as Excel sheets and Instant Messaging Platforms for the small-scale management of dairy goat breeding, milk production and processing, and sales operations of farms. All goats on the farm are tagged, and each goat is listed with an individual dossier in an Excel file. The dossier provides details of the pedigree of the animal, including date of birth and slaughter, the identity of the parents and grandparents, productivity levels, when the goats were bought or sold, etc., facilitating the prediction of what can be expected from a new-born that can then be compared with the actual output. The farmer can use the data to calculate how much feed is consumed by a single goat and how much milk they produce. The production and sale of dairy products are also recorded daily in Excel. Products are promoted and sold through Instagram and WhatsApp.
records.abstract: Managing and supporting market access for goat products

_annotations.Source: ["Desktop research","Information provided by a member of the organization","FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices"]
_annotations.Impact: Echki Sutu farm received support from USAID Kyrgyz Republic for the procurement of modern pasteurization equipment and a cheese press, increasing production volume and extending the shelf life of dairy products. The combination of these technologies with investments has expanded the production capacity of the dairy farm and has led to an increase in sales to Globus, a local supermarket chain.

records.title: NMA agro
records.description: NMA agro is a mobile app that helps farmers in Lithuania submit reports not only to the National Paying Agency (NPA), but also to the State Veterinary and State Plant Protection bodies about their commitments to public subsidies and legislation, including their cultivation of specific crops, their implemented investment projects, their livestock management, or the problems they encounter in the fulfilment of commitments. It also helps Paying Agencies and other related institutions to carry out compliance checks from the office. Compliance checks are carried out based on multiple data sources, including field photographs, satellite data and vegetation index layers. Any Lithuanian citizen can freely access the annually declared parcels and crops in Lithuania and can report any unattended areas, overgrown trees and shrubs, uncultivated land, environmental irregularities, etc. The NMA agro app provides users with access to news (articles), an Information Portal (to check the status of submitted applications, the amounts of support paid, information about the checks performed, notifications of activities performed sent by the mobile application), a calendar (listing main obligation deadlines, work) and the "Line of Trust" (reports of possible abuses by those receiving or applying for European Union support for agricultural projects, rural development and fisheries). The app also provides weather forecasts for all parts of the country, which is particularly important when planning agricultural work. The "Observe the fields" link opens the main window of the app in the form of a map, from which a form can be accessed to send messages about activities or problems encountered in the fulfilment of obligations. The list of activities is divided into activity types and subtypes, allowing the farmer to find the correct section, reducing the likelihood of inaccurate messages.
records.abstract: Government mobile app for land management and monitoring
records.owner_name: National Paying Agency under the Ministry of Agriculture of the Republic of Lithuania

_annotations.Source: ["Desktop research","Information provided by a member of the organization","FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices"]

SDGs.value: SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

_annotations.Impact: At the 2021 Regional Forum of the International Telecommunications Union (ITU), NMA agro was hailed as one of the four best examples of digital craftsmanship in the "Legal Regulation / Better Market Access / Financial Services and Insurance" category. According to the NMA website, by using the "NMA agro" app, farmers can not only monitor their fields, but also streamline their mandatory reporting to the public authorities, and check the compliance of their activities and investments with the EU and national legislation in the field of agriculture, food safety and the environment. One of the main advantages of this system is the reduction in the number of field visits required for audits and compliance checks. In the 2 years since the activation of the app, over 1500 reports of Sosnovsky's borscht, unattended fields and abandoned land have been submitted. The importance of the mobile application was particularly noted during the COVID-19 pandemic and the associated quarantine periods, when most checks were conducted remotely.

records.title: Single window
records.description: Single Window, supporting the registration of export-import and transit operations in Tajikistan, is an information and communication web-based app designed to speed up and simplify the exchange of information, documents and data related to export-import and transit operations in Tajikistan between the related bodies and those involved in foreign economic activity. Single Window seeks to eliminate the duplication of documents and the repeated appeals of entrepreneurs to authorized departments for access to public services. The system allows exporters and importers to submit the standard documents required by government agencies in one place on a single form, and to one agency. The main functions of the Single Window system include the registration of subjects of foreign economic activity; the receipt of relevant documents from users of the system for subsequent transfer to the relevant bodies for the issuance of trade permits; the transmission of documents, data and messages between the bodies and subjects involved in foreign economic activity; the management of laboratory expertise; the provision of statistical information and reports to the government and other interested registered parties; the provision of normative, legal and other documents in the field of foreign economic activity; and the receipt of payments for the services of the relevant bodies. The State Unitary Enterprise “Single Window Centre” is responsible for technical support and the technical operation of the system, working in close cooperation with the following government agencies: Agency of Standardization, Metrology, Certification and Trade Inspection; Committee of Food Security; Communication Service under the Government of the Republic of Tajikistan; the State Supervision Service for the Fields of Healthcare and Social Protection of the Population under the Ministry of Health and Social Protection of the Population of the Republic of Tajikistan; and the State Assay Supervision under the Ministry of Finance.

records.title: MAPEST e-marketplace
records.description: MAPEST is an e-commerce information portal for the dissemination of the market prices of dried fruits. The portal was launched by the International Association of Producers and Exporters of Agricultural Products of Tajikistan with the goal of uniting the Republic’s processing enterprises and farmers. The e-commerce promotes the interaction of all actors in the dried fruit supply chain, including farmers, processors, exporters and distributors, and also serves as a source of information on agrotechnology and agronomy, covering such topics as apricot types, ploughing and the available processing technologies. Furthermore, tractor services for production  are offered on the platorm, and laboratory services for processing and food quality assurance activities.
records.abstract: E-commerce and market prices information portal for dried fruits
records.owner_name: International Association of Producers and Exporters of Agricultural Products of Tajikistan

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: MAPEST facilitates easy access to the market prices of dried fruit, berries and nuts, making it easier for processors and farmers in Tajikistan to keep up to date with the products they want to buy or sell. The portal supports the maintenance of a competitive market, and ensures farmers get a fair price for their produce. The e-commerce also contributes to production by providing information on dried fruit cultivation and facilitating access to tractor equipment. Furthermore, farmers can make use of the MAPEST laboratory to ensure better quality dried fruit and to avoid quality and supply chain issues, thus contributing to more nutritious and higher quality dried fruits on the market. The e-commerce seeks to unite processing enterprises and farmers in the Republic of Tajikistan by forming a connection between all those involved in the dried fruit supply chain, allowing them to identify and capitalize on the provided opportunities to promote their products and services.

records.title: Mobile apps for Crop production
records.description: Mobile Apps AgroInformAsia is a set of mobile applications devoted to crop production and health, available for blackcurrant, onion, vines, greenhouse vegetables, cabbage, tomato, cucumber, corn and sugar beet. The apps provide information on varieties of seeds, soil quality and fertility, nutrient management, existing diseases, pests in the region, and approaches to pest and disease control and weed management, with particular focus on environmentally friendly farming. The apps also provide the users with lists of agri-input suppliers, traders and processors with their contact information. The apps can also be used to access weather forecasts and retail market prices in Tajikistan and Kyrgyzstan. Mobile Apps AgroInformAsia are a part of Agro Space platform, a web-based platform developed jointly by the Neksigol Group and AgroInformAsia as a hub for the hosting of various digital products developed for farmers.

The apps also provide retail market prices in Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan, as well as the contact details of agri-input suppliers and buyers of agricultural products, supporting the improvement of post-harvest management. Finally, the apps also list product purchasers, facilitating the strengthening of the connections between actors in the agricultural value chain, and providing more marketing opportunities.

records.title: CowManager
records.description: CowManager is an ear sensor technology for dairy farmers that provides accurate information about cow fertility, health, nutritional status and location, based on the animals’ ear temperature, activity, rumination, eating and resting habits. CowManager makes use of sensors, a router, software and a mobile app to log information about heat intensity and heat stage, thus maximizing heat detection. CowManager also sends alerts whenever a cow is not eating or ruminating, allowing early interventions, and thus minimizing the use of antibiotics and reducing milk drops. The tool may also be used to monitor the recovery of sick cows, substandard cow behaviour and ear temperatures. CowManager also provides insights into cow nutrition and well-being at a group level.

_annotations.Impact: CowManager supports herders in working efficiently and proactively, resulting in improved cow health and a more productive herd. It significantly reduces feed, labour and medical costs, leading to maximized profitability.

records.title: WFP Vulnerability Analysis and Mapping (VAM)
records.description: The World Food Programme Vulnerability Analysis and Mapping (VAM) information and analytical tool supports stakeholders in the conducting of geospatial and economic analyses, crop and food security monitoring and assessments, post-shock assessments and thematic analyses, among others. The primary goal of VAM is to provide timely, accurate and relevant information in support of World Food Programme (WFP) operations, and details of the food insecurity and vulnerability faced by the hungry poor. 100 percent of WFP project documents are based on VAM analyses. VAM also provides more easily digestible data visualizations online at dataviz.vam@wfp.org.
records.abstract: Tool for food security monitoring and analyses

_annotations.Impact: VAM serves as a source of credible, relevant and timely food security analyses, providing evidence supporting the design of WFP operations, as well as those of other humanitarian bodies. Assessing the degree of food security in specific geographic areas can help in the determination of priority areas for assessment and response. The tools also reveal the probable causes of food insecurity and vulnerability, thus aiding in the determination of affected populations, while identifying whether food assistance will improve their status. Ultimately, the tool facilitates the dispersal of food aid.

records.title: Digital Field Automation tool by FINCA
records.description: The Digital Field Automation (DFA) tool by FINCA allows accounts to be opened and loan application processes to be conducted in the field, making it easier for rural residents to gain access to financing. Using the DFA, accessible via a tablet, allows financial institutions to conduct loan application processes in the field – whether in the customer’s home or at their place of work.
records.abstract: Tool for conducting the loan application processes in the field

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The DFA makes use of a hybrid model for the delivery of financial banking services to farmers. It allows access to customers in remote and hard-to-reach regions of the country for whom visiting a branch can take time and effort. The ability to apply for loans in the field reduces the number of times rural customers have to visit a branch office. The impact of the tool was evaluated in Tanzania, where the Bank reached over 20 000 new customers and disbursed over 40 loans exceeding TZS 135 million (over USD 57 000) within 2 months of the launch of operations.

records.title: Central Asia Climate Information Platform
records.description: The Central Asia Climate Information app (CACIP) is a web-based app that helps stakeholders in Central Asia to access, analyse and visualize public-domain climate and climate-related data, thus supporting improved awareness, assessment and decision support operations. The information app garners appropriate data and information from global, regional, and local sources for Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan and Turkmenistan, and is incorporated with analytical tools and interfaces to aid their visualization and interpretation. The app hosts data on climate change, soil, land degradation and local weather, as well as such indicators as greenhouse gas emissions, soil moisture, soil carbon density, temperature, precipitation, historical climate statistics, weather forecasts and vegetation indices. CACIP was developed under the World Bank-funded "Climate Adaptation and Mitigation Program for Aral Sea Basin" (CAMP4ASB) initiative, led by the Regional Environmental Centre for Central Asia (CAREC), working in collaboration with the International Center for Agricultural Research in the Dry Areas (ICARDA) and its partners. As of December 2022, the WB project is ongoing, and CAREC is continuing to improve the website. A consortium of government agencies, international organizations and local NGOs established the CACIP Consortium to facilitate the provision of data and information (publications, reports, learning courses, etc.) to CACIP on a regular basis, to promote CACIP at global, regional and local levels, and to support resource mobilization and the creation of new partnerships.

records.owner_name: Regional Environmental Center for Central Asia

SDGs.value: SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

_annotations.Impact: The app facilitates in-country, regional and international collaboration and information sharing, providing visibility to original data sources that are interoperable with other databases, repositories, websites and systems. CACIP allows the Central Asian countries to access, analyse and visualize climate change-related data, and to use them for awareness-raising, assessment and decision-making operations.

records.title: Tajikistan Trade Portal
records.description: The Tajikistan Trade Portal is an information website run by the Ministry of Economic Development and Trade of Tajikistan. The website guides local and foreign entrepreneurs through the import, export and transit procedures of the country, thus facilitating more transparent and efficient trade. The user-friendly portal displays all the necessary documents and forms (i.e. licenses, permits, certificates, etc.) that businesses must submit or collect from the relevant regulatory authorities, and provides detailed information on the applicable fees and payments. The portal also provides analytical and statistical information on markets and producers. All information is certified and regularly updated by Tajikistan’s Coordination Committee on Trade Facilitation (CCTF), and the website can be embedded into the websites of other authorities to ensure consistency of information. The portal was developed with the support of the United Nations Development Program (UNDP) and the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE), and with technical assistance from the International Trade Centre (ITC) and the United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD).
records.abstract: Information portal to ease trade procedures
records.owner_name: Ministry of Economic Development and Trade of the Republic of Tajikistan

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth
SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

_annotations.Impact: The Tajikistan Trade Portal facilitates trade, thereby supporting the economic development of Tajikistan. The portal simplifies the trade process and makes procedures more transparent, and provides entrepreneurs, producers and farmers with the opportunity to export their products internationally. The extended reach of the market thus increases demand and product access. On the other hand, by simplifying the import procedures, farmers and producers gain greater access to input materials. Furthermore, the transparency assured by the portal, aids government institutions in becoming more robust, while farmers gain equal access to information, easing their engagement in trade. Lastly, the website facilitates the analysis of trade data and statistics, thus supporting economic planning and policy development.

records.title: Trade AgroInformAsia
records.description: Trade AgroInformAsia is an electronic free agriculture trade portal featuring 14 types of agricultural products and inputs for sale and purchase, supporting trade among the neighbouring nations of Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, China and the Russian Federation. The 14 products are agricultural machinery, containers and packaging, beekeeping, cereals and legumes, dried fruit, fruit, vegetables, livestock, poultry, plant protection products, fertilizers, processed products and seeds. Trade AgroInformAsia provides contact information for product providers. The system was developed in 2016 by the Neksigol and AgroInformAsia consortium under the technical guidance of the UNDP as part of the “Aid for Trade in Central Asia” project. Trade AgroInformAsia is part of the Agro Space e-commerce – a web-based e-commerce developed jointly by the AgroInformAsia company in Kyrgyzstan and AgroInform.TJ in Tajikistan as a hub for the hosting of various digital products developed for farmers.

records.title: Registered Exporter System
records.description: The Registered Exporter system (the REX system) is a system for the certification of the origin of goods, and operates an a self-certification principle. Operators themselves declare the origin of their goods with so-called “statements of origin”, which is a declaration of origin stated by the registered exporter on invoices, delivery notes, packing lists, or any other commercial document that identifies the goods and the exporter. The text used for statements of origin are provided in Annex 22-07 of Regulation (EU) 2015/2447. REX is implemented under the Generalized System of Preferences (GSP), through which the European Union grants certain preferential tariffs.
records.abstract: System for the registration and certification of goods and trade exporters operating outside the EU

SDGs.value: SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

_annotations.Impact: REX Registered Exporters can take advantage of the Generalized System of Preferences of the European Union, can shift from paper-based certificates of origin to electronic forms, and, once registered in the system, can obtain the exporter identification numbers required for the export of goods. On the other hand, economic operators can use statements of origin to verify the validity of the exporters' registrations.

records.title: Price Monitoring and Analysis System
records.description: The Price Monitoring and Analysis System is a web-based/mobile application that provides the user with access to prices of agricultural products and inputs in Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan. Retail prices are collected weekly by agents in 15 cities and districts in Tajikistan from the markets in Dushanbe, Hisor, Isfara, Ishkoshim, Jayhun, Khorugh, Khujand, Kulyab, Kurgantube, Kushoniyon, Murghob, Panjakent, Qubodiyon, Bokhtar, Gissar, Jayhun, Istaravshan, Khorog and Rasht. The prices of input supplies, on the other hand, are calculated for each month based on information provided by input suppliers, i.e. agro-shops. The portal also features a list of companies from where customers can purchase the inputs. The system contains a database of over 100 items with their current prices, including food commodities, agricultural products, inputs and non-food items (such as fuel, unskilled and skilled wage labour rates, etc.). In Kyrgyzstan, price data is available for 60 agricultural products in five cities, as provided monthly by the National Statistics Committee. The prices are also published in the monthly AgroInfrom.Tj newspaper, and can be communicated via SMS by signing up for another Neksigol product – SMS agroline. The tool was launched in 2010 by the Neksigol Group with the technical guidance of UNDP as part of the “Aid for Trade” project, and with HELVETAS under the “Local Market Development” project. Neksigol assumed full control of the project in 2016. Price Monitoring and Analysis System is part of the Agro Space website developed jointly by the AgroInformAsia company in Kyrgyzstan and AgroInform.TJ in Tajikistan as a hub for the hosting of various digital products developed for farmers.

records.title: LDN DSS
records.description: The Regional Land Degradation Neutrality Decision Support System (LDN DSS) is a web-based map-powered app developed by the FAO Regional Office for Europe and Central Asia that presents information on land degradation, land productivity, biodiversity, protected areas and topography, thereby helping identify intervention and improvement opportunities, and tracking progress and changes in selected elements.
records.abstract: Regional Land Degradation Neutrality Decision Support System in Europe and Central Asia
records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations, Regional Office for Europe and Central Asia

_annotations.Impact: The system facilitates the monitoring and evaluation of land degradation at different spatial scales, providing stakeholders with opportunities to optimize and adapt their land management efforts. It also allows the effective integration of different types and sources of information, supporting the preparation of reports for various purposes. Progressing towards land degradation neutrality can contribute to the achievement of multiple Sustainable Development Goals, including those related to climate change mitigation and adaptation, biodiversity conservation, food and water security, disaster risk reduction and poverty reduction.

records.title: Kitob e-library
records.description: Kitob AgroInformAsia is an online electronic agricultural library through which over 600 free educational, analytical, informational and other materials related to agriculture, rural life and the economies of Central Asia can be accessed. All materials are categorized under the following headings: Animals and livestock; Laws and regulations; Rural development issues; Educational video materials; Development organizations; Research and analyses; Marketing and Trade reports; Agricultural equipment and machinery; Natural resources; Plants and crops; Food and food products; Environmental protection; and Payment for services. Kitob AgroInformAsia is part of the Agro Space suite developed jointly by the AgroInformAsia company in Kyrgyzstan and AgroInform.TJ in Tajikistan as a hub for the hosting of various digital products developed for farmers.

records.title: Hosil.tj
records.description: HOSIL.TJ is an web-based online agricultural/farm input store and delivery service serving farmers in Tajikistan that offers seeds, plants and saplings, beekeeping accessories, organic fertilizers, mineral fertilizers, biological control agents, plant growth stimulants, plant protection chemicals and agricultural equipment, as well as services and other goods, at affordable prices. The primary function of the online store is the provision of certified, modern, high-quality, and environmentally friendly inputs supplies, although users can obtain support via the online chat or by calling the HOSIL.TJ call centre. Deliveries are priced based on the weight, region, mode of delivery and payment method. As an after-sales service, once the agri-inputs have been delivered to the customer, agronomists-consultants are on hand to advise how the agri-inputs should be used. HOSIL.TJ was developed under the United Nations Development Programme's InnoResponse Challenge II initiative. HOSIL.TJ is part of the Agro Space app – a web-based app developed jointly by the AgroInformAsia company in Kyrgyzstan and AgroInform.TJ in Tajikistan as a hub for the hosting of various digital products developed for farmers.
records.abstract: Agricultural store and delivery service of agri-inputs for farmers

_annotations.Source: Information provided by a member of the organization

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Hosil.TJ provides farmers with the agricultural supplies professional support they need. HOSIL.TJ facilitates the access of village farmers to agri-inputs, including those in remote locations, and so eliminates the need for farmers to go in person to district or provincial centres, and even other regions in the country, to purchase needed input supplies. HOSIL.TJ also assists reputable agricultural companies and interregional drivers in Tajikistan by increasing the number of customers for their products and services. Some 300 orders are placed through HOSIL.TJ every month on average.

records.title: GapSoft and HACCPSoft
records.description: Khujand Polytechnic Institute uses the GapSoft and HACCPSoft educational web applications to provide its students with practical demonstrations of the processes involved in the certification and auditing of food products in line with food safety standards. The study modules focus on food production standards at a farm level (Global G.A.P. – good agricultural practices) and food processing standards at a processing level (HACCP – hazard analysis critical control points). Students can use the educational web applications to view certified production processes in a virtual environment, in which all the production phases are tracked and production documents are recorded, while field visits can be carried out to check that the true situation corresponds to the declared one. Food safety certificates issued at the end of the production process certify that the food complies with safety standards. The web applications were developed under the "Higher Education for Central Asia Food Systems and Standards" project implemented by the Latvia University of Life Sciences and Technologies, in cooperation with Hilfswerk International. The project was funded by the European Union within the framework of the program "ERASMUS+" and serves the needs of small- and medium-sized enterprises in the education of highly qualified professionals who are familiar with international food safety systems and standards.
records.abstract: Food safety standards certification and food production auditing demonstration web applications for students
records.owner_name: Khujand Polytechnic Institute of Tajik Technical University

_annotations.Impact: The practical GapSoft and HACCPSoft tools upgrade existing higher education programmes and courses through the provision of content that responds to the needs of the modern labour market, and can create the preconditions required by companies to introduce quality systems to their operations that respond to the requirements of foreign markets, thus increasing the competitiveness of their enterprises.

records.title: EPP IS
records.description: The Electronic Public Procurement Information System (EPP IS) in Tajikistan allows electronic public procurement activities to be conducted in real-time. Through the system, government offices can request, order and purchase goods and services online from registered users. The e-procurement system hosts registries of vendors, procurement bodies, contracts and other documents, user instructions, a blacklist of unreliable suppliers, procurement announcements, reports, the results of contract executions, and more.
records.abstract: Electronic Public Procurement Information System
records.owner_name: Agency on Public Procurement of Goods, Works and Services under the Government of Tajikistan

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth
SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

_annotations.Impact: The e-procurement system was created to as part of a Strategy to Combat Corruption in the Republic of Tajikistan for the 2013–2020 period, launched upon a Decree by the President of the Republic of Tajikistan dated 30 August, 2013, No. 1504, and on the basis of a decision of the Government of the Republic of Tajikistan dated 29 December, 2012 No. 759 related to the creation of an Electronic Procurement Programme in the Republic of Tajikistan for 2013–2015. The Electronic Public Procurement Information System (EPP IS) was created to reduce costs, to ensure the effectiveness of public purchases, to provide transparency to public procurement procedures, to prevent corruption characteristics, to create favourable conditions for the free participation of suppliers and contractors in tenders while eliminating obstacles, to coordinate all stages of the state procurement management process, to reduce administrative burden by reducing the time and money spent on public procurements, and to simplify the procedures.

records.title: EastFruit
records.description: EastFruit is a web-based information and trade app that brings together the knowledge and experience of all participants in the fruit and vegetable market in Central Asia, the Caucasus and Eastern Europe. The app provides price information on over 30 fruit and vegetables in the countries of operation, as well as market drivers analyses and forecasts, fruit and vegetable sector news, fundamental market studies and retail audits, with access also to online consultations and success stories and opportunities for participation in trade forums, specialized seminars and conferences for agricultural entrepreneurs, technology specialists, marketers and managers. The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development contribute information and data to the app. The app has two adjacent Telegram channels that serve as trading apps for agricultural products and inputs.
records.abstract: An information portal and Telegram trade channel for agricultural producers

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The web-based app and channels enhance the market access of fruit and vegetable market participants, serving as a network through which business partners can be found. The tools help to increase the income of producers through the more efficient production, storage processing and marketing of fruit and vegetables, and by cutting out the middleman.

records.title: Electronic household books
records.description: Electronic Household Books is a data-entry system for household books (i.e. accounts)  maintained at municipal and jamoat (sub-district level of the government) levels that electronically facilitates the reporting and sharing of socio-economic indicators with the data warehouse of the central Agency on Statistics. Electronic Household Books collects the data of enterprises throughout the country and periodic statistical data on economic activity, prices, foreign trade, industrial and construction activities, agricultural, fishery and forestry activities, and climate and natural disaster information, among others. The move from paper-based Household Books to an electronic form is a part of the "Modernizing the National Statistical System in Tajikistan" project being implemented by the Agency on Statistics under the National Strategy for the Development of Statistics (NSDS) for 2021–2030, financed by World Bank. The project was launched in November 2021 when the Electronic Household Books system was tested and introduced in three districts in Tajikistan, and will conclude in December 2025 with a view rolling out the system across the entire country. This initiative is the first step towards the establishment of an electronic Population Register.
records.abstract: Web-based socio-economic e-reporting system
records.owner_name: Agency on Statistics under the President of the Republic of Tajikistan

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth
SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

_annotations.Impact: Shifting from paper-based household books to electronic ones and introducing an e-reporting system to aid mandatory reporting can reduce the reporting burden of users, improve the quality, availability and timeliness of regional agricultural statistics, and increase the coverage and transparency of data. The creation of more accurate statistics can support the improvement of social and economic policies, address spatial disparities and minimize inclusion and exclusion errors, while improving the quality and accuracy of agricultural, fishery and forestry, climate and natural disaster statistics. Electronic Household Books can collect data on sex, age group, disability and other variables, creating the basis for the Electronic Population Register.

records.title: CLARA
records.description: CLARA is an online tool developed by the International Finance Corporation (IFC) that provides financial institutions with support in decision-making by carrying out risk assessments of loans to agricultural borrowers. CLARA provides analytical indicators and makes predictive calculations of the projected cash flow of farms for the entire loan tenor, and compares available data for similar businesses and projects, thus identifying the financial needs for working capital requirements as well as agricultural equipment based on agronomic information and expert models. Analytical information and recommendations are stored in the service database and updated weekly. CLARA also allows access to production flow charts and the market prices of various agricultural products, updated quarterly.
records.abstract: Cash flow-linked agriculture risk assessment tool

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: CLARA allows financial institutions to significantly increase the efficiency of their credit analyses of agricultural borrowers, improving the access of agricultural enterprises to financing while increasing the quality of credit risk assessments, thus reducing the related operating expenses. This ICT solution helps standardize and streamline the cash-flow management of agricultural borrowers, thereby assisting financial institutions in carrying out effective credit assessment and monitoring operations.

records.title: AgroInform.Tj
records.description: AgroInform.Tj is a web-based agriculture information service that carries agricultural sector news, analytics and reports on topics such as the implementation of land reforms in Tajikistan, best practices in agriculture, information on crop production, livestock and poultry management, pest and disease control, green agriculture and the COTLOOK Cotton Index. The portal also carries advertisements supporting the purchase and sale of agricultural products and agro-inputs; information on available credits and the lending conditions of leading financial institutions; prices of more than 50 agricultural products in the main country and border markets, etc. The website also offers services related to soil analysis, weather notifications and the procurement of agricultural goods. Finally, the website also hosts informational and training videos on crop management. AgroInform.Tj is part of the Agro Space website – a web-based website developed jointly by AgroInformAsia, Kyrgyzstan and AgroInform.TJ in Tajikistan as a hub for the hosting of various digital products developed for farmers.
records.abstract: Agriculture information and news service

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The mission of AgroInform.Tj is to stimulate the agricultural market in Tajikistan by establishing business connections and providing accurate and detailed information in support of agribusinesses. For users that have no access to the Internet, AgroInform.Asia offers also a paper-based newspaper.

records.title: Business portal of Tajikistan and Central Asia
records.description: The Business Portal of Tajikistan and Central Asia (B2B) is an information app run by the State Unitary Enterprise "Tajinvest" under the State Committee on Investment and State Property Management of the Republic of Tajikistan aimed at supporting the establishment of international business partnerships through the creation of a directory of potential business partners in different countries. The app also serves as a communication app for the identification of potential partners, and for the dissemination of information on financial and economic statistics, regulations, open projects and investment opportunities. The Portal was launched as a part of the 2019 Action Plan "300 Days of Reforms to Support Entrepreneurship and Improve Investment Climate", and was developed with the support of the German Agency for International Cooperation (GIZ) and the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE).
records.abstract: Portal for the identification of international partners and investment projects
records.owner_name: State Committee for Investment and State Property Management of the Republic of Tajikistan

_annotations.Impact: The B2B portal can stimulate entrepreneurship, and increase exports and the flow of foreign investments into Tajikistan by allowing users to connect with potential international business partners, and by sharing information on financial opportunities and investment projects. By enabling entrepreneurs, producers, and farmers to register in the “Supplier Search Engine”, the app can stimulate the distribution of Tajik products internationally, thus supporting food security while at the same time providing economic support to Tajik farmers, producers and business owners. Furthermore, allowing Tajik business owners to connect with international partners supports Tajik farmers and producers in the establishment of partnerships, contributing to improvements in production practices through exchanges of knowledge, products and services. Finally, the advisory and statistical information provided on the app creates more equity in the Tajik business space through the open access provided to business guides, and insights into investment opportunities, sources and projects. This information can also be used for economic planning and the development of policies that support farmers and producers.

records.description: The regional “Sustainable agriculture for sustainable Balkans” project was established to fortify the advocacy capacities of CSOs and to support the formulation of regional policies emphasizing sustainable agriculture. records.title: Agri-calculators
records.description: Agri-calculators are an online tool for the calculation of the inputs necessary to grow vegetables. Three modules are available: a seed and seedling calculator; an irrigation water calculator; and a fertilizer calculator. The app has models for six types of crops, including tomato, cucumber, cabbage, eggplant, radish and carrot. The user provides details of the farm and planting, and the system then calculates the necessary inputs. Agri-calculators is part of the Agro Space suite of apps developed jointly by AgroInformAsia, Kyrgyzstan and AgroInform.TJ in Tajikistan as a hub for the hosting of various digital products developed for farmers.
records.abstract: Fertilizer, irrigation, water and seed calculators

_annotations.Source: Information provided by a member of the organization
_annotations.Impact: Agri-calculators assist farmers in calculating the required quantities of seeds and seedlings, fertilizers and water for the cultivation of crops, thereby facilitating effective planning and preventing the excessive and unnecessary use of inputs. This can help farmers reduce their production costs and increase their profits, while at the same time reducing the impact of their agricultural activities on the environment.

records.title: Trapview
records.description: Trapview is an automated pest monitoring solution that allows growers to remotely monitor pest insects caught in pheromone traps. The use of automated electronic traps ensures the efficient monitoring of pests, while the advanced artificial intelligence-based processing of trap data provides customers with an accurate and real-time understanding of pest population dynamics, as well as forecasts of the pest development stages in a specific area. Growers are alerted in real-time when the number of pests identified calls for insecticide spraying. Thus, Trapview serves also as a decision support tool for the planning of field activities and the optimal usage of crop protection resources. Trapview is capable of monitoring over 60 species of pest insects.
records.abstract: Decision support tool providing a pest monitoring and forecasting solutions

_annotations.Impact: Trapview can support plant protection decision-making processes by providing real-time information, allowing the forecasting of future pest levels and simulating different plant protection measure scenarios. Trapview solutions can further help in the management labour costs and other resources required for pest management. Trapview also makes pest protection activities more precise and targeted, making the use of pharmaceuticals less haphazard, and thus more sustainable. Furthermore, society can benefit through access to healthier food and the reduced chance of pest insects being resistant to insecticides. According to the company's website, organizations that use Trapview solutions report an average 5 percent increase in yield and quality. The 1000+ installed devices have helped produce over 12 million tons of food, have reduced CO2 emissions by 9 337 tons, have supported 59 847 hours of labour savings and have saved growers over EUR 130 million in costs (as of September 2022).

records.title: Smart Agro
records.description: Smart Agro is an SMS-based agrometeorological advisory service offered by IPKO. Registered farmers are informed via SMS about weather and soil conditions and any elevated disease risks. Under the pilot project launched in 2018, around 1000 farmers were given free access to an SMS service providing advice created by agronomists based on data from 16 weather stations in Kosovo related to four crops. The real-time data and advice provided to farmers contributed to better decision-making.
records.abstract: SMS-based agrometeorological advisory service for farmers

_annotations.Source: Information provided by a member of the organization
_annotations.Impact: The advisory service helps farmers make informed farming decisions, and anticipate such hazards as pests, disease and weather events. Only two farmers cancelled their subscription during the pilot. The data can be of use to multiple sectors, including insurance companies, banks, universities and public sector agencies in various roles, such as for guiding the creation of better insurance schemes, risk prediction, scientific research and improved planning.

records.title: Vodafone Çiftçi Kulübü (Vodafone Farmers’ Club)
records.description: The Vodafone Farmers' Club is a mobile subscription service offered by Vodafone Türkiye that can aid farmers in improving their farming practices by providing access to weather forecasts, agriculture information and news, while also facilitating their market access. The entry-level Farmers' Club package includes free occasional text updates related to farming subsidies, local fairs and trade shows, as well as news from the sector. Those opting for the advanced plan (the Farmer News Pack) receive (via SMS) two daily weather forecasts, weekly market price information on 93 products, agricultural news, agronomy tips and other information derived from official data for 966 districts. Farmers can request information relevant to a specific district and production area (fruit, vegetables, cereals, plants, livestock , beekeeping, etc.) as well as information about 93 specific crops. The Farmers’ Club features also a free virtual marketplace that connects buyers and sellers of agricultural products through a mobile channel. While SMS is the main channel for the delivery of content, Vodafone also maintains an Android application entitled “Vodafone Farmers' Guide” (Vodafone Çiftçi Kılavuzu). Vodafone partners with TABİT, a Turkish social enterprise that encourages smallholder farmers to embrace ICTs, for the creation of agricultural content, supported by the Turkish Agriculture Union (Türkiye Ziraat Odaları Birliği - TZOB), and drawing from the information provided by the state Meteorological Service (Meteoroloji Genel Müdürlüğü - MGM), the Union of Chambers and Commodity Exchanges of Türkiye (Türkiye Odalar ve Borsalar Birliği - TOBB), and the Ministry of Food, Agriculture and Livestock.
records.abstract: Farmer’s news package via phone by mobile network operator

_annotations.Impact: Vodafone Farmers’ Club provides access to a wide range of agriculture information and news, including product-specific disease warnings and risk information, as well as market information such as stock market prices, agricultural grant and investment supports, and free trade show invitations. Şekerbank offers interest-free loans allowing farmers to pay back their post-paid bills once a year.

records.title: Trajce Crvenov’s farm
records.description: Trajce Crvenov, a farmer from North Macedonia, combines traditional agricultural production with different innovative practices and technologies for the cultivation of non-traditional crops. Crvenov grows barley and sunflowers on his 60 ha of land, and cultivates lavender as an experimental agricultural output for the production of essential oils. Crvenov enters into contracts with post-harvest companies, ensuring he has a market for his produce every year. He is actively engaged in efforts to employ innovative precision agriculture solutions on his lands in the future.
records.abstract: Combination of traditional farming and digital technologies

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Trajce Crvenov's good practice of combining traditional agricultural production with innovative practices and technologies to increase efficiency and profitability, particularly, the use of drone and satellite imagery to support the analysis of farm data is exemplary for large-size and medium-size farms given the benefit of such data for informed decision-making.

records.title: Sensors for livestock monitoring and management
records.description: This software solution makes use of location data collected from solar-powered GPS ear tags, providing location data and GPS coordinates with an accuracy of 30–40 meters every two hours. The tags allow animals in the pasture to be located via a mobile application, while also providing proxy indicators on the health and biological status of the animals, and more.

_annotations.Source: FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices

_annotations.Impact: The research aims to provide efficient ICT solutions to meet the tracking, monitoring and data collection needs of livestock farmers. As of September 2022, the research is continuing. According to the Institute, the solution has made it possible to identify and prevent hazards on several occasions, and to limit the overgrazing of a particular pasture.

records.title: PoultryNET
records.description: PoultryNET is a app that is accessible via mobile phone or PC that supports poultry producers in increasing their efficiency and operation controls, while also constantly monitoring animal welfare and the environmental conditions in their barns. PoultryNET collects air temperature, air humidity, light intensity, air flow, and CO2 and NH3 levels from sensors throughout the supply chain, and generates prediction models and recommendations that farmers can use to support their decision-making based on real-time observations. The app hosts also financial and digital assistant modules that can be used by farmers for revenue and cost analyses, and for economic problem solving. The intention is to support farmers in the management of every step of broiler production.
records.abstract: Apps for poultry management

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: PoultryNET can help farmers can contribute to the efficiency and management of poultry farms, leading to improvements in meat quality and animal welfare, and a reduction in the negative environmental impact of poultry production. The system can also help farmers manage their operations more easily, through the provision of real-time data, prediction models, historic data and advice, contributing to reductions in costs and improvements in productivity, while making the process more secure and reliable. The app can be integrated with other software to improve data interoperability.

records.title: Open Foris
records.description: Open Foris is a set of free, open-source software tools developed by FAO and its partners to support the flexible and efficient collection, analysis and reporting of data. It includes survey design and data management tools (Arena, Collect, Collect Mobile); a data analysis and results calculation (Calc) tool; and several software tools based on Google Earth to support the collection of field data (Collect Earth) and satellite imagery (Collect Earth Online, Earth Map, SEPAL). The tools can be applied to such fields as environmental monitoring, biodiversity assessment, forestry and land use, forest inventories, etc., contributing to improvement in climate change mitigation plans and the development of more informed land-use policies.
records.abstract: Open-source software to facilitate flexible and efficient data collection, analysis and reporting
records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

SDGs.value: SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

_annotations.Impact: According to FAO news, Open Foris tools are helping people in 180 countries to collect, analyse and report data. The tools make data collection, analysis and reporting more accessible, accurate and transparent, and as a result, people and governments are able to measure, report, plan, devise policies and verify policy impacts more effectively. Open Foris has played an instrumental role in the development of transparent, reliable, relevant, accessible and sustainable National Forest Monitoring Systems in 45 countries. Open Foris tools and apps have been used for the provision of data to 70 percent of the 50 REDD+ Forest Reference Levels submitted to the UNFCCC. The 50 countries in question are responsible for 75 percent of the global deforestation, according to FAO’s 2020 Global Forest Resources Assessment.

records.title: Kultiva
records.description: Kultiva is a web-based app run by CARD AgroService that aids farmers in accessing farm inputs and equipment, such as fertilizers, agricultural machinery, milking equipment, among others. Rather than functioning as a dynamic e-commerce or online marketplace, the website provides the user with technical information about products. As further features, Kultiva provides technical assistance and consulting services related to agri-food processes, and a section listing the addresses and contact information of regional and local offices providing such services.

records.title: Kray Protection UAS
records.description: Kray Protection UAS is a crop-spraying drone that delivers fertilizers and pesticides to farmers’ fields. The prototype was presented at the Drone World Expo 2016 in San Jose, California, and by 2019 most of the testing had been completed. The company has since been preparing for mass production and rapid expansion on the market.

The drone promises less fuel, less maintenance and less staff requirements, along with outstanding performance. The costs of the application to 1/10th and less. The technology also supports no-till production, thereby contributing to land conservation and climate change mitigation.

records.title: Digitalization of pasture information for community-based pasture management
records.description: The digital community-based pasture management system has been developed in country under a Livestock and Market Development Project (LMDP) financed jointly by IFAD and the Government of the Republic of Kyrgyzstan. The project equips authorities with a tool for land management and land dispute mitigation operations, while also enhancing the utilization of land by farmers, augmenting pasture productivity and boosting resilience to climate change. The initiative equips pasture unions with the necessary technologies and training for the digitization of grazing area maps and the utilization of online geographic information systems.

_annotations.Source: FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices

SDGs.value: SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

_annotations.Impact: Baseline data at the initial phase of the project revealed that 42.4 percent of the respondents had been involved in disputes over pasture usage, which declined to 22.7 percent in 2016 and to 21.4 percent in 2018, and in the second phase, an 8 percent reduction in pasture access disputes was recorded. Notably, milk yield among the beneficiaries witnessed a 4 percent increase, and animal weights grew by 20–50 percent, which was attributed to the improved, resilience of pastures to climatic conditions and the enhanced availability of fodder.

records.title: CARD AgroCredit
records.description: Operated by the CARD AgroCredit Universal Credit Organization, CARD AgroCredit is an online app designed to guide farmers and other crucial stakeholders on the intricacies of loans, detailing the conditions, prerequisites and application procedures. The organization plays a leading role in the provision of loans to a broad spectrum of beneficiaries, including farmers, consumers and businesses. The organization also specializes in the leasing of vital agricultural machinery, tools and equipment to the farming sector. The strategically designed loans prioritize the modernization of production, material collection, production streamlining and the efficient marketing of services/products. Catering to the seasonal requirements of production and trade, the app is fortified with an online loan calculator, making loan calculations more accessible and straightforward.

records.title: DALATEK
records.description: DALATEK operates as a web-based app and mobile application that connects and streamlines the interactions of farmers with agri-food exporters and other actors on the agrifood value chain, such as logistic operators, quality assurance specialists, restaurateurs and refrigeration facilities. The web-based app and mobile application can be used to access training materials, supporting the management of the food supply chain. Overall, DELATEK is an easy-to-use mobile app that allows the user to find a job, sell a product, make a purchase and expand their knowledge. The app facilitates interactions at every stage of the process of preparing products for export, from harvesting to sending out invoices or certificates to the final consumer. DELATEK’s team is now working on building a database of trusted farmers with whom registered users can collaborate in the long term, and is looking into the provision of technology training to increase the number of qualified quality control specialists in the field to support the successful completion of transactions.
records.abstract: Platform featuring agricultural jobs, e-marketplace, and knowledge

_annotations.Impact: DALATEK seeks to harmonise business transactions, support the matching of users’ needs and reduce information asymmetries along the food supply chain. The application makes use of digital information-sharing technologies and procedures to enhance transparency and trust, and aims to reduce the bureaucracy and costs associated with the verification of food quality, while allowing store payments to be completed electronically.

records.title: CARPO
records.description: The CARPO software supports real-time agrometeorological monitoring, and serves as an early warning system for farmers and advisors in the Republic of Srpska that is accessible via the web or through a mobile app. CARPO was developed by DRAXIS (www.draxis.gr/projects/carpo-2) and is currently run by the Republic Hydrometeorological Institute of the Republic of Srpska. The system utilizes observations from a local network of agrometeorological stations to produce pest and disease forecasts for the different crops cultivated in the country. Based on these forecasts, the system sends out alerts and notifications to the users – primarily farmers and agronomists – advising them to take the necessary actions to protect their crops. The system also allows users to upload photos or report disease outbreaks, and to indicate their own parcels on the CARPO map to support the production of more specific forecasts. Users can also obtain recommendations from a team of expert advisors through the app.
records.abstract: Software for real-time agrometeorological services and plant prognostics
records.owner_name: Republic Hydrometeorological Institute of the Republic of Srpska

_annotations.Impact: The CARPO software provides farmers, advisors and scientific and educational institutions with quality, expert-sourced information on current pest and disease risks. CARPO also provides decision support about when and which control measures to apply to reduce potential crop losses, thus helping farmers reduce their pest protection product expenses, leading to higher-quality yields and healthier produce, thus reducing the negative impact on humans and the environment.

records.title: BeeProtect
records.description: BeeProtect is an online application through which farmers can notify beekeepers of planned pesticide applications, thereby preventing bees from being poisoned. It operates primarily as a tool for informing beekeepers when, where and what plant protection product sprayings will take place in the vicinity of their apiaries. BeeProtect allows the sharing of information between three key stakeholders: beekeepers, farmers, and the local/national administration, and at the same time, the application helps keep farmers informed about the installation of beehives near their agricultural fields.
records.abstract: System to alert beekeepers and protect bees from pesticide poisoning
records.owner_name: National Beekeepers Association of the Republic of Moldova

SDGs.value: SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

_annotations.Impact: The BeeProtect web and mobile application is a nationwide communication tool for beekeepers and farmers that can have significant positive impacts on both agricultural producers and beekeepers. By providing a app for farmers to input data on their planned pesticide applications, the app allows beekeepers to be informed in advance about the nearby use of chemicals that may harm their bees, allowing them to take the necessary measures to protect their operations through temporary relocations or the covering of their hives, protecting the health of the bee population, which is crucial for agriculture given the key role played by bees in pollination. By ensuring the safety of bees, farmers can also benefit from increased crop yields due to better pollination. The web application promotes communication and collaboration between farmers and beekeepers, which can foster a better understanding of each other's needs and concerns.

records.title: AMIS
records.description: The Agricultural Market Information System (AMIS) is a web-based database that provides continuous information and monitoring data on the agri-food markets. The database records the trade prices of agricultural outputs including the prices of strategic products provided by representative markets, providing the user with a transparent overview of movements in the agricultural product and food markets. The app also provides access to monthly reports of market prices for various crops and livestock, and features a “Buy/Sell” tab that provides information on, and links to external landing pages for the completion of transactions. The app thus operates also as a marketplace for the purchase and sale of agri-food outputs, although the marketplace was not operational as of March 2023. The system is being expanded to include market information on animal feed, raw materials, grape markets and wine.
records.abstract: Agricultural Market Information System
records.owner_name: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy of the Republic of North Macedonia

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth
SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

_annotations.Impact: The Agricultural Market Information System is fully compatible with the markets and trade policy of the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP). CAP requires the regular submission of market information to the European Commission, Directorate for Agriculture (DG-AGRI) by North Macedonia as a requirement for full membership of the European Union. The information provided by AMIS helps farmers better understand the market and make more informed decisions related to the production, pricing and marketing of agri-food products. It also provides the government with data that can aid in the monitoring, evaluation and formulation of more effective agricultural policies. The acquired information also helps strengthen the position of the national agri-food sector on the domestic and international markets, while providing accurate data for decision-making in the formulation of competitive agricultural policies.

records.title: Agrobot Lala
records.description: Agrobot Lala is an autonomous robotic system – an unmanned ground vehicle that collects and analyses in-field soil samples for nitrates. The robotic system analyses each soil sample individually in real-time, spending 30 minutes per sample, and the soil sample is then georeferenced, creating a map for precision base fertilizing. The system combines real-time analyses with AI and cloud-based solutions to generate multilayer maps indicating the locations where fertilization is necessary. Among the advantages, this robotic system reduces and optimizes the number and locations from which samples need to be taken. The user accesses an in-house-developed smartphone application that allows them to oversee and manage the robot’s tasks, to change the position of the robot, and to add and delete sampling points. The collected measurement data are then sent to the Cloud for further analysis and for the formation of prescription maps detailing variable fertilizer application rates. Agrobot Lala is lightweight, contributing to less soil compaction. The robot was field-tested on Serbia’s first digital farm in 2018.
records.abstract: Autonomous robotic system for real-time, in-field soil sampling and nitrate analysis

_annotations.Impact: The use of Agrobot Lala for soil sampling can increase the accuracy and precision of fertilizer applications, and reduce fertilizer waste and environmental pollution. The real-time soil analysis and georeferencing capabilities of the system allow farmers to take immediate action and adjust their fertilizer application rates. The in-house designed smartphone application also makes it easier for farmers to monitor and manage the robot's tasks, contributing to improved crop yields and increased profits. Finally, the lightweight robot leads to less soil compaction.

records.title: Agrobiznes library
records.description: The Agrobiznes Library is an open-access online app offering guides, brochures, didactic material, scientific publications and manuals about agriculture developed by specialists in the Republic of Moldova and abroad. The library includes materials in the Moldovan and Russian languages that are organized by topic. The library covers multiple agricultural production sectors (e.g., crop, vegetable and fruit production, livestock systems, fish farming, viticulture, beekeeping), technical support areas (irrigation, pesticide use, greenhouses) and organic agriculture, and provides support also for management and financial planning. Guides and manuals can only be uploaded by authorized institutions, and include international organizations (e.g., IFAD, USAID, EIB), NGOs, the central government and research institutions.

The publicly available information can positively contribute to the capacity-building efforts of all actors along the agricultural value chain.
