records.title: AgroApp
records.description: AgroApp is an online platform for agribusiness finance, connecting farmers with input suppliers and banks. Through this website, farmers can search and compare different loan offers from different affiliated banks. The solution aims at providing easy access for entrepreneurs to financial resources to foster growth and development of their business. AgroApp simplifies and accelerates the process of obtaining a loan for farmers for the purchase of fertilizers, seeds and plant protection products. The farmer only needs to type the company’s registration number and the loan amount into the AgroApp chatbot, the app automatically generates an agricultural producer’s loan application, and banks receive an application ready for financing almost immediately and can make a preliminary decision on granting a loan in a few hours. Typically, the traditional process takes months, AgroApp significantly reduces this application time.
records.abstract: Lending platform for farmers, suppliers and banks

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: AgroApp has the potential to streamline financial processes for farmers. The platform's automated credit application system, utilizing identification codes and predefined templates, accelerates loan processing compared to traditional methods. The direct linkage with over 70 registries fosters financial inclusion, empowering farmers with data-driven decision-making. Overall, AgroApp's innovative approach is aiming to achieve positive results in time and cost savings, reduced administrative burdens, and a transformative shift towards modernized and efficient agricultural practices.`

records.title: Agro.kg
records.description: Agro.kg is an agricultural portal for a one-way dissemination of agricultural news and a forum that offers a two-way exchange for users to send and receive content and engage into interactions in the field of agriculture. The portal offers also services for the purchase and sale of products, training materials, familiarization with agricultural news and participation in agricultural forums. Key features include comprehensive market information, weather forecasts, and expert advice. Distinctively, it facilitates direct communication between farmers, suppliers, and buyers, fostering collaboration and knowledge exchange. The platform addresses the challenge of information asymmetry in Kyrgyz agriculture, empowering stakeholders to make informed decisions and enhancing overall efficiency in the agricultural value chain.
records.abstract: News portal and forum

_annotations.Impact: Agro.kg aims at fostering connectivity and information exchange in the agricultural sector of Kyrgyzstan. The platform facilitates networking among them through forums, enabling discussions on crucial agricultural topics, publicizing products for sale or purchase, and providing updates on relevant subjects and events. It can reduce information gaps among farmers, suppliers, and buyers by providing real-time and precise market data. The platform facilitates direct linkages in the food and agriculture value chain, enabling users to identify nearby shops, markets, and communities for buying or selling inputs. The platform can serve also as a digital marketplace, allowing the effective promotion of agricultural goods.

records.title: Agritourizem
records.description: Agritourizem is an online platform facilitating the matching, accessing and exploring of agritourism experiences in Albania. It allows farms all over the country to get certified respecting a few quality criteria listed in the platform. The platform is organized in a few categories: agritourism experiences, farm experiences, camping experiences, tours, local Festivals, and a Map with the localisation of all the experiences. The agritourism platform is always updated with new articles and information, spotlighting traditions, histories, and local cuisines. Agritourizem addresses a significant challenge in Albanian tourism – the scarcity of authentic and dependable information. The platform is committed to continuous enhancements, actively seeking new entries to broaden its service spectrum across the entire country, from north to south. It aspires to serve as a catalyst for promoting the diverse businesses that form part of its network.
records.abstract: Web platform featuring agritourism initiatives
records.owner_name: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Agritourizem can have positive impact on various fronts, including local economies, cultural preservation, tourism experiences, community engagement, environmental awareness, and the overall growth and enrichment of agritourism in Albania. The platform aims to bridge information gaps between farms and visitors, facilitating access to details and the precise location of agritourism experiences across the country. Moreover, Agritourizem establishes meaningful connections between farms and rural communities, providing increased visibility for their services and creating avenues for additional revenue streams. By serving as a centralized platform not only enhances the visitor experience but also supports local enterprises in expanding their reach and impact. The application has the capacity be a catalyst for positive change by fostering collaboration and synergy between agritourism businesses, visitors, and governmental bodies, ultimately creating a more robust and sustainable agricultural landscape in Albania.

records.title: Afi2Go Prime
records.description: Afi2Go Prime is a digital system designed mainly for dairy farmers to manage their herds and milk quality. The system includes sensors for monitoring cows and their milk production as well as a farm management software accessible via a desktop-based or mobile app. The system enables dairy farmers to track data about cow pregnancy status, milk production, presence of diseases or unhealthy conditions. The mobile app allows the farmers and their team to complete and record the farm’s routine tasks out in the field. The design makes it possible to select workflows that match specific operations. The app enables on-the-go data entry and ensures real-time synchronization with the farm management software, guaranteeing that every piece of information is promptly updated on multiple devices. The interactive app notifies the farmers based on real time changes.
records.abstract: Digital herd management app

_annotations.Impact: Afi2Go Prime is expected to automatize and improve the precision of dairy farming activities. Herdsmen, inseminators, and vets are expected to benefit from the synchronised access to more data and information, such as task lists and cow cards, and record all actions directly via the app on their mobiles. Managers can use the app to monitor workers’ progress and the farm status, displayed on the dashboard. The technology aims also to facilitate the work for the farmers who can make smarter management decisions while working in the field, keep track of their cows in the field as tasks are being performed, and easily access information to make informed decisions.

records.title: µFarm
records.description: µFarm is a vertical aeroponic farming system designed for cultivating edible plants indoors.
records.abstract: Vertical aeroponic farming solution for cultivating edible plants

_annotations.Impact: µFarm offers an aeroponic growing environment that conserves up to 95 percent of water and accelerates plant harvest times, according to the company's page. As a soilless agricultural method, it eliminates the need for pesticides or additives, resulting in plants that require no washing, further contributing to water conservation. Based on vertical farming principles, this solution enables producers to achieve high yields in limited space. Nevertheless, this technology comes with installation, material, energy, and maintenance costs.  As current agricultural areas will not be sufficient to meet the food demand of a continuously increasing population, soilless farming techniques and the products produced in these ways can play an important role in addressing food insecurity.

The company currently supports the excess inventory management of manufacturing plants and distribution centres across the United States.

records.title: WOCAT
records.description: WOCAT's Global Database on Sustainable Land Management (SLM) is a free access source of field-tested SLM data, detailing SLM practices and maps from different locations around the world, and offers practitioners the opportunity to share their own SLM practices or maps.
records.abstract: World Overview of Conservation Approaches and Technologies

_annotations.Impact: The WOCAT Database is the primary database of SLM best practices, and is recommended by the UN Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD). Various outputs are generated: 1) numerous technologies have been tested in the field, and their effectiveness has been demonstrated in the prevention of soil degradation and improvements in crop yields; 2) the applied stakeholder approach has enhanced collaborations between local stakeholders, and has empowered them in their contacts with decision-makers and 3) the data can be accessed globally from the internet, and through the book “DESIRE for Greener Land”.

records.title: Meeting the European Union's digital agriculture requirements
records.description: "Meeting the European Union's Digital Agriculture Requirements” is a compendium that has been jointly produced by the FAO and ITU to help pre-accession countries and territories understand and meet the emerging EU requirements related to digital agriculture. The compendium emphasizes the importance of digital agriculture for achieving sustainable development and details the steps necessary for integration with the EU digitalization into framework. The main highlights of the compendium include: 1) an overview of why digital agriculture is becoming increasingly instrumental for the achievement of the EU’s sustainability objectives, affecting also pre-accession countries and territories; 2) a detailed examination of emerging EU requirements and opportunities for digital agriculture, with specific focus on the Common Agricultural Policy; 3) guidance on EU pre-accession funding, instruments and delivery mechanisms for digital agriculture; and 4) voluntary checklists to guide the self-assessment of pre-accession countries and territories around EU’s digital agriculture requirements and opportunities.
records.abstract: An ITU-FAO compendium for pre-accession countries and territories
records.owner_name: United Nations’ Food and Agriculture Organization – Regional Office for Europe and Central Asia; International Telecommunication Union – Office for Europe

_annotations.Impact: Understanding the latest developments and regulations related to digital agriculture in the European Union is becoming more challenging due to the continuous evolution and deployment of digital technologies, and the growing interrelationship between digitalization and agriculture across the whole EU Acquis. For the countries and territories whose negotiations ahead of accession to the European Union are continuing, this represents an additional undertaking, as they are being called on to meet these requirements, or indeed, go beyond them. Addressing this issue, the compendium has been designed to be a source of information for all pre-accession countries and territories, regardless of the timescale of their individual path to EU accession.

records.title: Connected farmers
records.description: “Connected farmers – A casebook of good practices and inspiring stories from Europe and Central Asia” highlights the transformative power of digital technologies in agriculture by presenting 25 compelling case studies of small-, medium- and large-scale farmers and agripreneurs who have successfully embraced digitalization. Case studies from Georgia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, North Macedonia, the Republic of Moldova and Uzbekistan are presented as real-world examples, some of which have been tested and replicated in diverse contexts and can serve as recommended models, while others show great potential for upscaling.

records.title: Climate Risk Toolbox (CRTB)
records.description: The Climate Risk Toolbox (CRTB) is a global geospatial tool hosted on FAO’s Hand-in-Hand Geospatial Platform targeting the identification and mitigation of climate risks in the agriculture sector in the early stages of the project cycle, and supports the inclusion of efforts to reduce such risks in project design activities. Risk is calculated based on the latest Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) definition, taking into account interactions between hazards, exposure and vulnerability, and the adaptive capacity component modulates the scope of the observed and projected risks.
records.abstract: Geospatial tool for the identification and assessment of climate risks in the agriculture sector
records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

_annotations.Impact: Around 190 projects have undergone screening around the world since 2020, including 15 FAO projects funded by the Global Environmental Facility in Europe and Central Asia, identified as low to moderate risk (as of July 2024). The screenings have been carried out primarily for projects in Türkiye, Uzbekistan, the Republic of Moldova, Kazakhstan and Turkmenistan, with focus on biodiversity conservation, sustainable fisheries, water management and food systems. The CRTB is a first-step tool for the baseline identification of climate risks at the earliest stages of a project and programme. Those identified as high or very high risk will be recommended for a more detailed assessment of the climate change data and the impacts on the agricultural sector, for example during project formulation or implementation, using more advanced tools, methods and climate services.

records.title: Smartway
records.description: Smartway is an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered solution that helps supermarkets handle food waste more effectively through four features: Smartdetection, which helps stores identify which products are nearing their expiration date; Smartdecision, which decides whether the expiring item should be discounted or donated; Smartdiscount, which prints out a discount label where required; and Smartdonation, which navigates the administrative procedures related to the donation of expired or near-expired items.
records.abstract: AI-powered solution to control food waste in retailers

_annotations.Impact: Smartway claims to reduce food waste by 80 percent while growing each store’s net profits by as much as 51 percent. The company has reported savings totalling USD 177 million through discounting, and preventing 56 846 t of waste. According to Smartway’s website, over 400 stores across France are benefitting from the technology, and the company has stated its intention to ramp up its research and development (R&D) operations to improve the technology.

records.title: Socleo
records.description: Socleo is a software partner that supports short supply chains within the agricultural and food distribution sectors. The company offers online and offline software that support producers, processors, collectives, distributors and territorial platforms in the efficient management of their commercial, logistical and administrative operations. Socleo’s software are tailored for short food supply chains in France, contributing to sales through an on-line store and a showcase website; logistics, through the management of inventories and deliveries; and administrative operations by generating invoices. It is a complete management platform that can be adapted to meet the needs of local food distribution networks. No delivery services are offered by the platform, delivery is managed by producers independently. The company offers also education and training in support of the digitalization of short food supply chains.
records.abstract: Software solutions for short supply chain operations in the food sector

_annotations.Impact: As of 2024, Socleo supports more than 550 short food supply chains through which the products of more than 4000 producers and processors are marketed. Around 14 000 sellers are listed, with a total annual turnover of EUR 112 million, as well as 235 000 buyers.

records.title: PHENIX
records.description: PHENIX is a platform through which consumers can buy surplus food from local businesses at a reduced price. PHENIX works in partnership with charities or other operations that can access the PHENIX app to learn what is available in real time and collect what they need according to a schedule established . PHENIX expanded its activities in 2024 with the launch of its own outlets under the name “NOUS anti gaspi (We are anti-waste)” specialized in the sale of products with short expiry dates, fruit and vegetables with appearance or size defects, downgraded goods or overstock.
records.abstract: Web application for the donation or sale of unsold food

_annotations.Impact: As of June 2024, PHENIX claims to have saved 150 million meals, or 10 million t of food, that would otherwise have been wasted. It states that almost 2 million baskets of food have been sold to date through the PHENIX app, equating to savings of 15 000 t in CO2 emissions based on an estimated 4.5 kg in savings for each basket.

records.title: KITRO
records.description: KITRO is a system combining a scale and camera with artificial intelligence (AI) that allows the measurement and monitoring of food waste to better understand the source of operational inefficiencies in the hospitality sector. Users receive personalized support in understanding the acquired data and in the achievement of sustainability goals. KITRO can benefit operations of all sizes, but especially those serving over 100 meals a day.
records.abstract: IT tool for commercial kitchens for the measurement and monitoring of food waste

_annotations.Impact: KITRO provides customers with detailed insights into their food waste, supporting the optimization of the operation and reductions in waste and outlays, and consequently, a reduced environmental impact. By providing customers with an overview of where food is being wasted and making suggestions on best practices, KITRO can help restaurants reduce avoidable food waste by up to 60 percent and increase their food profit margins by up to 8 percent, while also reducing their CO2 emissions, water consumption and land usage. KITRO’s AI-based technologies were used during the 2020 World Economic Forum to monitor and analyse the waste food produced by the event.

records.title: Matsmart
records.description: Matsmart is an e-marketplace for the sale of surplus Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG), such as dry food and non-food products that have been taken off the shelves, due to, for example, packaging changes, seasonality, faulty production or an approaching “best before” date. The goods are sold at 20–90 percent of their retail prices, and include pantry goods but no fresh, chilled or frozen food. The goods on offer are constantly changing as the needs of producers to move different products change.
records.abstract: E-marketplace for fast-moving consumer goods

_annotations.Impact: Matsmart addresses the growing problem of food waste as a channel for the redistribution of goods that would otherwise be discarded. The model resolves the overstock problems of suppliers by selling food at low cost to customers, contributing also to reductions in waste and increased gross margins.

records.title: Logicout
records.description: Logicout is an online calculator that estimates the greenhouse gas emissions and financial costs of food delivery operations, both for a simple round trip from the farm to the individual customer, and to several delivery points. The calculation takes into account the cost price per kilometre of the vehicle used, the time spent driving, and the many other logistical factors affecting deliveries, such as order taking, product packaging, order preparation and invoicing. Logicout can help when deciding on an appropriate sales price, and in the optimization of trips, informing the user whether it is profitable to deliver to a particular outlet, and on the best departure times to avoid traffic problems. Logicout also calculates the quantities of greenhouse gases and air pollutants emitted during the transportation of products.
records.abstract: Online calculator for measuring the environmental footprint and delivery costs in short food supply delivery operations

_annotations.Impact: The user data of operations that make use of Logicout can be followed on the application's home page. More than 5000 calculations have been made since the application entered into operation, across the national territory. The web application is simple and intuitive to use, and features not only a calculator but also an educational toolkit to support changes in the organization of logistics. At the time of writing, 716 accounts were registered on the site and the calculator has been visited 21 717 times.

records.title: Kikleo
records.description: Kikleo is a support, management and decision-making tool designed to reduce food waste in restaurants. Kikleo uses a camera, scale and artificial intelligence (AI) in an automated process to quantify the food left on plates by consumers, based on which the restaurant can cut down on food waste and benefit from the subsequent savings.

_annotations.Impact: The company claims that Kikleo can provide savings of up to EUR 10 000/year and reduce food waste by more than 50 percent, while contributing to savings of up to 15 000 kg in CO2 emissions per year for an average-sized restaurant. The solution can thus improve the financial performance of restaurants, increase customer satisfaction, and reduce the costs associated with the storage and treatment of bio-waste.

records.title: Innoscentia
records.description: Innoscentia carries out product microbiological and sensory shelf-life analyses for the evaluation of food products to determine their shelf life based on microbial growth and sensory characteristics (such as taste, smell, texture and appearance). Such analyses can help in understanding how long a product remains safe and acceptable for consumption, aiding in accurate shelf-life determination and, subsequently, reductions in food waste. Its sensors come in the form of labels that are attached to packaging and show the level of freshness, either visually directly on the label, through a digital smartphone app or as part of a larger system. The mobile app offers detailed information and data on food freshness drawn from reactive ink labels and provides real-time updates and insights into the microbial activity within food packages.
records.abstract: Product microbiological and sensory shelf-life labelling and app

_annotations.Impact: Innoscentia unlocks lost shelf-life by supporting the packaging and food sectors in optimizing their value chains. A prolonged shelf life of only 2 days could reduce retail waste by up to 50 percent and household waste up to 60 percent, with obvious benefits. Innoscentia has been recognized with numerous awards, such as the EAT-Forum Global Innovation Award in 2016 (https://www.innoscentia.com/).

records.title: Farmy
records.description: Farmy is an e-marketplace offering a huge selection of hand-picked products and groceries from hundreds of local producers. Farmy's logistics model aims to avoid the need for the interim storage of fresh produce and to cut down on food waste by delivering orders directly to the customer's doorstep. A large variety of products are offered, including fruit, vegetables, dairy, meat and pantry items, most of which are organic and are supplied with comprehensive information about the producer and product. The platform caters to various dietary needs, with lactose-free, gluten-free, vegetarian, and vegan options. Delivery costs and times are calculated on the website.
records.abstract: E-marketplace of locally sourced groceries

_annotations.Impact: Farmy supplies households throughout Switzerland with high-quality and sustainably sourced products for organic, regular and complete weekly shopping. percent of the products are sourced from within an 80 km radius of the hubs in Zurich and Lausanne, with a unique logistics concept that removes the need for intermediate storage, meaning that food is 3–4 days fresher than in the supermarket.

records.title: FoodTrack
records.description: FoodTrack is an online platform featuring multiple software through which local producers can connect with consumers. The platform hosts e-commerce functions; individual business websites/online boutiques; and decision support tools for the management of logistics and payments. Producers are chosen carefully and must provide relevant documents on offered products, although the registration process is simple once the provided information has been verified. The seller lists his/her address and delivery preferences, and can list his/her products online after validation by the site administrators. Home delivery or drop-off points, such as a specific market, can be arranged with the consumer, considerably reducing transport costs, or the customer can collect their order directly from the producer's store if the latter has a fixed point of sale. Foodtrack.fr arranges the delivery once a purchase has been made. Regardless of the delivery choice of the seller, orders are paid online and prepared only after the payment has been received.
records.abstract: Software supporting online sales of the vegetables, fruit and products of local producers

_annotations.Impact: As of July 2024, 162 producers and 965 consumers are registered with FoodTrack. The platform encourages locavorism, and offers economic, health and ecological advantages, promoting short supply chains and local production.

records.title: FIT (Food Intel Tech)

The results are reported in weekly performance reports, available in nine languages, supporting kitchens in improving their operations.

FIT Food Waste Monitoring Tech was awarded a Solar Impulse Efficient Solution Label in 2020.

records.title: Bankuet
records.description: Bankuet is a platform through which people can make donations to food banks – charitable organizations that donate food to those in need in the United Kingdom. Bankuet converts donations into the items requested by food banks, ensuring the recipients receive the supplies they need most, contributing to reduced waste and efficient distribution to those in need. Bankuet pools together donations, allowing it to benefit from the discounts applied to bulk purchases, i.e. for every GBP 1 donated, Bankuet delivers more than GBP 1 worth of supplies directly to food banks. Goods are ordered upon receiving a request from a food bank, eliminating waste and ensuring the recipients receive what they need most.

_annotations.Country of origin: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
_annotations.Impact: Bankuet supports over 100 food banks in 51 cities across the United Kingdom, and fed roughly 20 000 people in 2020.

records.title: FAO Digital Services Portfolio (DSP)
records.description: The FAO Digital Services Portfolio (DSP) has been designed for the dissemination of information to the food and agriculture and related sectors and to scale up the provision of agricultural services to smallholders and family farmers to promote their digital inclusion. The key features of the platform include weather forecasts with alerts, livestock management advice, commodity pricing information and nutritional guidance. Designed as a flexible digital public good, the platform is easy to use and customizable to meet different needs, and has been incorporated with such additional features as plant disease recognition functions in Georgia or animal feed calculators in Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan.

records.title: AMAPj
records.description: AMAPj is software that supports small-scale/organic producers in the creation of websites and online systems for sales of their products directly to businesses or consumers. Both browser and mobile application are available, accessible only by the members of the Association pour le Maintien d'une Agriculture Paysanne (Association for the Maintenance of Peasant Agriculture – AMAP). Producers can manage numerous supply chain management activities through the website and app, such as value propositions, membership payments, deliveries to producers, accounting, etc.
records.abstract: Software simplifying the management of contracts
records.owner_name: AMAPj (Association pour le Maintien d'une Agriculture Paysanne)

_annotations.Impact: As of July 2024, AmapJ is in use by 440 AMAP members (consumer groups) from France, Belgium and Luxembourg, and is being tested by approx. 30 other AMAPs. AmapJ facilitates transactions between consumers and farmers, and so has been designed to be as simple to use as possible. The software facilitates management operations, but without removing the need for communication between the parties involved. One of the strongest features of AmapJ is its distribution of tasks across the AMAP members, and so avoids over-reliance on a single person.

records.title: Agrioli
records.description: Agrioli is a plant disease and pest management tool that analyses photos of crops affected by pests, diseases (fungal, viral, bacterial) or nutrient deficiencies, after which it provides a diagnosis and offers tailored advice to the user. Agrioli hosts a freely accessible library of pests, diseases, bacteria and fungi that can be filtered by type and target crops. As of May 2024, the tool can support the management of plant pests and diseases affecting 77 different agricultural crops.
records.abstract: AI-based plant disease and pest management system

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Agrioli leverages AI-based image recognition technologies, allowing farmers and farm advisors to rapidly diagnose pests and diseases in their plants, including fungal, viral and bacterial infections and nutrient deficiencies through a simple image upload. This diagnostic capability helps reduce the time and effort typically required for the manual identification of crop problems, allowing for quicker interventions and supporting improved crop health management.

records.title: Sinpeks
records.description: Sinpeks is an online platform for the purchase and/or rental services of a wide range of agricultural machinery and equipment. Users can find tools for soil preparation, including ploughs, harrows and rotary tillers, as well as such specialized equipment as mowers and mulchers, designed to support the efficient management of vegetation. Harvesting equipment can also be acquired from the platform, including grain mills and grape crushers, as well as irrigation and water management equipment for crop cultivation and maintenance. Sinpeks also facilitates the rent or purchase of processed product handling equipment, such as mixers, while users requiring larger items can rent such items as tractors. The platform can also be used for bulk purchases of fertilizers. In cases where certain products are not readily available, Sinpeks allows users to request specific items.

_annotations.Impact: In addition to the ability to purchase equipment, Sinpeks also offers flexible rental options, which is particularly beneficial to users who do not need machinery on a full-time basis or who want to avoid large upfront costs.

Furthermore, by streamlining the data collection operation and simplifying reporting, PigVision reduces administrative burdens and enhances operational transparency.

records.title: GeoInnovus
records.description: The GeoInnovus Automated Control System for Agricultural Machinery is a high-precision guidance system designed for self-propelled agricultural machinery, including tractors, combine harvesters and sprayers. Designed to function without manual steering, it allows machinery to follow pre-programmed routes, bringing precision and efficiency to such agricultural activities as seed planting, fertilizer distribution, pesticide application, etc. Satellite guidance and real-time corrections based on GPS signals ensure the accurate positioning of the machine, minimizing overlaps and gaps in the field.
records.abstract: Automatic control systems for agricultural machinery

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: By automating the steering and guidance of machinery, the GeoInnovus Automated Control System for Agricultural Machinery enhances efficiency, allowing farmers to cover more ground in less time with centimetre precision. The system also reduces input waste by ensuring that resources such as seeds, fertilizers and pesticides are applied exactly where they are needed, optimizing their use and lowering costs. Furthermore, by eliminating the need for manual steering, the system allows farmers to focus on other tasks.

It includes seasonal guidance on the planting and pruning of crops, protecting plants from pests, managing livestock breeding and feeding, and beekeeping. The calendar helps farmers stay on schedule by notifying them of essential farming operations and the implementation of best practices throughout the year.

records.title: Inspire Geoportal
records.description: The INSPIRE Geoportal is an online catalogue listing the national geoportals that are aligned with the INSPIRE Directive, and contains a specific section for agriculture-related geoportals in the European Union (e.g. IACS, LPIS). The Geoportal offers access to a vast collection of spatial data sets produced by various public authorities across Europe. Users can search, view and download geospatial information on such topics as environmental protection, land use, transportation, etc. The portal is designed to improve transparency, facilitate data sharing, and support decision-making related to geographic and environmental issues, and serves as a central access point for spatial data resources, making it easier for stakeholders, including researchers, policymakers and the general public, to access high-quality geographic data.
records.abstract: European portal for geospatial data provided under the INSPIRE Directive

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The INSPIRE Geoportal plays a central role in the European efforts to improve access to and the use of geospatial data across the Member States and EFTA countries. It supports the sharing of spatial data on a variety of topics, including environmental protection, transportation and urban planning. Recent monitoring reports claim that the portal has successfully facilitated the integration and dissemination of spatial data with significant participation from the European Union and EFTA countries. The portal has also been instrumental in providing public authorities, researchers and policymakers with access to essential data in support of their support decision-making processes related to sustainability and environmental governance

records.title: E-farm
records.description: E-farm is an online marketplace facilitating direct transactions between farmers and end consumers for the sale of agricultural produce (such as vegetables, fruit and dairy products), processed foods (such as jams and fermented vegetables), inputs (such as fertilizers and seedlings), and artisanal products (such as handicrafts and hand-made cosmetics). Customers can filter their searches for available products to identify special offers, discounts and promotions. E-Farm also features a dedicated section for news related to the agri-food sector, as well as content on best practices in agriculture.
records.abstract: Online marketplace for agri-food products

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: E-farm connects farmers directly with customers, shortening the supply chain and allowing farmers to retain a greater share of the sale proceeds. Consumers, on the other hand, gain access to a broader variety of fresh and niche products, including artisanal goods and home-made foods. E-farm can boost local economies by developing the market relations of rural producers.

records.title: Data Food Consortium
records.description: The Data Food Consortium initiative aims to facilitate the interoperability of short food supply chain platforms through the development of an open standardized digital language. The intention in this regard is to enhance collaboration among producers, distributors and other actors involved in short food supply chains and the food ecosystem in general with pooled data and efficient information flows, thus supporting local food systems, reducing environmental impacts and promoting transparency and fairness. The Consortium encourages collaboration and democratization within the food and technology sectors.
records.abstract: Common and open digital language supporting the development of short supply chains

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The Data Food Consortium strives to facilitate the consistent exchange and interpretation of data, supporting streamlined communication and collaborations among diverse stakeholders. The solution seeks to save time and to provide reliable data to food producers and the organizers of short food chains by reinforcing cooperation and ensuring the synergy of different actors through efficient data flows and the mutualization of transport systems. Though the solution is being adopted after the early stage, overall, it is expected to support local authorities in developing territorial food markets and in overcoming the limits of logistic flows while simultaneously reducing the environmental footprint of short food supply chains.

records.title: ASIG Geoportal
records.description: The ASIG Geoportal is a web-based application managed by the Albanian State Authority for Geospatial Information (ASIG) serving as a central hub for the dispersal and sharing of geospatial data and services related to many fields,  including agriculture and aquaculture. It is integrated with interactive tools that support the exploration of maps, datasets and thematic layers related to land use, infrastructure, the environment and other spatial information categories. Currently, it hosts 26 maps of geo-localized data concerning hydrography, geology, land cover, land use, species distribution, agricultural and aquacultural facilities, and much more.
records.abstract: National Geospatial Information Infrastructure

_annotations.Impact: The ASIG Geoportal supports access to standardized geospatial data in Albania, enhancing transparency, efficiency and decision-making in many sectors, including urban planning, environmental protection and infrastructure development. Its alignment with the INSPIRE Directive offers interoperability and streamlined data sharing among institutions, and supports evidence-based governance, benefiting both public administration and private users.

records.title: Geo-spatial mapping of chestnut forests
records.description: FAO, with the support of Albanian State Authority for Geospatial Information, is developing a geo-spatial map of chestnut forests in the Tropoja region using high-resolution satellite imagery to monitor changes in land cover and forest health status over time. The initiative forms part of the “Sustainable Chestnut Value Chain Development” component of FAO’s  “One Country, One Priority Product” (OCOP) programme.
records.abstract: Remote sensing for the monitoring of changes in land cover and for tracking forest health status
records.owner_name: FAO; Albania’s Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development; Albania’s Ministry of Tourism and Environment; Tropoja’s local municipalities; Albania’s State Authority for Geospatial Information (ASIG)

_annotations.Impact: The project was launched in 2023, and so at the time of writing in November 2024 the project can still be considered too young for an impact assessment. The use of geospatial data in decision-making processes is expected to empower farmers and improve the management of chestnut resources. The utilization of such technologies as satellite imaging and GPS mapping helps in the precise measurement of chestnut cover in Tropoja, allowing the effective monitoring of large chestnut areas, the tracking of chestnut health, which is important given the presence of the Asian Chestnut Gall Wasp in the region, and the assessment of changes in land cover to climate change.

records.title: EU environmental information systems

records.abstract: In-depth information and data on specialized environmental topics

_annotations.Impact: As of November 2024, the EU Environmental Information Systems have gathered data from 38 member and cooperating countries and 400+ national partner institutions, with 200+ datasets and 295+ employees. The systems play a significant role in the EU environmental governance as a source of accurate and current data that informs policy decisions, ensures compliance and tracks environmental targets across the Member States.

records.title: Hepyerinden.coop
records.description: Hepyerinden.coop is an online marketplace designed within the scope of the Syrian Refugee Resilience Plan targeting the empowerment of women-led cooperatives in rural Türkiye by connecting them directly with consumers. Launched with support from the FAO and the European Union, the project promotes economic independence by allowing local cooperatives to market and sell handmade and agricultural products, such as preserves, dried fruit and cosmetics, across the country. The platform enhances the visibility of women producers, reduces intermediaries, and supports sustainable development by emphasizing local production and community resilience.
records.abstract: Cooperative-led online marketplace supporting women and Syrian refugees

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The online marketplace connects cooperatives and their member producers, facilitating the sale of local agricultural and artisanal products directly to consumers. It supports digital marketing by incorporating tools for branding, quality standardization and market expansion with particular focus on sustainable agriculture and community resilience. The digital infrastructure aids cooperatives in navigating modern trade dynamics, leveraging e-commerce to reach broader audiences while promoting Syrian refugees and the economic independence of women​.

records.title: Fascicolo aziendale
records.description: The “Fascicolo Aziendale”, or farm register, is a unique electronic database of farm-level data on each farm registered in Italy with a fiscal or TVA number, or that has been the recipient of EU, national or regional public subsidies or grants. The farm register is regulated by the European Union and national laws such as the national Circolare AGEA n. 67143 of 12 September 2023.  The farm register contains  primarily structural and infrastructural information, including 1) structural composition; 2) cultivation plans; 3) livestock composition; 4) intangible assets; 5) memberships of associations; and 6) listings on other registers and databases, including voluntary control systems supporting certification.
records.abstract: Electronic registry of farm information for statistics, administration and subsidies

_annotations.Impact: As of November 2024, the Italian farm register lists approximately 1.5 million farms covering around 13 million ha. of agricultural land. A digital dossier system is used to centralize essential information on each farm, such as ownership, land use, crop types and compliance with agricultural policies, and these records allow Italian and EU authorities to manage agricultural subsidies, conduct inspections and monitor environmental impacts. The farm registry data is regularly updated by farmers in collaboration with farmers’ associations (CAA), and is critical for Italy's compliance with the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) of the European Union and related administrative controls.

records.title: Developing digital marketing capacities
records.description: As part of the Digital Villages Initiative, FAO, with the support of local partner “Social Development Investment”, has provided training to Tropoja’s communities and rural businesses, with particular focus on women, young people and small-scale farmers, providing them with an understanding of the state-of-art opportunities offered by digital marketing. Under the so-called “Developing digital marketing capacities” training, customized capacity development sessions have been held for more than 15 rural businesses to increase their digital marketing skills, while ad hoc coaching has supported the upgrade or creation of new added-value services through digitalization. The intervention has further facilitated the creation of a community-driven brand to support the promotion of Tropoja’s food, community and territory to a wide audience.

records.title: EU Twinning Project in Montenegro
records.description: This EU Twinning project with the Republic of Montenegro is part of the Instrument for Pre-accession Assistance, aiming to strengthen the capacity of public administration in the agricultural and rural development sectors in line with the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP). The primary objective of this 30-month project is to gradually develop the agricultural sector in Montenegro to strengthen its position withing market forces, while progressively aligning the nation’s agricultural policy with the CAP and the EU legal framework in the field of agriculture and rural development (Chapter 11 of EU pre-accession negotiations). records.title: Watson
records.description: Under the Watson research and innovation project, Digital technologies are being designed and integrated into food supply chains in an attempt to tackle fraudulent practices in the food supply chain and to improve overall transparency for the benefit of both consumers and food authorities. The digital solutions are being tested and applied across six use cases in different European countries, each considering unique operational challenges and environments, and include: 1) tackling the counterfeiting of wine in Portugal; 2) preserving the authenticity of PGI honey in Spain; 3) ensuring the rapid traceability of extra virgin olive oil in Italy; 4) identifying possible manipulations at all stages of the meat chain in Germany; 5) improving the traceability of high-value products in the cereal and dairy chain in Finland; and 5) combating white fish counterfeiting in Norway.
records.abstract: Project using ICTs to tackle fraudulent practices in the food supply chain

_annotations.Impact: As of November 2024, the Watson project is still in its early stage. Overall, the research and innovation project aims to make food chains more sustainable by reducing food fraud and improving transparency through innovations in track-and-trace mechanisms to ensure the accuracy of food product information along the supply chain; by equipping authorities and policymakers with the necessary data and insights needed to monitor the entire food supply chain; and by increasing consumer awareness of food safety, promoting healthier lifestyles and supporting the development of greener and more sustainable food ecosystems.

records.title: CAP Area Monitoring Services
records.description: The “CAP (Common Agricultural Policy) Area Monitoring Services” platform offers customized Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem services, supporting the area monitoring system of the Member States within the scope of the CAP. The platform facilitates the checking of crops and cultivation on all agricultural parcels in an area of interest to determine whether farmers are fulfilling the commitments they made when requesting subsidies. Satellite imagery is used for the identification of parcels, the monitoring of cultivation stages and the identification of crop types. The platform can operate at a broad range of scales, from millions of parcels down to individual plots (pixels).
records.abstract: GIS-enabled services supporting the area-based monitoring of CAP interventions

_annotations.Impact: The CAP Area Monitoring Services provided by Copernicus are powerful tools supporting agricultural management and compliance monitoring within the European Union. The real-time monitoring of land use, crop conditions and environmental compliance is offered based on satellite data, allowing national authorities to accurately and efficiently ensure that farmers meet their CAP obligations. This remote-sensing capability reduces the need for on-site inspections, cutting down on administrative costs and increasing transparency and accountability in the distribution of subsidies. Farmers, on the other hand, benefit from the service through access to guidance on sustainable practices and the optimal use of resources, allowing them to meet environmental standards, and to respond proactively to such issues as drought or crop health concerns. Overall, CAP Area Monitoring Services have the potential to contribute to a more sustainable, data-driven agricultural sector, supporting the EU goals of environmental protection and food security.

records.title: Agridata space
records.description: AgriDataSpace is a multi-year project paving the way for a European agricultural data space and a common agri-data framework supporting standardization in the sharing, processing and analysis of data in a secure, trusted, transparent and responsible environment. The initial stages of the project will see the development of a framework, the establishment of partnerships and the creation of the necessary technical infrastructure, with the aim being to enter into full operation by the end of the 2020s. The project is providing new opportunities for the monitoring and optimization of natural resources and is stimulating data-driven innovations.
records.abstract: Project for the development of a European framework for a secure and trusted agricultural data space

_annotations.Impact: As of November 2024, there have been no assessments of the impacts achieved by the project, although the overall desired objective is to develop a conceptual reference architecture for a common agricultural data space and a reference technology canvas. The project seeks to enhance implementation and inclusivity, and to engage stakeholders in various evaluation and validation activities with the goal of reaching broad consensus on the development of a roadmap that complies with all requirements, and ultimately, the creation of a comprehensive plan for the creation of an agricultural data space for the European Union.

records.title: Information management system for official controls - IMSOC
records.description: The EU Information Management System for Official Controls (IMSOC) is an integrated electronic information system developed by the European Union to support and streamline official controls related to food safety, animal health, plant health and animal welfare in the Member States. IMSOC facilitates the exchange of information, documentation and notifications among EU countries and the European Commission, supporting the coordinated and efficient monitoring of compliance with EU regulations.
records.abstract: EU-integrated system ensuring compliance with agri-food chain rules

_annotations.Impact: IMSOC’s main impact is enhanced food safety, animal health and plant protection standards in the European Union. IMSOC has been developed as a data sharing, transparency and traceability solution for the European Union that brings together various systems (such as TRACES, RASFF and ADNS) within a single, coordinated platform, allowing the Member States to respond quickly and effectively to health risks, contamination events and disease outbreaks. This unified approach has reduced administrative burdens and has enabled the more consistent application of regulatory controls across the EU borders, preventing unsafe products from entering the food supply chain. Moreover, the rapid alert and notification mechanisms within IMSOC have facilitated faster and more coordinated responses to potential public health threats, improving risk management and boosting consumer confidence in the safety of EU food products. The system has also helped align import controls with EU standards, strengthening the oversight of products coming from outside the Block.

records.title: TRACES
records.description: The Trade Control and Expert System (TRACES) is an online platform operated by the European Union for the tracking of animal and plant health certification. Certificates are required for the import of animals, animal products, food and feed of non-animal origin and plants into the European Union, and for the intra-EU trade and EU exports of animals and certain animal products.
records.abstract: European Union’s online animal and plant health certification platform

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Each year, vast quantities of live animals and goods are traded within and outside the European Union for the benefit of over 440 million Europeans. As of November 2024, TRACES is in use in around 90 countries around the world by more than 113 000 users for the issuance of sanitary and phytosanitary certificates and official documents required for imports, intra-EU movements and exports from the European Union of animals and goods. The main impact of the TRACES system has been the streamlining of the certification process and entry procedures through the fully digitized and paperless workflow, in line with the European Commission’s policy priority: “A Europe fit for the digital age.

records.title: Europhyt
records.description: EUROPHYT, an amalgamation of the words “European” and “Phytosanitary”, is a notification and rapid alert system supporting the interception of plant consignments of plants and plant products imported into the European Union or traded within the European Union itself due to health concerns. EUROPHYT is an essential support tool for the implementation of preventative measures, ensuring that data on risks to plant health related to the trade of plants and plant products is up-to-date and accurate.
records.abstract: European Union Notification System for Plant Health Interceptions

_annotations.Impact: According to the latest annual report, in 2018, EUROPHYT issued 9053 notifications of interceptions of consignments due to non-conformities with EU requirements, of which 8720 were of non-EU origin. The total number of notifications reporting the presence of harmful organisms (HOs) exhibited an increase over the previous year, but was still lower than in 2014. Through the efficient sharing of data on non-compliant consignments and pest interceptions, EUROPHYT supports timely preventive actions, which may include quarantines or rejections, to prevent the spread of pests and diseases. The system supports coordinated efforts targeting the maintenance of plant health standards, the minimization of economic impacts on agriculture and the protection of the biodiversity of the Member States.

records.title: Animal Disease Information System
records.description: The EU Animal Diseases Information System (ADIS) is a tool for the registration and documentation of the infectious animal diseases identified by the Animal Health Law (AHL), allowing the evolution of outbreaks to be monitored. ADIS provides uniform conditions for the implementation of Union notification and reporting as provided by Regulation (EU) 2020/2002. It is a disease management tool that sends out alert notifications and detailed information about any significant animal disease outbreaks in the countries that are connected to the application.
records.abstract: European Union’s digital platform for the collection and analysis of animal health data

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: ADIS can support policymakers in making well-informed choices based on the most current and accurate information. ADIS is designed to reduce administrative burden and to ensure the consistency of data through efficient, one-time reporting by the EU Member States and the associated countries. The interconnection of ADIS and WAHIS brings several advantages, such as enhanced data quality and consistency on a global scale; streamlined notifications by Member States; and improved decision-making.

records.title: Organic Farming Information System
records.description: The Organic Farming Information System (OFIS) is a centralized database facilitating the exchange of information and notifications between the European Commission and the Member States, as requested in the latest legislation related to organic farming. One of the main roles of the system is to support the rapid notification of irregularities identified within the organic supply chain. OFIS gathers information on: 1) ingredient authorisations; 2) control authorities and control bodies in the European Union, the European Economic Area and Switzerland; and 3) control bodies and equivalence authorities. The EU Member States upload information on the current legislation related to organic farming. The OFIS database supports the exchange of agricultural data on organic products among the EU nations and the European Commission, as well as up-to-date information to the public.
records.abstract: Centralized database of current EU legislation pertaining to organic farming

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Electronic information systems like OFIS have the potential to increase consumer confidence in organic labelling, leading to a broader acceptance and willingness to pay for organic products. By standardizing and sharing certification information across the Member States, OFIS can simplify compliance checks, supporting the free movement of organic products within and outside the EU market, and thus reducing the bureaucratic barriers to organic farming and businesses. The system has also strengthened fraud detection and regulatory compliance through its inclusion of information on all Member States, supporting the rapid detection and remediation of non-compliances. The result is a more uniform enforcement of organic standards across the European Union and beyond.

OFIS gathers information on: 1) ingredient authorisations; 2) control authorities and control bodies in the European Union, the European Economic Area and Switzerland; and 3) control bodies and equivalence authorities. The EU Member States upload information on the current legislation related to organic farming. The OFIS database supports the exchange of agricultural data on organic products among the EU nations and the European Commission, as well as up-to-date information to the public.
_raw.Impact: Electronic information systems like OFIS have the potential to increase consumer confidence in organic labelling, leading to a broader acceptance and willingness to pay for organic products. By standardizing and sharing certification information across the Member States, OFIS can simplify compliance checks, supporting the free movement of organic products within and outside the EU market, and thus reducing the bureaucratic barriers to organic farming and businesses. The system has also strengthened fraud detection and regulatory compliance through its inclusion of information on all Member States, supporting the rapid detection and remediation of non-compliances. The result is a more uniform enforcement of organic standards across the European Union and beyond.

records.title: e-Submission Food Chain Platform
records.description: The e-Submission food chain platform is an electronic submission system through which applicants can submit applications online for the registration of novel and traditional foods within the European Union and non-EU countries. Novel and traditional foods are regulated within the European Union by Regulation (EU) 2015/2283, and the platform was established following the adoption of Regulation (EU) 2019/1381 on the transparency and sustainability of EU risk assessments in the food chain. Applicants can use the e-Submission food chain platform to follow up their applications, from submission to outcome.

records.title: Vineyard register
records.description: The Vineyard Register is a database of winegrowers in the EU Member States and pre-accession countries, containing details of their location, size, grape varieties and ownership. The register allows the European Union to monitor vineyard planting and removal, ensuring compliance with the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP). The Register was established in accordance with Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2019/934, and is an important tool supporting the implementation of the Common Market. The minimum information to be reported in the vineyard register is defined in Annex III to IV of this regulation. Member States are responsible for setting up their own internal systems, updating the vineyard register and providing regular reports to the European Commission.
records.abstract: Mandatory EU register of winegrowers and viticulture area(s)

_annotations.Impact: According to the integrated farm statistics announced by Eurostat based on data acquired from the vineyard registers of the Member States, there were 2.2 million vineyard holdings in the European Union in 2020, operating around 45 percent of the world’s wine-growing areas. The main expected impacts of the Vineyard Register are enhanced transparency and management by private and public actors such as the European, national and regional authorities in the supervision and regulation of the vineyard plantations and wine trade. By combining GIS with detailed vineyard registers, the European Union, its Member States and its pre-accession countries can efficiently manage vineyard data, monitor vineyard activities, support environmental protection and regulate the wine market within the block.

records.title: Integrated Administration and Control System (IACS)
records.description: The Integrated Administration and Control System (IACS) is a management tool used by the European Union to oversee the implementation of the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) in the Member States. The system is integrated with various administrative and control mechanisms including those dealing with agricultural subsidies (both area- and animal-based interventions), compliance with environmental regulations, and the eligibility of land parcels for support under CAP eco-schemes.
records.abstract: System overseeing the implementation of the EU Common Agricultural Policy

_annotations.Impact: The impacts of IACS relate to its individual components, as well as the sum of their integration. Overall, IACS helps prevent non-compliance by supporting beneficiaries in making accurate aid applications, thus protecting the financial interests of the European Union and supporting the implementation of national CAP Strategic Plans.

records.title: Land Parcel Identification System
records.description: The Land Parcel Identification System (LPIS) is a geographic information system used by EU Member States for the management and monitoring of agricultural land eligible for payments under the European Union’s Common Agricultural Policy (CAP). The LPIS serves as a spatial database of agricultural parcels that supports the accurate dispersal of farm subsidies while ensuring that land is being used according to EU agricultural policies. It was introduced to reduce fraud and ensure the integrity of CAP funding, offering benefits to farmers, environmental regulators and policymakers by improving the accuracy and traceability of agricultural data in the European Union.
records.abstract: GIS used by EU Member States for the management and monitoring of agricultural land eligible for payments

_annotations.Impact: Currently, over 135 million reference parcels are recorded in LPIS across the 27 EU Member States, helping to ensure eligibility for subsidies and compliance with environmental regulations. The total area registered in the LPIS covers a significant proportion of agricultural land in the European Union. The LPIS has shown itself to be invaluable for the verification of subsidy eligibility and compliance checks, contributing to a more accurate distribution of CAP funds, which amounted to approximately EUR 45.5 billion in 2015​. The system is also playing an increasing role in enforcing environmental standards, enhancing transparency, reducing errors and ensuring the proper allocation of EU funds while also supporting the development and application of environmental and land management policies.

records.title: Farm structure survey
records.description: Eurostat carries out a Farm Structure Survey (FSS) every 3 years to obtain reliable data on the structure of agricultural holdings in the European Union, contributing to the creation of a statistical database that can be used to assess the agricultural situation in the European Union. The survey results are used subsequently to monitor trends and transitions in the structure of European farms (agricultural holdings) and to support the management, evaluation and design of the environmental, economic and social aspects of the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP). The acquired farm structure data serves as quantitative evidence supporting the monitoring of several of the UN’s Sustainable Development Goals (SGDs) as part of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development adopted by the UN Member States in 2015.
records.abstract: Survey for the regular collection of reliable statistics on the structure of EU farms

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Eurostat has been collecting farm structure microdata in the European Union since 1990, both through an agricultural census (every 10 years) and sample surveys every 3 years. Some 1.7 million farms were included in the 2016 FSS, while in the 2010 agricultural census, data were collected from over 12.8 million farms, each of which provided data related to 250–400 variables. Farm structure data play a crucial role in policymaking as a key input when designing the CAP, which is managed and funded at an EU level using resources from the European Union’s budget. The acquired data also support policymakers in activities related to environment, regional development and climate change

records.title: CrowdFarming
records.description: CrowdFarming is an e-marketplace that connects producers and consumers in the provision of value-added logistics, transport packaging, customer relations and advertising services. The initiative supports the sale of seasonal products from organically certified producers and/or regenerative farmers, as well as the transition of farmers to organic farming.
records.abstract: E-marketplace connecting producers and consumers with delivery services

_annotations.Impact: The company reports that the CrowdFarming has contributed to an increase in the number of permanent workers in one-third of the producers that make use of the marketplace. As reported by the marketplace, more than 40 percent of participating farmers are young (aged <40 years), 283 farmers in 17 different countries are selling crops via CrowdFarming, and 216 088 consumers have registered active adoptions. It is reported that by the end of 2023, 13 600 consumers had ordered seasonal boxes.

records.title: e-Ambrosia
records.description: e-Ambrosia is the European Union’s official register of geographical indications for wine, spirits and agricultural products, helping verify the authenticity of the products by confirming they meet specific regional and quality standards. The register, guaranteeing the certification, transparency and protection of product names linked to specific locations, supports consumers and producers alike.
records.abstract: EU register of geographically indicated goods

_annotations.Impact: As of November 2024, the e-Ambrosia database is host to over 3300 registered geographically indicated products, including foods, wines, spirits and aromatized wines, all of which are protected under EU geographical indications regulations. Registration helps protect the unique characteristics, quality and reputation of products linked to specific locations and traditional production methods within the European Union through a legal framework that safeguards them from imitation and misuse. The e-Ambrosia platform has brought this information together in a single database, having been was previously scattered across three separate registers, simplifying access for producers, consumers and regulatory bodies alike. The overall goal of e-Ambrosia is to increase transparency, to reduce the administrative burden on registered operators, and to protect consumers and farmers engaged in high-quality production.

records.description: BeeConn is an electronic scale for beehive monitoring and beekeeping management. The wireless monitoring device allows beekeepers to monitor their apiaries, providing real-time information on the weight, temperature and relative humidity of the hives.

records.title: Farm Sustainability Tool for nutrients (FaST)
records.description: The FaST (Farm Sustainability Tool) platform, supported by the European Union, hosts digital tools that support sustainable nutrient management, making use of satellite data (from Copernicus and Galileo) in support of the agricultural and environmental initiatives under the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP). FaST supports decision-making, resource management and regulatory compliance among farmers, offering such features as satellite imagery, fertilization recommendations and climate data, and connects farmers, advisors and paying agencies for data sharing and the simplification of administrative processes. The platform has been established as part of the European “Farm to Fork” strategy – one of the central pillars of the European Green Deal. As part of the CAP support to Farm Advisory Services (Article 15.4(b) to the Regulation (EU) 2021/2115), EU countries are to make a Farm Sustainability Tool for nutrients (FaST) platform available to the farmers from 2024 at the latest.
records.abstract: Nutrient management platform

_annotations.Impact: As of November 2024, there is limited data on the use and impacts of the FaST platform. Its widespread use by the beneficiaries of nutrient management-related CAP interventions is expected to contribute to the objective of reducing fertiliser use by at least 20 percent and nutrient losses from both organic and mineral fertilisers by at least 50 percent by 2030, while ensuring no deterioration in soil fertility.

records.title: Bee Varroa Scanner (BeeVS)
records.description: BeeVS is an electronic scanner that is able to photograph beehive trays and count the number of varroa mites using a trained artificial intelligence (AI) algorithm. The scanner collects standard statistical data on the spread of varroa across the entire apiary, contributing to a reduction in the number of varroa treatments by limiting applications to families that show a critical infestation threshold; reducing the time needed to carry out checks; documenting the spread of varroa at an apiary level; and identifying varroa outbreaks at the beginning of the beekeeping season, thus avoiding the infestation of all colonies in the apiary.
records.abstract: AI-based scanner for counting Varroa destructors

_annotations.Impact: The website reports that as of September 2024, Bee Varroa Scanners had counted over 6 million varroa mites since their first adoption, scanned over 50 000 beehives and saved around 700 hours of manual work.

records.title: Farm Sustainability Data Network

records.title: Digitalization of official food safety control procedures
records.description: This good practice describes the experience of the Public Health Agency of Barcelona (ASPB) in its transition from a fully paper-based system to a digital-based system, bringing consistency and transparency to official food safety controls. As reported in 2021, the digital system comprises an electronic standardized compliance checklist that can be accessed via a web-based application and hardware devices (e.g. smartphones or tablets). The digital system records, analyses and facilitating communication among private and public food actors. The electronic standardized compliance checklist comprises up to 228 possible compliance questions (depending on subject), and the results of the inspection are shared immediately with the food business, along with any corrective actions required for non-compliances and action deadlines. The inspection results are stored on the cloud-based servers of the ASPB and can be analysed to support monitoring operations, thus contributing to the continuous improvement of the Barcelona food safety control system.
records.abstract: Electronic compliance checklist of official food safety control procedures

_annotations.Impact: FAO reports that the digital system has improved the consistency of controls, has increased communication between the food businesses and ASPB inspectors, and has contributed to an atmosphere of trust. The automation of processes based on pre-established rule-based instructions helps minimize errors, leading to savings in time. Furthermore, the problems encountered in understanding the handwriting of officers have been eliminated with the elimination of hand-written reports. Access to inspection reports has been made much easier than under the previous inspection system, supporting evidence-based analysis, monitoring, application and planning control activities. The transparent disclosure of inspection results benefits both food businesses and consumers in providing them with access to control-related information and data.

records.title: Tropoja
records.description: FAO is piloting the Digital Villages Initiative (DVI) in Tropoja, Albania under the TCP/RER/3905 “Digital Villages in Action” programme. FAO’s DVI readiness assessment of the villages in Tropoja  reports a digitalization status of “growing”, with high potential to move to a future “blossoming” status. A strong and accessible mobile internet connection can be found in most locations in the Tropoja villages, although variables such as speed and stability can vary depending on such factors as electricity stability; and the number of connected users, especially in the touristic season. Fixed broadband connectivity is limited due to the mountainous conditions. While most inhabitants own a smartphone, only a few households are equipped with computers or tablets, and these are predominantly families with young children. Smartphones are mostly used to access such social media platforms as WhatsApp, Instagram and TikTok, to access information or for human-to-human interactions.
records.abstract: Pilot village under the FAO Digital Villages Initiative (DVI)
records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The overall goal of this pilot DVI project in Tropoja is to enhance agricultural production, to facilitate access to rural services and, ultimately, to improve livelihoods in the region. To this end, the project seeks to increase the utilization of digital technologies in the Tropoja villages, and to leverage their local strengths to tackle the challenges they face. By the end of 2024, 15 rural businesses have benefited from capacity development programmes addressing such issues as digital marketing, while the municipality of Bajram Curri and other villages in the Tropoja have worked together on the development of a digital territorial brand. The project is being conducted in partnership with another flagship FAO initiative in the country – One Country One Priority Product – targeting improvements in the monitoring and resource management of chestnut forest resources through the creation of a GIS-based map of chestnut forests.

_raw.Description: FAO is piloting the Digital Villages Initiative (DVI) in Tropoja, Albania under the TCP/RER/3905 “Digital Villages in Action” programme. FAO’s DVI readiness assessment of the villages in Tropoja  reports a digitalization status of “growing”, with high potential to move to a future “blossoming” status. A strong and accessible mobile internet connection can be found in most locations in the Tropoja villages, although variables such as speed and stability can vary depending on such factors as electricity stability; and the number of connected users, especially in the touristic season. Fixed broadband connectivity is limited due to the mountainous conditions. While most inhabitants own a smartphone, only a few households are equipped with computers or tablets, and these are predominantly families with young children. Smartphones are mostly used to access such social media platforms as WhatsApp, Instagram and TikTok, to access information or for human-to-human interactions.
_raw.Impact: The overall goal of this pilot DVI project in Tropoja is to enhance agricultural production, to facilitate access to rural services and, ultimately, to improve livelihoods in the region. To this end, the project seeks to increase the utilization of digital technologies in the Tropoja villages, and to leverage their local strengths to tackle the challenges they face. By the end of 2024, 15 rural businesses have benefited from capacity development programmes addressing such issues as digital marketing, while the municipality of Bajram Curri and other villages in the Tropoja have worked together on the development of a digital territorial brand. The project is being conducted in partnership with another flagship FAO initiative in the country – One Country One Priority Product – targeting improvements in the monitoring and resource management of chestnut forest resources through the creation of a GIS-based map of chestnut forests.

records.title: European Digital Innovation Hubs Network
records.description: The European Digital Innovation Hubs (EDIHs) Network is a community of tech experts that work together in support of the digital transformation of Europe’s businesses and organizations.
