records.title: Agricultural Market Information System
records.description: The Agricultural Market Information System (AMIS) is an Information and communication technology (ICT)-based platform used by the European Commission, the Member States, and agri-food trading actors operating within and outside the European Union to report and access visual data related to agricultural markets, such as prices, production volume, and imports and exports. European Union countries communicate the data to the Commission, which makes the information available on its agri-food data portal and EU Market Observatories. As of November 2024, the existing agri-food data portal will be expanded to include the most recent indicators, making them available to all online, including, for example, data on the costs and margins associated with different stages of the food chain.
records.abstract: Platform for the monitoring and analysis of EU agri-food markets

_annotations.Impact: AMIS seeks to improve the knowledge and regulatory capacity of public authorities in the agri-food markets and to address the lack of market transparency and information asymmetries in the agri-food markets, especially during times of high price volatility and market crisis. AMIS is expected to contribute to efficiency in the markets, and to provide farmers and other agri-food actors with access to the most accurate data.

records.title: Chemometric Brain
records.description: Chemometric Brain is a cloud-based software that makes use of near-infrared (NIR) technologies and artificial intelligence (AI) for digitized quality control, fraud detection and production monitoring in the food sector. Chemometric Brain controls all the raw materials as they enter the factory and all batches of the final product that are manufactured.

_annotations.Impact: Chemometric Brain aims to enhance quality control processes in the food industry by improving the traceability and homogeneity of ingredients and products. Chemometric Brain facilitates real-time, accurate analysis, enabling companies to detect food fraud, ensure compliance and maintain high standards of food safety and quality. The success stories featured on the website report increased efficiency in quality control, a reduced need for specialized chemometric expertise and faster implementation of quality control processes.

records.title: Regional Technical Platform on Green Agriculture
records.description: The Regional Technical Platform on Green Agriculture (RTP GA) for Europe and Central Asia is a digital, user-friendly, open, intraregional and interregional gateway for the sharing of information, and a knowledge repository that facilitates connections among expert networks on various technical issues related to Green Agriculture. RTP GA presents exemplary models and experiences in the region and beyond related to different technical issues, ranging from Natural resources, biodiversity and green production, to the Green Supply Chain, Consumption, Food Loss and Waste and Cross-Cutting Areas.
records.abstract: Knowledge sharing platform
records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

_annotations.Impact: RTP GA represents the main body of governance related to mainstream Green Agriculture in Europe and Central Asia, and has three main objectives: 1) to share successful experiences and facilitate interregional exchanges of good practices – for which FAO and its development partners in the region have a comparative advantage related to technical areas of work relevant both to the region in question and other regions; 2) to build on existing regional-level technical networks to further develop, connect and strengthen regional and interregional technical networks; and 3) to create a knowledge repository containing key information on selected technical topics, focusing on normative work, projects, initiatives and programmes of FAO and its partners.

records.title: EX-ACT
records.description: The Environmental eXernalities ACccounting Tool (EX-ACT), known previously as the EX-Ante Carbon Balance Tool, provides decision-makers with the information necessary for the development of activities in support of international climate commitments and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The current version of the tool assesses greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and potential carbon sequestration from planned, ongoing or completed agrifood activities. EX-ACT has a broad scope, covering various agricultural sub-sectors, such as forestry, land use, coastal and inland wetlands, fisheries and aquaculture, the use of various agricultural inputs, and the construction of agricultural infrastructures.
records.abstract: Environmental externalities accounting web-tool
records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

_annotations.Impact: EX-ACT can support the identification of the climate mitigation outcomes of agricultural interventions; can aid countries (public and private sectors) in accessing funding from international financial institutions; strengthens the capacities of national and international stakeholders in estimating, monitoring and evaluating progress towards their emissions reduction goals; and supports policymakers in integrating climate change mitigation objectives into national strategies and international commitments, such as Nationally Determined Contributions or National Adaptation Plans.

records.title: ERPagro
records.description: ERPagro is an Enterprise Resource Planning software that supports the monitoring, management and optimization of the processes of agrifood companies and cooperatives, from seed to market. It is a modular system that supports decision-making based on a real-time analysis of agribusiness activities. ERPagro analyses various agricultural processes and production stages, including seedling and nursery operations, greenhouse and open-field activities, labour management, activity planning and execution, treatments, tasks, procurement, packing operations, accounting, salaries, marketing and sales, human resources, etc.

records.title: USAID Regional Water and Vulnerable Environment Activity
records.description: The United States Agency for International Development (USAID) Regional Water and Vulnerable Environment Activity seeks to strengthen regional capacity in support of the management of shared water resources, and to mitigate environmental risks in the Syr Darya and Amu Darya River basins. It further seeks to encourage the raising of a new generation of Central Asian professionals trained in the principles of integrated water resource management (IWRM) and the Water-Energy-Food-Environment (WEFE) Nexus, encouraging long-term sustainable water management and water cooperation at a basin level to spur economic growth in the region. At the core of the activity has been the establishment of a new metering system for measuring water flow, allowing the agency to make more accurate water allocations to agriculture, households and industry.
records.abstract: Regional capacity building for shared water resources management and the mitigation of environmental risks in Central Asia
records.owner_name: United States Agency for International Development (USAID)

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The project has enhanced the understanding of the Water-Energy-Food-Environment (WEFE) Nexus in Central Asia through the organization of 17 online lectures involving over 1000 specialists, and the provision of training to ten young researchers. It has led to the introduction of IWRM and WEFE Nexus curricula within regional universities and the launch of a Community of Practice e-platform (https://www.riverbp.net/eng/community_of_practice/). The overall impact has been the improvement of regional cooperation in the sustainable use of water resources, the mitigation of environmental risks in the Syr Darya and Amu Darya River Basins, and the development of 24 modelling scenarios for the Syr Darya River Basin in support of sustainable water usage.

records.title: LowCo
records.description: LowCo is a non-profit e-marketplace that connects local producers and artisans with consumers. The platform applies selection criteria to producers and artisans who want to join that can be either self-checked by the producers and artisans, or by ambassadors or producers who are already registered. The criteria are graphically represented by 12 badges that advise consumers when selecting products, including: 1) short-circuit products; 2) locally produced products; 3) locally transformed products; 4) products for local valorization; 5) products created within a circular economy; 6) zero waste products; 7) products without packaging; 8) fair trade products; 9) small scale trade; 10) agroecological products; 11) secondhand products; and 12) products with sustainability related labels.
records.abstract: Non-profit e-marketplace connecting local producers and artisans with consumers

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The organization reports that, by January 2023, more than 1600 producers in Belgium, including artisans and small-and medium-sized enterprises, had registered with the online marketplace and were benefitting from the online sale and communication channels. The online marketplace selection criteria seeks to support a vulnerable but sustainable segment of the market, offering space to small-scale and locally engaged enterprises and businesses.

records.description: The ‘‘How to ensure digital strategies benefit rural communities” briefing document offered suggestions of how the digital strategies being developed at different levels across Europe could be applied to meet the needs and ambitions of rural communities while achieving the objectives set out in the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) strategic plan. records.title: Smart Villages and rural digital transformation
records.description: The “Smart villages and rural transformation” document of the European Network for Rural Development supports those involved in the EU Rural Development Programme (RDPs), as well as other rural stakeholders, in the design and implementation of Smart Village initiatives in key policy domains (food, generational renewal, productivity, mobility, etc.). The document underlines the importance of the digital transformation of villages and rural areas, identifying five stages of village development on the journey to becoming a smart village: excluded, connected, engaged, experienced and player.

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The long-term aim of Smart Villages Strategies is not just to level the digital playing field and bridge the digital divide between rural communities and urban areas, but also to foster partnerships between cities and rural communities. Rural areas are thus encouraged to advance through the various stages of a genuine digital transformation – from digital isolation to connection – and to become digital players in their own right.

records.title: Strategy of agriculture & rural development of Ukraine - 2030
records.description: The “Strategy of agriculture & rural development of Ukraine (2030)” targets the development of a competitive, sustainable and diversified agrifood sector in the country in accordance with the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) of the European Union. The document lists seven strategic goals to be achieved by 2030: 1) increasing institutional capacity through the creation of an inclusive policy for the development of agriculture and rural areas; 2) achieving food security by ensuring public access to high-quality, nutritious and safe food products; 3) ensuring the sustainability of the agricultural sector, and a stable and fair income for producers, thus increasing their competitiveness; 4) demining and land reforms in support of the effective use of land; 5) climate change mitigation and adaptation through climate-oriented agriculture; 6) modernization of the agricultural sector through process development, innovation, digitization and knowledge exchange; and 7) the creation of necessary conditions for the development of rural areas. Each strategic goal is backed by a vision and a list of relevant sub-goals.

records.owner_name: The Ministry of Agrarian Policy and Food of Ukraine

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The strategy aims to strengthen institutional capacity, ensure food security, and contribute to the maintenance of a stable and fair income for producers, while also enhancing their competitiveness. It addresses such critical areas as land reform, demining, climate change mitigation and adaptation, the development of processing industries, innovation, digitalization and knowledge exchange, with particular emphasis on young farmers and entrepreneurship among women.

_raw.Description: The “Strategy of agriculture & rural development of Ukraine (2030)” targets the development of a competitive, sustainable and diversified agrifood sector in the country in accordance with the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) of the European Union. The document lists seven strategic goals to be achieved by 2030: 1) increasing institutional capacity through the creation of an inclusive policy for the development of agriculture and rural areas; 2) achieving food security by ensuring public access to high-quality, nutritious and safe food products; 3) ensuring the sustainability of the agricultural sector, and a stable and fair income for producers, thus increasing their competitiveness; 4) demining and land reforms in support of the effective use of land; 5) climate change mitigation and adaptation through climate-oriented agriculture; 6) modernization of the agricultural sector through process development, innovation, digitization and knowledge exchange; and 7) the creation of necessary conditions for the development of rural areas. Each strategic goal is backed by a vision and a list of relevant sub-goals.
_raw.Impact: The strategy aims to strengthen institutional capacity, ensure food security, and contribute to the maintenance of a stable and fair income for producers, while also enhancing their competitiveness. It addresses such critical areas as land reform, demining, climate change mitigation and adaptation, the development of processing industries, innovation, digitalization and knowledge exchange, with particular emphasis on young farmers and entrepreneurship among women.

records.title: Towards a Central Asia-as-a Platform Strategy and a Digital Solutions Centre for Sustainable Development
records.description: The “Towards a Central Asia-as-a-Platform Strategy and a Digital Solutions Centre for Sustainable Development” working paper sought to promote discussions among government officials, experts and regional stakeholders in Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and Mongolia on the digital readiness of each country. The subjects covered included the impact of global trends, and the digital policies, strategies and initiatives in place to respond to these trends, which were presented in three sections: key global and regional trends in the digital transformation, national and subnational digital initiatives, and the rationale of the Central Asia-as-a-Platform Strategy. In the field of digital agriculture, the document presents a strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats (SWOT) analysis of how digital technologies could be leveraged to transform agriculture in Central Asia.

records.title: The smart village concept: examples from Poland
records.description: “The smart village concept: examples from Poland” is an in-depth qualitative study of ten smart villages selected from among those included within the smart village initiative in Poland. The study assesses how digital technologies and innovations have been used in daily life in the village to enhance quality of life, to improve the standard of public services and to make better use of local resources. The study answered the following seven research questions: 1) How is the concept of smart villages understood by different groups of village residents (initiators, beneficiaries and local authorities)? 2) What mechanisms impact the de-marginalization of rural areas? 3) How should support for smart villages in the coming years be programmed? 4) What resources are necessary for the implementation of smart initiatives? 5) What is the impact of smart solutions on the surroundings? 6) What guarantees of sustainability do the solutions hold? 7) Are the concepts of smart villages and smart cities related in terms of meaning?
records.abstract: In-depth study of smart villages
records.owner_name: Polish Academy of Science, Institute of Rural and Agricultural Development (IRWiR PAN)

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: This in-depth study aims to make the idea of smart villages more understandable, and clarifies the importance of changes and choices for local communities. Smart villages in particular should raise awareness of sustainable development, reduce disparities between urban and rural areas, improve the quality of infrastructure and rural services, establish social ties and collaborations between inhabitants, and promote the digital transformation. Several recommendations are made at the end of the study that highlight the importance of Information and communication technologies (ICT) for digitally poor areas, as well as campaigns to improve local digital skills.

records.title: Agriculture Technology Program (AgTech)
records.description: The “Agriculture Technology Program (AgTech)” was launched to support farmers, veterinarians, agribusiness processors and input suppliers in increasing their access to vital training and equipment and strengthening their market linkages in the horticulture and dairy value chains. The project had two key components: 1) improved genetics, education and organization, increasing the incomes of private livestock/agribusinesses; and 2) skill development for private producers, processors and marketers of fruit and vegetables.
records.abstract: USAID programme supporting the development of private enterprises, and improving the productivity of private, small and household farms
records.owner_name: Weidemann Associates, Inc., A Crown Agents USA Company

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: AgTech procured the necessary equipment for the establishment of the artificial insemination training centres, identified a suitable feed mix and practical tools for the livestock component, and promoted the development of working relationships with local entrepreneurs and international organizations in the sector. To ensure the sustainability of the project outcomes, AgTech provided training to 65 local veterinarians and zoo technicians on bovine artificial insemination techniques and equipped them with the necessary toolkits for the provision of breeding services to the nation’s livestock owners. In the horticultural sector, the project addressed food security issues with a seminar on forage crops, irrigation technologies and best greenhouse practices, providing the participants with opportunities to exchange knowledge of agronomic techniques and plant protection in Turkmenistan.

records.title: Brožiai
records.description: Brožiai, a village in Klaipėda district municipality in Lithuania, was selected for a Smart Village project under the Smart Rural 27 initiative to address the decline in the local population and the migration of its young people to urban areas. The project targeted the development of horticulture and the promotion of a sustainable local food economy through the promotion of short food supply chains, community entrepreneurship and healthy food.
records.abstract: Short food supply chain model for Klaipėda district

_annotations.Impact: Some 17 new jobs were created in Brožiai Smart Village, making it a successful example of local community entrepreneurship based on the interest and support of local residents, and led to its success being recognized on a national scale. The Brožiai community subsequently developed plans to expand the programme through the establishment of an organic food supply chain to improve the distribution and sales of local organic products, as well as a food policy laboratory, thus transforming the project into a more advanced Smart Village strategy.

records.title: Smart Specialization Strategy of the Republic of Serbia 2020-2027
records.description: The Smart Specialization Strategy of the Republic of Serbia 2020–2027 has targeted the development of the country’s innovation and research ecosystem by directing future investments in specific priority areas. These include the “Food for the Future” priority, targeting an increase in added value in the food production chain, while the “Information and Communication Technologies (ICT)” priority seeks to spur the development of a domestic ICT market that makes use of custom software products. Under the “Future machines and manufacturing systems” priority, the Research and Development (R&D) capacities of the business sector are to be advanced through scientific-financial collaborations, while the “Creative Industries” priority targets the protection of intellectual property.
records.abstract: Innovation and the enhancement of the research ecosystem to guide investment in priority industrial areas
records.owner_name: Government of the Republic of Serbia

SDGs.value: SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

_annotations.Impact: Serbia’s target for 2027 is to transform its economy into one based on knowledge and innovation, enhanced competitiveness and an improved global supply chain position through the provision of targeted support in a number of key areas. In the specific area of food production, the strategy’s desired impact is to promote R&D in agriculture and the food sector through incentives, and to link the country’s fast-growing food production companies with the creative industries and ICT.

records.title: The Concept Note of Industrial Agriculture Development 2021 - 2030
records.description: The “Concept Note of Industrial Agriculture Development of the Republic of Kazakhstan for 2021–2030” policy document produced by the Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan is the precursor to the establishment of a roadmap for the modernization of the nation’s agricultural sector, offering a baseline assessment of different aspects of agriculture in the country, and highlighting the areas prioritized for development, including horticulture, animal husbandry, agri-food processing, markets, etc. Aside from the plans for innovation and modernization, the document details the private and governmental support to be provided for the promotion of digital agriculture, promoting standard approaches that make use of satellite imagery and remote sensing technologies to determine crop acreage, to improve the application of agrochemicals and to aid in soil surveys.
records.abstract: Policy document describing the agricultural sector, development plans and government support

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The policy document enhances food security and agricultural productivity through the integration of modern technologies and sustainable practices into agricultural production, measured against baseline assessments as benchmarks in support of the design and evaluation of agricultural policies. The document also presents an outline of the government programmes addressing such systemic challenges as water scarcity in agriculture, enhancing agricultural resilience, strengthening infrastructure and reducing crop yield losses.

records.title: Republic of Moldova Digital Transformation Strategy 2023-2030
records.description: The “Moldova Digital Transformation Strategy (MDTS)” is a public-centric document aimed at improving societal well-being through the digital transformation of the country’s economy and society. The strategy lists six general objectives to guide activities: the development of a digital society; the growth of a robust and competitive Information and Communication Technology (ICT) environment; the creation of an innovative and resilient digital economy; the establishment of an efficient, smart and transparent digital state; the creation of a secure, accessible and inclusive digital environment; and the promotion of the Republic of Moldova as a trusted and reliable digital nation. The strategy supports the efforts of the Republic of Moldova to become an integral part of the European Single Digital Market, contributing to the growth of rural areas and supporting innovation in agriculture.

records.title: Business models for rural services
records.description: The “Business Model for Rural Services” briefing document explores the different approaches that could be applied to enhance the provision of rural services in the European Union, and describes four such models: the private sector model, the public sector model, the third sector model and the partnership model. The document offers recommendations on the selection of the optimum business model for the provision of rural services along with some sample initiatives. The third sector model is particularly relevant to the agricultural sector, offering examples that include social enterprises run by women’s farmer organizations and those supporting the inclusion of older adults and young people targeting increased household incomes for farms. Among the other models, the private sector model could also be considered applicable to the agricultural sector in its ability to enhance short supply chain initiatives for small food firms.
records.abstract: Briefing describing business services models in Europe’s rural areas

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The selection of an appropriate business model can ease the access of users to relevant information, improve the territorial and spatial planning of rural services, and enhance partnerships and the provision of rural services by the private, public and third sectors.

records.title: Cyprus Smart Specialisation Strategy 2030
records.description: The Smart Specialisation Strategy 2023 is an update to the 2015 Strategy identifying the priority sectors and segments of the technological landscape in Cyprus. The strategy has been updated to take into account new trends and opportunities with particular focus on digital technologies and advanced (innovative) materials; ecosystems, including those related to the agrifood, renewable energy, and maritime and shipping sectors; emerging ecosystems, including the space sector; and finally, enablers, covering health and the environment. The strategy can be of particular benefit to the agricultural sector in expanding its limited technological capacity, and to the agrifood sector through the promotion of precision agriculture, automation and robotics, thus contributing to the more efficient use of resources and improved farm management.

records.title: IPARD III Programme for the Republic of Serbia for the period 2021-2027
records.description: The “IPARD III Programme for the Republic of Serbia for 2021–2027” is a multiannual programme targeting the achievement of European Union pre-accession standards in farming, rural development, food safety, animal welfare and environmental protection. The programme supports agricultural producers in marketing their products in the European Union, and supporting them in the management of European funding. The project promotes investments into the physical assets of agricultural concerns and physical property related to the processing and marketing of agricultural and fishery products, agri-environmental-climate and organic production measures, the implementation of local rural development strategies with a LEADER approach, investments into rural public infrastructures, the diversification of agricultural properties, and the development of operations and technical aid.

records.title: Digital Agriculture Strategy of Hungary (DAS)
records.description: Hungary's Digital Agriculture Strategy (DAS) was adopted in 2019 as an important component of Hungary’s Food Industry Concept 2017–2050. The strategy sought to enhance the profitability of agricultural production through the analysis of collected data, automation and the efficient use of resources, with three main targets: the development and digitization of precision farming, improved agricultural decision-making through the use of new technologies, and the development of product pathways involving digital solutions. The strategy also envisaged the improvement of digital skills among farmers through the Digital Agricultural Academy, Digital Village Programme and advisory systems.
records.abstract: Enhanced profitability of agricultural production through digitalization

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The DAS strategy sought to increase productivity and efficiency in agriculture. It was hypothesized that the measures laid out in the strategy would contribute directly to the rural digitalization and the dissemination of digital technology solutions and services among homes, backyard farms, the economy and public life, thus contributing to an improved quality of life in rural areas. The ultimate goals of the strategy were more profitable and sustainable agricultural production, the retention of farmers in the farming sector, and the promotion of agricultural production among the young rural population as a career choice. A review and evaluation of the strategy has been planned with support from the Neumann Technology platform with a view to identifying possible improvements.

records.title: The Dutch Digitalisation Strategy 2021
records.description: The Dutch Digitalization Strategy (DDS) 2021 is an update to the previous DDS for the post-COVID-19 period. It reports on the digitalization efforts in the Netherlands, outlining the key results and the developments achieved to date in multiple sectors, and provides an overview of the results achieved since the last edition of the DDS. The strategy is centred around six priority areas: artificial intelligence (AI), data, digital skills and inclusion, digital connectivity, digital resilience and digital government. In the agricultural and food domains, the strategy calls for investments in digital technologies based on agricultural sustainability programmes, including the scaling up of precision agriculture in the Netherlands through the National Living Lab for Precision Agriculture, as well as blockchain in support of sustainable food production.
records.abstract: Integrated approach to sectoral digitalization

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The updated digitalization strategy provides details of the efforts in support of digitalization. For example, the Netherlands has further expanded its role as a living lab through the launch of 5G field labs and workplaces in which entrepreneurs can innovate and experiment with digital technologies. The desired impacts of the strategy include the achievement of a safe and sustainable food supply, improved food safety and a reduction in the environmental footprint of agriculture. Also targeted are enhanced agricultural efficiency and sustainability, the adoption of smart agricultural practices and improvements to the management of natural resources.

records.title: ANTARES
records.description: The ANTARES project has targeted the transformation of the BioSense Institute in Novi Sad, Serbia, into an application-oriented, market-driven European Centre of Excellence (CoE) for advanced technologies in sustainable agriculture and food security. The project has focused on three pillars of sustainability, including a strong research infrastructure, necessitating the construction of a new building and the acquisition of state-of-the-art equipment, a dedicated human resources plan, and scientific excellence.

records.title: National Policy Reports
records.description: Series of National Policy Reports produced by the EU-funded DESIRA research project examining the national and regional policies applied across the EU Member States related to the digitalization of rural areas with a twin-pronged approach, assessing how digitalization policies impact rural areas, and how rural development policies address digitalization. The report is presented in three parts, defining the context of rural digitalization, the policy framework for rural digitalization, and the challenges and opportunities. At the time of writing (September 2024), the reports cover only 15 of the 27 EU Member States, with the addition of Scotland (UK).
records.abstract: Analysis of the effects of national and regional digitalization policies on rural areas
records.owner_name: Digitisation: Economic and Social Impacts in Rural Areas (DESIRA)

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The analysis carried out by DESIRA documents the digitalization efforts and private strategies of the EU Member States, and can aid in the identification of policy gaps and areas in need of improvement in the digital public infrastructure. The reports can serve as a benchmark for other countries, encouraging the enhancement of inclusive digitalization and the integration of digital technologies into “smart” and “precision agriculture", thus contributing to the alleviation of human impacts on the environment, biodiversity and climate.

records.title: European Union’s Farm to Fork Strategy
records.description: The Europe-wide Farm to Fork strategy is at the heart of the European Green Deal, which aims to make food systems fair, healthy and environmentally friendly, and to make Europe the first climate-neutral continent by 2050. The strategy focuses on four main pillars: sustainable food production, sustainable food processing and distribution, sustainable food consumption; and food loss and waste prevention.
records.abstract: Sustainable food system for Europe

_annotations.Impact: As of 2024, no assessment of the impacts of the strategy had been made. The Farm to Fork Strategy aims to accelerate the sustainable transition of the European Union’s food system into one with a neutral or positive environmental impact; that supports the mitigation of climate change and its impacts; that contributes to the return of lost biodiversity; that ensures food security, nutrition and public health; and that preserves the affordability of food while generating fair economic returns, thus contributing to the competitiveness of the supply sector and the promotion of fair trade in the European Union.

records.title: Foresight study - Farmers of the future
records.description: The “Farmers of the Future” study was carried out to investigate the different typologies of European farmers that will dominate in the medium and long term under different drivers and megatrends in agriculture in the European Union, such as climate change and resource scarcity, technological change, infrastructural issues and changes in food/dietary demands. The report presents an assessment of the European landscape in 2024 and the possible policy implications for the 12 defined farmer typologies: adaptive, corporate, intensive, patrimonial, controlled environment, cell, social care, lifestyle, regenerative, urban, serious and community-provisioning.
records.abstract: Study forecasting the future personas of farmers and future landscapes in the European context
records.owner_name: Joint Research Centre (JRC), the European Commission’s science and knowledge service

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The study raises awareness of the future of farmers and farming in the European Union and fosters discussions of appropriate policies in this regard. It has served as a useful policy framework bringing together different stakeholders – including members of the public and policymakers – for direct engagement in discussions of food policy issues. It aims to increase the understanding of digitalization in agriculture and rural areas and to analyse the potential consequences or pre-requisites.

records.title: Digital Development Strategy 2024 to 2030
records.description: The Digital Development Strategy (DDS) 2024–2030 is a policy framework developed by the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland that outlines a vision for the inclusive, responsible and sustainable digital transformation of developing countries, built around four interconnected objectives: Digital Transformation, catalysing the economy, government and society through digital technologies; Digital Inclusion, ensuring no one is left behind in the digital world; Digital Responsibility, ensuring a safe, secure and resilient digital environment; and Digital Sustainability, promoting the use of digital technologies in support of climate change and environmental efforts.
records.abstract: Promoting inclusiveness, responsibility and sustainability

_annotations.Country of origin: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The initiatives included within the policy aim to reduce emissions and mitigate environmental impacts: by improving resilience and responses to climate change and disasters; by improving information gathering, the targeted delivery of humanitarian assistance, and the development of smarter and more sustainable techniques and practices; and by getting more farmers and small-scale producers involved through digital advisory services. The promoted digital technologies are expected to improve the monitoring of climate, biodiversity and ecosystems by increasing the quantity of data collected from cheaper sensors and ensuring the necessary computing power for its interpretation.

records.title: The European Union’ Common Agricultural Policy (CAP)
records.description: The European Union applies different interventions under the Common Agricultural Policy 2023–2027 (CAP) in its efforts to make rural areas and agriculture more competitive and sustainable. Support for digitalization is just one of the cross-cutting objectives aimed at simplifying the delivery of the CAP, contributing to the achievement of the ten specific CAP 2023–2027 objectives. To promote the necessary investments in digital technologies, services and skills, the CAP Strategic plans of each of the 27 Member States include a tailored digital strategy detailing the specific needs and circumstances in each country. The aim in this regard is to create an appropriate environment in which farmers and rural communities can take advantage of digital technologies, including high-speed broadband infrastructure, information technologies, and digital tools and services. As a result, the productivity and income of farmers is increased, and living standards in rural communities are improved. The CAP plans of the Member States explain how they will make use of the available instruments, namely the Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF), the Digital Europe Programme, the Horizon Europe Programme, the Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) and the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF), in their digitalization strategies in agriculture and rural areas, from which they can benefit in synergy with their national funds. The Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) of the European Union, established in 1962, is a unified policy that is applicable to all EU countries.
records.abstract: Strategic national and pan-European plans for CAP interventions

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: In the 2014–2020 period, the resources of the CAP were directed towards the provision of high-speed technologies and improved internet services and infrastructures to 18 million rural citizens – equal to 6.4 percent of the rural population of the European Union. The 2023–2027 Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) of the European Union aims to stabilize the income of farmers through direct payments, to promote sustainable practices, to support rural development and to ensure food security. It has, however, faced challenges related to the environmental impacts of intensive farming, income inequality in payment distributions, market distortions affecting global trade and bureaucratic complexity. More information about how the CAP supports the digital transformation of rural areas can be found here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UvVqdNpRXgo&list=PLyMUk47rPuqq76B2nX2SoqMCf5lPgn_Ay&index=14&ab_channel=DigitalEU

records.title: Digital National Register
records.description: The Digital National Register of Moldovan Farmers is a digital database of farmers and agricultural enterprises operating in the country that seeks to simplify their access to resources, subsidies, information, training and technological solutions.
records.abstract: E-gov information system and database of farmers and agricultural enterprises
records.owner_name: Ministry of Agriculture and Food Industry of the Republic of Moldova

_annotations.Impact: The registry aims to contribute to improved agricultural practices, and thus to increase the nation’s agricultural productivity. Plans are in place to develop the register with the addition of data provided by farmers and relevant public institutions. Farmers can access the registry to find data about their operations and a wealth of other useful information, such as agricultural news, and recommendations on how to improve their agricultural operations in terms of efficiency and productivity. The data provided by the farmers can support the development of government policies based on evidence and the real needs of farmers. In the future, only registered farmers will have access the subsidies and other forms of financial aid offered by the government.

records.title: Cherkasy Region Development Strategy 2021-2027
records.description: The Cherkasy Region Development Strategy 2021–2027 envisions the development of the Cherkasky region as the centre of the Ukrainian identity and food security through the hosting of high-tech industries, innovative enterprises and modern infrastructures. The strategy is targeting different goals related to digital agriculture, as well as key policy interventions that include: 1) the establishment of digital transformation of the regional development management system, involving the automation of management processes and the digitalization of services, thereby increasing efficiency and transparency; 2) the introduction of modern standards to support community development management, including the development of general plans, the implementation of geolocation-based social networks, and the establishment of geoinformation systems to enhance spatial planning and urban cadastre management​; 3) the use of electronic tools for open government, thus promoting transparency through electronic tools such as public budgets and electronic petitions, making government activities more transparent and accessible to the public; 4) the development of the digital infrastructure, including the informatization of rural areas and tracking of municipal vehicles with a view to optimizing logistics and service delivery in the region; and finally, 5) educational and skills development through which local managers can receive training in modern communication and information technologies, project management, SCRUM and data processing, thus improving the digital literacy and management skills of local government​. For further information: https://strategy2027-ck.gov.ua/en/
records.abstract: Strategy to improve the well-being of the regional population, raising the quality of life and education of its citizens

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth
SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

_annotations.Impact: The strategy aims to drive economic growth and job creation, and to improve quality of life in the Cherkasy region through initiatives promoting entrepreneurship, innovation and infrastructure development. In the long-term, the strategy will strengthen the cooperation between scientific institutions and the financial sector in support of innovation, income growth and domestic and foreign investment. Concerning agriculture, the strategy aims to support the development of new technologies and the attainment of scientific patents related to the deep processing of agricultural products, and to attract grants from businesses for research and development related to marketing strategies, technologies and tools for the promotion of agricultural products, including organic products.

records.title: National Field Lab for Precision Farming (National Proeftuin Precisielandbouw)
records.description: The National Field Lab for Precision Farming (NPPL) was launched to promote the adoption of precision farming solutions in the farming community, for which a few farmers were selected each year and provided with assistance in the implementation of such farming solutions. Among the offered solutions were those supporting the precision fertilization of grassland; the identification and protection of bird nests and fauna in grasslands; precision irrigation; weed detection and selective control; variable rate applications of fungicides on potato crops and flower bulbs; and optimized path planning over arable fields. The invited farmers were provided with guidance and support for up to 3 years by independent experts who ensured that any bottlenecks they encountered were quickly resolved. Interested farmers were able to follow the participants' progress on the NPPL website and through demonstrations and on-farm meetings.
records.abstract: Project supporting the adoption and integration of precision farming technologies among farmers
records.owner_name: National Field Lab for Precision Farming (NPPL)

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The farmers benefited from the implementation of the digital precision agriculture solutions and the support provided by experts, who guided their startup projects for up to 3 years. Other farmers and stakeholders were able to learn from these entrepreneurs by following their progress on the NPPL website, from project-organized events and from published articles. The project sought to facilitate an increase in yields and a reduction in costs, while minimizing the environmental impact of farming and improving food quality by promoting best practices in precision agriculture.

records.title: Republic of Moldova Digital Development Country Profile
records.description: The “Digital Development Country Profile – Moldova” was compiled as part of the ITU Office for Europe’s comparative analysis of the digital transformation of priority countries in the European region, namely Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, the Republic of Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Ukraine. The report addresses digital transformation based on the various experiences of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) – the UN specialized agency for Information Communication Technologies (ICTs) – and other UN organizations, offering a broad overview of the activities and projects being implemented at a national level and in the wider region. It presents a five-building-block framework for the assessment of digital transformation from a variety of perspectives, providing an understanding of how the various dimensions of digital development interact at a country level, including: 1) meaningful connectivity as a foundation for digital development and transformation, 2) the people-centric digital transformation, 3) the government-centric digital transformation, 4) the sector-centric digital transformation, and 5) the digital-centric innovation ecosystem. The current status of digital agriculture is presented within the “Sector-centric digital transformation” section of the report, providing a detailed overview of the digital agricultural sector in the Republic of Moldova with particular focus on the information systems developed for the agro-industrial sector, including the Digital Agricultural Register; the State Animal Register; the System of Identification and Traceability of Animals; and the Automated Information System for Management of Strategic Sanitary-Veterinary Measures. The country is working towards the diversification of agricultural practices and the development of a national digital agriculture strategy to address specific sectoral challenges.
records.abstract: Analysis of the digital development status of the Republic of Moldova
records.owner_name: International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Regional Office for Europe

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The report provides a framework for discussions of digital development at a country level in the Republic of Moldova based on the five building blocks identified for the nation’s digital transformation, as well as information about the Republic of Moldova for each block based on the experiences and activities of ITU and other stakeholders operating in the country and the wider region. The report serves as a reference for discussions of digital development at a country level, providing details of the relevant activities, initiatives and projects developed by the involved UN agencies and their experiences in the digital transformation of the Republic of Moldova. Stakeholders are thus supported in making informed decisions regarding policies, investments and strategies related to ICTs, while dialogue and collaboration between government entities, the private sector, organizations, civil society groups and international partners are facilitated. The generation of coordinated and effective efforts are thus supported in the nation’s digital transformation, the setting of realistic targets, learning from best practices and adopting the successful strategies applied in peer countries.

records.title: Bulb Revolution 4.0 (Bollenrevolutie 4.0)
records.description: The Bulb Revolution 4.0 programme was supported under ”Vision Vitale Teelt 2030”  (Vital Cultivation Vision 2030) – the Dutch flower bulb sector's sustainability strategy – with the involvement of farmers, mechanization companies and technical researchers, and promoting the use of precision agriculture solutions in the flower bulb sector. Activities within the programme were grouped under five work packages: 1) BULBS 4.0 in the field, involving the development of an autonomous machine with multiple roles, but with particular focus on disease detection; 2) BULBS 4.0 in the barn related to processing operations, looking into methodologies for the detection of diseased or abnormal bulbs; 3) data management, assessing the need for monitoring and analysis within bulb cultivation operations and building an inventory of possible solutions and systems; 4) demonstration activities, involving engagements with entrepreneurs with a view to improving processes, garnering support and raising awareness; and 5) communications and project management, promoting the adoption of the Innovation Circle methodology already being used for interactions with entrepreneurs. The programme also explored solutions to the labour shortage, addressing the need for workers to carry out the intensive tasks in the field and shed during peak times.
records.abstract: Dutch Initiative focused on precision agriculture and technological developments in the bulb-growing sector
records.owner_name: Horticulture & Starting Materials of the Ministry of Agriculture, Nature and Food Quality

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Precision agriculture is highlighted as a key solution in the Vital Cultivation of Flower Bulbs 2030 Vision (the Dutch flower bulb sector's strategy for a sustainable future). The Bulb Revolution 4.0 project has facilitated the implementation and dissemination of knowledge through the involvement of companies, innovation circles and the farming community, the latter of which can install and test the offered digital solutions. The project has also targeted the dissemination of knowledge of the offered techniques and technologies, thus enhancing the sector in support of the Vital Cultivation vision.

records.title: Carbon Initiative for Climate-resilient Agriculture (CARBONICA)
records.description: The Carbon Initiative for Climate-resilient Agriculture project, known also as Carbonica, is a 4-year project (2023–2026) targeting the connection of the carbon farming innovation ecosystems of Greece, North Macedonia and Cyprus. The Carbonica Excellence Hub (CEH) established under the project was envisaged to bolster place-based innovation and excellence in the three countries, aiming to increase the collective understanding and uptake of carbon farming methods and thus reduce agricultural greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. The project targeted five main outcomes: 1) the establishment of a Joint Strategic E&I strategy including research priorities, themes, actions and focus areas for each country, as well those to be applied jointly, taking into consideration current challenges, research trends, stakeholder needs and current carbon farming policies; 2) the creation of a toolbox of carbon-farming solutions; 3) the creation of two lab prototypes – one as a carbon farming solution, and one as a carbon footprint accreditation/certification protocol; 4) the development of an e-learning platform covering such topics as carbon farming solutions, carbon footprint certification protocols, business development and policy design; and 5) the production of a single policy recommendation document for dissemination within the European Union.
records.abstract: Carbon innovations in farming ecosystems targeting reduced greenhouse gas emissions
records.owner_name: Foodscale Hub Greece Association for entrepreneurship and innovation Astiki Mi Kerdoskopiki Etaireia

_annotations.Impact: The impact of the project has been strongly related to the establishment of the Carbonica Excellence Hub (CEH) and the planned focus on long-term cross-border collaboration and strong viable linkages between the actors of the quadruple helix (policy, industry, academia and civil society) within the three innovation ecosystems, motivating knowledge transfer, sharpening entrepreneurial skills and expanding collective capacity in carbon farming. The project was also envisaged to support the creation of business opportunities related to carbon farming by bridging the gap between science and industry, establishing poles of attraction for innovators and investors, and improving the uptake of carbon farming methods.

records.title: Digitisation: Economic and Social Impacts in Rural Areas (DESIRA)
records.description: DESIRA was launched as a Horizon 2020 project under the coordination of the University of Pisa with the participation of 25 partner organizations (research institutes, NGOs and SMEs). The project was designed around seven Work Packages aimed at improving the capacity of society and political bodies to respond to the challenges associated with digitalization in agriculture, forestry and rural areas. DESIRA built on the Socio-Cyber-Physical Systems concept to provide a better understanding of the impact of digitalization. The project-specific objectives were listed as: to fill the gaps in socio-economic knowledge related to digitalization in agriculture, forestry and rural areas; to assess the past and current socio-economic impact of digitalization in regards to the SDGs; to improve the capacity of communities to prepare for the future risks and opportunities related to digitalization; to improve the capacity of rural communities to take advantage of the opportunities offered by digitalization, as well as their resilience to the associated risks; to promote online and offline interactions and the sharing of knowledge among a wide range of stakeholders; and to increase the uptake of societal concerns in ICT-related policy and innovation; and to align digitalization scenarios with societal needs and expectations. To this end, DESIRA made use of a network of “Living Labs (LL)” established in 20 European Regions and the EU Rural Digitization Forum to discuss the digitalization of agriculture, forestry and rural areas.
records.abstract: European project assessing the socio-economic impact of digitalization in rural areas

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: DESIRA has shown how digital solutions can be game-changers for rural areas, for example, in the fields of environmental risk management, supply chain transparency, the provision of public services and keeping agricultural activities alive in many rural contexts. The project has further identified barriers and constraints to digitalization in 20 local contexts, and has addressed specific local needs and expectations with a policy analysis and roadmap report. An ethical code has also been developed under the project that can serve as a guide for technology developers and policymakers alike. DESIRA has shown that despite the emphasis on sustainable digitalization and dedicated resources stressed in the European Union, national-level implementations are still falling short.

records.title: Digitalisation for sustainable agri-food systems: The Greek approach
records.description: The “Digitalisation for sustainable agri-food systems: The Greek approach” study describes the significant changes witnessed in the agricultural sector in Greece that led to volume constraints and stagnation in production value, rising production costs and a decline in gross value added. The study explains how digitalization can contribute to the sustainability of farming systems from an economic, social and environmental perspective by helping farmers produce more – and better – with less, while at the same time contributing to efforts to combat climate change. The Greek approach referred to in the study was a pioneering alliance at an EU level of the 72 leading agricultural cooperatives in Greece, the banking sector (the Piraeus Bank Group) and the IT sector (Neuropublic SA), all of which have contributed to the creation of the Gaiasense smart farming system. The system plays host to a broad range of information technologies and agronomy knowledge, adopting a holistic technological and business approach to the creation of a one-stop shop for a multitude of services in one location. Gaiasense was launched in 46 areas in Greece in 2019 for 30 different crops, with the intention of covering a total of 300 000 ha of farmland, amounting to approximately 10 percent of the arable land in Greece, by 2020.
records.abstract: Study on the use and impact of smart farming agriculture

_annotations.Impact: The “Digitalisation for sustainable agri-food systems: The Greek approach” resource has supported the use of smart farming technologies for the consistent reduction of the use of plant protection products, as well as production water and fertilizers, while also contributing to an increase in productivity and economic benefits (reduced inputs + productivity increase), and improvements in risk management and quality. Important results were achieved in the use of Gaiasense for nine crops (table and clingstone peaches, almonds, table grapes, pistachio nuts, olive trees, beans, potatoes and cotton) in the first 2 years of implementation. The study highlighted how the use of smart farming technologies could help farmers.

_raw.Short description: Study on the use and impact of smart farming agriculture

_raw.Description: The “Digitalisation for sustainable agri-food systems: The Greek approach” study describes the significant changes witnessed in the agricultural sector in Greece that led to volume constraints and stagnation in production value, rising production costs and a decline in gross value added. The study explains how digitalization can contribute to the sustainability of farming systems from an economic, social and environmental perspective by helping farmers produce more – and better – with less, while at the same time contributing to efforts to combat climate change. The Greek approach referred to in the study was a pioneering alliance at an EU level of the 72 leading agricultural cooperatives in Greece, the banking sector (the Piraeus Bank Group) and the IT sector (Neuropublic SA), all of which have contributed to the creation of the Gaiasense smart farming system. The system plays host to a broad range of information technologies and agronomy knowledge, adopting a holistic technological and business approach to the creation of a one-stop shop for a multitude of services in one location. Gaiasense was launched in 46 areas in Greece in 2019 for 30 different crops, with the intention of covering a total of 300 000 ha of farmland, amounting to approximately 10 percent of the arable land in Greece, by 2020.
_raw.Impact: The “Digitalisation for sustainable agri-food systems: The Greek approach” resource has supported the use of smart farming technologies for the consistent reduction of the use of plant protection products, as well as production water and fertilizers, while also contributing to an increase in productivity and economic benefits (reduced inputs + productivity increase), and improvements in risk management and quality. Important results were achieved in the use of Gaiasense for nine crops (table and clingstone peaches, almonds, table grapes, pistachio nuts, olive trees, beans, potatoes and cotton) in the first 2 years of implementation. The study highlighted how the use of smart farming technologies could help farmers.

records.title: Tomaszyn
records.description: Tomaszyn is a small village in the Warmia-Mazury province of Poland with ten households, where all landowners, villagers and farmers in the village are members, partners, or employees of the local Ostoja Natury cooperative.  Several projects have been launched in Tomaszyn since 2019 under the Smart Rural 27 initiative, including a Bio Hub ecosystem and a farm producing high-quality products, by partnerships of ecological and traditional producers in the Warmian-Masurian Voivodeship and beyond.

The primary objective of the smart village is to better organize farmers engaged in organic food production and to enhance their position in the production chain, leading to more stable and higher incomes. Furthermore, as it expands, Bio Hub is developing also as a facility for the storage, packaging and preparation of ecological products for the market. As a result, the multi-element sales and distribution sub-system is gaining strength, and as of October 2024, more than 50 local entities are included in the Bio Hub Producer’s Group.

records.title: Lormes
records.description: Lormes is a French village close to the Morvan Regional Nature Park in Burgundy with a population of around 1300. Although unemployment has never been a major problem, Lormes has faced the challenge of being an unattractive place to live. Its journey under the Smart Rural 27 initiative to become a smart village began in the early 2000s with the adoption of a ground-breaking territorial 2.0 policy to bring the economic and social potential of Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) and the internet to remote rural areas. Since then, the municipality has placed its support behind a number of different initiatives, such as a “digital mission” and “digital passport for all” programme supporting the digital integration of the local community and the provision of education to farmers, local businesses and public administrators, as well as the creation of a Rural Hub entitled “Portes du Morvan”, where the potential of local skills can be maximized through the provision of office space and IT support services.
records.abstract: Smart Villages Initiative supporting economic and social development through digital transformation

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Since its launch in 2008, the digital hub has been providing access to digital technologies in support of the local development of Lormes and the surrounding area. As of October 2024, some 2000 premises have been provided with access to the local fibre optic network.

records.title: Šmarje
records.description: Šmarje, a coastal village in Slovenia, is highly reliant on the port of Koper for access to services in support of its olive growing and winemaking operations, but faces such challenges as limited jobs, brain drain and poor internet access. This Smart Village, under the Smart Rural 27 initiative, was the first in the region to develop its own digitalization strategy, with initial focus on enhancing the internet access of the rural community through the creation of a network of wi-fi access points in the village. As part of their digital transformation, they established the Divina Wine Hub as a rural Digital Innovation platform, and the SmartAgroGrape digital platform for winegrowers in an attempt to reduce the burden of agriculture on the environment.
records.abstract: Smart Villages Initiative supporting olive oil and wine production through digital technologies

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Through SmartAgroGrape, around ten farms have taken part in training programmes and have transferred their own knowledge to the project stakeholders. Young winegrowers and winemakers make use of the available digital tools to optimize their vineyard management and to promote and sell their products. The attractiveness of the rural area as a place to live and work has been increased by the new forms of stakeholder involvement, bringing together policymakers, businesses, academia and civil society.

records.title: Cloughjordan
records.description: Cloughjordan Smart village is a community-led initiative in central Ireland to address the challenges of an aging population, a scarcity of local employment and the low uptake of digital technologies by local farmers. Under the Smart Rural 27 initiative, in 2008 the village of Cloughjordan launched the Cloughjordan Community Farm to promote local food and small-scale, community-supported agriculture. One of the smart initiatives established by the Cloughjordan Community Farm is the Open Food Hub, where the local farming and producer communities can sell their products through a digital platform – the Open Food Network – creating a direct connection between producers and consumers. The village has also developed the WeCreate Enterprise Centre – an incubation centre that supports digital fabrication projects in such areas as green buildings, renewable energy and local food – through which open-source hardware and software solutions that improve community resilience are shared.
records.abstract: Smart village initiative promoting renewable energy, local food security and collaborative digital solutions

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Remote collaborations that make use of digital platforms and softwares can have had a significant impact on local livelihoods in Cloughjordan ecovillage. Cloughjordan’s digital transformation has led to a reduction in work-related journeys, supported by the advent of collaborative platforms, and amplified by the pandemic response. This has contributed to a reduction in carbon emissions, a rural repopulation and a strengthening of local economies, as well as an improved quality of life.

records.title: Kythera
records.description: Kythera is one of the largest islands in Greece, and has an economy based primarily on tourism. Among the challenges faced by the island are the maintenance and attraction of new inhabitants, and the depletion and decreasing quality of water stocks (water, irrigation, drainage). Under the Smart Rural 27 initiative, a Smart Village strategy was launched in 2020 that included a “Sustainable Energy Action Plan”, a “Sustainable Urban Mobility Plan” and a “Water Resources Management Plan”. One of the main objectives of the Smart Village Strategy is to promote agricultural and environmental sustainability through the introduction of new agricultural technologies and smart farming solutions on the island.
records.abstract: Smart Village initiative promoting agricultural and environmental sustainability

_annotations.Impact: The Smart Village Strategy aims to enhance the production of local products, primarily olive oil, honey, and aromatic and medicinal plants, while promoting the preservation of Kythera’s landscapes, ecosystems and biodiversity. There is a further goal to increase the quality of tourism on the island by supporting alternative forms of tourism through the promotion of cultural heritage, the natural beauty of the island and local products.

records.title: Rhineland-Palatinate
records.description: Rhineland-Palatinate is an industrialized region in the west of Germany with a strong agricultural sector, linked mainly to wine production and characterized by smallholders farmers, that has been severely affected by demographic changes and rural depopulation. Under the Smart Rural 27 initiative, the Digital Villages Rhineland-Palatinate project was launched with the involvement of three municipalities: Eisenberg; Göllheim and Betzdorf-Gebhardshain. A living lab approach has been adopted for the project under which successful prototype digital solutions to local challenges are further developed by the Fraunhofer Technical Institute and other stakeholders.
records.abstract: Smart village initiative supporting the co-creation of cross-sectoral sustainable digital solutions
records.owner_name: Regional Ministry of Internal Affairs and Sports of Rhineland-Palatinate

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The project has led to the development of six digital apps linked to a unique IT platform that boasts nearly 130 000 users across Germany. The project has been scaled up to the national level, and more than 200 municipalities across Germany are now making use of the digital tools created by developers in the pilot phase. The Digital Villages initiative has also triggered the development of a new initiative named “smart regions” that supports the digitalization of larger territories.

records.title: Göttingen
records.description: Göttingen is composed of 12 municipalities with around 150 000 inhabitants, and has a mixed economy in which industry, academia, agriculture and forestry all play a part. Göttingen is facing the challenges associated with an aging population, limited agricultural revenues, high energy prices, dependency on external energy sources, and the high amount of agricultural residues and forest biomass that needs to be managed. Under the Smart Rural 27 initiative, the city is attempting to address these issues by launching the Bioenergy Villages initiative in Reiffenhausen, Barlissen, Wollbrandshausen and Krebeck – four villages with populations ranging from 300 to 800. The initiative foresees the development of a sustainable model in which the villages produce and consume biogas-sourced energy created from local agricultural residues under a circular economy approach. The model also foresees the establishment of a community-owned heating plant powered by forest biomass that can satisfy the village's heating needs.
records.abstract: Smart Village initiative promoting local biomass as a community-owned energy source

_annotations.Impact: Local farmers and communities have diversified their income through the sale of the energy produced from biogas. The project has also brought significant social, economic and environmental benefits by reducing carbon dioxide emissions, soil erosion and nitrate leaching, making the village more sustainable.

records.description: The Municipality of Babina Greda in eastern Croatia is strategically positioned close to major European routes, and has an economy that is dominated by agriculture and livestock farming. records.title: Alsunga
records.description: Alsunga is a village in Latvia's second smallest municipality with a local economy built on forests and agriculture. The home production and cultural heritage of the Alsunga region are popular among tourists, and are among Alsunga's economic specializations. However, the village is facing challenges to its economy due to the declining working-age population and a shortage of housing. To encourage residents to stay in Alsunga, a Smart Village Strategy has been implemented under the Smart Rural 27 initiative with particular focus on the development of small local businesses and a robust tourism strategy, for which a voluntary association named the Smart Village Action Group has been established.
records.abstract: Smart Villages initiative aimed at boosting the local economy and the retention of young people

_annotations.Impact: The strategy targets the development of local value-based small businesses and the retention of the village population. records.title: Ostana
records.description: Ostana is an Occitan multi-centric settlement in Po Valley in the north-western Alps, facing Monviso mountain in Italy. The village has for years suffered from severe depopulation, with a current population of only 50 permanent residents that increases to 500 with tourists and second-home owners during summer and peak seasons. Under the Smart Rural 27 initiative, in 2020 the village launched the “Smart Village Strategy of Ostana (Italy)” in an attempt to attract new qualified inhabitants to the area with different professional competencies, such as researchers, farmers and artists, through the promotion of cultural and social innovations as well as green economy initiatives. The Smart Village Strategy promotes collective and sustainable forest management and local wood supply chain valorization.

The Smart Village Strategy of Ostana aims to promote the sustainable management of natural resources, leading to new job opportunities, while at the same time increasing landscape value and climate resilience.

records.title: Oliete
records.description: Oliete, a village in Aragon in Teruel province in the Andorra-Sierra de Arcos region of Spain, has an abundance of olive groves, some 70 percent of which were identified as abandoned in 2014. Under the Smart Rural 27 initiative, and inspired by the Scottish Highlands' rural model and ApadrinaUnOlivo.org, the village of Oliete has been using information and communication technologies (ICT) to promote the adoption and protection of the olive trees. Pilot Rural Awakeners Centres have been created through a partnership of Oliete City Council and other local entities, and are serving as entrepreneurship hubs that combine various rural development methodologies and foster capacity building in the use of ICT.

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The Smart Rural Awakener Centre seeks to create sustainable business opportunities, and to show that rural areas have a future by leveraging their resources and utilizing the available ICT and digital tools and local capabilities. The apadrinaunolivo.org initiative has recovered 100,000 abandoned centenary olive trees since 2014 through the adoption of an environmental, social and sustainable rural development approach.

The apadrinaunolivo.org initiative has recovered 100,000 abandoned centenary olive trees since 2014 through the adoption of an environmental, social and sustainable rural development approach.

records.title: Vila Boa do Bispo
records.description: The village of Vila Boa do Bispo is a parish council in northern Portugal within the Marco de Canaveses municipality that is experiencing issues related to climate change (forest fires, heavy rainfall, lack of potable water) and energy poverty. Under the Smart Rural 27 project, the village is attempting to address these challenges by focusing on Smart Community-Building, Sustainable Governance and the Circular Economy. The municipality has launched the VBBZERO strategy in an attempt to transform the town into a carbon-neutral community, and is implementing several key initiatives to this end, such as OMNIA – a knowledge and skills development initiative in which innovative green entrepreneurship models are adopted for NEETs (Not in Education, Employment or Training) in support of the circular economy, and DESUWOW – supporting the Development of professional Skills for the use of Urban solid Wastes and Organic Wastes in agriculture.
records.abstract: First carbon-neutral Freguesia (community) in the northern region

SDGs.value: SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

_annotations.Impact: Vila Boa do Bispo is seeking to become the first carbon-neutral Freguesia (community) in Portugal, and to create a system in which everything is integrated within a circular model (from clothes to construction materials). In addition, it aims to enhance tourism and the local culture, promote sustainability, improve transportation, advance education, and support entrepreneurship and job creation. The OMNIA project is seeking to attract the involvement of at least 180 participants and 30 partners.

records.title: Nätradalen
records.description: Nätradalen is a valley in Sweden that is host to the towns and islands of Sidensjö, Bjästa, Köpmanholmen, Strängöarna, Trysunda and Ulvön, with a combined population of approximately 6400 permanent residents, and a very clear connection to the Höga Kusten (The High Coast) United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) World Heritage site. The Bygdsam Nätradalen organization is a collaboration of representatives from the business community, civil society organizations and the municipality that was established to promote Nätradalen’s cultural heritage and to make it a more attractive place to both live and work. Operating under the Smart Rural 27 initiative, the organization has launched several activities, including free training courses for entrepreneurs and business associations, covering such topics as social media marketing. Bygdsam Nätradalen is also host to a social enterprise that helps people back into the labour market return through on-the-job training, rehabilitation courses and internships, working in collaboration with various agencies and partners.

By simplifying the process for small producers to reach out with their local products, the platform strengthens their brand and helps them sustain their activities.
