records.title: North-Western Kuhmo
records.description: North-Western Kuhmo is a scarcely populated area in the central Kainuu region of Finland that has an economy based primarily on forestry and agriculture, while the information society and public services are all but absent. Electricity is needed to power public services systems, therefore, as part of the Smart Rural 27 initiative, the village and a local cooperative decided to look into more sustainable solutions to manage energy supply, and the establishment of a fibre network incorporated with easy-to-use sensor equipment. Studies were launched into the use of renewable energy sources, more specifically photovoltaics and/or wind turbines, for the vulnerable village, increasing the resilience of the village through the provision of a democratic and open network for use in times of crisis.
records.abstract: Increased resilience through the establishment of a democratic and open fibre network in Kainuu

_annotations.Impact: The Northwest-Kuhmo Village fibre-optic network and off-grid photovoltaic system ensure access to reliable communication channels and energy sources, which are vital in times of crises, supporting also local businesses, particularly those engaged in forestry and agriculture. The democratic and inclusive network promotes community engagement and sustainable development, although not without challenges related to the high initial costs, the maintenance requirements and the potential technological barriers. Overall, the project aims to improve the quality of life in the region, contributing also to economic stability.

records.title: Diksmuide
records.description: Diksmuide is a municipality in the province of West Flanders comprising Diksmuide and its 14 communes. The main economic activity in the region is dairy farming, and the famous Diksmuide butter. The ticket office of the train station in Diksmuide closed in 2021 and had a marked impact on the local community until a local organization decided to repurpose the train station in 2023 under the Smart Rural 27 initiative. The proposed smart solution has multiple features, including skills training, marketing local food, digital support and bike services.
records.abstract: Repurposing the train station in Diksmuide into a multifunctional hub and promoting local food products in West Flanders

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The primary goal of the initiative is to integrate the social economy into everyday community life in a way that is both visible and accessible. It aims to rehabilitate those outside the labour market through employment opportunities and skills development, supporting their reintegration into society. Additionally, the initiative seeks to provide a direct connection between local agriculture and consumers by centralizing sales of fresh, local products through accessible platforms. This approach supports local farmers and ensures the provision of high-quality, sustainable products to the market. Ultimately, the initiative strives to create a more inclusive, supportive and interconnected environment for all.

records.title: Mouans-Sartoux
records.description: Mouans-Sartoux is a small town on the French Riviera in southeastern France that encountered an issue in the 2000s related to the lack of local organic agriculture. Under the Smart Rural 27 initiative, a 6 Ha municipal farm was created in 2010 to promote the local cultivation of food and the supply of school canteens, and members of the public have also been contributing to the local cultivation of food through self-production. The Centre for Sustainable Food Education (Maison d’Éducation à l’Alimentation Durable - MEAD), launched by the municipality in 2016, spearheads the development and strengthening of sustainable food and agriculture on the municipality’s territory, and oversaw the development of the Mouans-Sartoux food strategy (2020–2022), addressing economic, social, environmental and governance issues. The main goal in the reinvention of Mouans-Sartoux as a “smart village” is to increase the use of digital solutions, as key factors in the town’s sustainable food project.
records.abstract: Promoting local food and supply school canteens in the South-East Riviera

_annotations.Impact: Mouans-Sartoux has launched an ambitious and advanced food project that is supported by the local community and has been recognized at both a national and international level. It is the first French town to boast 100 percent organic school canteens, from nurseries up to middle school (since 2012 for nurseries, kindergartens and primary schools, and since November 2019 for middle schools) and to set up a municipal farm that provides 85 percent of the vegetables used in school.

records.title: Baix Solsonès
records.description: Baix Solsonès is a rural area with strong farming traditions and a few densely populated centres. Territori de Masies is a rural cooperative through which residents, associations and companies from the towns of Baix Solsonès work to promote and protect the region’s culture and traditions. Several projects are carried out by the cooperative under the Smart Rural 27 project, including the collective purchase of solar panels to boost self-sufficiency in energy production; the creation of a cultural tourist route to encourage people to discover the territory; an online store for the sale of local products; and the organization of fairs, meetings and events for the promotion of the territory.

_annotations.Impact: The village has been promoting and protecting the region's traditional ways of life, landscapes and rural culture through the promotion of six agrotourism itineraries, engagement with farms and the organization of other local activities.

records.title: Arvieu
records.description: Arvieu is a small village in France’s Occitanie region with a rich heritage that is under threat from desertification and a lack of opportunities. Under the Smart Rural 27 initiative, the Laëtis digital cooperative in the 2000s started to reverse the desertification of rural areas through the creation of the digital third-place “Le Jardin d’Arvieu”, with the participation of the general public and a public-private partnership involving local institutions and Laëtis.

records.title: Alsómocsolád
records.description: Alsómocsolád is a settlement in the northern corner of Baranya County in southern Hungary that is experiencing an aging population and the outmigration of young people seeking a better life, leading to a continuous population decline. A liveable settlement has been created under the Smart Rural 27 initiative with the development of the village’s public utilities, telecommunications and IT connections. The village has also committed to a switch to renewable energy in support of energy efficiency and climate protection, and the recreation of its traditional assets through an “Eat our own bread” programme.
records.abstract: Addressing the declining population in Alsómocsolád, Baranya County

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The village has for 32 years been working to create a municipality with a developed infrastructure and active population.  Through the “Eat our own bread” Economic Development Programme, local farming opportunities are promoted encouraging the use of existing small gardens, farm buildings and assets, as well as local forests, fields and arable land by members of the public in a sustainable way.

records.title: Čierny Balog
records.description: The economy of the eight settlements Krám, Medveďov, Balog, Fajtov, Jánošovka, Komov, Pustô, Dobroč that make up the village of Čierny Balog is historically linked to forestry and timber– its extraction, processing and transport – as well as coal mining. Under the Smart Rural 27 project, an association called Bioenergia Bystricka was established to run a pilot project between 2011 and 2012 investigating the use of the large amount of locally produced secondary wood materials for the generation of energy in Čierny Balog, facilitating the switch from coal to biomass.
records.abstract: Support for renewable energy and the bioeconomy

_annotations.Impact: According to 2021 data, the self-sufficient heating system has reduced the cost of heating public buildings by 20–30%, with the further benefits of reduced CO2 emissions and a cleaner working environment.

records.description:
Tílos is a small Greek island and municipality in the Aegean Sea, and is the first energy-efficient island in
Greece. Under the Smart Rural 27 initiative, an innovative hybrid system is being developed and operated
on the island that makes use of solar and wind energy. An energy storage system covers the electricity
needs of the inhabitants of the village of Livadia (approx. 500 inhabitants).

records.title: Molenlanden
records.description: Under the Smart Rural 27 initiative, Molenlanden – an inner periphery municipality of Rotterdam in the Netherlands – is aiming to become greener through improvements to its waste management operations, and by increasing its reliance on sustainable energy, with the overarching goal of becoming a climate-proof region. The village, supported by the Foundation Sustainable Molenlanden, promotes initiatives and projects in four areas: energy transition, biodiversity, climate adaptation and circularity. Nature, the community and digitalization are the main targets of the initiative.
records.abstract: Promoting energy transition, biodiversity, climate adaptation and circular economy

_annotations.Impact: The initiative seeks to promote the transition to sustainable energy and reduced CO2 emissions, and to bring biodiversity to the local gardens and streets, allowing the settlement to absorb the increased rainfall that has come with the changing climate, to minimize heat stresses, and to play host to more insects and birds. As an overall impact, Molenlanden envisages a greener community, sustainable houses that use sustainable energy, and a climate-proof region.

records.title: Baia dei Gelsomini
records.description: The Baia dei Gelsomini is a touristic community of around 130 houses in Palizzi Marina at the southernmost point of the Italian peninsula, comprising mostly holiday houses but with a few residents and some agricultural activity. The community is situated in a region that is highly vulnerable to energy poverty but with a favourable climate to produce renewable solar energy. The village is currently engaged in the establishment of a renewable energy community under the Smart Rural 27 initiative. At the time of writing in 2024, a feasibility study is underway as part of the Rural Energy Community Advisory Hub (RECAH) project investigating photovoltaic production.
records.abstract: Renewable Energy Community (REC) in Calabria Region

_annotations.Impact: The main goal of the project is energy independence and the full decarbonization of the energy used for the operation of the wastewater treatment plant, street lighting, and the pumping, storage and distribution of drinking water. Ultimately, the aim is to secure a convenient source of renewable energy with competitive generation and distribution costs for all members of the community, including residents, small local farmers and the municipality.

records.title: Smart Villages in Finland
records.description: The “Smart Villages in Finland: ideas for designing support in the future CAP Strategic Plans” resource introduces the main ideas presented at the 9th meeting of the Thematic Group (TG) on Smart Villages, held in Finland on 20–21 November 2019. The document highlights the steps needed to support Smart Villages in the future Strategic Plan (SP) under the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), including: 1) Identifying the needs of rural communities, 2) Mapping the existing policy support framework, and 3) Designing a targeted package of interventions.
records.abstract: Ideas for designing support in the future CAP Strategic Plans

_annotations.Impact: Interventions designed to support Smart Villages target the development of broadband infrastructures in rural areas, the enhancement of the quality and reliability of services, and efforts to improve the dissemination of knowledge, thus boosting digital literacy and changing attitudes towards technology. Such interventions also aim to encourage stronger cooperation, communication and interaction among stakeholders, both within and between regions, as well as the integration of new arrivals (immigrants) and young people. There is also a stated aim to create a team of Smart Village Innovation Brokers who can improve the access of rural communities to specialized knowledge in areas such as digital technologies, energy, mobility, service innovations, etc.

records.title: Älvbyarna
records.description: Älvbyarna, meaning "the River Villages", is a cluster of six smart villages – Veikars, Anixor, Voitby, Martois, Staversby and Miekka on the Kyrö River in Korsholm, Finland. Since 2023 the villages have been piloting local energy solutions under the Smart Rural 27 initiative with the long-term goal of creating a smart food hub that brings together, educates and inspires local people to follow a sustainable way of life.

_annotations.Impact: The Älvbyarna villages project aims to reduce the carbon footprint of the local area through the promotion of sustainable practices, while empowering the community, especially young people and small-scale farmers, in the adoption of green solutions.

records.title: Castelo Rodrigo
records.description: Castelo Rodrigo smart village, part of the Smart Rural 27 initiative, is one of the 12 villages in the Network of Historical Villages covered by the Portugal Collective Efficiency Strategy (CES), a policy instrument under the EU Cohesion Policy for the economic development of low-density territories. The CES responds to the need to diversify and strengthen entrepreneurship associated with rural innovation and to promote innovation in tourism. Strategies have been put in place in Castelo Rodrigo to support the transition to a green economy, and to promote such aspects of the local culture as recipes, cooking methods and traditional products, contributing to the preservation of regional dishes and the promotion of the local hospitality.

_annotations.Impact: The transition of the village into a smart destination would seem to have improved the quality of life of the residents, while also enhancing the experience of visiting tourists and the working conditions of professionals employed in the territory.

records.title: Smart Villages in Poland
records.description: The “Smart Villages in Poland: ideas for designing support in the future CAP Strategic Plans” briefing introduced the main suggestions of how the design of Smart Villages could be supported in future Strategic Plans (SP) under the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) in Poland. According to the briefing, Member States should apply the following procedure when deciding on the support to be provided to Smart Villages: 1) Identify the needs of the rural communities of potential Smart Villages, 2) Analyse the existing policy support framework to identify any opportunities and gaps; and 3) Compile a targeted package of interventions that wouldallow rural communities to take an initial idea for change through to its sustainable scale-up.
records.abstract: Ideas for designing support in the future CAP Strategic Plans

_annotations.Impact: Internet access and digital skills in Poland are lower in rural areas, but are essential for rural development in many fields. The careful design of interventions in support of Smart Villages will allow them to respond in a fast and flexible manner to the economic, social and environmental needs of local communities. Such an approach will avoid duplications with existing structures and strategies and policy support tools, will advise what worked and what did not in previous applications, and will aid in the design of targeted interventions.

records.title: Košeca
records.description: Košeca is a village and municipality in Ilava District in the Trenčín Region of north-western Slovakia that has been struggling with the issue of inadequate waste disposal and the lack of motivation among residents to recycle their waste. A waste tracking system has been launched under the Smart Rural 27 initiative to monitor the amount and types of the produced waste.
records.abstract: Smart village in Ilava District with a sustainable waste management system

_annotations.Impact: The application of the waste management system has led to a decline in the amount of unrecycled waste produced by Košeca, improving the way of life in the village, while responsible citizens have benefitted from lower bills. In this regard, the benefits to rural community have been both ecological and economic.

records.title: Sabugu
records.description: The Sabugueiro Digital Village is a smart mountain village in Seia Municipality in Central Portugal and it is the first Smart mountain village designated under the Smart Rural 27 initiative. Sabugueiro has been facing the issue of poor connectivity and limited potentialities and socio-economic assets due to its mountain location and rural context. Drawing upon support from the Vodafone Foundation, three solutions have been implemented to address these issues.
records.abstract: Improving water and energy consumption in Serra da Estrela

_annotations.Impact: The project has led to a 12 percent reduction in water losses from the distribution network, while in terms of improving energy efficiency, the new energy measuring devices have shown a daily energy consumption reduction of 8.8% compared to the previous public lighting system. Overall, the project has contributed to the economic development and environmental performance of this rural village, while also improving the quality of life of the community.

records.title: National Strategic Plan for Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) 2023–2027
records.description: The National Strategic Plan for the Common Agricultural Policy 2023–2027 (PSP) (orig. Piano Strategico Nazionale per la Politica Agricola Comune [PAC]) is a strategic plan targeting the modernization of the Italian agricultural sector through various initiatives, some of which are digital. Within the plan, 23 out of the 77 rural development interventions listed are focused on digitalization, including technological support concerning agricultural, environmental and climate  measures, investments into material and non-material assets, investments for attracting new farmers  , cooperation, and integrated interventions   for the dissemination of knowledge and innovations.
records.abstract: Strategy for the modernization of the Italian agricultural sector through digitalization
records.owner_name: Ministry of Agriculture, Food Sovereignty and Forestry of Italy

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The policy aims to contribute to three main areas: 1) The reduction of the digital divide, through which the unequal digital access of different regions and agricultural enterprises will be resolved and equal access to opportunities for all stakeholders will be ensured; 2) increased data utilization, contributing to the improvement of decision-making processes and resource management in agriculture, and 3) the development of digitized entrepreneurial models, aimed at enhancing the competitiveness and sustainability of agricultural enterprises.  Overall, the plan addresses such challenges as the limited digital infrastructure, data scarcity and the uneven technology uptake of different regions, and stresses the importance of the adoption of technologies for competitiveness, sustainability and rural development. In this way, it seeks to unlock economic opportunities, improve resource management and enhance overall agricultural resilience.

records.title: How to support Smart Villages strategies which effectively empower rural communities?
records.description: The “How to support Smart Villages strategies that effectively empower rural communities” document provides preliminary orientations on the support provided to Smart Villages during and after the 2020 Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) programming period (2014–2020). The document draws from the discussions of national and regional policy-makers and implementers involved in the ENRD Thematic Group on Smart Villages. The resource outlines the key elements of the Smart Villages Strategy, being the presence of an active group of citizens, a community vision, the identification of new and innovative solutions, a road map of interventions, soft investments, long-term financial sustainability and linkages with other strategies.
records.abstract: Orientations for policy-makers and implementers

_annotations.Impact: The briefing document aims to support national and regional policymakers and to help rural communities in the effective implementation of Smart Village Strategies, supporting them in tackling their unique challenges and empowering local communities in the testing and application of innovative solutions to broader societal challenges.

records.title: Killeedy
records.description: Launched under the Smart Rural 27 initiative, the Killeedy Smart Village project encouraged infrastructural investments and the development of governance tools to meet the community needs of two small Irish villages in County Limerick in such areas as wastewater treatment and renewable energy with wind turbines, in accordance with the Killeedy Parish Plan 2019–2022 and the Energy Master Plan. The smart village project was launched to address the issue of the dwindling village populations and the direct impact on housing availability due to the creation of new businesses to attract new inhabitants. Applying a smart village approach, the community established the necessary infrastructure to meet housing needs and comprised three main components: establishing an Enterprise Park to accommodate businesses, a renewable energy feasibility study and a Pub-to-hub programme to promote music culture and attract tourism.
records.abstract: Smart and sustainable energy community in County Limerick

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The village has made great strides in the field of renewable and sustainable energy through the creation of an integrated constructed wetland that can treat all of the wastewater generated by the community, and the creation of a clean and independent energy source in the form of an off-grid solar system. Furthermore, 14 thriving companies have been established in the new Enterprise Park, where 200 valuable job opportunities have been created. The village now plans to solidify its commitment to a greener future through the development of solar and wind energy infrastructures that can produce 5 MW and 4.9 MW of energy, respectively.

records.title: Internet of food & farm 2020 (IoF2020)
records.description: oF2020 was a research and innovation project exploring the potential contributions of IoT technologies to the European food and farming sector, aiming to make precision farming a reality and take a step towards a more sustainable food value chain. The project, which ran between 2018 and 2021, included seven work packages and 33 use cases organized around five sectors (arable, dairy, fruit, meat and vegetables), with the goal of developing, testing and demonstrating the use of IoT technologies in operational farm environments across Europe. The IoT solutions were developed following technical, business and ethical considerations, and were aimed to reach a commercial stage by the end of the project. Leveraging IoT technologies, the described field operations were carried out automatically by autonomous devices, and the measured data were automatically returned through the cloud, made accessible to research institutes and fed into computer models for further improvement. The information and researchers' contacts were made publicly available, along with examples of how digital technologies, especially IoT, could be leveraged to improve production.
records.abstract: Exploring the potential of IoT-technologies for the European food and farming industry

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The goal of IoF2020 was the creation of a lasting innovation ecosystem supporting the uptake of IoT technologies in the agriculture and farming sectors. Over the course of the project, 33 use cases were implemented and monitored to demonstrate how digital technologies, particularly IoT, could enhance governance and productivity across the entire supply chain. The project supported the adoption of sensors and precision farming technologies, taking a step towards a more data-driven food value chain. The project envisioned improvements in yield and product quality through the use of IoT technologies, reductions in pesticide and fertilizer use, and enhanced food traceability, thereby improving food safety.

records.title: SmartAgriHubs
records.description: SmartAgriHubs was a research and innovation project aimed at consolidating and fostering a European-wide network of Digital Innovation Hubs for Agriculture (DIHs) as part of the digital transformation in support of sustainable farming and food production. The project employed a multi-stakeholder approach to the maintenance of a broad value-chain network across the EU member states. The consortium included a diverse network of start-ups, SMEs, business and service providers, technology experts and end-users. At the heart of the project were 28 flagship agricultural innovations, facilitated by DIHs in nine Regional Clusters that incorporate all the European member states. SmartAgriHubs targeted the creation of a strong, multi-layered network of agricultural Digital Innovation Hubs (DIHs) and Competence Centres (CCs) that could exchange knowledge and create a pan-European market for digital solutions related to farming and food production. The project was built on a solid network of CCs connected to a layer of adjacent regional DIHs that were coordinated by regional clusters and managed at a European project level. The SmartAgriHubs network incorporated five basic concepts that were based on validated methodologies and models: (i) the Competence Centreswere the cornerstones of the DIHs, through which expertise, test infrastructures and other crosscutting resources could be accessed; (ii) Digital Innovation Hubs (DIHs) matched competences with demands, ideas, funding, etc., orchestrated and supported by concrete services to translate this interaction into; (iii) Innovation Experiments (IEs) in which the ideas, concepts, prototypes, etc. were further developed, tested and, ultimately, introduced to the market;  (iv) an Innovation Services Maturity Model (ISSM) providing the necessary monitoring, assessment and support allowed the innovation services of the DIH to reach the desired level;  and (v) an Innovation Portal with a searchable register, facilitating knowledge exchange, brokerage services, etc. that was still active as September 2024.
records.abstract: Project supporting the digital transformation of the European agri-food sector through a network of Digital Innovation Hubs

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The SmartAgriHubs project has been able to operationalize the DIHs concept, and has established a broad network of 400 DIHs all over Europe. Each DIH has the ambition to stimulate and facilitate digitals innovation in the local farming practice. The project also succeeded in getting countries involved in the agri-digital ecosystem that used to be less involved in digital innovation EU projects. This is particularly visible in Eastern and Northern Europe. The capacity building activities within the project aimed to empower DIHs to provide relevant services and improve their operations. Different activities, including a needs assessment, tools to measure DIH services maturity, the DIH observatory and capacity building webinars and peer exchanges were organized within the SmartAgriHubs framework also through the Innovation Portal. In general, SmartAgriHubs aimed at digitizing over 2 million farms across Europe, introducing 80 new digital solutions to the market, and raising €30 million in additional funding from various sources.

records.title: Agricultural Interoperability and Analysis System (ATLAS)
records.description: ATLAS is a research and innovation solution aimed at the development of an open interoperability network of agricultural applications in support of data-driven agriculture. The main purpose of the service-oriented ATLAS architecture is to interconnect the different technologies employed by end-users. The users thus gain access to an interconnected ecosystem of digital solutions for the automation of farm governance, as well as information collected by multiple applications held in a centralized service registry, supporting their analysis and decision-making activities. records.title: National Strategy on Agriculture and Rural Development for the Period 2014–2020
records.description: The National Strategy on Agriculture and Rural Development 2014–2020 is a programme aimed at increasing the competitiveness of Moldova’s agri-food sector through comprehensive restructuring and modernization. The aim is to improve the conditions of those living and working in rural areas, while creating synergies between agri-food activities and the natural environment. The programme interventions include digitalization aspects, including the establishment of electronic information systems, as well as the provision of financial support to farmers for investments, and supporting cooperation and networking in the field of digital agriculture. The programme aims to align the Republic of Moldova with the policies and instruments of the European Union and features six chapters that take into consideration economic resource management and the social challenges related to agriculture and rural development.

records.title: Demeter
records.description: DEMETER was a large-scale agritech research and innovation project funded under the EU's Horizon 2020 programme between 2019 and 2023, aiming to facilitate and speed-up the deployment of data-driven, smart farming solutions as part of decision support and control systems within the agricultural sector. The project supported farmers in decision-making, allowing them to harness the full value of their own data and knowledge, and those shared by others. The innovative features of DEMETER included a human-in-the-loop model combining human expertise, digital information, interoperable data, services, platforms, machine-to-machine communication and human knowledge, supported by technologies as IoT, Earth Observation, Big Data and AI and targeting the transformation of agricultural practices. The project proposed the establishment of an Agricultural Interoperability Space (AIS), a reference architecture that supports the interoperability of different platforms and data sets for the agri-food sector.  The platform aims at improving existing information models in terms of data sharing and interoperability, therefore empowering farmers and controlling the use of data for the exploration of new business models. DEMETER supports the establishment of productivity and sustainability benchmarks, and it promotes the creation of tailored solutions to innovate supplier-farmer interactions. To meet the defined objectives, DEMETER was divided into seven Work Packages: Project Coordination; Data and Knowledge; Technology Integration; Performance Indicator Monitoring; Benchmarking and Decision Support Pilot Management; Business Modelling, Innovation Management, Exploitation and Standardization; and Multi-Actor Ecosystem Development.
records.abstract: Promoting the use of digital devices and platforms in the agrifood sector in 18 countries

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The research and innovation project sought to empower farmers through the provision of data-driven decision support tools, and by supporting the interoperability of different stakeholders in collaborations; promoting sustainable farming practices, driving economic growth through innovation, and guiding evidence-based agricultural policies. The project saw the participation of 18 countries and 60 partners through a multi-actor approach across the value chain (demand and supply), aiming to support 6,000 farmers through 20 pilot projects, and with over 38000 devices and sensors. The overall global outreach of the project was 47 countries, 69 farmers association and a total of 1.5 billion People.

records.title: Assessing the Framework Conditions for Social Innovation in Rural Areas
records.description: The “Assessing the Framework Conditions for Social Innovation in Rural Areas” resource paper presents a comprehensive framework for understanding and promoting social innovation in rural areas, including digitalization, highlighting the distinct challenges faced in these regions, such as geographical remoteness, infrastructure deficiencies and declining populations. The paper further emphasizes the role of digitalization in rural areas and how it impacts social innovation by supporting the adoption of new business models, teleworking and community engagement. This paper’s proposed approach includes a dashboard with five dimensions and 17 sub-dimensions related to social innovation, aiding in the translation of qualitative inputs into quantitative indices. The goal is to create a comprehensive database of information related to local social innovation, and to transform what are largely qualitative inputs into quantitative indices that can be compared across time and place. This innovative approach circumvents the difficulties encountered in measuring social innovation by proposing a systematic framework for the evaluation and support of rural social innovation ecosystems, and proposes an approach that can help policymakers understand the local social innovation ecosystems, with particular emphasis on such rural-specific elements as land use, and to benchmark a variety of relevant policy areas across different territories.
records.abstract: Framework for the clarification and promotion of social innovation in rural areas
records.owner_name: Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The paper aims to support public sectors in such activities as policymaking, providing a systematic dashboard that can help in understanding rural social innovation ecosystems. This tool facilitates the better benchmarking of rural regions in support of data-driven interventions and decisions, and empowers such local actors as civil society, social enterprises and rural communities through the promotion of innovative projects that leverage local resources and technology, while also enhancing community resilience. The potential positive impacts of the paper include the stimulation of economic development through the encouragement of local entrepreneurship and job creation in rural areas.

records.title: Georgia Digital Development Country Profile
records.description: The "Digital Development Country Profile - Georgia" is part of the ITU Office for Europe’s regional effort to provide a comparative analysis of the digital transformation of priority countries in the European region,  namely Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, and Ukraine. The report analyses the nation’s digital transformation based on the various experiences of ITU, the UN specialized agency for ICTs and other UN system organizations, offering a broad overview of the activities and projects being implemented at the national level and in the wider region. It describes the status of the digital development of Georgia based on 5 building blocks: meaningful connectivity, as the foundation for digital development and transformation; the people-centric digital transformation; the government-centric digital transformation; the sector-centric digital transformation; and the digital-centric innovation ecosystem. The status of digital agriculture is analysed under the “Sector-centric digital transformation” section, providing a detailed overview of the digital agricultural sector in Georgia with particular focus on capacity building among farmers, tools that support advanced analytics, policy-making and reporting, and inter-agency coordination for the production of agriculture-related SDG indicators. The report also mentions the Strategy for Agriculture and Rural Development 2021–2027, which includes data also on the non-agricultural sectors, the sustainable use of natural resources, ecosystem conservation, adaptation to climate change, food product and animal feed safety, and the development of veterinary and plant protection systems.
records.abstract: Analysis of the country’s digital development status
records.owner_name: International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Regional Office for Europe

_annotations.Impact: This document provides a framework for the clarification of the digital development across the five identified building blocks of the digital transformation. It provides information about Georgia for each domain based on the experiences and activities of ITU and other stakeholders operating in the country and the wider region. The report aids stakeholders in making informed decisions related to policies, investments and strategies related to ICTs, and can also serve as a reference source for discussions of digital development at a country level, as well for the stock-taking of the activities, initiatives, projects and experiences of UN agencies involved in the digital transformation of Georgia. It can further serve as a guide for future dialogue with country stakeholders and pave the way for increasingly fit-for-purpose engagements of the UN system in the country.

It aims to help stakeholders make informed decisions regarding policies, investments and strategies related to ICTs, and to enhance the dialogue and facilitate collaborations between government entities, private sector organizations, civil society groups and international partners. It should thus facilitate more coordinated and effective efforts in achieving the digital transformation, setting realistic targets, learning from best practices and adopting successful strategies from peer countries.

records.title: DIPOL
records.description: DIPOL is a research and innovation project that has been financed by the Ministry of Science of Montenegro through a scientific research grant, awarded that aims to validate and demonstrate the adoption of the latest precision agriculture and smart food production solutions in IT, focusing on two elements: vineyard/farm production and the food supply chain in Montenegro. The project has several objectives. First, it analyses the digital transformation in agriculture and the food supply chain in Montenegro through case studies targeting the identification of system requirements on selected test sites, leading to the creation of detailed design specifications and interventions. Second, it supports the implementation of pilot precision agriculture projects that make use of state-of-the art sensors and an Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled digital farming platform, and a supply chain platform based on digital product identifiers, allowing the use of blockchain-based technologies. Finally, it facilitates research activities and the development of new decision support components based on the use of collected data and machine-learning and artificial intelligence algorithms.
records.abstract: Research and innovation project promoting the digital transformation of agriculture and the food supply chain in Montenegro
records.owner_name: Faculty for Information Systems and Technologies of the University of Donja Gorica (FIST-UDG)

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The DIPOL project platform encourages the involvement of young researchers, supporting the sustainability of research activities related to the digital transformation in agriculture and the food value chain. To date, one BSc thesis and four MSc thesis have been completed, and two of these student authors have enrolled in PhD studies, one of whom is the recipient of a PhD stipend from the Ministry of Science. The project studies have been related in five publications presented at scientific/technical conferences, and in one scientific journal (SCI level). The project members have engaged and collaborated with several industry partners in the implementation of field pilots. In general, the project aims to have a positive impact on agriculture as a major component of Montenegrin economy, and its agriculture and agri-food production through research activities.

records.title: Second Institutional development and agriculture strengthening project (MIDAS2)
records.description: The Second Institutional development and agriculture strengthening project (MIDAS2) is funded by the World Bank, and is designed to increase the competitiveness of Montenegro's agricultural enterprises and fisheries in line with the EU pre-accession requirements, including its electronic information systems. Component 1 of the project involves the provision of grants with the aim of diversifying income opportunities and enabling the adoption of modern, energy-efficient technologies within the agricultural and fisheries sectors. Furthermore, to support Montenegro in its implementation of the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), the project will fund rural development measures, including agro-environment initiatives, in alignment with EU management and control systems, and the gradual development and introduction of the Integrated Administration and Control System (IACS). Component 2 focuses on strengthening food safety, veterinary and phytosanitary services, making a crucial contribution to the quality and safety of agricultural products, both for domestic consumption and for the export markets. Finally, Component 3 supports the development of essential infrastructures and capacity building in the fisheries sector, ensuring that fishermen have access to safe, sanitary landing facilities and ports equipped with the necessary auxiliary services. Among the innovative elements are the introduction of a grant programme that follows a “learning by doing” approach, allowing beneficiaries to pre-finance investments and receive reimbursements only after the successful completion of the project. The project encourages the utilization of funding and resources from private companies. By attracting private sector investments, the project aims to amplify the overall impact of the funds, encouraging private stakeholders to implement agro-environmental measures to mitigate greenhouse gas emissions. The project also incorporates a well-organized and regulated framework for the handling, processing and disposal of animal waste, significantly reducing the emissions associated with livestock disposal.
records.abstract: Project targeting the improvement of the competitiveness of agriculture and fisheries in Montenegro

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The project aims to stimulate economic opportunities of Montenegrin producers to access new markets and generate more jobs in rural areas through the grant program that will support farmers and agriculture holdings engaged in farm diversification and on-farm processing. The improved quality of life in rural areas is expected to contribute to reduced rural to urban migration. Up to 2023, under the indicator to improve competitiveness of agriculture and fisheries in Montenegro, the number of supported farmers reached by the grant programme providing them with agricultural assets or services were 3598.

records.title: EU Code of Conduct on agricultural data sharing by contractual agreement
records.description: The “EU code of conduct on agricultural data-sharing by contractual agreement” is a non-binding guideline developed by a consortium of private actors operating in the agriculture and machinery sectors that regulates and promotes the transparent, fair and efficient sharing of agricultural data. The code establishes key and general principles regarding: 1) data ownership, 2) data access, control and portability, 3) data protection and transparency, 4) privacy and security. 5) liability and intellectual property rights, and calls for the transparency, security and interoperability of data sharing contracts, ensuring data ownership for farmers and fostering collaboration among various stakeholders in the agricultural sector. It contains four case studies showcasing such practical applications as the usage and processing of data in precision feeding and animal disease forecasting. The code also provides references to the most relevant regulatory frameworks related to the sharing of agricultural data, serving as a practical reference for involved parties.
records.abstract: Non-binding document providing guidance on the use of agricultural data, and the principles and relationships within the agri-food chain
records.owner_name: Committee of Professional Agricultural Organisations (COPA); General Confederation of Agricultural Cooperatives (COGECA)

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The “EU code of conduct on agricultural data sharing” is a pioneering non-binding governance document regulating the use of non-personal data in the field of agriculture. While it cannot be used as a legal document, it references several binding EU regulations. Its guidance on the inclusion of agricultural data within contractual agreements aims to improve resource efficiency, productivity, animal welfare, resilience to climate change, and to support the achievement of more prosperous living conditions for rural communities.

records.title: Empowering rural smallholders in Turkey through digital marketing and business solutions in post COVID-19 period
records.description: The “Empowering rural smallholders in Turkey through digital marketing and business solutions in post COVID-19 period” report, prepared jointly by IFAD, FAO and the UNDP with technical support from the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry (MoAF) of Türkye, assesses the availability of digital business solutions in the agriculture sector and the demand for these services among rural smallholders in Türkiye. This report should be considered a second phase study, referring to the results of the Rapid Impact Assessment report published in 2020. The document presents a series of policy recommendations on how to promote the use of digital platforms, particularly among smallholder farmers. During the COVID-19 pandemic, farmers faced challenges in gaining access to product markets, labour, inputs and capital markets, and digital platforms at the time provided farmers with the opportunity to mitigate the influence of the pandemic on agriculture, especially for marketing. This report focuses in particular on the digital platforms operated by government bodies, private companies and non-profit organizations in support of the marketing of agricultural products, agricultural extension services, agricultural input purchases and rural finance, and showcases how these technologies have the potential to support farmers that are still suffer the effects of the pandemic in overcoming the above-mentioned challenges. To determine the needs of farmers and to assess the demand for digital technologies, an online survey was conducted with farmers in the regions where IFAD-funded projects are being implemented by the MoAF, to which a total of 56 farmers belonging to farmers’ cooperatives or producers’ unions responded.
records.abstract: Report on the adoption and impact of digital marketing and business solutions in agriculture

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The report constitutes a step towards a supply-and-demand analysis of digital platforms in Türkiye, and highlights the factors that could reduce the adoption barriers and increase the use of digital platforms among farmers.

records.title: Towards a Green and Digital Future
records.description: The European “Towards a Green and Digital Future” study analyses how current and future digital technologies could become key enablers in support of the twin (green and digital) transition by 2050, the year in which the European Union aims to have become climate neutral. The study is based on a review of literature and expert consultations, validated by 11 workshops with over 200 participants, taking a close look at five economic sectors that are among the highest greenhouse gas emitters in the EU: agriculture, building and construction, energy, energy-intensive industries, and transport and mobility. Several case studies have been selected that present a variety of different possible green digital solutions, with descriptions of how their successful implementation by 2050 could support the green transition. The study outlines the key requirements for the successful management of the twin transition and examines its tension points, such as how digital technologies may also bring additional environmental burdens, and how economic, social and political factors may impact the twin transition. The section on agriculture explores the use of technology for the environmental monitoring and tracking of biodiversity deficits, as well as of product residues within the circular economy. It is mentioned that digital technologies may also contribute to efficient systems management, and thus increase productivity through the more targeted application of feed, water, energy, fertilizers and pesticides. Additional areas in which digitalization can play an important role incşude farming, forestry, manufacturing, and the diverse services in rural areas outside those related to food, farming and tourism
records.abstract: Study outlining the key requirements for a successful twin green and digital transition in the European Union

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The main impacts of the study include its promotion and anticipation of the required steps for a successful twin (green and digital) transition, mitigating climate change and environmental degradation, while reducing the European Union’s reliance on energy imports. Conversely, the digital transition holds the potential to reshape prevailing practices related to both the economy and society. While pinpointing promising technologies in various economic sectors, the report also proposes strategies that support and bring synergy to the green and digital transitions. It further details such challenges as the Russian aggression against Ukraine and the COVID-19 pandemic and their effects on the transitions, providing a comprehensive overview in support of the concurrent green and digital transitions as essential activities for the preservation of a livable planet and the harnessing of economic opportunities. The report presents information, considerations, case studies and examples of future scenarios in support of a sustainable digital and green transition.

records.title: Bosnia and Herzegovina Digital Development Country Profile
records.description: The "Digital Development Country Profile - Bosnia and Herzegovina" is a part of the ITU Office for Europe’s regional effort to provide a comparative analysis of the digital transformation of priority countries in the European region, namely Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, the Republic of Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, and Ukraine. The report analyses the nation’s digital transformation based on various experiences of ITU, the UN specialized agency for ICTs and other UN organizations, offering a broad overview of the activities and projects being implemented at a national level and in the wider region. The report describes the status of digital development in Bosnia and Herzegovina according to three building blocks: 1) access, relating to the status of the ICT infrastructures; 2) adoption, addressing digital skills and other such training; and 3) value creation, related to availability of digital public services. The status of digital agriculture is analysed specifically in the "value creation" section. The report provides an overview of the challenges to digital agriculture and the efforts to digitalize information, productivity and farm management in Bosnia and Herzegovina, and also explores such issues as education, health and waste management.
records.abstract: Analysis of the country’s digital development status
records.owner_name: International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Regional Office for Europe

_annotations.Impact: The report aims to serve as a source of reference for future dialogues with country stakeholders related to the promotion of digitalization and related initiatives in Bosnia and Herzegovina. It can also serve as a baseline study guiding strategic decisions on initiatives to be undertaken within the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) on digital and ICT development matters. Finally, the report brings together numerous initiatives related to the digital transformation of the country.

records.title: A smart and sustainable digital future for European agriculture and rural areas
records.description: The ”A smart and sustainable digital future for European agriculture and rural areas” document is a Declaration reflecting the common intention of 26 EU Member States to address the economic, social, climatic and environmental challenges facing the EU's agri-food sector and rural areas. It highlights the need to encourage the long-term evolution of farming systems to make them more resilient and efficient, and underlines the potential of digital technologies to help tackle such challenges. The Declaration in particular aims to strengthen the support provided for research, and promotes the establishment of an infrastructure that supports innovation and the creation of a European dataspace for smart agri-food applications, while maximizing the impact of ongoing initiatives that support the result-based transition of the CAP through the development of innovative and digital solutions for both rural stakeholders and institutions. In proposing these actions, the Member States are addressing the challenges faced by the agricultural sector in the EU, such as the environmental pressures related to climate change, the loss of biodiversity, the lack of traceable and quality products at affordable prices, the shortage of farm labour and the lack of a digitally skilled workforce, all of which are hindering the modernization of the sector.
records.abstract: Declaration of cooperation between 26 European countries

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The Declaration contributes to the increased use of digital technologies in agriculture, aiming to improve the quality of life of farm workers and the rural population in the EU Member States. It is known that such technologies can support the optimization of many aspects of farming by supporting decision making and reshaping the functioning of agri-food markets, however, broadband accessibility in rural areas in the EU is still at 53 percent. Aside from the predicted positive impact on the quality of life of farm workers and the rural population, it is thought that the policy document will help attract members of the younger generations to farming and rural business start-ups.

records.title: Digital excellence in agriculture report
records.description: The “Digital Excellence in Agriculture” report is the outcome of the Digital Excellence in Agriculture: FAO-ITU regional contest on good practices advancing digital agriculture in Europe and Central Asia, organized by FAO and ITU. The report presents a summary of the main trends in digital services and products, the most important technologies used, as well as the difficulties and challenges encountered in the development of digital agricultural applications. The solutions put forward by 29 finalists are presented in seven categories, with details of the key challenges they address, the digital technologies they use, and their journeys and plans for the near future based on the information provided. Winners of the 7 categories are: Local Food Nodes, Organic Farm Knowledge, High-Precision Weed Control in Organic Farming, Nedap CowControl, AGRIVI Farm Management Software, Disease and Pest Forecast with Artificial Intelligence and OLIO.

_annotations.Impact: It is believed that the collected knowledge, good practices and innovative solutions could be scaled up for practical use and replication by all stakeholders. The report shows how ICTs can play an emerging role in the development of regional agricultural landscapes and drive agricultural development.

records.title: Digital technologies in the grain sector of Ukraine
records.description: The report assesses the extent to which Ukrainian farmers have adopted digital technologies, the many barriers preventing them from doing so, and the considerable opportunities these technologies present. The report further offers sharp insights into their potential contributions and how best they can be sustained. It showcases the results of a research that included extensive interviews with the administrators of different sized farms in Ukraine, and considers the level of interest among larger farmers in the adoption of precision agriculture technologies, and their benefits in terms of improved productivity, lower costs and reduced greenhouse gas emissions, despite the relatively high initial investment costs. It concludes with a list of recommended actions, calling on four specific groups to embrace digital technologies and thus contribute to the development and transformation of Ukraine’s grain sector: the private sector, financial institutions, the public sector and international organizations.
records.abstract: Adoption and opportunities assessment report
records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

_annotations.Impact: The report aims to support stakeholders in the Ukrainian grain sector through its analysis of the institutional support for digital technologies, and the potential for increased competitiveness and productivity through the use of precision agricultural technologies (PATs), remote sensing technologies and distributed ledger technologies (DLT) by Ukrainian farmers. The report recommends a series of measures to support the uptake of particular technologies at farm level, but also institutionally, shedding light on how the adoption of technologies can be supported financially.

records.title: Gender Digital Divide Assessment: Uzbekistan
records.description: The Gender Digital Divide Assessment investigates the extent of the gender digital divide in Uzbekistan, and is based on a theory of change model that measures the country’s starting point (Foundations), the inputs (Enablers) that contribute to reducing the gender digital divide, the outcomes (Impacts) of such efforts and the role of women in society (Cross-cutting themes). The factors assessed in the Foundations section are “online safety and security”; while digital skills and literacy programmes, relevant content, and laws and policies are covered in the Enablers section; “use and leadership” in the Impact section; and “social norms, registrations and policies'' in the Cross-Cutting themes section.The assessment is based on data drawn from a desk research, expert interviews, and online and offline surveys/interviews. The desk research included an analysis of the regulations, the current government and donor initiatives, and other available data. The online survey was applied to 8607 respondents (49 percent of whom were women), while the Offline Survey-Interviews targeted a gender-balanced sample of respondents (1050) in six regions of Uzbekistan. The main goal of the study is to identify the existing gaps and barriers preventing the equal digital inclusion of genders and to provide key recommendations to government and international organizations. The report lists the priority actions required to bridge the gender digital divide in Uzbekistan.
records.abstract: Nationwide assessment of the status of the digital divide between genders in Uzbekistan

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: From a research point of view, the assessment can serve as a strong baseline and benchmark reference for future studies, being based on data garnered during an extensive survey in Uzbekistan that was carried out to identify the current digital landscape in the region, the main challenges faced by the public in accessing and using digital technologies, and the root causes of the gender digital divide. The data derived from the survey could contribute to the creation of a solid and scientific database and the formulation of recommendations of how to bridge the divide, thus contributing to SDG4. In recognition of the importance of digital skills and access to digital resources for the country's growth, the report offers potentially significant insights into the enhancement of the use of technology in Uzbekistan, particularly among women. The recommendations include the implementation of measures to increase the level of connectivity of in communal areas, the development and inclusion of cyber ethics and cyber hygiene subjects in school curricula, the provision of support to the media and civil society in the generation of interesting digital and women-related content, the selection of a set of international indices (such as ITU, GSMA, GDDI, UNDESA) for the measurement of the gender digital divide based on international standards, and the inclusion of a data collection requirement in government programmes.

records.title: Ukraine Digital Development Country Profile
records.description: The “Digital Development Country Profile – Ukraine” is an assessment report documenting the digitalization status of Ukraine, and has been compiled as part of the regional effort of the ITU Office for Europe to carry out a comparative analysis of the digital transformation status of priority countries in the European region, namely Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Republic of Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Ukraine. The report draws upon the various experiences of ITU, the UN specialized agency for ICTs and other UN system organizations to provide a broad overview of the activities and projects related to digital transformation being implemented at a national level and in the wider region, and describes the status of digital development of the country according to 5 building blocks: meaningful connectivity as foundation of digital transformation; people-centric digital transformation; government-centric digital transformation; sector-centric digital transformation, including e-agri and e-health; and, finally, the digital-centric innovation ecosystem. The digitalization of agriculture is analyzed under the “Sector-centric digital transformation” section of the report, providing a detailed overview of the level of digitalization in the sector in Ukraine, with particular focus on access to geospatial data for land management (StateGeoCadastre), collective impact initiatives ( AgroHub) and smart farming solutions, including: the digitalization of agricultural trade through mobile devices, yşeld predictions and maximization, and the mitigation of threats to crop yields.
records.abstract: Analysis of the status of digital development in the country
records.owner_name: International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Regional Office for Europe

_annotations.Impact: The report can serve as a baseline for comparative assessments, and as a guide for future dialogue with country stakeholders for the promotion of digitalization and related initiatives in Ukraine. The document can inform policy decisions aimed at promoting digital innovation and adoption within the sector, and can serve as a basis for collaborations among various stakeholders, including government agencies, agricultural organizations, technology companies and research institutions. It aims to support national decision-makers and international stakeholders in carrying out coordinated and effective efforts towards the nation’s digital transformation, and in setting realistic targets, learning from best practices and adopting successful strategies from peer countries.

records.title: Turkey Climate Smart and Competitive Agricultural Growth Project (TUCSAP)
records.description: The Climate Smart and Competitive Growth in Agri-food Value Chains in Turkey project is funded by the World Bank and implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry of Türkiye. Under the USD 374.27 million project, the agri-food sector is supported from 2021 to 2028 in its efforts to become more climate-smart and inclusive by enhancing the government’s capacity for land-use planning and agricultural data collection, and by supporting innovation and the use of smart farming/climate-smart technologies and practices among farmers and agricultural enterprises. The project is implemented under three components: 1) Institutional Capacity Strengthening for Climate Smart Agri-food Policy, Planning and Investments; 2) Investments for Enhanced Productivity, Resource-Efficiency and Climate Resilience; and 3) Project Management and Monitoring and Evaluation. The project, through various interventions that include grants, training and technical assistance, addresses challenges of low productivity and unsustainable practices, while simultaneously enhancing resilience to climate change.
records.abstract: Supporting climate-smart approaches in the agri-food chain and land-use planning

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The project targets such positive outcomes as increased agricultural productivity, efficiency in the use of resources, increased resilience to climate change and strengthened institutional capacity. Efforts to enhance data collection, interoperability and management will be supported, and the project also aims to address some of the key issues faced by the agrifood sector in Türkiye, such as low productivity, unsustainable production practices and vulnerability to climate change by enhancing agricultural profitability and sustainability.

records.title: National Pathway for food systems transformation in support of the 2030 agenda
records.description: The National Pathway for food systems transformation in support of the 2030 agenda in the Republic of Armenia aims to enhance the efficacy of the agricultural sector, improve food safety, encourage the introduction of modern technologies, and increase the export volumes and revenue positions of all players in the value chain, primarily small commercially oriented farmers, producer groups, processors and exporters. The policy lists seven strategic priorities that have been defined specifically for Armenia’s agriculture sector: (1) increase the competitiveness and efficacy of Armenia’s agriculture sector, (2)ensure food safety; (3) develop local markets and increase exports; (4) improve food security and nutrition; (5) develop the nation’s institutional and human capacity; (6) support sustainable rural development; and, (7) promote digital agriculture and technological innovations. For the last of these items, the document focuses on such specific objectives as investments into national digital agriculture platforms and digitalization initiatives, promoting the broader (non-digital) innovation and uptake of agricultural technologies, furthering the digitalization of the government agriculture systems and developing the digital capacity of the Ministry, and increasing the capacity of farmers and the education system related to digital agriculture and innovation.

records.title: Unleashing the Power of Digital on Farms in Russia – and Seeking Opportunities for Small Farms
records.description: The “Unleashing the Power of Digital on Farms in Russia – and Seeking Opportunities for Small Farms” report has brought together information from various sources, including reports, websites and interviews with companies, experts, farmers and developers, identifying the most common and useful technologies in global agriculture for adoption in the Russian agricultural context. The collected information provides an overview of the current situation and presents options for the enhancement of agriculture in the Russian Federation, identifying the technologies and tools currently in use by small- and medium-sized farmers, and those with potential that have yet to be adopted.
records.abstract: Analysis of the digital agriculture tools, technologies and services currently in use by small- and medium-sized farmers, and other potential resources

While multiple stakeholders can benefit from the report, its focus is on smallholder farmers, aiming to narrow the gap between them and the rest of the sector and prevent their exclusion from the benefits of the development of the sector.

records.title: Acceleration of digital transformation in agriculture sector for ensuring sustainable food security
records.description: The “Acceleration of the digital transformation of the agriculture sector to ensure sustainable food security” needs assessment report provides information about the digital transformation and smart agriculture applications in agriculture and e-commerce in Türkiye in the COVID-19 pandemic era. Based on both qualitative and quantitative data and primary and secondary research, the report focuses particularly on key agricultural indicators, digital agriculture concepts, the impact of smart agricultural practices, and the effectiveness of the digital transformation in agriculture from economic, social and cultural perspectives. The assessment was carried out in three phases: Phase 1) An assessment of the current situation, following a step-by-step process under the following headings: Materials and Method; Key Indicators of Agriculture in Türkiye; Digital Agriculture Concept and its Development; Digital Agriculture Components; Importance of Smart Agricultural Practices and Applications Around the World in the COVID-19 Era; The Situation of Smart Agriculture in Türkiye; E-Commerce Term Components in Agriculture; and, E-Commerce Effects and Contributions to Agriculture. Phase 2) Data gathering and analysis involving the collection of valuable data from 85 field studies (by 35 institutions/organizations and 50 producers) covering 14 provinces in Türkiye. Phase 3) Policy recommendations contributing to the improvement of the production and sustainability of digital applications in the agricultural sector considering the need to adapt quickly to changing conditions, especially in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The assessment suggests possible areas for intervention and initiatives to address the identified challenges.
records.abstract: Needs assessment and policy recommendations report
records.owner_name: Standing Committee for Economic and Commercial Cooperation of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (COMCEC)

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The report assesses the digital transformation of agriculture in Türkiye during the COVID-19 pandemic (2021), highlighting the challenges and identifying areas in need of improvement. The report can be used as a benchmarking and baseline reference, and the included data can help agricultural stakeholders improve productivity and sustainability by suggesting digital solutions, thus benefitting both large producers and smallholder farmers. The report claims that smallholder farmers tend to be reluctant to adopt digital solutions due to their limited budgets and knowledge, but suggests that this can be remedied by leveraging the recommendations included in the assessment, possibly with the support of organizations and the public and private sectors.

records.title: Digital Ecosystem Country Assessment Toolkit
records.description: The Digital Ecosystem Country Assessment (DECA) Toolkit is a methodological guide supporting the identification of development opportunities and risks in a country’s digital ecosystem, thus aiding in the development, design and implementation of USAID’s strategies, projects and activities. The toolkit was developed to serve as a guide for further country researches and was compiled based on lessons learned during four pilot assessments conducted between winter 2019 and autumn 2020 in partnership with the USAID Missions in Colombia, Kenya, Nepal and Serbia. The assessments were carried out over 5 months in three phases: desk research and planning, interviews, and data analysis and report writing, and covered three main topics: 1) Digital Infrastructure and Adoption, 2) Digital Society, Rights and Governance, and 3) Digital Economy
records.abstract: Methodological guide supporting the identification of development opportunities and risks within a country's digital ecosystem

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The DECA Toolkit offers insights into a country's digital ecosystem, thus supporting informed decision-making related to digital programming and investments, and fostering more targeted and effective initiatives through the leveraging of digital technologies for development. By providing a shared understanding of the digital landscape, DECA seeks to promote collaborations and greater coordination among stakeholders, thus maximizing the impact of digital development interventions. DECA can contribute to the design and implementation of more sustainable initiatives by identifying development opportunities and risks

_raw.Impact: The DECA Toolkit offers insights into a country's digital ecosystem, thus supporting informed decision-making related to digital programming and investments, and fostering more targeted and effective initiatives through the leveraging of digital technologies for development. By providing a shared understanding of the digital landscape, DECA seeks to promote collaborations and greater coordination among stakeholders, thus maximizing the impact of digital development interventions. DECA can contribute to the design and implementation of more sustainable initiatives by identifying development opportunities and risks

records.title: USAID Digital Agriculture Ecosystem Assessment - Tajikistan
records.description: The USAID Digital Agriculture Ecosystem Assessment assessment in Tajikistan, commissioned by USAID/Tajikistan and conducted by NIRAS in 2021/22, adoptsan ecosystem approach to understanding the market landscape and the needs of farmers inregards to their access to and use of digital tools. The assessment utilizes a desk research, expertinterviews and farmer focus group discussions (FGDs) as the primary data sources.The reportprovides critical insights into Tajikistan’s needs, value chains and sectoral bottlenecks, as well asthe digital connectivity status and accessibility to technology with the overall aim of understandingthe potential for digital agriculture services, platforms, systems and applications (apps). The report provides details of several digital agricultural solutions that arein use in the country and platforms providing weather forecasts, market prices and advice ondifferent crops.

records.title: Approved 28 CAP Strategic Plans (2023–2027)
records.description: The summary of the 28 approved National Common Agriculture Policy (CAP) Strategic Plans for 2023–2027 presents an overview of the key elements of the approved plans underpinning the EU’s policy implementation for 2023–2027, including their support of the cross-cutting objectives of digitalization. The document outlines the key elements and choices set out by the Member States in their plans and provides responses to requests for information, while summarizing what content and goals of the plans. The overview is organized around all CAP interventions, and includes those specifically targeting digitalization, with descriptions of digitalization strategies, rural broadband investments and installed technologies; and farm advisory, knowledge transfer and cooperation support in the form of LEADER/CLLD, Smart Villages or EIP-AGRI Operational Groups. It also presents examples that can serve as a further basis for the exchange of information and mutual learning. As a further focal point, the resource also addresses digitalization in support of the modernization and the simplification of the CAP delivery model, and its monitoring and evaluation.

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The summary overview facilitates the cross-comparison of the policy interventions designed by the 27 EU Member States in relation to digital agriculture. The impacts of these interventions are to be assessed during bi-annual performance reviews based on common output and result indicators.
