records.title: Digital Development Country Profile – Republic of North Macedonia
records.description: The “Digital Development Country Profile – Republic of North Macedonia” is a part of the ITU Office for Europe’s regional effort to provide a comparative analysis of the digital transformation of priority countries in the European region, namely Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Republic of Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Ukraine based on the various experiences of ITU, the UN specialized agency for ICTs, and other UN system organizations. In doing so, it provides a broad overview of the activities and projects being implemented at a national level and in the wider region, describing the level of digital development in the countries according to five building blocks: meaningful connectivity, as a prerequisite for the digital transformation; people-centric digital transformation; government-centric digital transformation; sector-centric digital transformation, including e-agri and e-health; and, finally, the innovation ecosystem. The level of agricultural digitalization is analysed in the “Sector-centric digital transformation" section. The text provides a detailed overview of the level of digitalization in agriculture in North Macedonia with particular focus on land management, forest monitoring, climate resilience, e-government systems and web platforms hosting agri-environmental indicators in a digital spatial format, as well as training materials
records.abstract: Analysis of the country’s digital development status
records.owner_name: International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Regional Office for Europe

_annotations.Impact: The report provides baseline information for comparison assessments, while also serving as a guide for future dialogues with country stakeholders related to the promotion of digitalization and its related initiatives in North Macedonia. It supports stakeholders in making informed decisions regarding policies, investments and ICT strategies, while also enhancing the dialogue and facilitating collaborations between government entities, the private sector, organizations, civil society groups and international partners, thus contributing to the generation of more coordinated and effective efforts in support of the digital transformation, the setting of realistic targets, learning from best practices, and the adoption of successful strategies applied in peer countries.

records.title: Tunduk  (Түндүк)
records.description: Tunduk  is State Portal of Electronic Services ,a key portal that facilitates the provision of state and municipal services in electronic form. In addition to offering general services such as checking fines, passport and driver's license status, obtaining certificates, Tunduk provides specific services from the Ministry of Water Resources, Agriculture, and Processing Industry of the Kyrgyz Republic. These include accessing information on whether a citizen has registered agricultural livestock and details about identified animals, integrated through the Animal Identification and Traceability System. Tunduk also offers services from the State Agency for Land Resources, including obtaining extracts of real estate rights from the Unified State Register, state registration of property rights and encumbrances, detailed technical information about properties, property rights history, and certificates regarding ownership rights of real estate objects.
records.abstract: Portal of e-government services
records.owner_name: State Agency Tunduk under the Ministry of Digital Development of the Kyrgyz Republic

SDGs.value: SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

_annotations.Impact: The State Portal of Electronic Services has a significant impact. By digitizing and automating service delivery, the portal streamlines administrative workflows, reducing the need for physical paperwork and in-person visits. It enhances accessibility for individuals in remote areas, provided there is reliable internet connectivity. The portal also allows real-time tracking of requests and provides detailed status updates, thereby improving transparency and fostering greater accountability in government operations. Personal data protection is upheld through secure data exchanges and robust authentication mechanisms, including the Unified Identification System.

records.title: Digitisation Strategy for the Agri-Food and Forestry Sector and Rural Areas
records.description: The Digitisation Strategy and Action Plan for the Agri-Food and Forestry Sector and Rural Areas (hereinafter, the Strategy) of Spain defines the strategic direction, measures, resources and timeline of efforts to boost the digital transformation of the agri-food and forestry sector and rural areas in the country, and the development of the necessary instruments planned for their implementation. The Strategy is implemented through biannual action plans subject to monitoring and development. The three objectives of the Strategy are: 1) to narrow the digital divide, 2) to foster data usage and 3) to boost business development and the creation of new business models. The Strategy promotes collaboration among stakeholders in integration with other policies, and addresses such challenges as the fragmented organizational structures anddemographic shifts in rural areas.
records.abstract: Strategic lines and implementation instruments for the digital transformation of Spain's agrifood sector
records.owner_name: Ministry of agriculture, fisheries, and food of Spain

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The overall goal of the Strategy is to provide cross-cutting support to the achievement of Spain’s National and European agricultural policy objectives, including creating quality jobs in the agri-food and forestry sectors in support of the rural economy, developing new business models in rural areas that make use of digital technologies, increasing access to markets for rural farmers, improving farm productivity through data-driven decision-making and enhancing the economic sustainability of smallholder farmers. The Strategy promotes the creation of tailored advisory services and training programmes designed to bolster the skills and knowledge of smallholder farmers.

records.title: Sanarip Aimak (Санарип Аймак)
records.description: Sanarip Aimak is a platform that facilitates communication between local self-government bodies and public administration through inter-departmental electronic interaction. The primary goal of the system is to enhance the efficiency of local self-government and automate the work of specialists providing public services. It collects, processes, and provides essential information for decision-making in local governance and public administration. The system's key objectives are to automate local government activities, promote effective communication with individuals and legal entities, combat corruption, ensure transparency, manage population and household registration, streamline data collection for elections and referendums, create a centralized database, and support social protection programs for local communities.

records.title: Agrodrone.kg
records.description: Drones by Agrodrone’s  are used for precise field spraying of chemicals enabling accurate and efficient input use, reducing chemical waste, and minimizing soil compaction by eliminating the need for traditional ground-based machinery. This results in lower operational costs for farmers while preserving soil health. The drones can spray up to 1 hectare per hour,  improving time efficiency compared to conventional methods.To request this service, users must place a call or submit an application through the “Farmer’s Personal Account” mobile application. Within 1-2 hours, Agrodrone.kg specialists will contact the user to confirm order details, including field size, required treatments, and preferred scheduling. At the scheduled time, a drone operator will arrive on-site with the agrodrone, necessary technical equipment, and water. The operator will then define the field boundaries and conduct preparatory work. The farmer is responsible for providing details on the treatment preparation and the application rate per hectare. The drone operator will prepare the solution and perform the spraying of the field.
records.abstract: Drones for precision agriculture

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Agrodrone.kg provides drone-based spraying services that ensure precise application of chemicals, optimizing their use. The drones reduce costs by using 20 times less working fluid per hectare and eliminate the need for water supply and ground equipment. They can significantly save time, covering up to 6 hectares of land in just one hour. The drones effectively reach hard-to-access areas and avoid soil compaction, maintaining efficient operations without impacting soil health.

records.title: AlpStroy
records.description: AlpStroy’sguided and automatic parallel driving systems encompassparallel guiding systems for manual driving and systems for automatic driving are designed to optimize a wide range of fieldwork activities, including sowing, planting, spraying, fertilizer spreading, and strip cultivation. They deliver highly precise positioning of the machinery with accuracy ranging from less than a meter to a few centimeters, depending on the task's requirements. By leveraging these systems, farms can minimize operational redundancies such as overlapping passes and gaps between coverage, leading to optimized input usage and improved field productivity.

records.title: Chuy Mal Bazar (Чуй мал базар)
records.description: Chuy Mal Bazar is a Telegram group dedicated to buying and selling of live animals and fresh meat in the Chuy region of Kyrgyzstan. Sellers typically post a few photos, a description, their address, and a contact number. Interested buyers can respond directly to sellers via private messages on Telegram or contact via a phone call. This method allows sellers to avoid spending extensive time at animal markets, enabling them to conduct their sales online efficiently.
records.abstract: Telegram channel for marketing and sales of livestock

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Chuy Mal Bazar Telegram group enhances market reach for smallholder and medium-sized farms. Given that Telegram is one of the most widely used messaging platforms in Kyrgyzstan, it is easily adopted by users. The group enables these farms to increase their visibility beyond local animal markets and facilitates direct communication between sellers and buyers, leading to quicker transactions. Moreover, the platform provides free advertising, which helps reduce costs for smaller farms and producers.

records.title: Green Heritage (Зеленое наследие)
records.description: The Green Heritage portal was developed to facilitate the revitalization of forests. It offers open information on planted trees, including details by region and type, boundaries of allotments for new plantings, and updates on the status of existing plantings. Additionally, it allows individuals and organizations to register as volunteers for tree planting and includes a functionality for making donations to support future planting efforts.

records.title: The Global Temperature Trend Monitor
records.description: The Global Temperature Trend Monitor is an application that monitors the evolution of the global surface air temperature in recent decades until the present, and uses a simple model (using a 30-year linear trend) to estimate the level of global warming on the date up to which the trend is calculated, and the date when global warming will reach the 1.5°C limit of the Paris Agreement if the trend is maintained. The application offers a graphical representation of the change in the global average surface air temperature each month up to the selected month with respect to the pre-industrial period. A grey box indicates the estimated “global warming’” in the selected month, while a red marker indicates the point in the future at which the trend line will reach the 1.5°C limit. The estimated 1.5°C limit date, i.e. when the temperature linear trend and the 1.5°C limit line will intersect, varies depending on the set of years used for the trend estimation.

_annotations.Impact: The Global Temperature Trend Monitor raises awareness of long-term global warming trends by providing up-to-date data on global temperatures.

records.title: AITS (СИОЖ)
records.description: The Animal Identification and Traceability System (AITS) is a platform designed to record data on identified animals, including their movements, owners, farms, and veterinary and sanitary conditions. It aims to promote interaction, efficiency, and transparency for veterinarians, livestock owners, and government entities. The system uses unique identifiers to ensure that each animal is distinctly tracked, enabling detailed documentation of their location, farm, and veterinary status. Current services offered by AITS include animal registration and deregistration, tracking the number of registered animals by region and village, recording animal arrivals and removals, checking animal details, finding local veterinarians, and verifying the authenticity of veterinary documents.

records.owner_name: State Inspectorate for Veterinary and Phytosanitary Safety under the Government of the Kyrgyz Republic

SDGs.value: SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

_annotations.Impact: AITS supports enhanced animal health and welfare through detailed tracking and documentation of animal health, movements, and veterinary conditions, which ensures timely vaccinations and health plans. It increases efficiency by streamlining processes related to animal management, reducing administrative burdens, and improving operational efficiency for veterinarians and government entities. Additionally, AITS promotes transparency by providing clear records of animal health and movements, which supports better compliance with veterinary regulations and enhances the credibility of veterinary practices and government oversight.

records.title: Pochva A (Почва А)
records.description: Pochva A is a portal that facilitates agrochemical soil analysis. The system introduces an online application submission process for agrochemical soil analysis, allowing farmers to request evaluations of their agricultural sites. Through this digital interface, farmers can also conveniently check the results of the agrochemical soil analysis, conducted at soil and agrochemical stations under the State Design Institute for Land Management "Kyrgyzgiprozem," once the soil samples are delivered to sample collection points. The platform provides guidance on soil sampling and submission, and it offers free access to soil health data. Additionally, Pochva A offers analytics on soil health and the number of analyses conducted per region.

records.title: Climate Campaigners app
records.description: The Climate Campaigners app features diverse challenges that can help the general public to live more CO2-neutral lives. Customers can receive tips and inspiration, and track and analyse their CO2 savings – in detail and real time. The app connects customers with Climate Campaigners from 13 cities – from Dublin and Milan to Lahti. Customers can see which challenges are the most popular in real time and share their ideas and experiences with others. Completed challenges are rewarded with “Coins” that can be redeemed for such products as organic groceries. Users can connect with other users around the world and invite one another through social media and chat features to participate in particular pro-environment challenges.

records.title: Farmable
records.description: Farmable is a mobile app designed in Norway specifically for “top” fruit, being fruit grown on trees such as apples and pears. All data from field operations are collected in one place and form the basis of a digital model for the farm that supports decision-making. The benefits to the grower include: 1) crop treatment suggestions and access a spray calculator that specifies the amount of product needed; 2) a job management function that uses global positioning system (GPS) technologies to track spraying in the field and to log activities automatically; 3) the easy identification of issues in the field from app’s field notes, which can be shared with agronomists or other team members along with GPS coordinates; and 4) harvest logging, allowing the user to track the yields of trees at a block level.
records.abstract: Mobile farming app boosting tree crop yields and reducing waste

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The Farmable app tracks orchard inputs down to the row level, giving growers more precise control of their water, energy, fertiliser and pesticide inputs, while increasing crop yields, thus contributing to the nutritional needs of the growing population. Farmable also enhances efficiency by cutting down on environmental waste, as well as water and energy inputs. Furthermore, the use of fertilizer and pesticides is reduced, lowering the risk of potentially harmful runoff. In addition, human resources and logistics can be optimized, eliminating the unnecessary use of energy-consuming vehicles and equipment, all of which contribute to greater profits.

records.title: Co$ting Nature
records.description: Co$ting Nature is a web-based policy support system for natural capital accounting and ecosystem service analyses that incorporates detailed global datasets and spatial models for biophysical and socioeconomic climate and land-use processes and scenarios. It calculates a baseline for current ecosystem service provision, and allows interventions (policy options) or change scenarios to be applied to understand their impact on ecosystem service delivery. The tool features more than 140 input maps, and calculates the spatial distribution of 18 ecosystem services and combines these with conservation priority maps, threatened biodiversity and endemism data to understand the spatial distribution of critical ecosystems to support the determination of conservation priorities. Outputs are in the form of a series of summary maps expressed in relative terms (0–1) that combine the outputs of different modules (ecosystem service bundles).

records.title: Vkursi Zemli
records.description: The Vkursi Zemli online database provides maps and analytics about the agricultural land in Ukraine broken down based on more than 100 criteria based on land plot, owner and user. Through Vkursi Zemli, agribusinesses can effectively manage and monitor their land resources while service and financial companies can better navigate their clients' businesses. The database provides information about the parameters of land plots (category, purpose, owner, tenant, lease terms, etc.), tenants and lease information, as well as a normative monetary valuation of land plots in terms of purpose, the number of land plots and their areas. The database further offers access to data on any restrictions and encumbrances related to particular land plots as well as any legal cases.
records.abstract: Database providing maps and analytics on Ukrainian agricultural land and producers

_annotations.Source: ["FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices","Information provided by a member of the organization"]

SDGs.value: SDG 16: Peace, justice and strong institutions

_annotations.Impact: The online database provides decision-making support to various actors in the agricultural value chain, and can help protect farmers’ rights related to land. The tool allows farmers to learn more about their land, to check whether the land is registered electronically and to identify the true owner of the land. If the online database identifies a mistake in the state registries, the farmers can act promptly to address the situation. _raw.Description: The Vkursi Zemli online database provides maps and analytics about the agricultural land in Ukraine broken down based on more than 100 criteria based on land plot, owner and user. Through Vkursi Zemli, agribusinesses can effectively manage and monitor their land resources while service and financial companies can better navigate their clients' businesses. The database provides information about the parameters of land plots (category, purpose, owner, tenant, lease terms, etc.), tenants and lease information, as well as a normative monetary valuation of land plots in terms of purpose, the number of land plots and their areas. The database further offers access to data on any restrictions and encumbrances related to particular land plots as well as any legal cases.
_raw.Impact: The online database provides decision-making support to various actors in the agricultural value chain, and can help protect farmers’ rights related to land. If the online database identifies a mistake in the state registries, the farmers can act promptly to address the situation. Subscribers can also sign up to be alerted if the legal status of their land changes, or if restrictions or encumbrances are placed on their land.

records.title: Adopt an Olive Tree
records.description: The "Adopt an Olive Tree" initiative is managed via an online app that connects olive tree farmers in Greece with consumers around the world. Consumers who adopt an olive tree receive a yearly harvest of high-quality olive oil, while simultaneously supporting sustainable farming practices in Spain. To participate in the initiative, consumers visit the Adopt an Olive Tree website and select a tree from one of several participating farms in Greece. The initiative has helped small-scale farmers access new markets and increase their income, while also preserving traditional farming practices and promoting environmental sustainability. More info is available at www://apadrinaunolivo.org/es.

records.title: Varsling Innen PlanteSkadegjørere
records.description: Varsling Innen PlanteSkadegjørere (VIPS) is an open-source app providing prognosis, monitoring and decision support in agriculture. It can be accessed via a mobile app and/or web-based app, and provides observations, forecasts and decision support for the integrated management of agricultural pests, diseases and weeds. The app makes use of data from most online weather stations, public weather data networks and weather forecasts, allowing pest and disease models to be based on specific local conditions with multiple sources of input data. Pest and disease observations can be reported via one’s smartphone and reported using online maps. The website features maps on which model outputs are linked to geographical locations, and presents risk alerts in green, amber and red to indicate whether there is a need for further action. Detailed breakdowns of the risk levels associated with each pest or disease risk model can be accessed via the system. VIPS also facilitates access to a decision support tool developed by Danish IPM Consult for the management of weeds in cereal crops, including adaptations to fit Norwegian conditions, and a direct link to RimPRO which provides warnings on apple scab and codling moth outbreaks. Norwegian VIPS users can access information via the VIPS website, or can subscribe to SMS or email risk alerts. Final decisions on the actions to be applied in the fields are decided by the farmer or in collaboration with the local agricultural advisory service.
records.abstract: Automatic forecasting system for agricultural pests and diseases
records.owner_name: Norwegian Institute of Bioeconomy Research (NIBIO); Norwegian agricultural extension service (Norsk landbruksrådgivning)

_annotations.Source: ["Desktop research","FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices"]

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: In a survey carried out by NIBIO in 2021, 1 070 potato producers were approached to take part, and 369 responded. The survey results indicated that over 60 percent of the respondents had made direct use of VIPS services or had received alters, suggesting that farmers are willing to make use of alternative sources of information to steer their farming decisions during the growing seasons. Pest and disease warnings have been open and freely available to Norwegian farmers and advisors through the web site www.vips-landbruk.no since 2001, providing data from a network of more than 80 weather stations. Additional locations can be added by linking private weather stations to the system. Users can access specific risk models for 16 pests and diseases, as well as damage thresholds for several pests, and information and reports on pest and disease observations for a wide range of agricultural crops.

records.title: SUTTI Digital Solution Suite
records.description: The SUTTI Digital Solution Suite features three mobile and desktop applications that facilitate scalable capacity building across fragmented agricultural supply chains, connecting smallholder farmers, field officers, local buyers and industrial partners/stakeholders with agriculture production and post-harvest solutions. The suite provides access to e-learning modules for farming, peer support systems, up-to-date market prices, and supply chain impact and monitoring data. The SUTTI Digital Solution Suite is a digital operational tool created under the Ksapa SUTTI Initiative, and targets the delivery of hybrid capacity-building programmes through the provision of face-to-face and digital training to smallholders, thus boosting professional training, and monitoring the impact in the process. The Digital Solution Suite offers three different apps to suit different target users: the SUTTI Training Participants App, the SUTTI Reporting Dashboard and the SUTTI Operational Management System. The SUTTI Training Participants App facilitates the two-way transfer of information to and from smallholders and other users based on an off-road solution that is adaptable to rural and vulnerable populations and accessible by those who are less tech-savvy and illiterate. It incorporates an e-learning module, a chat-based helpline, a market price information database of daily commodity prices, a portal that increases the access and knowledge of users related to products and services, and a sales and transaction module through which users can keep track of their transactions. The SUTTI Reporting Dashboard app, on the other hand, allows industrial groups and sponsors to monitor all aspects of the capacity building programmes provided through the Training Participants App, with details of progress in training deployment, and assessments of the economic, environmental and social impacts of training based on key performance indicators, providing a better understanding of procurement by accessing farmer’s sales and transactions module. The SUTTI Operational Management System is the back-office tool that allows field instructors to manage the operational aspects of the applied programmes, including the enrolment of farmers, the management of training programmes and the operational follow-up procedures. Instructors are sourced in-house by Ksapa, utilizing its expert knowledge in the fields of sustainability, finance & investment, digital solutions, agronomy, development programs design and management and impact measurement.
records.abstract: E-learning app aiding the delivery and monitoring of capacity building programmes

_annotations.Source: ["Desktop research","Information provided by a member of the organization"]

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: According to the website, the SUTTI Digital Solution Suite can support farmers with improved technical, business, and soft skills, can increase crop yields through the dissemination of best practices, and can increase farmer revenues through diversification. It is especially useful for those in isolated and remote locations where market access is limited, serving as a source of knowledge and innovation through accessible learning modules. The Training Participants App also reaches some farmers indirectly through peer-to-peer chats, positively influencing the practices of five to ten non-participant farmers, thus boosting SUTTI’s impact. Moreover, SUTTI can also positively impact climate change (carbon sequestration & GHG emissions avoidance) through innovative technical itineraries with positive carbon impacts resulting from reduced irrigation, fewer inputs, less tillage, diversification & waste valuation. The 10-year objective (by 2030) of SUTTI is to reach 1 million beneficiaries, to provide 5 million hours of training, to increase farmers’ revenues by EUR 150 million, and the sequestration/avoidance of 4.5 million t CO2 in carbon emissions.

records.title: Soliq
records.description: Soliq is a mobile app that serves as a comprehensive management tool for taxpayers, including individuals and entrepreneurs,  providing access to various tax-related resources and services. The electronic services offered through the mobile app include updated news related to tax legislation, regulatory documents, Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) and case studies related to taxation. Among its key features, the app allows access to personal tax accounts, and can be used to pay and track taxes, and to receive statements from personal account cards. It can also be used to transfer funds from personal bank cards, and to generate financial documents.

records.title: i-bee
records.description: i-bee is an app that allows beekeepers to monitor THE temperature, sound, hive weight, population count and motion in their apiaries through the use of sensors and data transmission stations connected to a smartphone app. The app also sends out push notifications to the beekeepers in the event of an emergency or critical situation that threatens the hives. Beekeepers can remotely monitor the status of their apiary and hives in real time, and the hive weight data supports them in the control of the honey harvest. The app provides temperature and humidity data to the beekeeper all year round, alerting him/her to any need for insulation or ventilation. The sound data, on the other hand, provide the beekeeper with information about the brood of the queen and the swarming process. The app also features a beekeeper's diary that is free to use.
records.abstract: Apiary monitoring mobile application

_annotations.Source: ["Desktop research","FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices"]

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: According to the website, i-bee contributes to the reduction of all possible risks, including disease and loss of bee swarm, and aids in the improvement of planning and the recording of technological operations. The mobile app allows all data to be uploaded to an Excel file for further processing. For agricultural holdings, the main focus is on analysing the number of bees and tracking honey production, while for nomadic apiaries, emphasis is on the timely movement to new blooms. Industrial apiaries require deep and consistent monitoring on a hive-by-hive basis, and the collection of extensive data for future season planning. For private beekeepers, the app facilitates the online monitoring of their apiary, and rapid response in times of need.

records.title: Sencrop
records.description: Sencrop offers numerous farm management solutions to farmers based on agro-weather monitoring, data analysis and visualization through a mobile device or desktop app. Sencrop acquires data from rain gauges, anemometers and wetness sensors allowing professionals to instantly access ultra-local weather data for any location, 24 hours a day. The data can be transmitted by 0G signal. Users can, in real time, access their data via the mobile app, personalize alerts to position an intervention at the best time, and intervene in the event of disease outbreaks or frost. Water accumulations can be calculated to plan a treatment after a rain, or to predict phenological trends thanks to the water accumulations expressed in days and cold hours. The four weather monitoring tools available are Raincrop, Windcrop, Leafcrop and Solarcrop, which can be used separately or together. Raincrop comes equipped with a dual-trough swivel system for the accurate measurement of cumulative rainfall, and data is drawn from three temperature and humidity sensors ensuring the provision of reliable weather data and preventing measurements from drifting over time. Windcrop is an independent sensor that ensures stable free readings, and provides data on average wind speeds and gusts. Leafcrop simulates a real leaf at the heart of the foliage cover, where it measures leaf humidity, temperature and air conditions, as well as the leaf humidity rate. Another three temperature and air humidity sensors are placed nearby that measure local weather conditions. Solarcrop is a patented pyranometer or irradiance sensor that measures ultra-local solar radiation levels, which can be used for optimum irrigation management.
records.abstract: Data-driven agri-weather solutions

_annotations.Source: ["Desktop research","FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices"]

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The weather stations set up in fields provide reliable, accurate and ultra-local data remotely, supporting decision-making in planning and the streamlining of daily tasks, as well as the management of chemical inputs, thus contributing to crop care and productivity. In France, 1645 agricultural data points are now live, and the Sencrop team  has started to expand in Europe with dedicated vendors in the Netherlands. In 2018, dedicated sales teams settled in the UK and Spain.  To date, 3422 stations have been sold, and a new cooperative partnership has been established with the Chamber of Agriculture of Île-de-France. In 2019, Sencrop’s third station – Leafcrop (the connected wetness sensor) won an award at SIVAL, and fundraised approximately USD 11 million.  In the same year, Sencrop started establishing private networks for larger organizations, and in 2020, the start-up acquired its competitor Visio-Green. It now operates 15 000+ agricultural data points.

records.title: TOMCHI
records.description: TOMCHI is a mobile app for the management of water developed by the Ministry of Water Resources of Uzbekistan in collaboration with the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation. It provides information on water-saving irrigation techniques and provides the user with the approximate cost of introducing water-saving technologies. The app serves as a platform for the communication of providers and users of water-saving technologies, and aims to raise awareness, to encourage user feedback, to reduce information asymmetries about the technologies,  and to promote the adoption of technology-driven water-saving practices.
records.abstract: Mobile application for water management and water-saving irrigation techniques
records.owner_name: Ministry of Water Resources of Uzbekistan

_annotations.Impact: TOMCHI aims to address the critical global issue of water management. The application brings together a wealth of information on water-saving techniques and serves as a platform for stakeholder discussions. Given the significant role of agriculture in water consumption in Uzbekistan, facilitating access to such knowledge is crucial. The tool's ability to calculate costs related to these techniques can aid in informed decision-making.

records.title: Hydromet.uz
records.description: The UZHYDROMET website, powered by the Hydrometeorological Service of Uzbekistan, offers the general population of Uzbekistan comprehensive access to a wide array of hydrometeorological information and services, including real-time weather conditions, 3-day forecasts, and environmental and agro-meteorological bulletins, while also allowing specific hydrometric data to be requested from the data archives. Users can check specific mountainous regions for potential dangers, such as landslides, and obtain certificates for comparisons of hydrometeorological equipment and measurement tools. Users seeking certification for their hydrometeorological equipment and measuring tools usually strive to validate the precision and reliability of the data generated by their devices. Acquiring a certificate typically indicates adherence to the recognized standards and ensures that the measurements and readings obtained using certified equipment are precise and trustworthy.

Users seeking certification for their hydrometeorological equipment and measuring tools usually strive to validate the precision and reliability of the data generated by their devices. Acquiring a certificate typically indicates adherence to the recognized standards and ensures that the measurements and readings obtained using certified equipment are precise and trustworthy.

UZHYDROMET can also support risk management by providing early warnings of extreme weather conditions and potential dangers in mountainous regions.

records.title: Organic Farm Knowledge
records.description: Organic Farm Knowledge is an online app that provides access to practice-oriented tools and resources related to organic farming that can help improve production through cross-border exchanges of knowledge among farmers, farm advisers and scientists. The app can be used to access factsheets, guides, online calculation tools and videos presenting scientific and practical advice, created for and by practitioners, facilitating access to and the implementation of knowledge. The covered themes include arable crops, soil quality and fertility, nutrient management, pest and disease control, weed management, animal husbandry, ration planning, and organic seed and plant breeding, and plans are in place to add such themes as fruit production, farm economics, food chain management and biodiversity to the list, among others.
records.abstract: Portal for the promotion of knowledge exchange among organic farmers and advisors

_annotations.Source: ["Desktop research","FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices"]
_annotations.Impact: A user survey was conducted from 8 June to 10 July 2020 in 11 different languages, garnering 71 responses in total, primarily from organic farmers, researchers and advisors. The results revealed that most users wanted to (1) learn something new about organic farming, (2) to browse innovations, and/or (3) to find a solution to a specific problem. Online information was by far the most important source of information for all the respondents, far exceeding discussions with farmers, advisors and/or researchers, as well as printed material. An online tool or app is essential for attracting the attention of the younger generation of farmers.

records.title: Food Confidence Platform
records.description: Food Confidence is a blockchain-based traceability system that identifies, monitors and aids in the resolution of supply chain problems instantaneously for the benefit of multiple actors. The system makes use of blockchain technologies to alert actors in real time of any risks or non-compliances. The system comprises multiple technologies and modules that independently digitize, standardize, audit, track and trace, measure and monetize food data for the immediate benefit of a business. Food Confidence currently offers six modules, and a further module is under development. The different modules, which can be used all together or separately, are priced based on the selected package, being: FoodTwin Generator, LiveAudit, LiveTrack, LiveScan, CSR Analyzer, Fresh Origin and FoodTwin Exchange (in development), all of which come with training and support. Food Twin Generator converts unstructured food data into standardized digital twins automatically through a live dashboard. LiveAudit delivers real-time quality assurance through batch compliance checks as a replacement for manual audits in agribusiness. The tool also simplifies supplier vetting and automatically verifies product and supplier attributes for safety and customer satisfaction. LiveTrack offers real-time, batch-level traceability to food supply chain managers, following the food to accurately map the real-time, real-world journeys of the ingredients and finished products. LiveScan offers a simple approach through which food brands can connect with consumers using dynamic data. By scanning the label, consumers can access batch-level, consumer-friendly details about the real history of a food product. The CSR Analyzer automatically calculates Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), sustainability, and other Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) metrics based on real-time, end-to-end supply chain data. FreshOrigin allows retailers to inform shoppers exactly where their unpackaged produce is sourced, spotlighting upstream farmers and producers.
records.abstract: Blockchain-based traceability of agri-food supply chains

_annotations.Source: ["Desktop research","FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices"]
_annotations.Impact: This data-driven traceability system was founded by two experts with over 40 years of collective experience in the food sector. The developed technologies address many of the challenges encountered in achieving end-to-end traceability. In the world of fragmented supply chains and non-digitized systems, the website suggests that the system can meet the emerging and urgent needs for a more efficient audit and traceability system, especially as new legislation takes effect around the world. The Food Confidence app introduced LiveAudit, a real-time digital auditing tool enhanced with blockchain technologies, to improve the food industry’s audit cycles, ensuring data accuracy and identifying non-compliances in real time, thereby improving food safety and reducing waste. In the short term, clients using this app gain comprehensive supply chain traceability, and aggregated and standardized data in one secure hub. This allows the rapid adaptation to consumer demands for knowledge of product origin and quality. In the long term, users can digitize their supply chains and make real-time data-driven decisions. LiveAudit further aids the early identification of non-compliances in production, preventing issues from reaching consumers. Food Confidence is preparing to introduce Food Twin Exchange to its portfolio as an e-commerce space where agribusinesses can buy and sell access to food product data through the blockchain.

records.title: Genpro
records.description: Genpro is an online app developed for recording data related to the management of genealogical or herd livestock books in Portugal and Spain. It aids in the recording and management of data on livestock breeds, including cattle, sheep, goats, horses and pigs. The application allows for the recording of all kinds of animal data, such as ear tags, ID numbers, genealogies, weights, artificial insemination and medication status, etc. Genpro was developed initially for farmers’ unions and associations engaged in the management of herd books, and the app has been developed while maintaining an ongoing relationship with these associations. The app keeps records of all monitoring data related to local domestic breeds, which can be updated by users and accessible by anyone with an account. The R.campo Android app can be used alongside Genpro for the collection of animal data in the field, and technicians from the farmers’ associations can use Genpro to collect data from several farms and obtain a full portrait of a specific breed. The data can then be used to design and implement conservation programmes that are then passed on to the farmers. These procedures can also be carried out by individual users.
records.abstract: App for the tracking and management of livestock

_annotations.Source: ["Desktop research","FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices"]
_annotations.Impact: Established in 2006, Genpro maintains livestock data records of the genetic health of breeds to avoid inbreeding, which can lead to breed extinction, and to develop and implement marketing strategies for such animals, making local communities more sustainable. It is currently being used by farmers’ associations in Portugal and Spain, and features a total catalogue of 81 livestock breeds. More than 12 million animals and more than 3200 users have been registered to date. Genpro partners with the Portuguese Research Center for Agriculture (INIAV), which uses the app for the genetic evaluation of animals, facilitating the characterization of the animals of each breed, which can aid in conservation strategies.

records.title: Hive-Tech
records.description: HiveTech is a monitoring system for beekeepers that supports beehive management and increases honey production through the use of GPS-referenced data related to humidity, temperature, sound and weight. The data can be accessed through hardware now known as Hive-Tech Pro Version 2 and through apps. Use of the application requires the user to purchase the Hive-Tech hardware, featuring aluminium rods integrated with sensors and SIM technologies that are used to collect hive data. The user can then integrate their hives with the 3Bee system by following instructions in the app, thus allowing hive monitoring. Apiaries and the creation and management of hives are enhanced by the data visualization tools that record weight, internal and external temperatures, moisture and sound, supported by real-time weather forecasts, vocal recognition software for audio-note recording, calendar-based activity planning, and the ability to receive updates and alert notifications. The app also features a marketplace through which users can sell their honey at retail prices across Europe through the “Adopt a Hive” app. The app is freely accessible, however, the user must have purchased 3Bee’s hardware to access Hive-Tech.
records.abstract: Beehive monitoring hardware and app

_annotations.Source: ["Desktop research","FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices"]

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The intended benefits of this technology relate to the welfare status of beekeepers; the optimisation of honey production; the reduction of bee losses due to starvation; and the enhanced ability to move hives to the most profitable locations. According to 3Bee, the company has to date contributed to the protection of 120 million bees, enabling the pollination of nearly 72 billion flowers. The company has stated that beekeepers have seen a 300 percent improvement in productivity by minimizing losses and enhancing honey revenues. The core business regards the Bee-project facilitated through a growing network of the company’s app and Hive-Tech hardware, however, the grants and the CSR projects carried out with corporate entities have provided 3Bee, with the opportunity to develop new ideas targeting other farming sectors, such as livestock farming, harvesting or pollination.

records.title: DRON AGRO ASSISTANCE
records.description: DRON AGRO ASSISTANCE is a drone service offered by Dron Assistance SRL that supports various agricultural processes, including, but not limited to, crop sowing, monitoring, and pesticide and fertilizer applications. The drone service can be applied to various crops, such as grains, cereals, legumes, vegetables, fruit, etc., for the monitoring of plant health, yield, irrigation and fertilizer deficiencies, weed and pest outbreaks, among others. DRON AGRO ASSISTANCE was the first company in the Republic of Moldova to receive approval from the civil aviation authorities to conduct agricultural aircraft operations using drones.
records.abstract: Agricultural drone service

_annotations.Source: ["Desktop research","Information provided by a member of the organization"]

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The services provided by DRON AGRO ASSISTANCE can make sowing, spraying and monitoring activities easier, faster and more effective. The use of drones in agriculture can support the more responsible use of water and fertilizers, and can help farmers avoid tyre and track induced soil compaction. According to company estimates, the service costs are offset by the substantial savings that are achieved, in that the drone service requires 20 percent less pesticide and significantly less water. The service also eliminates the 5 to 10 percent crop loss and the soil damage attributable to the use of agricultural machinery, while also speeding up agricultural processes. The service can also be attractive for smallholder farmers, who can avoid the financial burden of purchasing equipment. A company representative stated in an interview that in 2023, traditional spraying in Moldova (using a tractor and sprayer) cost around USD 50 per ha , and that using the drone service can help farmers economise on field treatments.

records.title: Uzman Çiftçi
records.description: Farmer Expert (Uzman Çiftçi) is a free online app that serves as a blockchain-based marketplace in which farmers register, set their prices and sell their products directly to consumers, retailers and food processors. The platform features a social media page where users can post their agricultural stocks or demands. The platform makes use of SMS, an online payment system and a chat channel for direct communication, business transactions and brokerage services. The platform makes use of blockchain-based traceability to ensure transparency along the supply chain. Users can upload or access information about the origin of the listed products, the fertilizers used, food safety lab results, and much more, by scanning a QR code on the page of each product. Furthermore, innovations such as an “ugly fruit” section promote sustainability and reduce waste by promoting the sale of imperfect fruit. The platform also features an educational channel, Ureten TV, through which farmers are kept updated on industrial trends, economic conditions and innovative solutions. All these facilities are accessible through the e-commerce pages, allowing customers to order fresh, local produce within Türkiye that are promoted through the website, providing smallholders with more opportunities to sell their products. The company provides logistic support, making deliveries from farms to processing facilities in less than an hour, according to the website.
records.abstract: Blockchain-based e-commerce for agrifood products

_annotations.Source: ["Desktop research","FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices"]

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The platform is available for use throughout Türkiye. Some 11 000 farmers have registered to date, working with 150 agricultural engineers, and more than 195 000 agricultural products have so far been delivered within the country.

records.title: BrioAgro Aqua
records.description: BrioAgro is an intelligent system for the management of automatic smart irrigation based on collected soil and environmental data. The system, available as a mobile app and via an online app, processes and visualises the information obtained from low-cost technologies, including field sensors and satellite data. This system is adaptable to greenhouses and outdoor agriculture systems, including olive groves and vineyards. The soil moisture calibration algorithm is connected to the irrigation system, and so irrigation is begun automatically when the crop needs it, with precise calculations of the amount of water required, thus preventing water wastage. The system also provides alerts to farmers of any conditions that may threaten their crops, and advises them to take appropriate action in real time via the mobile app. The app can be used to monitor treatment tanks and pipe pressure, and to oversee motorized battery charging in solar energy systems, with potential uses in an expansive range of sectors. It is also adept at controlling both water and fertilizer pumps, maintaining fertilizer lines, managing irrigation ponds and recording rain data through pulse rain gauges. It also provides access to past irrigation data and offers flexibility between traditional and sensor-driven irrigation methods. In greenhouse applications, it can monitor conditions both inside and outside, and can assess fertilizer levels in olive groves and vineyards.
records.abstract: Automatic smart irrigation management

_annotations.Source: ["Desktop research","FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices"]

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: According to their website, BrioAgro reduces the risks associated with water loss and increases irrigation performance (20 percent or more) and irrigation quality, while also reducing the percolation of fertilizers and plant protection products that can permeate into underground aquifers. Tests performed in 2019 in olive groves in Spain and Portugal revealed a reduction of around 70 percent in fertilizers used. BrioAgro can support the application of smart irrigation and fertigation programmes, triggering watering when needed at the right time and in appropriate quantities, thus increasing profits. It also uses the collected information to create predictive harvesting models for each crop in the region. The solution has been tested by many farmers in different regions of Spain, and has been shown to meet the requirements of both small and large agricultural enterprises, and to be adaptable to all types of irrigated crops.

records.title: Youth digital innovation programme
records.description: As part of the Digital Villages Initiative (DVI) in Uzbekistan, FAO, working in collaboration with IT-Park, has supported the implementation of a special digital innovation programme aimed at mobilizing young talents in Fergana valley to co-develop digital solutions aimed at resolving the challenges faced by their rural communities. The programme was launched with a “Digital Villages Camp” – a skill development programme – and culminated with a hackathon aimed at accelerating the development of digital innovations. The Camp introduced 25 participants aged between 16 and 30 to the fundamentals of the Internet of Things (IoT) in smart farming, and over the following five weeks, the young talents gained knowledge and hands-on experience in programming IoT devices through the use of open-source solutions. Away from the IT-Park classrooms, the students spent significant time in the field, devising and testing smart solutions tailored to the unique needs of smallholder farmers in the Fergana Valley. The Hack4DigitalVillages innovation challenge was hosted in partnership with OSCE and the CGIAR Accelerate for Impact Platform, and attracted 244 applicants, and 36 teams were ultimately selected to prototype their digital solutions with the active participation of smallholder farmers. The winning teams received awards totalling USD 13 000 and mentorship packages. More information is available at www.fao.org/countryprofiles/news-archive/detail-news/ru/c/1670036/ and www.fao.org/europe/events/detail/hack4digitalvillages-innovation-challenge/

_annotations.Source: Information provided by a member of the organization

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The Digital Villages Camp and Hack4DigitalVillages initiatives have had a profound impact on technological innovation, while also addressing the agricultural challenges faced in the Fergana Valley. The Digital Villages Camp provided essential skills and hands-on experience to the young talents, supporting them in the development and implementation of digital solutions for smart farming. The subsequent Hack4DigitalVillages challenge showcased the tangible outcomes of the skill development programmes, with the winning teams presenting innovative projects integrating technologies such as IoT, automation, data management systems, and artificial intelligence with a view to enhancing agricultural practices. Such initiatives not only demonstrate the potential of digital solutions, but also encourage the active involvement of smallholder farmers in the co-creation process, ensuring that the technologies developed are tailored to the real needs of the local community.

_raw.Description: As part of the Digital Villages Initiative (DVI) in Uzbekistan, FAO, working in collaboration with IT-Park, has supported the implementation of a special digital innovation programme aimed at mobilizing young talents in Fergana valley to co-develop digital solutions aimed at resolving the challenges faced by their rural communities. The programme was launched with a “Digital Villages Camp” – a skill development programme – and culminated with a hackathon aimed at accelerating the development of digital innovations. The Camp introduced 25 participants aged between 16 and 30 to the fundamentals of the Internet of Things (IoT) in smart farming, and over the following five weeks, the young talents gained knowledge and hands-on experience in programming IoT devices through the use of open-source solutions. Away from the IT-Park classrooms, the students spent significant time in the field, devising and testing smart solutions tailored to the unique needs of smallholder farmers in the Fergana Valley. The Hack4DigitalVillages innovation challenge was hosted in partnership with OSCE and the CGIAR Accelerate for Impact Platform, and attracted 244 applicants, and 36 teams were ultimately selected to prototype their digital solutions with the active participation of smallholder farmers. The winning teams received awards totalling USD 13 000 and mentorship packages. More information is available at www.fao.org/countryprofiles/news-archive/detail-news/ru/c/1670036/ and www.fao.org/europe/events/detail/hack4digitalvillages-innovation-challenge/
_raw.Impact: The Digital Villages Camp and Hack4DigitalVillages initiatives have had a profound impact on technological innovation, while also addressing the agricultural challenges faced in the Fergana Valley. The Digital Villages Camp provided essential skills and hands-on experience to the young talents, supporting them in the development and implementation of digital solutions for smart farming. The subsequent Hack4DigitalVillages challenge showcased the tangible outcomes of the skill development programmes, with the winning teams presenting innovative projects integrating technologies such as IoT, automation, data management systems, and artificial intelligence with a view to enhancing agricultural practices. Such initiatives not only demonstrate the potential of digital solutions, but also encourage the active involvement of smallholder farmers in the co-creation process, ensuring that the technologies developed are tailored to the real needs of the local community.

records.title: Fishing license (Рыболовный билет)
records.description: Fishing license is an online application form for obtaining a fishing license for recreational fishing in the waters of the Kyrgyz Republic. It covers 7 regions of Kyrgyzstan, verious rivers and lakes, and fish species. Fishermen can obtain one of the four types of ticket: 1) ticket for marinka, crucian carp, perch, rudd, roach, ide, bream, tench, chebak, chebachek, dace, barbel, crayfish; 2) ticket for carp, barbel, catfish, asp, grass carp, silver carp, roach, pike, snakehead, pike pench; 3) river trout; 4) river osman. Tickets are valid for 3 days.

records.title: GRAND EXPERT
records.description: GRAND EXPERT is an online platform providing beekeepers with a suite of tools. The Beekeeping Electronic Scales offers real-time hive monitoring for beekeepers, enabling remote management and instant alerts. It also enhances precision beekeeping practices. The Plant Chemical Treatment Process Monitoring System is an online service that replaces traditional notifications to rural dwellers, beekeepers, and food consumers about planned agricultural chemical treatments. It sends alerts to registered users, particularly beekeepers, providing real-time information about upcoming treatments. This initiative aims to reduce the harmful environmental impact of pesticides by improving public awareness. Both solutions contribute to sustainable agriculture, environmental protection, and the well-being of beekeepers and the community. GRAND EXPERT also provides access to knowledge and advisory in the beekeeping sector with an online library and by gathering useful information on beekeeping procurement companies and public organizations working on apiculture.
records.abstract: Cross-sharing for beekeepers about planned treatments

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The Beekeeping Electronic Scales can have a positive impact on reducing human health and animal welfare risks associated with chemical pesticides by notifying citizens and giving beekeepers real-time hive weight data, improving hive management, and optimizing honey production. The SMS remote control feature makes operation convenient and transparent. The Plant Chemical Treatment Process Monitoring System addresses environmental and public health concerns related to agricultural chemical treatments.

records.title: Status of Digital Agriculture in 18 countries of Europe and Central Asia
records.description: This report analyses the adoption of digital agriculture and strategies in 18 countries across Europe and Central Asia, addressing various dimensions, such as ICT access and usage, the presence of strategies, policies or legislation regulating the issue, and the availability of digital services and applications in agriculture. Among the countries reviewed, a number of countries have been identified as having adopted a systematic approach to the development of a national e-agriculture strategy: Albania, Armenia, the Republic of Moldova, the Russian Federation, Türkiye, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. In general, the report provides a comprehensive overview of the digital landscape in the analysed countries.

records.title: Smart Villages in Azerbaijan
records.description: The “Smart Villages in Azerbaijan” report is the primary outcome of an analytical and research initiative of World Bank that seeks to identify potential policy choices aimed at fostering technology and social innovation-driven smart village approaches. These approaches aim to enhance service delivery and promote local economic development in rural areas, with primary focus on supporting communities, in collaboration with local government and the private sector, in identifying opportunities and implementing solutions tailored to their specific needs. This is achieved based on bottom-up participatory needs assessments, knowledge and innovation transfer, and policy incentives, the integration of which can result in customized smart solutions for rural areas, leading to improved local economic development, enhanced connectivity, better services, increased livelihoods and incomes, and an overall improved quality of life. The paper is presented in six sections, each addressing a key aspect of the research and analysis undertaken to conceptualize and apply the smart village concept in Azerbaijan.
records.abstract: Analysis and Roadmap Framework

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The “Smart Villages in Azerbaijan” lays down a reference framework for the assessment of smart village readiness, offering valuable insights to policymakers and local authorities. The potential outcomes, including improved economic development, enhanced connectivity, better services and increased livelihoods, align with the overarching goal of elevating the quality of life in rural communities. The structured approach of the report, addressing key aspects of the research and analysis, positions it as a valuable resource that can guide initiatives aimed at transforming rural areas in Azerbaijan, with the potential also to serve as a model for similar global contexts.

records.title: Tarsim
records.description: Tarsim is an online application portal supporting the state-subsidized provision of insurance to farmers against natural disasters and other risks. The online portal can be accessed by all farmers and growers in Türkiye, who can make use of the available insurance packages. The portal is free to use after the user creates an account, and provides access to information about the different types of insurance available. In addition to the web platform, there is also Tarsim Mobil, a mobile application designed to make agricultural insurance easier to manage. It is used to reach agricultural insurance applications via smartphones and tablets, independent of location and time, and to ensure sustainability in communication with stakeholders. Tarsim Mobil is an application developed within TARSIM (Agricultural Insurance Pool) and addresses the longstanding issue of low agricultural insurance coverage by fostering a public-private partnership. While TARSIM standardizes insurance contracts, centralizes loss adjustment activities, and efficiently utilizes government subsidies, the application aims to support farmers in accessing these proposed services through the use of internet, by incorporating a web-based system for seamless operations, SMS and mobile apps for policy issuance, and employs remote sensing, GIS, and big data for risk assessment.
records.abstract: Agricultural insurance and risk management tools

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Tarsim, according to the website, provides access to knowledge and agricultural insurance, cutting out the fees associated with intermediaries. The TARSIM Mobile application supported by the government, aims at offering affordable insurance to farmers, trying to protect them from financial losses caused by unpredictable events. The rise in premiums and coverage indicates increasing farmer adoption. The collaboration between the government and insurance companies fosters a robust and sustainable system. A 17 percent yearly increase in insured farmers reflects growing trust and participation. The use of GIS and remote sensing enhances data-driven decisions, improving overall efficiency. Tarsim Mobile aims at simplifying the lives of stakeholders by providing a comprehensive and accessible platform for managing agricultural insurance-related tasks and accessing relevant information with ease.

records.title: Sustainable Management of Water Resources in Rural Areas in Uzbekistan
records.description: Within Component 2 of the “Sustainable Management of Water Resources in Rural Areas in Uzbekistan” project, the primary objective was to enhance the technical capacities of water management organizations operating at basin, water user association and farm levels. The goal of the project, funded by the European Union, UNDP and the Government of Uzbekistan to the tune of USD 6 428 150, was to ensure that rural communities could derive concrete benefits from the sustainable management of natural resources. The overarching intention was to improve the resilience of users to disasters and climate change by optimizing water supply and enhancing the efficiency of water resource management at various organizational tiers.
records.abstract: Technical Capacity Building (Component 2) Project #: 00090379 EU-WATER

_annotations.Impact: The final evaluation report suggested the project had been successful in implementing a water management programme  and greatly improved access to water by farms and the rural population in Uzbekistan, with improved water supplies to 13 000 ha of land, and providing thousands of people with easy access to safe drinking water.

records.title: Raccolti di Comunità
records.description: Raccolti di Comunitá is a social farming community that is connected through an online platform and engages in multiple cooperative activities. Farmers can join the cooperative through the online app, and benefit from the cooperative’s brand. The platform also allows its users to organize and participate in social and inclusive farming activities. The platform also allows users to buy and sell food products issued by social farming  and produced by members of the cooperative. Finally, the platform facilitates community exchanges for peer-learning, as well as project development and fundraising activities.
records.abstract: Online farming community

_annotations.Source: Information provided by a member of the organization

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The platform encourages cooperation among its members, and promotes the image and marketing of social farming operations, products and activities, especially in the Umbria region of Italy. The online platform supports the textual, visual and relational exchanges unfolding in social farming in the region, and its scope is now extending beyond Umbria. Cooperative members can link their own websites to the platform giving further reach to their activities. The online platform is a tool through which members combine their resources and efforts with a common goal.

records.title: Promoting agritourism and cultural engagement through digital marketing in Lolazor
records.description: As part of the pilot Digital Villages project in Tajikistan, and with the assistance of a local partner – the Tourism Development Centre – FAO is supporting the development of digital, rural and agri-tourism in Lolazor Digital Village by creating complete seasonal touristic itineraries, enhancing the capacity of the Lolazor community in rural and agri-tourism, and raising awareness and engagement with Lolazor's offerings through representation on travel websites, a social media presence and partnerships with travel agencies.

records.title: Piloting Digital Villages in Central Asia
records.description: The "Piloting Digital Villages in Central Asia” FVC/GLO/171/MUL project has been implemented by FAO in Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan through the so-called Flexible Voluntary Contribution (FVC) pooled funding tool. The initiative has facilitated the establishment of Central Asia’s first digital villages under the FAO Digital Villages Initiative (DVI). Over 30 villages were assessed using FAO’s Readiness Assessment Tool to identify those with the highest potential for success in their transformation into Digital Villages. In Uzbekistan, the project organizers identified and collaborated with the neighbouring rural communities of Novkent and Yuksalish in Fergana Valley. The project saw young local people getting involved in a dedicated innovation programme through which they acquired coding skills and collaborated with farmers to come up with innovations making use of cost-effective yet high-quality IoT sensors designed for small greenhouse owners. In Tajikistan, Lolazor village enhanced its mobile connectivity and increased its agritourism potential through digitalization with a view to attracting tourists to the scenic Hisor Valley. All rural communities underwent capacity development and living labs initiatives to identify the challenges they face and to come up with solutions. Furthermore, a twinning programme was launched facilitating the exchange of knowledge between communities and organizations in Uzbekistan and Tajikistan. In Kyrgyzstan, a “Digital Villages Farmer Service Centres” model was conceptualized to pave the way for the digitalization of public services in agriculture. On a regional scale, an AgriTech Observatory was established, among other knowledge-related projects.

_annotations.Impact: The project brought about the establishment of the first Digital Villages in Central Asia. By piloting  IoT sensors and smart technologies, small-scale farmers can increase their climate resilience, while enabling the remote monitoring and control of agricultural conditions. The focus on capacity development and innovation has instilled a culture of digital empowerment, while improving mobile connectivity in Lolazor village in Tajikistan has not only paved the way for agritourism, but also enhanced the promotion of local products. Knowledge exchanges and twinning programmes have facilitated collaborative problem-solving and the enrichment of community knowledge. The conceptualization of "Digital Villages Farmer Service Centres" in Kyrgyzstan has brought about a shift towards the digitalization of public services in agriculture, promising sustained benefits.

records.title: Mon bagage numérique
records.description: Mon bagage numérique is a website containing a vast toolbox supporting the digitalization of rural tourism in Wallonia. The website is organised in three sections: a diagnostic self-assessment tool to measure the level of digital maturity of an actor in the tourism market; a catalogue containing more than 200 options for the enhancement of digital skills (capacity building webinars, awareness-raising events, mentoring and training); and digital vouchers made available by the regional authorities in support of private initiatives (audits of digital tools; mentoring in the diagnostic analysis of digital maturity; personalized mentoring programmes; software and hardware purchases). Users can access a large number of audio-visual materials in French that can aid in the assessment and development of digital skills aimed at adapting tourism offers to meet digital demands.

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The goal of the website is to increase the level of knowledge and the digital capacity of actors in the tourism sector. By mutualizing common benefits such as knowledge sharing and purchases of capacity-building tools, the website and the team behind the initiative are seeking to reduce the individual financial outlays of organizations that want to learn and better equip themselves for the upcoming digital challenges and opportunities.

records.title: Living labs in Novkent, Yuksalish and Lolazor Digital Villages
records.description: Living Labs have been identified as a valid method of bringing together diverse stakeholders, including end-users, researchers, private sector organizations and policymakers, to collectively address pressing development challenges. The approach has been successfully implemented in Novkent and Yuksalish, two rural communities in Uzbekistan, and in the village of Lolazor of Tajikistan, as FAO’s first pilot Digital Villages in these countries. In Uzbekistan, Living Labs have led communities to collaborate in the identification and testing of innovative solutions to such critical issues as water scarcity, plant disease, climate change and production challenges. In Tajikistan, three thematic Living Labs have been organized focused on agri-entrepreneurship, livestock and pasture management, and access to funding through small grant programmes for individual farmers and women entrepreneurs. By employing co-exploration, co-design, and co-experimentation approaches, the participants of the Labs identified the main challenges they faced, and developed innovative business ideas and social projects aimed at tackling agricultural and livelihood issues.

By bringing together end-users, researchers, private sector organizations and policymakers, the Living Labs have raised awareness about the challenges faced by the communities and have facilitated the identification of solutions. Both the physical and virtual meetings have supported the sharing of knowledge and idea development. As a result of the three Living Labs hosted in Lolazor, the community has become more active on social media platforms, and has started marketing its agricultural products, such as grapes and apples, as well as seedlings. Furthermore, the community has embraced social media for the sharing of daily news and captivating landscape views through the Telegram “Digital Lolazor” chat group, featuring news articles related to the village, including construction projects and traditional celebrations, and other relevant information.

records.title: Low-cost IoT sensors for greenhouse monitoring
records.description: As part of the Digital Villages Initiative (DVI) in Uzbekistan, working in collaboration with IT-Park and the FAO Smart Farming for the Future Generation project, FAO has supported the installation of smart sensors in ten greenhouses owned by smallholder farmers in the villages of Novkent, Yukhsalish and Dustlik in the Fergana valley. The sensors were assembled at low cost (less than 100 USD) by using open-source solutions and good quality sensors, and by mobilizing young people in the local community as part of the Digital Villages Camp. Farmers equipped with the sensors can monitor the temperature, humidity, soil moisture and light in their greenhouses and can control their drip irrigation systems.

Among the benefits of the programme to the farmers were the facilitation of precision farming through real-time monitoring, resource efficiency through controlled irrigation, improved crop health management and increased productivity, all provided by cost-effective solutions making use of accessible technologies. The user-friendly Telegram bot interface ensured easy operation by the smallholders, even those with limited technical expertise.

records.title: Novkent
records.description: Located in Uzbekistan's Fergana Valley, Novkent village was one of the first pilot Digital Villages in the country, alongside the adjacent Yuksalish village. The village of 568 households is spread across an area of 160 ha, with a local economy that is based primarily on agriculture. Local farmers focus on cultivating raspberries, lemons and vegetables, often utilizing greenhouses. Under FAO’s Digital Villages Initiative (DVI) and more specifically the “Piloting Digital Villages in Central Asia” project (FVC/GLO/171/MUL), young people in the village have participated in a special innovation programme aimed at equipping them with coding skills, fostering collaboration with farmers and the development of innovations. Worthy of note among these innovations are the cost-effective yet high-quality IoT sensors that have been designed specifically for small greenhouse owners. To disseminate valuable agricultural knowledge, YouTube and Telegram channels have been established that serve as repositories for best agriculture practices, allowing for dynamic exchanges among community members. Furthermore, the rural community has embraced various capacity development and living labs initiatives to come up with practical solutions to the challenges faced by the community. Finally, a twinning programme has facilitated exchanges of knowledge with Tajikistan, promoting cross-cultural learning and collaboration between the two regions.

Small-scale farmers, and women and young people in particular, have been the main beneficiaries of these initiatives. Through targeted programmes such as innovation sessions targeting young people and women-only living labs, the community has witnessed a positive upturn.
