records.title: IoT sensors for irrigation water accounting
records.description: Under FAO’s “Integrated Natural Resources Management in Drought-Prone and Salt-Affected Agricultural Production Systems of Central Asia and Türkiye” project, six Internet of Things (IoT) sensors have been integrated into the irrigation systems run by the water resource management departments in the Kochkor district in Kyrgyzstan. The sensors provide real-time information on the volume of water at the gauging stations of Kockhor district that is transmitted to computers equipped with a specialized program for data processing. The purpose of this automated water accounting system is to provide control over water distribution among users, demonstrating the benefits of a transparent system for the dissemination of water distribution information. District water management specialists process the received information to gain an accurate understanding of the irrigation water situation in the district. Based on these data, agreements are made with water users, and payments for water deliveries are calculated and scheduled.
records.abstract: Kochkor villages
records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

_annotations.Source: Information provided by a member of the organization
_annotations.Impact: The installation of IoT sensors to support irrigation water accounting in Kyrgyzstan’s Kochkor district was carried out to address the challenges associated with the absence of an objective and reliable system for irrigation water accounting. The absence of water accounting has historically resulted in such issues as non-compliance with irrigation norms, the inefficient utilization of water resources, and the degradation of the reclamation state of lands. Irrigation water is now accurately accounted for, calculated and distributed based on availability and the needs of farmers, leading to a decline in conflicts and misunderstandings among community members. Furthermore, the systems have streamlined the monitoring process for the staff of the district water resource management and the Water Users Association by providing real-time information on water levels and distribution among users directly to their offices, thus removing the need for physical checks at the gauging stations. This transition from manual checks has not only led to savings in time, but also reduced resource-intensive tasks.

records.title: Famio
records.description: Famio is an online app that operates as management software for farms and rural enterprises hosting such recreational events as workshops and other activities, and as a booking channel for end users, primarily families and children. The online app lists available recreational activities organised by categories, and offers also a step-by-step process through which visitors can find information on upcoming events, book a place, make payments, and leave comments and feedback. Users can download and save the invoices and proofs of payment needed by the tax authorities and social security offices.

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The online app aims to streamline and simplify the administrative management of farms and enterprises offering recreational activities, and further, to consolidate offers and enhance the online searchability and comparability of organizations. Among the testimonials listed on the website, one user stated that “Famio offers unique and prompt assistance in personalizing online subscriptions and the dissemination of information through newsletters and other channels”. Another client highlighted the savings in time facilitated by Famio, while another testimonial shared the positive feedback received from families who had made use of the app as an interface with a farm running a summer school for children.

records.title: Gîtes et chambres d'hôtes de Wallonie
records.description: The Fédération des Gîtes et Chambres d'hôtes de Wallonie non-profit organization, established in 1989, operates an online app that showcases the vast quantity of rural accommodation offered in the Wallonia region of Belgium. Hosts can post their accommodation with image and text information, while visitors and tourists can use the search tools to identify suitable locations and the contact details of the provider.

records.title: DVI twinning
records.description: Twinning is a cooperation model involving both formal and informal structures at local levels, bringing together local communities (villages, local stakeholder groupings and alliances, or other local structures such as Local Action Groups) that share common areas of interest. DVI twinning facilitates horizontal linkages, cooperation and mutually beneficial exchanges of knowledge between peers, while reducing gaps in knowledge and digital imbalance, fostering the transfer of good practices, and encouraging cooperation with a view to reducing the digital rural divide. DVI twinning was initially piloted in 2022 between three rural communities - Përmet (Albania), Rahovec (Kosovo*) and Lormes smart village (France), leading to the creation of linkages, cooperation and knowledge-sharing. Several online workshops were held to introduce the local actors to each other, to understand the contexts of the three villages and their developmental needs, to exchange good practices and to identify actions with the potential to formalize twinning programmes in the future. DVI twinning has also been initiated between Lolazor, the pilot Digital Village in Tajikistan, and the Novkent and Yuksalish pilot Digital Villages in Uzbekistan, formalized through the signing of two Memoranda of Understanding after a week of exchanges during which a delegation from Tajikistan (village leaders, farmers, university officials, students and practitioners) visited Novkent and Yuksalish. During the visit, the members engaged in a series of activities and brainstorming workshops aimed at identifying common problems and sharing good practices. *All references to Kosovo should be understood to be in the context of the United Nations Security Council resolution 1244 (1999).

records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

_annotations.Source: Information provided by a member of the organization
_annotations.Impact: For Përmet, Rahovec and Lormes, the mutual discovery phase laid the groundwork for potential future cooperation, fostering the development of relationships between local actors, including government representatives and grassroots champions, and facilitating a more comprehensive understanding of developmental needs and challenges. Overall, the twinning model has proven to be an effective tool for mutual discovery, laying the groundwork for a sustainable and cooperative future for the three distinct communities. In Uzbekistan and Tajikistan community members can now actively participate in discussions and exchange information on regional weather patterns, and can provide updates on farming activities, share best agriculture practices, and discuss potential collaboration opportunities and more through a Telegram group. Moreover, DVI twinning has played a key role in the establishment of cooperation between Fergana State University and Tajik Agrarian University, and plans are already in place for a visit of representatives of Tajik Agrarian University to Fergana State University in December 2023 where they will deliver lectures as part of the established cooperation.\nFAO has financially supported the pilot Digital Villages project in Tajikistan as well as the activities of the Tourism Development Centre.

records.title: Digital soil maps in Permet village
records.description: In 2020, FAO conducted an evaluation of land use, water resources, and agroecological conditions in the area surrounding Përmet, aiming to improve accessibility to soil data and to develop the first digital soil maps in Albania. The map preparation operations utilized a combination of GIS technologies, field assessments and sampling, and the digital soil maps were subsequently developed based on the collected information highlighting the specific agro-ecological situations, types of agriculture land, changes in land use, risk of flood, risk of erosion, agricultural land occupied by constructions, land use (agriculture and other uses), total available water, natural drainage, irrigation and drainage channels (network), watersheds, zoning of selected agriculture production (vineyards and fruit trees) and heavy metal deposits in the soil.
records.abstract: Digital Villages initiative (DVI)
records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

_annotations.Source: Information provided by a member of the organization
_annotations.Impact: The creation of digital soil maps for Përmet can strongly support the rural development of the area. The maps offer accurate and accessible insights into soil characteristics, helping farmers make informed decisions, while optimizing their crop planning and resource management. At an administration level, this crucial information supports government structures in implementing sustainable agricultural practices, fostering overall growth and resilience in the local agricultural sector.

records.title: DVI hub
records.description: The DVI hub in the Novkent and Yuksalish pilot Digital Villages in Uzbekistan serves as a centralized platform for the dissemination of agricultural information and resources, providing farmers with timely insights, promoting continuous learning and facilitating peer-to-peer exchanges of knowledge. The hub's overarching goal is to modernize farming practices, boost productivity, enhance community collaboration, and equip farmers with the necessary knowledge and skills to navigate challenges and take advantage of the available opportunities. The hub hosts curated resources related to farming in Uzbekistan, including tutorials, articles and best practices, and offers guidance on land programmes, available subsidies and registration processes.

records.title: Digital literacy training
records.description: In the pilot Digital Villages of Novkent and Yuksalish in Uzbekistan, and Lolazor in Tajikistan, FAO, in collaboration with its partners and local experts, has carried out a capacity-building programme aimed at equipping farmers with the necessary skills for the effective use of their mobile devices. The training provided in the two countries followed similar curricula, with focus on basic digital literacy skills, social media management and digital marketing. The training in Uzbekistan showed the participating farmers how they could navigate Telegram and YouTube to find information, verification and discussions, and informed them about privacy management. The farmers learned to make optimum use of such Telegram features as channels, bots and polls. The segments related to YouTube focused on farming techniques, machinery maintenance and crop care, while the benefits of social media were explained for such activities as product presentation, buyer communication and market expansion through professional profiles. Specific digital platform sessions complemented the agriculture-related training, while entrepreneurship training empowered the farmers with business development tools, market insights and digital marketing strategies. They were also given guidance on how to set up online sales channels through e-commerce integration. In Tajikistan, the initial training centred on digital safety, setting up Google accounts and online banking, as well as various previously underutilized phone functionalities. The training then delved into the various free-access agriculture-related applications and online platforms available to farmers in Tajikistan, including an online calculator for inputs, mobile apps containing sources of information and knowledge about specific crops and livestock, as well as other information and e-commerce resources. The training concluded with a presentation on the fundamental aspects of digital marketing through Instagram and Facebook. The 3-day programme included practical exercises and homework.

records.title: Albania Digital Agenda 2022-2026
records.description: The National Digital Agenda of Albania for 2022–2026 contains the vision for the next phase of the country’s digital transformation. The strategy envisages the provision of “comprehensive and borderless digital services for citizens and businesses” across various sectors, such as those related to health, infrastructure and agriculture – including livestock and fishing – among others. It is built around four main pillars: (1) enabling digital policies, intelligent processes and advanced solutions on secure platforms; (2) digital business: accessible and proactive services, and business-ready operations; (3) digital education and digital skills: transformation of learning and education; and (4) digital citizens: citizens and privacy, transparency of data and citizen services.

_annotations.Impact: Albania's Digital Agenda for 2022–2026 seeks to bring about transformative changes in different sectors, including agriculture. The strategy relies on such cutting-edge technologies as blockchain, artificial intelligence and machine learning, aiming to enhance efficiency in agriculture, streamline information management systems, and improve forest and water monitoring.

records.title: Agrovisio
records.description: Agrovisio is an app that helps agricultural commodity buyers and farmers estimate price trends based on historical data & real-time crop supply dynamics, making use of remote-sensing satellite and, where necessary, drone imagery. The app displays crop area data and monitors crop growth for both growers and buyers, and updates its crop supply insights field by field every 5 days.

records.title: Digital Agriculture Strategy of Armenia
records.description: Developed with the technical assistance of FAO, Armenia's national strategy for digital agriculture for the period 2021–2030 is geared towards ensuring sustainable agricultural development and rural livelihoods through the targeted use of modern digital technologies. This vision is underpinned by strategic priorities including the digital exchange of data and knowledge among stakeholders, the creation of digital market linkages in the agricultural value chain, the provision of digital financial services, the digitalization of agricultural supply chain management, macro agricultural intelligence and data analytics, and the digital empowerment of young people and women in agriculture. A detailed action plan for 2021–2023 complements the strategy, outlining specific activities that include capacity development, education, promotional campaigns, the establishment of technical facilities, and collaboration with various stakeholders. Overall, the comprehensive strategy aims to harness digitalization to enhance agricultural processes, improve market access and empower diverse stakeholders within the agricultural sector.

records.title: Digital Demo Farm in Tajik Agrarian University
records.description: FAO established a digital demo farm on the premises of Tajik Agrarian University under the Digital Village Initiative in Tajikistan. The educational farm, located in the Hisor region, was equipped with digital technologies, including smart insect traps and a smart irrigation system with the participation of two private companies: Smapp Lab (Hungary) and Wes Trade (Italy). Wes Trade installed their Irrigoptimal smart irrigation technology in the apple orchards of the educational farm, facilitating the control of water expenditures and needs based on data provided by in-soil sensors and a weather station. Smapp Lab, on the other hand, contributed several smart insect traps (known as Smapp Lab) for the cotton fields and orchards that allow the tracking of insect swarms through smart sensors installed in each trap.

Students undergo in-field training at the educational farm every year, exposing them to the advantages and intricacies of digital technologies from an early age, thus creating a catalytic effect. The participating companies were able to develop connections with FAO partners in Tajikistan, including the Industry Development Fund (IDF), contributing to the country's digitalization efforts. For instance, Wes Trade will formalize its commitment through the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding with the IDF, paving the way for continued partnership and distribution activities within the country.

records.title: Accueil Paysan
records.description: Accueil Paysan is a well-established network of rural farmers and organizations that support the promotion and improvement of agroecological farming in rural France. The network makes use of an online app that connects communities with farmers offering farm-based products, farm accommodation, activities for children and people with disabilities, and artistic activities.
records.abstract: Portal for the promotion of farm accommodation and activities

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The online platform aims to reduce information asymmetries in the promotion of countryside experiences and rural diversification. Farmers can register their activities on an online platform that shares their ethical principles and missions as regards agroecology, rural community rights, fair living conditions, the solidarity economy, and the deepening of the human and ecological relationship. Small-scale or medium-sized farmers with limited access to the necessary resources to build and maintain their own digital profile can benefit from the Accueil Paysan online portal by promoting their products and services, and linking their work with other allied parties. The ethical code and functioning of the online platform is integrated with the rural social fabric in France, and seeks to counter the dominance of the commercial online travelling agencies in the field of rural tourism through the development of a solidarity economy.

records.title: Locust GIS (CCALM)
records.description: Locust GIS, which operates in the Caucasus and Central Asia (CCA) under the name CCALM, is a comprehensive system that has been developed for data analysis and forecasting in support of locust management. Targeting initially the national level, but with potential for regional application, CCALM has been integrated with a range of functionalities that are particularly adept at producing outputs to aid the analysis of Italian (CIT), Moroccan (DMA) and Asian Migratory (LMI) locusts data and the creation of forecasts. They include maps showing locust densities, treated areas, and areas infested or treated with densities above the Economic Threshold (ET). The full utilization of the Automated System for Data Collection (ASDC), as the primary data source for GIS, along with other sources, is vital for the maximization of the effectiveness of CCALM.
records.abstract: Caucasus and Central Asia Locust Management System
records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

_annotations.Impact: Efforts are currently focused on facilitating the operational use of both the Automated System for Data Collection (ASDC) and the Caucasus and Central Asia Locust Management System (CCALM) in countries in the Caucasus and Central Asia (CCA), for which users are provided with the necessary equipment and technical assistance to ensure the accurate completion of the ASDC forms and the efficient use of the system. The assistance being provided includes Training-of-Trainers programmes and coaching to enhance the use and management of CCALM at a national level. The effective operational use of both ASDC and CCALM is anticipated to significantly enhance the collection, analysis and forecasting of locust data in the CCA region, which is expected to contribute to early warning systems and prompt response mechanisms, aiding in the prevention of locust infestations. According to the website, an important goal related to the “Programme to improve national and regional locust management in Caucasus and Central Asia (CCA)” (under Result 3), subject to the availability of funding, is to see ASDC and CCALM in operational use in all or most CCA countries by 2025.

records.title: Accueil Champêtre en Wallonie
records.description: Accueil Champêtre en Wallonie is an online app displaying the regional offer of on-farm diversification in Wallonia (Belgium). The app contains a catalogue and a filtered search function to aid in the identification of farms offering services related to agriculture, such as food processing, recreational activities, countryside walks, golf, farm visits, team building, room and space rental, farm shops, etc. Farmers can log in to the app and upload images and information on the products or services they offer, while members of the public, tourists and any other interested parties can use the search tool to peruse and select activities within a customisable distance.

records.title: Plantix Crop Doctor
records.description: Plantix is a mobile application and web-based library designed to help farmers and gardeners identify and manage plant diseases, pests and nutrient deficiencies. The app provides customized solutions based on AI and image recognition technologies. Users can connect with a community for the sharing of knowledge and to receive advice. In India, an integrated marketplace aids users in sourcing appropriate chemicals.
records.abstract: Mobile app providing free diagnoses for crop problems and treatment suggestions

_annotations.Source: ["Desktop research","Information provided by a member of the organization"]
_annotations.Impact: Plantix aids in the early detection of plant issues, helping prevent crop damage. The app also provides access to resources for the management of diseases, pests and nutritional deficiencies. In India, it offers organic solutions, that reduce the reliance on chemicals. A survey found that 57 percent of users improved their farming knowledge, 20 percent increased their crop production and 17 percent reported an increase in income.

records.title: scoutlabs
records.description: scoutlabs (prev. SMAPP LAB) is a digital tool that monitors insect activity and environmental conditions, providing farmers and other users with actionable insights and forecasts. The service is based on data from trap installations that is used to generate knowledge on recommended optimal control measures, accessible via a mobile application or online app. The scoutlabs database features more than 180 different insects affecting various crops, including vegetables, fruit, cereals, etc. The SMAPP LAB company collects data from its insect monitoring network that covers all regions in Hungary, and uses the data to predict route and flight season dynamics, allowing farmers to apply precise and efficient control measures.
records.abstract: AI-powered tool for insect monitoring and control services

_annotations.Source: ["Desktop research","Information provided by a member of the organization"]
_annotations.Impact: The scoutlabs insect monitoring system can help in the fight against insect outbreaks and thereby stabilize food security. Using the data gathered from the SMAPP LAB network can provide 50 percent savings in insecticide costs (based on customer feedback), which contributes to reducing the CO2 emissions associated with their manufacture. The scoutlabs traps installed in 18 countries provide an overview of pest pressure in Europe, Central Asia, etc., revealing how pests migrate from region to region, revealing the potential of scoutlabs to become a global monitoring solution. According to a company representative, the scoutlabs solution provides actionable insights for less than 0.5 EUR/hectare, considering the fact that one trap covers around 25–30 ha.

records.title: Agrozamin
records.description: AgroZamin is an e-commerce e-commerce that connects sellers and buyers of agricultural inputs in Uzbekistan. The e-commerce features a wide range of products, including agrochemicals, seeds, plant protection products, machinery equipment, among others. The e-commerce also facilitates the trade of services, such as brokerage operations, while also allowing users to identify potential business partners in the EU Member States, diagnoses of agricultural equipment, etc. Farmers can also sell their produce directly through the e-commerce without paying additional fees.
records.abstract: E-commerce for agricultural inputs and services

_annotations.Impact: AgroZamin can help farmers, especially smallholders, in accessing new markets that were previously out of their reach due to geographical or logistical barriers. The site also provides farmers and buyers with real-time information about the price, availability and quality of products, leading to more efficient and transparent transactions. AgroZamin can reduce the transaction costs associated with traditional agricultural trading, such as those related to transport and storage, resulting in higher profits for farmers and lower prices for buyers.

records.title: METOS
records.description: METOS is a weather monitoring and irrigation control system that helps farmers optimize crop yields and save water. The system is based on a combination of sensors, weather stations and control units connected to a Cloud-based app that provides real-time data and alerts on weather conditions, soil moisture and water requirements. The system helps farmers make informed irrigation decisions, ensuring that crops receive just enough water to optimize growth while minimizing waste and reducing water usage. METOS also offers consultation and support services, providing farmers with expert advice on how to make the most of their technologies.
records.abstract: Hardware and software for environmental monitoring and supporting farming decisions

_annotations.Impact: METOS offers weather monitoring and precision agriculture solutions, with particular focus on production. The advantages offered by METOS include increased efficiency and optimization in farming processes, resulting in improved yields and the more economic use of resources. Farmers can access accurate and up-to-date weather and climate information, as well as data on soil moisture levels and other key metrics that impact crop growth and health, allowing them to make informed decisions about when to plant, when to irrigate and when to harvest their crops. The FieldClimate MOBILE APP can be useful for smallholders, as it provides real-time access to weather and soil data via a smartphone app.

records.title: Seljak.me
records.description: Seljak.me is a app for agricultural producers and consumers that features an e-marketplace for agricultural goods and services, agriculture-related news and good practices in Montenegro, listing also relevant agribusinesses in the country. The app has been developed to close the gap between small producers and consumers in Montenegro, and the knowledge app covers such topics as food safety, market information and prices, food and vegetable production, beekeeping, and more. The site also posts official information and statements from the Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications. The list of agribusinesses on the app includes a short description, relevant links and contact details.
records.abstract: E-marketplace and knowledge-sharing app

_annotations.Source: Information provided by a member of the organization

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: According to a representative of the organization, over 8000 deals were finalized through the app in 2022, which is evidence that the portal helps close the gap between small producers and customers, providing an online marketplace for the purchase and sale of local produce and cattle, removing the need for intermediaries. The organization also promotes fair pay by personally advising farmers of a reasonable price for their products.

records.title: Open Food Hub
records.description: An Open Food Hub is a community of farmers and local producers who have joined forces to sell their produce through a community-owned open-source software app designed specifically for the sale of food. The “Hub” sells items (to the public or other businesses) by more than one supplier, and can be likened to a physical farmers market where customers can access food grown and supplied by different local farmers, as well as baked goods, handicrafts and even produce imported by local wholesalers. Food producers create an online shop on Open Food Hub through which they can receive payments and make sales through other shops on the app. Wholesalers, on the other hand, can integrate with existing systems, manage buying groups and supply produce through national or regional networks of food hubs and shops. Finally, communities can gather producers in the area for the establishment of a virtual farmers’ market.
records.abstract: Food e-marketplace in Cloughjordan Smart Village

_annotations.Impact: The Open Food Hub contributes to the community and local development in Cloughjordan by enabling livelihood diversification and opening up opportunities for the development of new local food enterprises. Opportunities are created for producers and food enterprises to meet and collaborate in training and other events, shortening the long supply chains, increasing local food security and strengthening the resilience of the community.

records.title: Local Food Nodes
records.description: Local Food Nodes acts as a bridge between food producers and local consumers. Producers showcase their offerings, while consumers place orders by making direct payments to the producer. Pickups and deliveries are made at predefined nodes enabling producers to cater simultaneously to multiple consumers and allowing consumers to collect food from various producers in one location. The app is tailored to aid small-scale producers in accessing the market, enhancing their financial sustainability, and encouraging more people to engage in local food production
records.abstract: Connecting consumers with local producers

_annotations.Source: ["FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices","Desktop research"]
_annotations.Impact: Local Food Nodes has reimagined the food value chain, allowing producers and consumers to deal with each other directly. The app eliminates the middleman, and empowers farmers in promoting their products digitally, and facilitates direct customer interactions. This not only strengthens the financial position of small-scale producers, but also provides consumers with diverse food options. The app has currently attracted fewer than 3200 registrations. The average order value is €11, and there are 280 nodes as of July 2023

records.title: Leilão a Bordo
records.description: Leilão a Bordo is an online auction app that supports the digitization of fish sales, linking buyers directly with the adherent boat with the goal of streamlining the initial sale process and unlocking new business opportunities. The digital auction system allows buyers to bid on national boat catches from fish registration at sea to their sale on land. The app promotes fish traceability and brings together stakeholders in the value chain, while smart labelling ensures product quality and provides consumers with comprehensive fish data, aiding them in making informed choices.
records.abstract: Digital auction app connecting buyers with fishermen

_annotations.Impact: Leilão a Bordo offers full fish traceability from source to final destination. It supports consumers in making conscious purchasing decisions and provides fishermen with tools to aid their access to the market, the efficient sale of their catch and a reduction in potential surplus in artisanal fish trading.

records.title: iVeg
records.description: The Almeria SmartAgriHub is a pioneering project that aims to promote innovation, sustainability and competitiveness in the agrifood sector in Spain. Located in the Almeria region, the region of Spain with the highest concentration of greenhouses in the world, the project is an ecosystem of innovation that brings together farmers, technology providers, researchers and other stakeholders for the creation, testing and implementation of innovative solutions. Among the solutions developed to date is iVeg, an application that combines various data sources to optimize the production of greenhouse crops, providing real-time information about the state of the crops, including soil moisture, temperature, humidity and other key parameters. The application aims to optimize also greenhouse management in terms of water, fertilizer and energy use.
records.abstract: Greenhouse tomato supply chain based on IoT technology and decision support system (DSS) in the Almeria SmartAgriHub

_annotations.Impact: The iVeg application allows farmers to adjust their irrigation schedules, fertilization regimes and other aspects of crop management to achieve higher yields and better quality crops, and to reduce their environmental impact. The iVeg application also enhances transparency and quality standards, and provides details of products and processes in every link on the supply chain, thus contributing to the standardization and interoperability of information.

records.title: E-audit
records.description: E-audit employs the Internet of Things to aid auditors in the inspection of wineries and vineyards. The system ensures that the grape and wine production processes are tracked accurately, that documented processes are correct, and that the information reported for certification aligns with the actual conditions. It certifies wines with Designation of Origin and Geographical Indication, and those stating the grape variety and/or age.
records.abstract: Internet of Things applied for the efficient auditing of wine certification

_annotations.Source: FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices
_annotations.Impact: E-audit revolutionizes the wine certification process with through its digital reporting capabilities and DIONISO and SIAN integrations, providing auditors with access to trustworthy and current data related to wine production. Having access to real-time, georeferenced sensor data in vineyards ensures audit accuracy and minimizes human error, leading to enhanced quality control and a more streamlined certification procedure.

records.title: FarmGeoBalance
records.description: FarmGeoBalance is a web-based application that utilizes satellite data, and weather and soil information to provide olive oil producers in the village of Kythera with personalized recommendations for crop management. It is an innovative tool developed as part of the Kythera Smart Village project aimed at promoting sustainable and efficient agriculture on the Greek island of Kythera. FarmGeoBalance has been developed to assist farmers in controlling, adapting and managing their crops easily and quickly, and to facilitate and simplify the product certification process. After identifying olive oil producers interested in testing and demonstrating the system, a total of 12 olive groves were geolocated across the island, and data were monitored with the use of drones and satellite imagery. Aside from certification, a mobile app and Internet geobase contribute to the monitoring of production levels and the results of farming practices, e.g. on the biodiversity of farms.
records.abstract: Web-based application for the management of olive production in Kythera  Smart Village
records.owner_name: MedINA (The Mediterranean Institute for Nature and Anthropos); University of the Aegean

_annotations.Impact: FarmGeoBalance can help olive oil producers improve their yields and reduce costs, while also promoting sustainable agriculture. By providing farmers with targeted recommendations based on accurate data, the application supports precision farming, and thus helps reduce the environmental impacts of agriculture. The technology can also help mitigate the effects of climate change, which is becoming increasingly important for the agriculture sector as extreme weather events become more frequent. The solution can also support the certification of the olive oil produced on the island and the granting of a Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) label, adding value to the olive oil and allowing it to be marketed at a higher price. Overall, FarmGeoBalance has the potential to make a positive contribution to the sustainability of agriculture on Kythera and beyond.

records.title: BestellBar
records.description: BestellBar is a local online marketplace through which local vendors can sell their products online, combining the advantages of online shopping with those of shopping with local retailers. Retailers in the region can list the products that members of the public can order online, and those participating include organic farms, local bakeries, vegetable farmers and regular supermarkets, as well as vendors of non-food goods. Once an order is placed, the system arranges the delivery, and volunteers from the village can help bring them to the door of the client with the support of a specific mobile app (LieferBar).
records.abstract: E-marketplace featuring local retailers from Rhineland-Palatinate digital villages

_annotations.Impact: BestellBar allows for the more efficient marketing of local food producers, creating direct links with their customers, thus supporting short supply chains. Users have the opportunity to buy local, healthy food without having to physically visit the local marketplace.

records.title: Arizor.uz
records.description: Arizor.uz is an information exchange system based on a mobile application, accessible from any connected device (phone, tablet, PC), through which beekeepers can access educational and informational data on beekeeping practices. The available information includes data on the location of bee colonies in Uzbekistan and bee poisoning hazard warnings. Pesticide applications for the treatment of crops are recorded on the app, which then sends out notifications to beekeepers. The application presents data on the colony locations of each beekeeper on a map, thus preventing bee farm overlaps. The system provides early warnings of pesticide applications to prevent honeybee losses, allowing beekeepers to act promptly to ensure the safety of their colonies. The app also provides data on the presence of melliferous flora, both wild and agricultural.
records.abstract: Information exchange system for beekeepers

_annotations.Impact: The app aids beekeepers in decision-making and action-taking, facilitating their timely market response, as beekeeper and bee product records play a vital role in the steady growth of the sector. The app's optimal apiary location feature in Uzbekistan promotes the efficient use of natural resources, while the early pesticide warning notifications help beekeepers prevent honeybee losses and optimize production. Timely field processing warnings minimize bee deaths from chemical poisoning during agricultural plantation treatments.  As of January 2023, the app has recorded over 100 downloads.

_raw.Title: Arizor.uz
_raw.Short description: Information exchange system for beekeepers
_raw.SDGs: ["SDG 2: Zero hunger","SDG 12: Responsible consumption and production"]
_raw.Description: Arizor.uz is an information exchange system based on a mobile application, accessible from any connected device (phone, tablet, PC), through which beekeepers can access educational and informational data on beekeeping practices. The available information includes data on the location of bee colonies in Uzbekistan and bee poisoning hazard warnings. Pesticide applications for the treatment of crops are recorded on the app, which then sends out notifications to beekeepers. The application presents data on the colony locations of each beekeeper on a map, thus preventing bee farm overlaps. The system provides early warnings of pesticide applications to prevent honeybee losses, allowing beekeepers to act promptly to ensure the safety of their colonies. The app also provides data on the presence of melliferous flora, both wild and agricultural.

records.title: AquaPin, AquaMobile and Fixeau
records.description: Salinization in the northern areas of the Netherlands means that agriculture is only possible thanks to the relatively thin freshwater lens in agricultural areas and the supply of freshwater via trenches. Aqua Pin is a device that comprises various sensors that measure the groundwater level, electrical conductivity and soil moisture of a plot. Using Aqua Mobile, farmers can easily measure the salt content in the ditch and drain, and the measurements are then saved on a web app using the Fixeau Mobile App. The app provides details of the current situation and offers predictions with regard to the quality of surface, drainage and groundwater.
records.abstract: Sensors, web-based app, and mobile app for water quality measurement
records.owner_name: Friesland, Groningen and North-Holland provinces in the Netherlands

_annotations.Impact: The solutions presented within the scope of the “Boeren Meten Water” project provide participants with insights into the problem of salinization, as well as reliable measurements that can be used to guide decision-making. Farmers can thus make more informed decisions about when and how much water to apply to their crops, resulting in improved crop yields and reduced water consumption.

records.title: ABA Online
records.description: ABA online is a digital app and mobile app that provides rural extension and advisory services to meet the needs of Albanian farmers and to develop their business and financial skills. The app provides technical knowledge through written and video materials addressing such issues as agricultural production, production technologies, raw materials, chemical and organic fertilizers, and pesticides; provides weather forecasts and market prices in three districts; offers policy-related information about such issues as agricultural certification, subsidy schemes and export standards; and provides regularly updated market price information on several commodities, such as vegetables and fruit, in three markets: Divjaka, Tirana and Lushnjë. ABA online also has a community feature comprising a forum and an area for obtaining expert advice. Farmers can use the forum to create dialogues and establish contacts with other farmers, and with experts and traders operating in agricultural fields. Farmers can also access an online advisory service to reach agricultural experts in the areas of livestock production, greenhouse vegetables, field vegetables, fruit trees, vineyards, olive & citrus cultivation, and beekeeping by contacting the experts via social media or an online form on the website. FED Invest also facilitates farmer engagement in ABA online through its physical ABA centre, where the agricultural experts and staff organise training sessions, including those aimed at developing digital skills.
records.abstract: Agribusiness advisory service

_annotations.Source: ["Desktop research","Information provided by a member of the organization"]

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The website offers market information, technical guidance, knowledge products and advisory services, all free of charge, facilitating the dissemination of information, expertise, education and knowledge of best practices and the promotion of financial literacy among farmers in Albania. The forum features over 240 discussion topics in the field of agriculture. In 2022, the “Ask the Expert” section addressed over 135 questions and answers. The online app also features over 20 tutorials and promotional videos and over 200 articles. Finally, farmers with limited digital skills are provided with face-to-face help by FED Invest staff and village advisors.

records.title: AquacultuER4.0
records.description: The University of Ferrara has developed an innovative system based on a network of sensors for the monitoring of water quality at fish and mussel farming sites. The system provides aquaculture operators with real-time information about the onset of critical situations through a dedicated mobile app. The aquaculture monitoring system records and stores all measured data, and provides fishers with relevant information on aquaculture facilities, allowing them to make informed farming decisions.
records.abstract: Precision farming in aquaculture for water quality monitoring
records.owner_name: Department of chemical, pharmaceutical and agricultural sciences, University of Ferrara

_annotations.Source: FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices
_annotations.Impact: The digitalization of aquaculture through innovative ICTs can increase the competitiveness and quality of the end product and improve the production process. This precision aquaculture system facilitates fishers in reacting to sudden changes in water quality and other emergencies. This precision aquaculture approach, by applying the control principles, can enable end-users to certify environmental conditions to meet the demands of a market that is sensitive to product provenance and sustainable fish and shellfish farming practices. It supports aquaculture businesses in being sustainable and ensures their compliance with industry and government regulations.

records.title: GosAgro.kz
records.description: GosAgro.kz is a web-based application created by the government of Kazakhstan for the management of information and the delivery of public support to farmers. The app operates as a digital hub of the Unified State Information System for the Subsidy of the Agroindustrial Complex (ЕГИСС) through which farmers can apply for, process and receive subsidies and financial assistance, requiring no extra steps from the farmer. An application listed on the "Waiting List" is considered approved and only awaits the issuance of appropriate funding. The applications of farmers are subsidized through the 355 financial institutions registered on the system.

records.title: Fly&See Agro drones
records.description: Drones by Fly&See Agro is a drone technology that aims to protect plants against disease through pest monitoring, soil condition assessments and the identification of problematic areas. Drones are used to monitor plant development dynamics and vegetation indices to support the estimation of fertiliser demands, and to identify disease and pest colony hotspots. The technology can be used to aid the management of medium and large farms in Russia. The Drones are also utilized for the application of growth stimulants, fertilizers and crop protection agents to different crops at any stage of growth. The Drones make use of multispectral and infrared imagery for the assessment of field risks and productivity, supporting the enhancement of yields and product quality. Furthermore, they can also support the creation of digital maps containing soil composition data, which can support optimal crop distribution during sowing, can coordinate plant protection measures with specialists, and can generate yield and agricultural productivity forecasts. Fly&See Agro use drones with entomophages.  The use of entomophagy to protect plants from pests contributes to reducing the pesticide load on plants and organic crops, preserving the earth and slowing down the oxidation and aggradation of the soil, preserving bees and other pollinating insects, and reducing the outlays on agricultural machinery. The company offers full technical support to all users of their Drone technologies, and is in the process of creating digital maps of lands (accessible from the company’s database), analysing soil composition and quality, and recommending how crops should be distributed during sowing, control vegetation in collaboration with specialists from the All-Russian Research Institute of Plant Protection.  The process of introducing drone technology in the field is divided into seven stages. The process begins with extensive research, monitoring crop fields to ascertain processing volume and scheme. Coordination follows, entailing requests for entomophagy introduction, contract agreements, cooperation terms and payment schedules. Then, the appropriate pheromone traps are selected based on the types of crops and pests. This is followed by the mutual definition of the time and standard for the introduction of entomophagy. The entomophages are then cultivated and tested for quality in vitro. Post this, entomophages are introduced via drone aircraft as per the predetermined schedule. Lastly, the efficiency of the entomophage application is assessed, ensuring crop conservation.
records.abstract: Drone technology for pest control and land management

_annotations.Source: ["Desktop research","FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices"]
_annotations.Impact: Fly&See Agro is currently treating over 40 000 ha of agricultural land each year. According to the company website, it can provide 90 percent protection from pests and 50 percent savings for farmers, though it is not specified if the stated savings are financial or relate to the volume of pesticides used. Smallholder farmers can unite to benefit from the entomophagous field treatment service when they and other nearby farms are supported and funded by civil society organizations. The company has stated that it hopes in the future to manufacture its own, inexpensive unmanned aerial vehicles for independent use by farmers.

records.title: e-Fitouz
records.description: e-Fitouz is an electronic system operated by the Agency for Quarantine and Plant Protection in Uzbekistan that has been developed for the online control of the import-export procedures related to plants and agricultural products in the country. The system facilitates the online exchange of such documents as the phytosanitary certificates required for the import-exports of Uzbekistan from/to the 122 countries that are signatories to the International Convention on Plant Quarantine and Protection. e-Fitouz further brings full automation to the obtaining of export certificates, the registry of imported products under the country's quarantine regulations, quarantine checks, the registry of restricted seeds and plants, and the registry of authorized importers, with external applications for phytosanitary certificates.
records.abstract: Electronic information system for phytosanitary controls and compliance
records.owner_name: Agency of Plant Protection and Quarantine of the Republic of Uzbekistan

_annotations.Impact: e-Fitouz has been pivotal in enhancing the pace and simplification of the administrative processes required for the export/import of plants and agricultural commodities between countries. By improving the efficiency and effectiveness of document transfers within the Agency and the associated entities, the system augments the quality and speed of data collection, processing and analysis in a secure data-sharing environment. It also fosters better interactivity among all participants in trade, making use of a unified informational framework, and expedites the creation of analytical reports. Furthermore, e-Fitouz also mitigates the chances of phytosanitary certificate forgery, thereby bolstering the credibility of Uzbekistan's exporters.

records.title: Bakus
records.description: Bakus are autonomous electric robots that can be utilized for pruning, weeding, and the spraying of pesticides and plant protection products in vineyard operations. Bakus robots operate remotely, and so promise greater hygiene and safety for vineyard workers through the removal of the need for direct contact with pesticides. VitiBot has created a universal platform for the management of many smart devices and power tools, produced both by VitiBot and other manufacturers. Bakus can be integrated with tools owned by the operator, both electric and non-electric, that allows them to suppress the use of herbicides by not directly handling chemicals. Bakus’ autonomous operations in the vineyard can be supervised from a simple smartphone, and can operate in conjunction with other devices in the vineyard, such as recuperator panels. Bakus can perform most soil working tasks in the vineyard under the supervision of an operator, thus reducing the use of phytosanitary products.
records.abstract: Electric and autonomous vineyard robots

_annotations.Source: FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The company has performed more than 500 demonstrations with the robot on farms in Europe, including those in the Czechia and Portugal, and plans to expand its operations and services across Europe. La Tribune identified VitiBot from among 10 000 start-ups as one of the companies that will “change the world”.

records.title: Automatic System for Data Collection (ASDC)
records.description: The Automatic System for Data Collection (ASDC) visualized data for locust control based on standardized chrono-, geo- and taxo- referenced locust field data and transmissions to the “Caucasus and Central Asia Locust Management System” (CCALM) operating through the Geographic Information System (GIS). ASDC provides visualized data in two forms to users: a Locust Survey Form and a Spray Monitoring Form, allowing national field observers to quickly report sightings or infestations of locusts in the field. Users can also view data on past or current infestations. Both forms allow the user to specify whether they are reporting or monitoring eggs, hoppers, adults or swarms, the specific species, including the three main pests affecting the region: the Italian Locust (CIT), the Moroccan Locust (DMA) and the Migratory Locust (LMI), and the country, region and type of vegetation. The Spray Monitoring Form also asks for weather conditions, spray applications, how the applications were made and the type of protection used. The app then uses a web server to report locust data to CCALM, which can only be done if the device has been authorized by scanning a QR code provided by CCALM.
records.abstract: Monitoring system for locust control in Central Asia and the Caucuses
records.owner_name: Institute of Space Technology and Technology

_annotations.Impact: ASDC was first implemented in Georgia and Armenia, but its scope has now been expanded to cover all ten of the CCA countries. As of 30 September 2021, more than 5000 reports have been submitted by 133 users from ten CCA countries (compared to the 4285 reports submitted by 100 users in eight countries in 2020). According to the most recent Workshop on Locust Data Analysis, Forecast and Reporting in Caucasus and Central Asia (CCA) in February 2022, 234 reports were uploaded during a locust survey, and 242 reports during control operations in the Baghlan, Balkh, Kunduz, Samangan and Takhar provinces in Afghanistan. In Azerbaijan, ASDC was used to carry out a locust survey of 99 043 ha (64 percent of the entire surveyed area) and during control operations on 17 813 ha (60 percent), resulting in the submission of 1302 Survey Forms and 298 Spray Monitoring Forms to the CCALM database. In the Russian Federation, 764 ASDC reports were submitted in 2021, resulting mostly from survey operations of 228 490 ha in the Saratov, Orenburg and Volgograd oblasts and the Stavropol territory, either from tablets or smartphones. More specifically, 288 ASDC reports were submitted related to 14 590 ha using 12 tablets in 12 districts of the Saratov oblast; 62 reports on 23 760 ha using three tablets in three districts of the Stavropol Territory; 54 reports on 2280 ha in three districts of the Orenburg oblast; and 360 ASDC reports on 187 860 ha using 30 smartphones in 25 districts of the Volgograd oblast. In Georgia, locust experts submitted 488 reports during a locust survey and 1046 during treatments, and stated that using ASDC and CCALM made it “easy to get information on locust surveys, to operatively react to complex situations and to prepare a plan for control operations and to carry out treatments. This provided savings in time.” ASDC is being introduced in Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan. FAO has delivered tablets to all five countries, and training courses were conducted in Uzbekistan and Tajikistan in 2022.

records.title: CROPIO
records.description: CROPIO is a digital app that can be accessed via a desktop or mobile app that makes use of high-resolution satellite images in support of real-time agricultural management, helping farmers predict average yields and improve agricultural productivity. The system identifies such key parameters as nutrient deficiencies, soil compaction, lack of water, crop estimation, insect damage, scorching caused by herbicides and weed pressure, allowing timely interventions.
records.abstract: Precision farming application based on remote sensing

_annotations.Impact: CROPIO can potentially reduce uncertainties in agricultural planning by accurately identifying crop issues. The app aims to bridge the data gap in the agriculture sector by transforming satellite imaging data into actionable insights.

records.title: Crystal.Eye
records.description: Crystal.Eye is an optical imaging technology for the identification and discrimination of features and objects that supports the real-time conducting of produce quality inspections. Crystal.Eye™ automates and upgrades the manual quality control processes to ensure greater consistency, leading to reductions in waste, costs and time. The conveyor belt system moves the fresh produce through the imaging area where a high-resolution camera system captures detailed images, both externally and internally. An AI application then processes the images and identifies target features or objects with reliable accuracy. The scanner facilitates the real-time grading and sorting of produce, content identification, shelf-life prediction, and pesticide and fungicide detection.
records.abstract: AI-based solution for quick, accurate and consistent analysis of produce quality

_annotations.Source: ["Information provided by a member of the organization","Desktop research"]
_annotations.Impact: Crystal.Eye can be considered a useful tool for processors and distributors of fresh produce in automating and increasing the efficiency of their quality control activities. The solution makes use of advanced optical imaging and AI for the real-time assessment of both external and internal product quality. This can enhance the accuracy of grading and sorting operations, while the digital records improve traceability from source to retail. As a by-product of its real-time analysis and digital record-keeping, Crystal.Eye could potentially aid in the reduction of QC-related costs.

records.title: AGRIVI
records.description: The AGRIVI Farm Management app is an integrated set of tools that support the management and monitoring of farmlands. The app features farm management software, such as farm insights, farm enterprise, farm advisory, agriculture supply chain, and makes use of sensors and the Internet of Things in support of weather, soil and fleet management. The app has full localization capabilities being adaptable to different units, currencies, countries and languages. It makes use of algorithms that are connected to local databases of pests and diseases, crop protection products and fertilizers, including details of their active ingredients, providing intelligence and insights. Users can plan, track and analyse all of their farming activities in the field, and can access business advice to support their marketing activities. Users can use the app to track, monitor and plan their farm activities and finances based on soil monitoring, weather predictions, pest predictions, vegetation indices, advanced sales, expense tracking and inventory management. The app also offers up-to-date best practices and tips supporting the production of over 100 crops.
records.abstract: Integrated farm management application

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: According to their website, AGRIVI seeks to change the way food is produced, and to positively impact 1 billion lives by helping farmers achieve sustainable, resource-efficient and profitable production. Since its establishment in 2013, the company has worked in agricultural value chains that include Driscoll’s, Nestle, Kimberly Clark, World Bank, BNP Paribas, Helvetas and the Ministry of Agriculture Croatia. The app can support the optimization of production by encouraging the use of best practices in agriculture, the protection of crops and yields through automated pest and disease detection in every field, and the achievement of better lives through sustainable and profitable agricultural production. In a case study of Telehuz Agriserv (a leading farming enterprise) using AGRIVI in Romania, it was reported that “The real-time insights into crop progress, the powerful farm analytics module and the finances module  were found to be especially useful, enabling Telehuz Agriserv to make better decisions with the support of AGRIVI software that ultimately improves the company’s bottom line”. AGRIVI also helped expedite the company’s agricultural digitalization process.

records.title: Agromart
records.description: Agromart is a multipurpose online app that connects farmers with qualified farm advisors and providers of agricultural services and products. The app publishes the agricultural commodity prices listed at multiple market sites across Uzbekistan, and features also educational materials, video lessons and agricultural news, as well as satellite imagery consulting and analytics. By accessing the “pocket agronomist”, farmers are provided with tailored advice based on satellite monitoring. As of October 2022, the development of a fintech product is underway that will enhance the financial literacy and bankability of farmers.
records.abstract: Knowledge, farm advisory, and e-commerce for agricultural producers

_annotations.Impact: Agromart champions sustainable agriculture, producing valuable content on such subjects as soil management, organic farming and drip irrigation. The app provides access to advisory services and knowledge databases, potentially reducing the risks faced by farmers related to harvest losses or planting timings. The provided knowledge and data help farmers manage their operations and respond to crises or price volatility. Agromart also serves as a marketing tool and connection hub for customers and suppliers in 14 Uzbek regions. Hosting over 1700 ads, the app contributes to a more effective and equitable supply chain.

records.title: Apiary Book
records.description: Apiary Book is a complete digital apiary management solution that increases the productivity of bee colonies and mitigates colony losses through its activities in support of the monitoring of beehives and its data analyses. Apiary Book comprises eight sections, access to which depends on the version of the app and the user’s device. The Apiary Book, the main feature of the app, allows the recording of information on the number, health and maintenance of bee colonies, their activity, the inspections and treatments carried out, and other operations related to beekeeping. Based on the recorded information, the beekeepers get immediate analysis, allowing them to check the history of a beehive, to manage their ongoing apiary activities or to plan for the future. Making use of QR codes, near-field communication tags, a voice assistant feature, and hands-free and offline storage, Apiary Book for Android (this feature is not currently supported by iOS) allows beekeepers to identify beehives, analyse their history and record information about the colony directly on a smartphone, even while working in the apiary. Supplementing this management tool is Apiary Sense, a remote hive monitoring system that provides real-time data on hive status powered by autonomous energy sources. The app's analytical capabilities provide the beekeeper with invaluable insights and trends, enhancing environmental and food safety assessment projects. Apiary Inform, a specialized communication app, disseminates important beekeeping news and alerts to the community, while Apiary Report connects beekeepers with farmers and local authorities for the early identification of problems. The independent Apiary Academy is an e-learning app that has been established to facilitate the global exchange of beekeeping knowledge. Community Support initiatives featture encourage communication, mentoring, and educational opportunities within the beekeeping community . Finally, Apiary Marketplace facilitates the sale of beekeeping products and equipment.
records.abstract: Beekeeping management

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The primary goal of Apiary Book, according to the website, is to help beekeepers around the world make better-informed decisions based on historical data, current conditions and best practices, to minimize bee colony losses and increase productivity. The app is accessible by all beekeepers around the world, and according to the website, is easy to use for beginners or professional beekeepers. As of July 2023, the app has more than 260 000 users worldwide, although it has very high growth potential, as in 2022, only 5 percent of the 60 000+ beekeepers in France were using the app.

records.title: agroNET
records.description: agroNET offers farmers a comprehensive suite of tools tailored to meet their specific needs. agroNET provides pre-packaged configurations for vineyard owners, crop producers, and poultry farmers, among others, designed to optimize their farming operations. Its specific packages optimize irrigation, control crop diseases, leverage satellite imagery for crop analysis, and facilitate livestock production through environmental monitoring, computer vision weight estimation, and AI-based wellness analysis, promoting transparency in the food supply chain. AgroNET includes such components as the Agriculture Information Model (AIM) for semantic interoperability, the DEMETER Enabler Hub (DEH) for centralized resource cataloguing, and the Stakeholders Open Collaboration Space (SOCS) for cooperative work among stakeholders. The app also provides tailored packages to meet specific needs, including vineyard farming, silo management, arable crop management, greenhouse management, asset monitoring, feed storage management, poultry farm management, feed mixture optimization, and mobile solar generation for cleaner energy in agriculture. agroNET can be used with other DunavNET tools, such as its Product Passport, agroNET, and fleetNET which potentially can improve transparency in the supply chain.
records.abstract: Suite of tools for sustainable farming operations

_annotations.Source: FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices
_annotations.Impact: agroNET has the potential to improve farm management, disease prediction and overall productivity, and can improve overall supply chain transparency when used in combination with other DunavNET tools. In a forecast modelling study of Botrytis cinerea (a fungus that attacks wine grapes) published in the Journal of Networking and Network Applications (2022), agroNET was able to reduce the use of pesticides in grape production by up to 20 percent (DOI:10.33969/J-NaNA.2022.020305)

records.title: Nedap Cow Control
records.description: Nedap CowControl is a cow management and monitoring suite that allows cow health and reproduction to be tracked by turning data garnered from SmartTag collars into real-time and relevant alerts, to-do lists, reports and barn maps, aiding farmers in the management and control of their herd on a computer or via a mobile device. Nedap’s SmartTags, which are worn around the neck or leg of the cow, identify each cow electronically and monitor activity, health, reproduction and location data 24 hours a day. For the monitoring of health, the SmartTags measure the eating, rumination, standing, lying, walking and inactive behaviours of each cow 24/7, and any deviations from normal behaviours are reported to the farmer on a list of animals to be checked. Health issues can thus be detected 2–3 days earlier than they would if left until visual symptoms emerged, allowing preventative actions or treatments to be started before they become severe. This ensures improved cow health, herd longevity, animal welfare and a significant reduction in antibiotic use.
records.abstract: Cow management and monitoring suite

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The Nedap CowControl solution can potentially improve the overall health and well-being of cows. By monitoring group behaviour, it can provide insights based on which, for example, feed efficiency and cow comfort can be increased. According to the website, Nedap CowControl, ensures cows become pregnant in a sustainable way. The SmartTags automatically detect cows who are in heat and their optimal insemination moment, allowing cows to be inseminated based on their natural heat/cycle, reducing the need for hormone programmes. This can increase animal welfare and drastically reduce hormone use, while vastly improving reproductive results. As stated by one farmer in the United States, “Overall, the pregnancy rate has increased from 25 percent to 33 percent, and heifers are calving earlier.” This can lead to a reduction in labour shortages and ensures a better work-life balance. A further important benefit to cows is the reduced stress associated with shorter lock-up times. According to a Nedap analysis, the system has been shown to increase milk production, feed efficiency, and animal health and welfare, while reducing antibiotics and hormone use. According to multiple, reviews on the Nedap site, the most important benefit to farmers is related to increased efficiency and sustainability.

records.title: AgriAnalytica
records.description: AgriAnalytica is an online app that matches supply and demand in agricultural finance, trade, knowledge and grants. It features a large database and an online community of farmers, financial institutions, agri-food input suppliers, processors, traders/buyers and farming advisors. The app serves as an integrated solution for the Ukrainian agricultural market, providing access to financing, farm management, accounting and credit analysis services. The app provides news and assistance in accessing loans, grants and information on government supports, commodity leasing and purchases, and agricultural insurance, accessible through five different modules. The Agri: Business Plan module provides tools to attract financial resources. The Agri: Accounting module supports the management of accounting entries and the production of automatically generated reports, including tax-declaration forms and financial statements. The Agri: Farm Management module enables farmers to organize their production processes effectively, control resource usage and make informed management decisions based on necessary analytics. The Agri: Сredit Analysis module supports the generation of an efficient and profitable agribusiness loan portfolio, significantly reducing transaction costs and risks through the contributions of the company’s financial advisors. Through the Agri: Financing module, farmers can explore the various available state support programmes and financial products provided by different institutions, as well as input suppliers and buyers, and submit online applications after identifying the best options for them. The Agri: Trading module allows buyers to search for goods filtered by crop, location, etc., and to access the seller's contact details, or negotiate directly through the app. Through Agri: Shopping, users can filter goods by type of input such as fertilizer, seed, etc. make transactions online and leave reviews. Finally, Agri: Consultant is a digital agriculture extension service through which farmers can obtain expert advice on all the above-mentioned topics and functionalities. The app also features a Climate Atlas, which was created in partnership with BMZ and presents detailed temperatures and precipitation predictions for the periods up to 2050 and 2080 in Ukraine, based on two standardized climate change scenarios (RCP 4.5 and RCP 8.5). It correlates these scenarios with data about key agricultural products in Ukraine, and thus helps users understand how climatic conditions affecting agricultural production may change in the future in their specific location. At the bottom of the page is a link providing access to experienced regional advisors through AgriAnalytica, contributing to risk assessments and adaptation planning, and identifying the suppliers of the necessary solutions through the Agri: Shopping module. If needed, help is also provided for the identification of financing for projects through the Agri: Financing module.
records.abstract: Integrated e-commerce for agri-food finance, inputs, knowledge, and supply

_annotations.Source: ["Desktop research","FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices"]

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: According to their website, AgriAnalytica can facilitate the access of farmers to finance, markets and knowledge by addressing the information asymmetries and financial gaps between the farming community and other value chain actors, namely financial institutions, input suppliers, agricultural produce purchasers, investors, donors, insurance companies and other businesses. There are currently more than 11 300 farmers registered on the AgriAnalytica app, accounting for more than 2100 million hectares of land. More than 29 banks, eight credit unions, and more than 60 suppliers and 60 buyers (traders and processors) have set up Partner Cabinets on the app. According to a blog post from 30 July 2023, AgriAnalytica plans to expand cross-border and cross-sector to include new geographies and new markets. The initiative has been made possible partly due to the support provided by the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) through the Agriculture Growing Rural Opportunities Activity (AGRO) implemented by Chemonics International.

records.title: Sustainable underwater farming with an aquaponics climate control system
records.description: The USDA-certified Aquaponics system is a virtuous cycle system for the simultaneous raising of fish and plants. Based on bio-engineering technologies, it uses no chemical fertilizers, as is the case with conventional hydroponic cultures, thus reducing operating costs, increasing production by 15 percent and reducing the risk of disease, with a relatively nutrient-rich approach. This system is being introduced for the first time in Central Asia, specifically in Southern Kazakhstan, with a 0.5 ha aquaponic greenhouse. The farmer uses an aquaponic mechanism that allows plants to derive the essential nutrients from fish waste products, promoting organic growth without resorting to such chemical inputs as herbicides and pesticides. As the plants absorb the nutrients, they simultaneously purify the water, creating a balanced environment for the fish. In the Korday district facility, six varieties of greens, including arugula and iceberg lettuce, as well as such aromatic plants as basil, are cultivated, and two types of fish, clarius and tilapia, are bred. A climate control system is also being developed for the optimization of light, humidity and temperature conditions, ensuring both the plants and fish can thrive. The system will also facilitate the monitoring of pH levels with a view to maintaining a comfortable environment for both. The farmer applied to Manna Cea for the creation of the aquaponic system, which is a company that uses AI and sensors to monitor and grow salad greens.

_raw.Title: Sustainable underwater farming with an aquaponics climate control system
_raw.SDGs: ["SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth","SDG 9: Industry, innovation, and infrastructure","SDG 12: Responsible consumption and production"]
_raw.Description: The USDA-certified Aquaponics system is a virtuous cycle system for the simultaneous raising of fish and plants. Based on bio-engineering technologies, it uses no chemical fertilizers, as is the case with conventional hydroponic cultures, thus reducing operating costs, increasing production by 15 percent and reducing the risk of disease, with a relatively nutrient-rich approach. This system is being introduced for the first time in Central Asia, specifically in Southern Kazakhstan, with a 0.5 ha aquaponic greenhouse. The farmer uses an aquaponic mechanism that allows plants to derive the essential nutrients from fish waste products, promoting organic growth without resorting to such chemical inputs as herbicides and pesticides. As the plants absorb the nutrients, they simultaneously purify the water, creating a balanced environment for the fish. In the Korday district facility, six varieties of greens, including arugula and iceberg lettuce, as well as such aromatic plants as basil, are cultivated, and two types of fish, clarius and tilapia, are bred. A climate control system is also being developed for the optimization of light, humidity and temperature conditions, ensuring both the plants and fish can thrive. The system will also facilitate the monitoring of pH levels with a view to maintaining a comfortable environment for both. The farmer applied to Manna Cea for the creation of the aquaponic system, which is a company that uses AI and sensors to monitor and grow salad greens.

records.title: Unified register of information systems for Uzbekistan’s electronic government
records.description: The Unified Register of Information Systems and Resources is a centralized online app for the documenting and management of the information systems and resources implemented and utilized by government bodies and entities in which the state holds a 50 percent or more share. Mandated by the Cabinet of Ministers of the Republic of Uzbekistan with Resolution No. 444 dated 16.07.2020, this system is accessible via a web interface, and serves as a cohesive information space for the efficient coordination of the Project Management Centre (PMC) and project executors. The Register hosts the information systems and resources of ministries, state committees, agencies, departments, local government bodies and business entities with significant state shares. It facilitates the systematic tracking of the information systems, databases and software technologies used by state organizations, providing a level of centralization that aids in the monitoring, development and implementation of projects while preventing the duplication of existing information systems. The key functions hosted by the Unified Register include: 1) The registration and accounting of information systems, databases and software products. 2) Conducting and monitoring application statuses for e-government project documentation.  3) Verification of authenticity in issued notifications and expert conclusions. 4) Supporting the direct interaction and communication of project stakeholders. 5) Facilitating transparent evaluations and post-monitoring of implemented e-government projects.
