records.title: Agricolus
records.description: Agricolus is an integrated system that allows farmers to monitor crops remotely using field mapping, vegetation indices and satellite data, and supports decision-making by providing forecasting models with a view to improving crop production and farm management. For agriculture field mapping, the platform relies on GIS inputs provided by Esri, a close partner of Agricolus, and the resulting field mapping services allow farmers to geolocate their fields and register all their related information. Vegetation indices are elaborated internally by the Agricolus team using satellite imagery, allowing farmers to assess the development and health of their crops remotely, and to efficiently plan their field interventions. Forecast models are used to anticipate phenological cycles, irrigation needs, and pest and disease outbreaks, allowing farmers to take the necessary measures, and to reduce their use of water, fertilizer and plant protection inputs. Smart scouting using the Agricolus Farmer mobile app allows farmers to geolocate their crop operations directly from the fields. Prescription maps created based on vegetation indices allow farmers to limit their use of fertilizers to only the necessary amounts. Agricolus combines these digital tools and data with a complete Decision Support System (DSS). The company also offers disease detection and field monitoring modules for different crops including olives, grapes, tobacco, maize, grain and tomatoes, and provides training in the use of AgriTech tools via the “Agricolus Professional Academy” and “Agricolus Educational Academy”.
records.abstract: Precision plant management system

_annotations.Source: ["Desktop research","FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices"]
_annotations.Impact: Agricolus strives to support farmers in increasing productivity and profitability, while reducing the impact on the environment, especially desertification and loss of biodiversity, and restoring the balance of the ecosystem. Agricolus can monitor adverse climatic events and pest and disease outbreaks thanks to its continuous and systematic monitoring of agro-environmental variables. The system has more than 4000 users in 56 countries and 33 partners on four continents. As of 28 July 2023, the mobile app Agricolus Farmer has been downloaded more than 1000 times from the Google App Store, where it has a 4.7/5 rating.

records.title: Skysens APM
records.description: The Skysens Agile Predictive Monitoring app (APM) is an industrial digitalisation app that makes use of edge deployable analytics, IoT capabilities and optional long-range wireless network technologies to improve industrial efficiency at all user levels, with applications in plant protection and agri-food supply chains. APM is based on software and hardware providing wireless communication for the connection of machines to the Internet. Skysens uses LPWA technologies to overcome the connectivity issues related to GSM-based or low-distance solutions. The monitoring app has a drag-and-drop interface, and users can design their own dashboards and view analytical data on any screen, even in night mode. APM offers smart reporting features, and can be used to send automatic and on-demand reports based on different data parameters. Users receive real-time notifications via SMS, email or voice calls. No coding is needed to set up analytics, making it accessible to all. Rules can be created, teams can be managed and data can be shared through customizations to the dashboard, while asset management tools allow users to monitor both physical and virtual assets, with a visualization option available for certain assets. The app also supports the creation of digital twins for efficient system monitoring.
records.abstract: Predictive monitoring with IoT and AI connections for industrial data

_annotations.Impact: In 2017, Skysens became the official IoT network infrastructure provider for Istanbul Airport. The company benefited from a seed investment in November 2017 by ACT Venture Capital, and now exports to 32+ countries. In 2021, Re Pie Asset Management invested in Skysens with USD 5 million company valuation.

records.title: Intrigue á la ferme
records.description: Intrigue á la Ferme is an outdoor recreational activity developed in Wallonia (Belgium). Participants in this location-based game make use of a connection to the Global Positioning System via a mobile device as well as other navigational techniques in a game of hide and seek. Participants hunt down caches, known as geocaches, at specific locations marked by coordinates around selected farms and rural villages. The digital game has been developed to support rural and urban communities in discovering local legends, cultures and histories in Wallonia while engaging in a fun activity. The online game guides the participants on a walking journey during which they must solve puzzles, identify objects and perform tasks requiring them to share their knowledge, collaborative skills and creativity. To date, eight different journeys have been created, set around five operational farms and three rural villages.
records.abstract: Geocaching recreational game supporting the discovery of Belgian farms and rural villages

_annotations.Impact: Intrigue á la Ferme is expected to revitalise rural areas through the promotion of interactive services and the promotion of rural-based attractions that integrate tourism, agriculture, culture and local foods. There have as yet been no studies carried out to collect evidence or testimonials of the ex-post impacts of this recreational activity. The fact that the app has been downloaded by more than 1000 times from Google Play Store, and updated at least four times, suggests that the pilot project is gaining traction.

records.title: Fuori di Zucca
records.description: Established in 2017, Fuori di Zucca (Eng. - Out of Pumpkin) is an organization that coordinates a Solidarity Purchasing Group (GAS in Italian) in the centre of the city of Perugia, Italy, without financial gain. GAS is run by volunteer consumers, and so 100 percent of the purchasing price from sales goes to the producer. The farmers are small-scale and are located close to Perugia, and follow ethical and sustainable farming methods. An organic label is not a prerequisite for Fuori di Zucca, as these farmers already produce organically, and consumers are actively involved along the chain. Every Friday, a WhatsApp message containing a Google Form is sent out by Fuori di Zucca to all GAS members, and users have until the following Monday to select the products they want on a Google Form, after which they receive a confirmation email. On Wednesday evening, the consumers meet the farmers to collect their orders, paying in cash or through electronic payments.
records.abstract: Selling food produced by local producers directly to consumers

_annotations.Source: Information provided by a member of the organization

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The combination of instant messaging (WhatsApp group) and Google Modules has helped overcome the challenge of using only emails for the collection of food orders in Fuori di Zucca, according to an article published on ARC2020.eu (accessed from www.arc2020.eu/italy-digitalisation-short-food-chain-and-sovereignty-fuori-di-zucca/). The same website states that since these two tools were introduced, Fuori di Zucca oversaw EUR 31 799.83 in total consumer expenditures in 2020, almost doubling the amount in 2018, when the system made use only of email, although much of this increase can be attributed to the specific circumstances of the COVID-19 pandemic. The number of purchases and the total expenditures are not the only parameters through which the impact of Fuori di Zucca. Social should be assessed, as there are also cultural and moral aspects that can be considered, such as the increased awareness of consumers related to food seasonality, education in traditional food recipes, and transparency in the origin of food products. With the support of digital tools, Fuori di Zucca can play an important educational and governance role in sustainable food consumption and production.

records.title: Farmers’ Telegram group in Kyrgyzstan
records.description: A Telegram group called Farmers (Фермерлер) has been established among smallholder livestock holders and crop producers in Kyrgyzstan, allowing them to connect and sell their products online. The group is an online peer-to-peer community that helps the members overcome the challenges of their remote locations and the country’s mountainous terrain. The app creator has also established a YouTube channel, Facebook and Instagram profiles for the sharing of agricultural knowledge. The group provides smallholders with cost-effective marketing opportunities and the chance to exchange information and advice.
records.abstract: Online farming community connecting farmers, advisors and food consumers

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: In Kyrgyzstan, the rural population in remote and mountainous regions in particular have turned to instant messaging groups like “Farmers” as valuable alternatives to traditional physical marketplaces. Although bazaars continue to be an integral part of the Central Asian culture, the COVID-19 pandemic has led to a decline in their influence, elevating the importance of digital platforms for the trade of goods. One member of the “Farmers” group in particular offered an explanation of the shift, claiming that he has relied on online marketplaces for the purchase of seeds and fertilizers for about a decade, and says that such platforms offer significant advantages to farmers who find it difficult to travel during the agricultural season. Given the time and cost associated with travel, especially to/from hard-to-reach areas, online marketplaces can be considered more efficient for purchases of vital inputs, providing savings in both resources and time during crucial agricultural periods.

records.title: Automated herd management system
records.description: Mambet, a farmer in Northern Kazakhstan implemented a cow herd management system on his farm of 1300 cattle farm, employing robots for automatic milking and adopting Dairyplan C21 Herd Management Software. The management software can cater to farms of all sizes and to specific requirements due to its modular framework with features for overseeing milking, reproduction, feeding and animal health. The key features enhancing its efficacy include a custom milk yield calculation system, precise individual animal identification and automated features like feeding and animal sorting through AutoSelect, FeedSelect and automatic oestrus detection. The farmer can add other programs to the system in future, such as sensors for tracking the weight of feed, as well as sensors for tracking cows.
records.abstract: Erkebulan's transformed dairy farm

_annotations.Impact: The software has facilitated the automation of the milking control process, the distribution of feed, the process of recognizing and sorting animals, as well as the process of recognizing the onset of heat in cows. Automation has allowed the farmer to assess the reproduction rate of his livestock, the amount of feed consumed and the health of the animals while managing his business. All of this helped Mambetov in the effective planning of his farming activities. The farm reached its production target of 12 tonnes of milk per day two years after launching the system. The ability to access accurate indicators for the herd, for each group of animals and for each individual cow allows farm workers to continuously monitor the health of the animals. The farm, which operates with 1300 head of cattle, employs only two reproduction technology workers, and the farmer claims that three more would be required in the absence of the herd management programme. Digitalization has further removed the need to carry out the routine collection of data on animal productivity, as the software records the volume of milk produced by each cow on a daily basis. According to the farmer, the use of digital technologies has made it possible to attract young specialists to the farm, who are in short supply in rural areas. Since launching the system, five young professionals have been employed.

records.title: Elloha
records.description: Elloha is a complete online app supporting the management of multiple booking channel, with no commission fees. The app further supports the creation of multilingual websites and marketplaces, and booking engines for farm campsites, recreational activities, direct sales, agritourism, and more on-farm diversification. Users can register and benefit from the Elloha online app that acts as a software, offering many functionalities. For instance, Elloha can be used to create and manage bookings, to automatically create and animate websites, to post offers on such leading online travel agencies as Booking.com, Airbnb and Expedia, and to create and sell gift cards. The site also facilitates online payments and manages multiple administrative documents, such as customer files, notices, invoices and e-mailing campaigns, all from a single portal. Elloha also offers a blog and campus where users can access relevant information, webinars, video tutorials, trainings, news and the latest trends, all accessible for free.
records.abstract: All-in-one online service solution for agritourism farms

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: In testimonial posted on the company website, the user stated that Elloha had reduced their commercial dependence on large online travel agencies, with over 62 percent of bookings now being made through their website. Elloha offers easier referencing and searchability, and promises a higher volume of direct bookings for users, including agritourism farms and rural collectives. Another user comment on the company website said: “With Elloha, I was able to design our guest house website myself, even though I have no expertise in this area. As for its daily update, it’s real child's play!”

records.title: Applied robotic herd management system in a dairy farm in South Kazakhstan
records.description: A dairy farm in South Kazakhstan has adopted a robotic cow management and breeding system that automizes the milking and recording of health metrics  for the entire herd. Up until 2013, all tasks on the farm, including feeding and milking, were carried out manually, resulting in an overconsumption of feed and reduced milk yields. By 2015, the farm had introduced Holstein-Friesian breed cows from Canada, prompting a need for advanced herd management. This led the management to invest in Swiss robotic milking machines equipped with various features, including manure removal scrapers and cow back rubbers, and the adoption of the DeLaval DelPro™ FarmManager dairy management system. The system automates milking tasks using machines operated by a single person, and relying on the cow's own schedule for milking. Each cow wears a smart collar for the collection of such data as location, milk production and health metrics, while automated machines help calculate feed ratios and manage manure removal. This holistic system, applied to a herd of 1520 cows, can be remotely accessed for real-time monitoring.

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The application of the robotic herd management approach has led to savings in time and labour, while optimizing such processes as automated milking, artificial insemination, veterinary care, feeding and manure removal, and increasing milk yields. _raw.Description: A dairy farm in South Kazakhstan has adopted a robotic cow management and breeding system that automizes the milking and recording of health metrics  for the entire herd. Up until 2013, all tasks on the farm, including feeding and milking, were carried out manually, resulting in an overconsumption of feed and reduced milk yields. By 2015, the farm had introduced Holstein-Friesian breed cows from Canada, prompting a need for advanced herd management. This led the management to invest in Swiss robotic milking machines equipped with various features, including manure removal scrapers and cow back rubbers, and the adoption of the DeLaval DelPro™ FarmManager dairy management system. The system automates milking tasks using machines operated by a single person, and relying on the cow's own schedule for milking. Each cow wears a smart collar for the collection of such data as location, milk production and health metrics, while automated machines help calculate feed ratios and manage manure removal. This holistic system, applied to a herd of 1520 cows, can be remotely accessed for real-time monitoring.

records.title: Digital technologies for apple production
records.description: Tiriphoni Gardens is a well-known agricultural company in the Shida Kartli region of Georgia that is famous for its apple production. The company uses a wide range of digital technologies and tools for its production, sorting and storage activities. It occupies 31 ha of land, of which 28 ha is occupied by an apple orchard that makes use of precision agriculture equipment, including an automated irrigation and fertigation system, a meteorological station, and sensors measuring temperature, humidity, precipitation, and pests and disease. Tiriphoni Gardens harvests around 1000 tonnes of apples annually, which are sorted and graded by size, colour and weight through the use of an apple sorting line and ISO-certified cold storage facility.
records.abstract: Tiriphoni apple farm

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Tiriphoni Gardens launched its operations in 2014, and it is today one of the largest apple producers in Georgia, leading in 2017 to it being granted European Union (EU) quality certification. As a net importer of apples, Georgia imports significantly more apples than it exports. Consequently, Tiriphoni Gardens’ produce is primarily sold within the Georgian market, contributing to national sovereignty. The company is the first in Georgia to obtain GLOBAL G.A.P. certification for apple production. One of the challenges faced by Tiriphoni Gardens is the lack of specialized laboratories in Georgia for quality control testing, meaning that it must send products to laboratories abroad and pay the associated high costs for such services. The integration of a weather station and sensors contributes to efficient resource utilization and timely interventions, as well as the efficient use of water, fertilizers and pesticides when needed. The operation’s environmental footprint is thus reduced as Tiriphoni Gardens does not overconsume resources, using only what is needed in terms of fertilizers, pesticides, and water for production. Furthermore, the employees are less exposed to chemicals, and the potential adverse effects on their health are reduced. The automated grading and sorting line helps to achieve efficiencies and reduce labour costs through automation, while also increasing marketability by ensuring consistent quality standards, meaning higher prices and better profitability for the producer. It can also reduce food losses by separating apples that are not marketable for sale, but that can be consumed in other ways.

records.title: Applied soil moisture sensors
records.description: A farmer has developed an advanced irrigation management system on a large-scale farm in the Qaraganda region of Kazakhstan that utilizes moisture sensors and weather stations, providing real-time, accurate soil moisture readings at various depths that are transmitted automatically to the computers of the farmer and an agronomist. The farmer utilizes the system for potato cultivation. By monitoring the moisture content of the soil, the farmer can determine the precise irrigation needs of their crops, preventing over or underwatering. The system has been instrumental in improving crop yields, most notably potatoes and alfalfa, ensuring they receive the exact amount of water needed. The farmer used data from Metos weather stations and tested different soil sensors until he identified what worked best for his potato farm.
records.abstract: Sustainable wet crop cultivation in the Qaraghandy region of Kazakhstan

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: This good practice addresses the challenges posed by Kazakhstan's harsh continental climate, enabling the adoption of sustainable agriculture practices, providing savings in such valuable resources as water and electricity, and enhancing the overall farm productivity. The implementation of this practice has helped the farmer improve the quality and yield of the potatoes produced on his farm. In 2021, the farmer achieved yields of 43–45 tons per ha, reportedly much higher than a few years earlier, before he started making use of moisture sensors for the management of irrigation.  His later use of moisture sensors to control the irrigation of alfalfa improved the quality and volume of the crop by 20–30 percent. The adoption of moisture sensors has also improved the efficiency of water and electricity usage on the farm. The irrigation project has created additional jobs for women, as the farm needed to take on additional workers in its potato storage facility. While only 5 percent of the workforce were women before the project started, women now make up 30 percent of the team.

records.title: Agrobiznes
records.description: Agrobiznes is a website that serves as a central hub for the dissemination of a range of information and farming advice, as well as communication services. It is organized into multiple sections, including an area devoted to news and current affairs, a digital library, a weather forecast service, community building and digital transformation initiatives, and agro-educational resources. Agrobiznes also provides access to free specialized commercial services, making it a vital source of information for farmers, organizations and others with interests in the agricultural sector. Agrobiznes delivers daily agricultural news, articles and practical insights. The app addresses also the particular issues encountered by women farmers, with the majority of the editorial team being women. "AgroPodcast2", sponsored by FAO, focuses on specialized agricultural topics and can be accessed through Soundcloud. Bi-weekly newsletters are distributed via email or WhatsApp. The “Agrobiznes digital library” contains over 100 agricultural guidebooks, some in Russian, and has been established in collaboration with USAID and Tekwill. “AgMeteo”, developed with iMetos and Moldova Agroindbank, offers real-time weather data from 100+ stations, aiding in pest and disease prevention. The community initiatives include the Agrobiznes Viber communities and the annual AgTech conference, promoting tech in agriculture. In terms of education, Agrobiznes links to accredited agricultural institutions in Moldova and has hosted the AgTech Academy for young graduates. The app serves also as a job portal, and a Telegram job channel and can be accessed to identify internship opportunities. Finally, the “AgroMag digital marketplace” is a B2B app featuring 50+ companies and 1,500 products, along with a detailed agricultural business directory.
records.abstract: Agricultural news, articles, jobs and more

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: According to Agrobiznes, the website is visited annually by around 2 million unique visitors. The social network community has around 100,000 followers (through Facebook, Viber, Telegram, WhatsApp, YouTube, Instagram and the Newsletter). It is the largest agricultural knowledge and information app in Moldova, and its success has been recognized by local and international organizations, which have created or joined initiatives in collaboration with Agrobiznes users. In 2021, the Romanian Agrobiznes website was launched (agrobiznes.ro), followed in 2022 by the Italian website (agrobiznes.it). These two developments serve as evidence of the replicability of this information technology, and show that the approach implemented in Moldova can be adopted in other countries, despite differences in socio-economic contexts.

records.title: Organic Way (Органски свет)
records.description: The Consumers Organization of Macedonia (COM) has created the Organic Way web app Organic World as part of the Organic World initiative. The platform aim to promote organic food and increase consumer awareness of the associated benefits. The platform also features a map that can be used to plan tours of producers of organic food in Macedonia, detailing shops, restaurants and accommodation providers offering organic products. The platform can be used to search for outlets for the purchase or consumption of organic food, to plan visits to the producers of organic food in Northern Macedonia, and to learn about organic food and its benefits for the environment and health.
records.abstract: Web app for consumers of organic foods

_annotations.Impact: According to the Consumers Organization of Macedonia, the platform has been developed with the collaboration of food producers and organic food outlets from all over the country. More than 1000 people have downloaded the app from Google Play Store to date. The project employs a networking and advertising component as a modern tool for public outreach, which has aided in the dissemination of the core messages more widely and to larger audiences via the Internet. Such a public outreach created a more favourable climate for policy advocacy efforts related to government authorities, farmers’ organizations and supermarket chains. By raising public awareness and attracting significant consumer support for the cause through online promotions and media appearances, the project has provided considerable support to the efforts to promote the adoption of a policy framework on organic production as a sustainable form of agriculture. The project partners and relevant stakeholders have encouraged supermarket chains to collaborate with farmers involved in the project activities and to commit to expanding the organic sections of their shops.

records.title: Foodback
records.description: Foodback is a website and online community that supports innovation in the agriculture and food sectors, building bridges between various actors in the food and agriculture ecosystem, supporting impact-oriented start-ups through acceleration and incubation programmes, and providing investment, financing and internship opportunities in Türkiye and the European Union. It facilitates the Food’s local operations of Europe’s leading innovation initiative – the European Institute of Innovation and Technology (EIT), providing women-led agri-food start-ups with educational tools, mentoring, community building, access to EIT Food resources and pre-seed financing (USD 5000–10000).
records.abstract: Community that supports food and agricultural co-innovation

_annotations.Impact: The community has hosted a variety of awareness-raising events, trainings and demo days. One such event was Champ Sharing, hosted by EIT, which featured awareness-raising events, mentorship & matchmaking programs for entrepreneurs, bootcamps and demo days. The main topics of the awareness-raising events held to date have been food waste, food innovation, agriculture and food sustainability, where experts and ventures explained their sustainable food chain experiences. The bootcamps feature workshops/training sessions during which creative idea-generation exercises are hosted to encourage the creation of food entrepreneurs, and where the participants benefitted from the feedback in their groups. Seed funding amounting to EUR 30 000 (USD 32 778) was awarded to two of the participating ventures based on the outcome of a Jury.

records.title: RAMAS
records.description: RAMAS by AgFutura is a digital extension service that makes use of the Internet of Things (IoTs) as well as external data sources, supporting decision-making in farming and facilitating real-time monitoring and the provision of advisory services via the app and a mobile app. The experts and specialised software of RAMAS analyse the data received from IoT sensors installed on farms and generate evidence-based reports and recommendations for farmers. The testing phase of RAMAS started in 2019, and the initial market launch is expected in 2023.

The system may also contribute to the responsible use of natural resources by controlling the application of inputs, such as water and chemicals, according to the plants’ needs.

records.title: xFarm
records.description: xFarm is an integrated system created around mobile and web apps that supports farmers in the management of their field operations, soils, machinery, irrigation, crop protection, livestock, documentation, economic accounting and logistics. The system, which was devised by Matteo Vanotti, a farmer himself, seeks to simplify the collection and analysis of data, thereby reducing paperwork, enhancing efficiency and supporting data-driven decisions. Built on a robust foundation that combines free Cloud-based farm management software, IoT field sensors known as xSense, and premium services, xFarm offers a multi-layered approach to modern agriculture. The application's management software simplifies administrative tasks with its intuitive interface, while its IoT sensors capture crucial field data in real-time supporting such functions as disease anticipation, water optimization and pesticide reduction. Adding a layer of security and transparency, xFarm makes use of blockchain technologies to trace all field operations, and leverages Cloud computing to provide users with flexible access to their data from any location. Furthermore, the application utilizes remote sensing to deliver vital field data directly to farmers' smartphones, including vegetation indices and prescription maps for variable-rate fertilization. Accessible in six languages and available in a free version, xFarm is a versatile tool that is suitable for farms of all sizes, needs and financial capacities.
records.abstract: Farming data management platform

_annotations.Source: ["Desktop research","FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices"]

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: By 2020, xFarm’s user base had grown from 4000 to 30 000, and today, more than 32 000 farmers use xFarm to digitalize their farm operations. The company has 50 000 followers on Facebook, and more than 3000 followers on Instagram and LinkedIn. The company website claims that the xFarm has contributed to the avoidance of 27 141 tonnes of CO2 equivalent and 3501 602 m3 of water.

records.title: Şeker Mobil
records.description: Şekerbank offers banking and loan services via an online and mobile app designed to meet the financial needs of agricultural stakeholders in Türkiye. Using the online bank's Calculation Tools, potential borrowers can easily select the type of credit they require and specify a loan amount along with the maturity period of their choice. The tools then calculate the expected monthly instalment amount thereby aiding customers in financial planning. Şekerbank's renewed mobile application, “Şeker Mobil”, serves as a convenient platform allowing customers to conduct their banking transactions securely and effortlessly 24/7, without needing to visit a physical branch. The application features products aimed at simplifying the financial lives of farmers and producers, with sections for agricultural loans, a “Hasat” card for the purchase of farming inputs, and financial or loan advice.
records.abstract: Mobile app for agricultural loans and banking solutions

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: The app can be used by smallholders, the main users of the app, to access agricultural loans in Türkiye. Şekerbank started to receive loan applications via the Internet and mobile branches after reaching out to tradesmen and farmers via digital channels. Access to the bank’s services has become easier and faster, according to the website, and tradesmen and farmers can now make rapid applications to meet their banking needs with instant responses.

records.title: Smart pheromone trap
records.description: Smart traps are plant pest control tools that operate similar to conventional, analogue pheromone traps, but differ in their use of integrated cameras to monitor infestations, and their use of computer vision algorithms and AI technologies to study and differentiate insect species. The built-in sensors count the number of pests caught, and the collected data is sent to the farmer's smartphone using IoT technologies in the form of daily reports. The programme also warns the user if the population reaches the control number at any of the monitored sites. In addition to up-to-date factual information, the system can make a predictive analysis of the distribution of pests, allowing the farmer to carry out the optimum preparations for plant protection. One pheromone trap is installed for every 4–5 ha of farm, while scientific research requires a placement of one trap for every 100m2 area. The pheromone installations also make it possible to determine when, where and against which pests pesticides were applied, reducing the use of disinfectants by at least 50 percent and crop destruction by 60 percent.
records.abstract: Plant pest control tool
records.owner_name: The Plant Protection Agency of Uzbekistan

_annotations.Impact: The Smart Pheromone Trap applies multiple technologies to pest management as a data-driven approach supporting farmers and researchers in Uzbekistan. Utilizing IoT, AI and machine learning technologies, the solution provides users with real-time information and predictive analyses of the pest populations in their fields. Strategically placed traps offer insights into pest prevalence, steering the application of pest management practices and potentially reducing the need for widespread pesticide applications. Moreover, the derived data can influence decision-making related to pest control, potentially impacting crop yields and enabling a more targeted approach to pest management. The system, overall, aims to blend technological interventions with agricultural practices in a app that can assist farmers in navigating the uncertainties and challenges posed by pest infestations, while aligning with certain sustainability aspirations.

records.title: O'ZAGROLIZING
records.description: O’ZAGROLIZING is a mobile application designed to bridge the gap between farmers and modern agricultural equipment leasing in Uzbekistan. The “O’ZAGROLIZING” mobile application provides users with rapid access to information about JSC “Uzagroleasing” and its regional divisions (branches), the leasing terms, and a catalogue of agricultural machinery and equipment. The mobile app contains a list of tractors and other agricultural equipment, as well as other items, from which the user can select what they need and make a preliminary calculation of leasing cost. The user can also request a consultation with a specialist from Uzagroleasing JSC. O’ZAGROLIZING provides real-time data through a user-friendly interface, addressing the challenges faced by farmers in securing appropriate equipment for efficient agricultural production.
records.abstract: Mobile app for accessing information about leased agricultural equipment

_annotations.Impact: O’ZAGROLIZING empowers Uzbek farmers by offering an easily accessible platform for the identification and securing of leased agricultural equipment. The app streamlines such processes, thus contributing to efficiency in agricultural practices and the facilitation of modern farming techniques, contributing potentially to increases in agricultural output in the region. The benefits voiced by the technology provider include rapid access to information about available machinery or equipment; the ability to leave an online request for a call back; prompt access to information on current contracts; information on previously submitted leasing applications; and the ability to monitor the technical status of leased equipment by regional representatives of Uzagroleasing JSC.

records.title: Orbit
records.description: Orbit is a field scouting app that supports real-time crop monitoring by making use of satellite-based remote sensing. Orbit’s easy-to-use interface, 24/7 expert support and cutting-edge technologies allow farmers to manage risks and optimize production. The main functions of the application include: remote crop monitoring; comparisons with neighbours' yield potentials; irrigation advice;variable rate application; 24/7 expert agronomist access. Farmers can be kept informed about their fields and supported in making data-backed decisions. This agriculturally-oriented application utilizes satellite imagery also for the early identification and mitigation of such issues as nutrient deficiencies and irrigation anomalies. It amalgamates technology and agronomy, resulting in a app that supports risk management and optimized production by delivering critical data directly to farmers and agronomists, ensuring the integration of data-driven decisions into agricultural practices.
records.abstract: Field scouting app supporting real-time crop monitoring

_annotations.Impact: Orbit contributes to the reduction of crop loss and optimization of production by supporting the early detection of potential issues, efficient farm management and strategic planning based on data-driven insights and recommendations. Through its comparative yield analysis, irrigation advice and 24/7 expert support features, among others, it empowers farmers in making informed decisions that enhance yield, thereby contributing to increased food production and sustainability in agriculture.

records.title: Kiva
records.description: Kiva is an online crowdfunding app and mobile app that connects individuals who are seeking to improve their lives through small agricultural loans with potential sources of funding around the world. Borrowers apply for loans through local partners to fund various projects and activities in agriculture, healthcare, education, etc. Information about the loan, once submitted, is carefully edited and translated by a global network of volunteers, and made accessible to a global community of lenders. Once a loan has been fully funded, the local partner disburses the funds to the borrower. The disbursement and repayment of the loan are managed directly by Kiva in the United States.
records.abstract: Crowdfunding app for microloans supporting agriculture and rural development

_annotations.Source: ["FAO-ITU Digital Excellence in Agriculture call for good practices","Information provided by a member of the organization","Desktop research"]

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: Kiva has overseen the crowdfunding of loans amounting to USD 1.6 billion (as of Sep 2023). According to the website, Kiva’s borrowers have a 96 percent repayment rate. The impact of Kiva's operations, as stated in the testimonies of various beneficiaries on the website, underscores the effectiveness of the microloan programme. Malik, a student who runs a cafe in the West Bank, states that the financial support he received facilitated his return to academic studies, while still contributing to his family's living expenses. "My life improved after I took out the loan. I was able to look after my interests again, returning to complete my studies while still helping my family with living expenses," he states. It is worthy of note that Kiva loans helped many people endure the economic fallout related to the COVID-19 pandemic. For instance, Feride, a grocery store owner in Türkiye, said that her microcredit had been instrumental in the sustaining of her business in the most challenging times. "Everyone struggled when the pandemic began. We faced hardships, which led me to apply for this microcredit. It eased our struggle, thankfully," she notes. According to the website the average repayment of loans disbursed through Kiva is 96.4 percent.

records.title: My Cattle Manager
records.description: My Cattle Manager is a mobile application designed specifically to aid dairy and livestock farmers in the management of their operations more efficiently. Users can track and record such cattle-related events as insemination, pregnancy and vaccinations, and can monitor milk production, income and expenses. The application provides real-time reports in both visual and PDF formats, making it easier for farmers to make data-driven decisions. The app can be accessed offline, allowing the management of tasks even when no Internet connection is available. The app also facilitates family tree tracking, which allows farmers to monitor lineage and make informed breeding choices. Multiple cattle breeds can be managed through the My Cattle Manager app, giving users the flexibility to access breed-specific statistics at any given time. The app also features financial management that allow the tracking of farm cash flows, while customizable reminders ensure timely data entry. The app supports data sharing across multiple devices, which makes it ideal for multi-user environments, and a web version is available for centralized data management and advanced reporting. Users can print out the reports or export them in various formats, such as PDF, Excel and CSV.

records.title: Gaiasense
records.description: Gaiasense is a smart farming system available both as a mobile app and online app that continuously records and analyses field-based data, featuring also technological tools that support farm management and an advisory service. Farmers, researchers, and advisors can make use of the collected data to make informed decisions about water and soil management, pest control and farm operations. The system is structured around four key dimensions, namely: Remote, Field, Eye and Farm. In the “Remote” dimension, the system periodically updates satellite imagery to provide detailed data on plant growth and soil conditions, regardless of the farm's location. The “Field” dimension uses strategically placed sensors in agricultural areas to continuously collect air, soil and plant condition data for further analysis. The “Eye” dimension makes use of a network of specialists who use advanced tools to collect field samples, adding an extra human layer of expertise to the data observation and collection process. Finally, the “Farm” dimension allows producers to digitally record their work activities, the inputs they use and the harvest outcomes, without requiring any specialized computer skills. Gaiasense is designed to be customizable to different regional conditions, including soil types, microclimates and crop varieties. The minimal annual subscription fee and the absence of any upfront investment outlays for hardware ensure the accessibility of the multidimensional data even to smallholder farmers. Users register through the website and can utilize the app immediately through a structured annual subscription.
records.abstract: Digital farm management and advisory system

_annotations.Impact: Gaiasense, today, covers more than 25 types of crops, and has infrastructure installed in 70 different regions across Greece covering more than 150 000 acres. It has been downloaded over 5000 times from the Google Play Store. The company claims that in a few years, most of the Greek agricultural land will be covered. The company claims that its priority is now to integrate new regions of the country where there is more interest in terms of the local productive economy.

records.title: İş Bank Online Agricultural Credit
records.description: İş Bank offers a specialized financial solution for farmers in the form of “Instant Agricultural Loans” specifically for agricultural inputs. The loans are available to all through the bank’s mobile app and online app, regardless of whether an applicant has a pre-existing commercial credit limit with the bank. Applicants can request instalment payments up to 50 000 TL (equivalent to approx. USD 1740), with a maximum maturity of 12 months. Applications can be submitted through İşCep or the Internet Branch and are evaluated in real-time. Upon approval, the loan amount is immediately credited to the applicant's demand deposit account. Farmers can apply for loans through the İşCep app, the Internet Branch or in person at İş Bank branches through the Imece Card and Agricultural Loan Application page. İş Bank reserves the right to change the loan conditions, including possible requests for collateral.

records.title: ExactFarming
records.description: ExactFarming is a multifunctional online app supporting digital agronomy and the real-time monitoring of fields. The app makes use of different tools and products, that can be accessed also by farmers, agricultural input producers and other stakeholders in the supply chain, such as financial and insurance institutions; and seed, fertilizer and agro-chemical producers and distributors. The app makes use of satellite monitoring to aid in the analysis of field conditions and yield predictions; weather forecasting, helping farmers make informed decisions; and a robust communication infrastructure that promotes the seamless sharing of data and collaboration among farmers, consultants and contractors. The solution addresses the challenges of effective farm management and data-driven decision-making, and optimizes agricultural production through intelligent insights.

It further offers mechanisms supporting the mitigation of risks and the anticipation of issues based on data-driven insights and forecasts. The app endows its users with various functionalities aimed at supporting agricultural productivity and sustainability by aligning technological interventions with farming activities, thereby creating an environment that emphasizes informed decision-making in support of improved agricultural outcomes.

records.title: Farm Records
records.description: Farm Records is a record-keeping app that has been designed to help farmers manage their expenses, income and overall profitability. The mobile app supports detailed record-keeping for various aspects of farming, including farm and unit details, investments, harvests and labour usage. It contains features for tracking both inflows (sales) and outflows (expenses), thereby providing a comprehensive overview of the farm's financial health, based either on the Lebanese Pound (LBP) or US Dollar (USD), and allows farmers also to document their home consumption. Farm Records offers reporting capabilities that allow the creation of profit and loss statements for the entire farm, individual units or specific seasons, thus providing enhanced business insights. These reports can be easily saved in PDF format for further analysis or record-keeping.

records.owner_name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations

SDGs.value: SDG 8: Decent work and economic growth

_annotations.Impact: To date, nine farm business schools have been hosted, in Mhaydthe (Rachaya district, Bekaa), Aley (Aley district, Mount Lebanon), Baakline and Mresti (Chouf district, Mount Lebanon), Boudai (Baalbek District, Baalbek-Hermel), Karm Chbat, Hrar and Aidamoun (Akkar district, Northern Lebanon) and Jezzine (Jezzine District, South Lebanon). According to FAO, the mobile app has been further developed based on the feedback of the farmers who participated in the pilot FBS. The farmers recognized it as essential for the improvement of their farming activities, to facilitate farmers’ engagement in record keeping activities,  and to ensure informed decision-making by leveraging the benefits of digital technologies.

It contains features for tracking both inflows (sales) and outflows (expenses), thereby providing a comprehensive overview of the farm's financial health, based either on the Lebanese Pound (LBP) or US Dollar (USD), and allows farmers also to document their home consumption. Farm Records offers reporting capabilities that allow the creation of profit and loss statements for the entire farm, individual units or specific seasons, thus providing enhanced business insights. These reports can be easily saved in PDF format for further analysis or record-keeping.
_raw.Impact: To date, nine farm business schools have been hosted, in Mhaydthe (Rachaya district, Bekaa), Aley (Aley district, Mount Lebanon), Baakline and Mresti (Chouf district, Mount Lebanon), Boudai (Baalbek District, Baalbek-Hermel), Karm Chbat, Hrar and Aidamoun (Akkar district, Northern Lebanon) and Jezzine (Jezzine District, South Lebanon). According to FAO, the mobile app has been further developed based on the feedback of the farmers who participated in the pilot FBS. The farmers recognized it as essential for the improvement of their farming activities, to facilitate farmers’ engagement in record keeping activities,  and to ensure informed decision-making by leveraging the benefits of digital technologies.

records.title: Electronic government of the Republic of Kazakhstan
records.description: The Electronic Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan is an information and registration web- and mobile-based app that provides all citizens of Kazakhstan with access to government services for such purposes as the issuance of documentation and the submission of payments, while also facilitating the interactions of government agencies and the general public. The site can be used to access over 350 services and projects, including registration systems, databases and documentation, online queues at service centres and systems for the validation of payment receipts. For example, the project “E-licensing” automates and simplifies the procedure for obtaining a business licence or permit, while the “E-notary” system facilitates the registration of notary activities and document validation. The other services offered are certifications for real estate, disabilities, pensions, and healthcare.  Actors in the agriculture value chain can use the tool to register such inputs as farm equipment, veterinary drugs and feed additives, to obtain agricultural production, processing, livestock and fishery subsidies, to access phytosanitary certificates to facilitate the export of quarantinable products, and to obtains various licences, such as those required by veterinarians and for the import of pesticides, and for work in environmental protection. The app also contains information about subsidy application procedures, regulations and applicable taxes. Furthermore, the app can be used to make state tax payments and for the payment of state fees related to the issuance of identity documents and certificates, for mobile and other communication services, and to pay fines and utility bills. The e-Government portal contains a register of government services with details of submission processes, the relevant authorities and the applicable laws. The portal serves further as a line of communication between citizens and the government, allowing feedback on the services undergoing development through “service testing”, as well as an “Open Government” system for poll responses, participation in the drafting of laws and interactions with government officials. Finally, a “Smart Bridge” project has been developed to connect government systems with the private sector that serves also as a business registration app. e-Government services can be accessed via a mobile application that also contains a database of connected citizens . Another mobile app named “Saqbol” facilitates coronavirus tracking. The app was developed with the help of the “National Information Technologies” Joint-Stock Company, and the state-owned Government for Citizens corporation supported the integration of services into a single portal, and now manages the external perimeter and portal technologies. Before 2022, the implementation of the e-Government digitalization project was led by Zerde National Infocommunication Holding, and the digitalization implementation program is currently being managed by the Ministry of Digital Development, Innovation and the Aerospace Industry.

records.title: AgroHouse
records.description: AgroHouse is an e-commerce for the purchase of agricultural inputs, facilitating the selection of products, the organization of shipping to a convenient address and the completion of payment procedures. AgroHouse is based in Tashkent, and is a leading distributor of premium agricultural products to Central Asia. Its imports of high-calibre European-branded items, such as seeds, crop protection tools and fertilizers, have allowed AgroHouse to develop deep connections with leading brands in Europe. Aside from distribution, the company also specializes in local product trials, market research and product registration activities, and arranges workshops and seminars. Its primary objective is to become a provider of a full range of services, ensuring sustainability while adding value to all stakeholders.
records.abstract: Marketplace for sales of agricultural inputs and services

_annotations.Impact: The e-commerce system of AgroHouse is expected to speed up, standardise, and facilitate the trade and distribution of agricultural inputs produced by European providers among Central Asian farmers. Beyond the e-commerce system, the website seeks to provide agri-input buyers with access to several complementary services with a view to boosting productivity in the region. The standardized information provided for all products listed in the e-commerce catalogue, as well as the website media support, including photos, videos and downloads, contribute to the reduction of information asymmetry in the purchasing process.

records.title: Agroplatforma
records.description: Agroappa is an online information system designed to streamline interactions between farmers, suppliers and service providers. Overall, Agroappa integrates several online information and exchanges related to farm accountability; crop and livestock management; business transactions of agri-food inputs and outputs; and access to financing and insurance. Soft loans, crop planning, contracts, insurance and leasing are among the essential services that can be accessed electronically, ensuring transparency and efficiency. The online information system aids farmers in the digital placement of crops and ensures smooth coordination between all those involved. Agroappa also functions as a primary loan disbursement system, featuring a unified register that assigns each land user an electronic passport and a unique identification number. Producer proposals for crop placements for future harvests are displayed and approved on an electronic map. The document flow between agricultural entities and their service providers is fully digitized. Advanced features, such as the real-time tracking of loan settlements and the digital processing of such agreements as futures contracts and insurance policies, are to be incorporated in the future.
records.abstract: Unified information system for agricultural operations
records.owner_name: Ministry of Agriculture of the Republic of Uzbekistan

_annotations.Impact: Agroappa promises the reduction of paper-based transactions, and greater simplification, transparency and efficiency in Uzbekistan's agricultural sector, from farming to administration and trade. It aims to close the existing information gaps, thus ensuring timely loan disbursements, and serves as a unified system for crop planning, documentation and land user assessment.
